en.name: Sala Farnese
description:
The hall shows the late Renaissance layout typical of the Italian wall decoration painting tradition. This style is especially employed in public and noble residences and at the same time recalls the use of fake pictures framed by telamones, inaugurated by the Carracci.  
The scenes are depicted inside large framed squares or ovals that simulate paintings hanging from the walls. These are alternated with painted monochrome decorations of fake sculptures or architectural elements.  
The original painted vault was demolished in the late nineteenth-century and replaced with the present wooden coffered ceiling.  
The 4 scenes in the ovals and small squares show episodes that have their roots in the local religious history and popular devotion: *The Restitution of the Holy Band of the Virgin*, *The Miracle of the Blessed Virgin of San Luca*, *Saint Petronius Handing the Theodosian Privilege to the Magistrates of Bologna*, *Cardinal Albornoz Examining some of the Projects for the Navile Canal*. The 4 main pictures illustrate episodes with popes and kings who had a special role in the European history: *The Coronation of Emperor Charles V*, *King Francis I Heals the People affected by Scrofula*, *The Triumphal Entrance of Pope Paul III in Bologna*, *Pope Urban II blesses the Bolognese Crusaders Leaving for the Holy Land*.  
The frescoes were made by a team of Bolognese painters led by Carlo Cignani which included Lorenzo Pasinelli, Luigi Scaramuccia, Girolamo Bonini, Giovanni Maria Bibiena, Emilio Taruffi. This academic and narrative style is typical of the Bolognese Baroque tradition.

The so-called Farnese Hall was the great entrance to the papal cardinal Legate’s residence, on the second floor in the Municipal Palace of Bologna. Its name comes from a monumental statue of pope Paul III Farnese once present in the hall.  
The fresco decoration covering the walls celebrates important episodes in the history of Bologna, such as *The Coronation of the Emperor Charles V* that took place in town in 1530.
artist: Giovanni Maria Bibiena (1625–1665) and Bartolomeo Morelli known as il Pianoro (dead 1703); Luigi Scaramuccia (1616–1680), Carlo Cignani (1628–1719) and Emilio Taruffi (1633–1696)
history:
This cycle of frescoes shows 8 episodes of the history of Bologna. The images celebrate the glorious time of the rule of the Papal States over the town and the powerful Farnese family, including popes and cardinals. Cardinal Legate Girolamo Farnese commissioned the entire wall decoration in 1660 and linked his name to this enterprise.  
This enormous room, formerly known as Royal Hall, was meant to house official ceremonies taking place in the Cardinal Legate's residence. This room was also the antechamber to the Chapel, which is located on the right side.  
Thanks to the large staircase located inside the Palace, even processions with horses could reach the great hall.  
The seventeenth-century monument dedicated to Pope Alexander VII was once standing in the adjoining Swiss Hall. It was moved against the back wall of the Sala Farnese in 1845, during some restoration work. It stands as a substitute for the marble statue of Pope Paul III by Giovanni Zacchi da Volterra which was lost after the Napoleonic invasion.
keywords: Papal ceremonies; Charles V; Clement VII; Carlo Cignani; Luigi Scaramuccia; Francis I; Farnese family; Fresco; Historical painting; Emilio Taruffi; Paul III; Figural decoration; Girolamo Bonini known as il Pianoro; Giuseppe Maria Bibiena; Paolo III; Crusades; Kings of France; re taumaturghi; Scenography
tags: Girolamo Bonini known as il Pianoro
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Sala Farnese (Palazzo Comunale)
description:
La sala presenta lo schema decorativo tipico della tradizione italiana tardo rinascimentale, impiegato soprattutto in residenze pubbliche e nobiliari, e riprende la tradizione post-carraccesca del quadro riportato inframmezzato da telamoni.  
Le scene sono dipinte entro ampi rettangoli e ovali con cornici che fingono dipinti appesi alle pareti; ai finti dipinti si alternano decorazioni monocrome che imitano  sculture o decorazioni architettoniche.  
Il soffitto dipinto originale fu demolito alla fine del diciannovesimo secolo e sostituito dall'attuale soffitto ligneo a cassettoni.  
Quattro scene entro ovali o rettangoli di minori dimensioni rappresentano episodi legati alla storia religiosa locale e alla devozione popolare: *La restituzione della* *Sacra Benda della Vergine*, *La Madonna di S. Luca fa cessare la pioggia, S.* *Petronio trasmette il privilegio teodosiano, il Cardinale Albornoz esamina alcuni progetti per il canale  Navile*. I quattro dipinti più grandi presentano episodi che hanno per protagonisti papi e re che hanno svolto un ruolo di primo piano nella storia europea: *L'incoronazione di Carlo V, Francesco I re di Francia cura gli ammalati di scrofola, L'ingresso trionfale a Bologna di Papa Paolo III, Papa Urbano II benedice i crociati bolognese in partenza per la Terra Santa.*  
Gli affreschi furono dipinti da un gruppo di pittori bolognesi diretti da  Carlo Cignani: Lorenzo Pasinelli, Luigi Scaramuccia, Girolamo Bonini, Giovanni Maria Bibiena, Emilio Taruffi. Il loro stile accademico e narrativo è tipico della tradizione barocca bolognese.

La cosiddetta Sala Farnese era l'ingresso monumentale alla residenza del cardinal legato, posta al secondo piano del palazzo Pubblico di Bologna. Il suo nome deriva da una statua di papa Paolo III Farnese che un tempo si trovava in questo luogo.  
La decorazione ad affresco delle pareti ricorda importanti episodi della storia di Bologna, come l'I*ncoronazione di Carlo V*, avvenuta nella città nel 1530.
artist: Giovanni Maria Bibiena (1625–1665) e Bartolomeo Morelli detto il Pianoro; Luigi Scaramuccia (1616–1680), Carlo Cignani (1628–1719) e Emilio Taruffi (1633–1696)
history:
Il ciclo di affreschi illustra otto episodi della storia di Bologna che celebrano l'epoca gloriosa del dominio pontificio sulla città e la potente famiglia Farnese che potè contare tra i suoi membri vari papi e cardinali: tra questi il cardinal  Legato Girolamo Farnese che commissionò l'intera decorazione murale nel 1665 e legò il suo nome a questa impresa pittorica.  
Colloocata nel nucleo più antico dell'agglomerato di edifici che costituiscono l'attuale palazzo Pubblico, nel Medio Evo era destinata  a magazzino di granaglie; denominata poi  Sala Regia, questo vasto ambiente fu destinato ad ospitare le cerimonie ufficiali che si svolgevano nella residenza del cardinal legato e soprattutto era l'anticamera della sua cappella, posta sul lato destro rispetto all'ingresso.  
Anche sfilate a cavallo potevano raggiungere questo vasto salone, grazie all'ampia scalinata posta all'interno del palazzo.  
Il monumento seicentesco dedicato a papa Alessandro  VII, che un tempo si trovava nella vicina sala degli Svizzeri, fu trasferito sulla parete di fondo di questa sala nel 1845, in occasione di alcuni lavori di restauro, in sostituzione del monumento marmoreo a Paolo III, di Giovanni Zacchi da Volterra, disperso durante l'invasione giacobina.
keywords: Cerimoniale papale; Carlo V; Clemente VII; Carlo Cignani; Luigi Scaramuccia; Francesco I; Farnese; Affresco; Pittura di Storia; Emilio Taruffi; Girolamo Bonini detto il Pianoro; Giuseppe Maria Bibiena; Paolo III; Decorazione figurata; crociate; re di Francia; re taumaturghi

en.name: *The Temptations of Saint Antony*
short_description:
The painting by Domenico Morelli shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris, it’s among the artist’s most complex artworks. Both realistic and symbolic elements characterise the painting, as well as a strong mystic, but at the same time erotic, tension. Inspired by *La Tentation de Saint-Antoine* by Gustave Flaubert from 1874, the painting shows realism in the imaginary setting influenced by oriental elements. The work was finished in 1878 and sent to the French merchant Goupil to be shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris. It was also presented at the National Exposition in Turin in 1880 and completely misunderstood by contemporaries who blamed Morelli for having resigned to make fashionable art.  
A smaller version of it was painted by the artist while making a lot of preparatory drawings in which Saint Anthony is standing next to the rock wall. In the final version the Saint is seated on the ground trying to resist the temptations embodied by the two half-naked women on the left.
keywords: Realism; France; La tentation de Saint-Antoine; Orientalism; Orientalist painting; religious topics; exoticism; eroticism; woman; international exhibitions; universal exposition; national exposition; exoticism in fine arts and literature
partner: MIBACT | National Gallery of Modern Art (GNAM)

en.name: Theresian thaler
short_description: The Maria Theresian Thaler, a large silver coin originally created by Queen (Empress) Maria Theresia, minted in Austria until 1890. It was used in the Arabic Peninsula as a means of payment. This coin was countersigned at the Arabian mint of Ras Bab el Mandeb in 1890.

en.name: Men meeting in a guesthouse
description:
The coffee fireplace is located on the narrow side of the guesthouse near the entrance door, and coffee pots of various sizes adorn its cornice. Guests are offered bitter coffee as soon as they enter the typically one-room building. The pot of coffee is ready and needs only to be heated.  
If necessary to support the guesthouse, villagers bring coffee beans or coffee powder from the nearest town. Bitter coffee is also served in private households on happy and sad occasions, such as religious feasts and funerals. The use of these guesthouses in rural northeast Syria corresponds to that of the urban room type *diwan* in Damascus, the *qa’a* in Aleppo, the *mudif* in southern Iraq, and the *mafraj* in Yemen.

en.name: A seat on a train. In *Unfortunately, it was paradise: Selected poems* (M. Akash & C. Forché, Trans. & Eds.; S. Antoon & A. El-Zein, Trans., p. 180). University of California Press.
description:
Mahmoud Darwish, who was born in al-Birwa in Galilee in 1941 and died in Houston in 2008, was a Palestinian poet whose work turned the loss of home into one of the central themes of modern Arabic literature. His village was destroyed in 1948, and when his family secretly returned from Lebanon, he grew up under what Israeli law classified as "present absentee" status, effectively an internal refugee. His early poems, among them "Bitaqat Hawiyya" (Identity Card), published in 1964, made him a leading voice of Palestinian resistance poetry. His political life, however, came at a high personal cost. A member of the Israeli Communist Party, he was arrested several times and placed under house arrest, and in 1970 he left to study in Moscow before moving to Cairo. This marked the beginning of some twenty-five years of exile, taking him through Beirut, Tunis and Paris. He served on the PLO Executive Committee and drafted the 1988 Palestinian Declaration of Independence, but resigned from the committee in 1993 in opposition to the Oslo Accords. He returned to the Palestinian territories in the mid-1990s and later divided his time between Ramallah and Amman. Over the years, his poetry became less directly political and increasingly lyrical and reflective, a language in which exile, memory, love and death appeared as questions of human existence as much as of national history. His public readings drew  
  
audiences of thousands across the Arab world, and he remains one of the most widely read Arab poets of the twentieth century.
keywords: Palestine; Refugee; Poetry; Activism; Israel; Arab

en.name: Base for a tray (*sinija*)
description: The *Sinija* (Tr. *sini*) is a large, round tray made of copper or brass. It was used for serving food or as a floor dining table – a *sofra* (Tr. *sofra*). tTherefore it had an important place in the shared living culture of the Ottoman Balkans among urban populations of different confessional and ethnic backgrounds. The diameter of *sinijas* sometimes reached 1–2 meters or more. When used as a floor dining table, the *sinija* was placed on a wooden or iron base. Valued for their craftsmanship, locally produced or imported *sinijas* have also found a place in the interiors of the modern age as wall decor or top parts of decorative side tables placed on custom-made bases of different styles.
dates: Hegira late 13th–early 14th century / AD late 19th–early 20th century
keywords: floor dining table; carving; Ottoman Balkans.

ar.name: مسجد السليمية.
description:
بني مسجد السليمية على يد المعمار العثماني الشهير سنان في منطقة تدعى قواق ميداني أو ساريبايير. ويعتبر من أهم المباني في تاريخ العمارة العالمي، فهو تحفة معمارية: صرح ذو تصميم مميز. يقع المسجد، وكذلك المدرستان المحيطتان به من الجنوب الشرقي والجنوب الغربي، وسط فناء مساحته 190x 130 م. وقد أضيف إلى المجمَّع، من الجهة الغربية للفناء، صفٌ من الحوانيت ومدرسة التسميع (القرَّاء) على يد المعمار داؤود آغا في عهد السلطان مراد الثالث (حكم في الفترة 982- 1003/ 1574- 1595).  
  
يتألف المسجد من قاعة للصلاة، مستطيلة، شبه مربَّعة، في الجهة الشمالية، وفناء ذي أروقة. وهناك ثلاثة مداخل للفناء: من الشمال والشرق والغرب. ويوجد في وسط الفناء نافورة ماء ذات 12 ضلعاً. وثمة فسحتان في الرواق، المخصص للمتأخرين بالقدوم، سقفت كل منها بقبو خشبي، بينما باقي الفسحات مغطاة بالقباب. وتبرز في كل زاوية من زوايا قاعة الصلاة مئذنة بارتفاع 71 م وبثلاث شرفات. ويمكن الدخول إلى شرفات المئذنتين الشمالية الشرقية والشمالية الغربية بواسطة ثلاثة سلالم مستقلة.  
  
المعلم الرئيسي الذي يمنح مسجد السليمية عظمته المعمارية هو سقف قاعة الصلاة. ترتفع القبة الصرحية إلى 42.25 م ويبلغ قطرها 31. 28 م، وتقوم على ثمانية أعمدة لكل منها 12 ضلعاً. منطقة الانتقال من المسقط شبه المربع إلى القبة نفذت بواسطة كوات ضخمة في الزوايا. تمَّ تعزيز العمودين الشرقي والغربي بدعامتين لكل منهما، تستتران خلف الأروقة والشرفات. وفي الداخل تمَّ تزيين المساحات الفاصلة بين الجدران والأعمدة بشرفات بارزة. في مسجد السليمية تخلَّى سنان عن المساحات ذات القباب النصفية والقباب الثانوية التي استخدمها في مبانٍ أخرى ذات تصاميم مركزية (باستثناء نصف القبة التي تغطي مساحة المحراب)؛ وهكذا فقد حلَّ مشكلة الانسجام في المساحات الداخلية. يوجد في وسط قاعة الصلاة مقصورة للمنشدين، تحتها سبيل ماء؛ أما مقصورة السلطان فتقع في الزاوية الجنوبية الشرقية.  
  
الجدران الخارجية الرئيسية للمبنى مكسوة بحجارة مربعة منحوتة، في حين بعض العناصر المعمارية، كالمدخل الرئيسي والمحراب والمنبر، مكسو بالرخام. أما جدران المساحة المقبَّّبة للمحراب وجدران مقصورة السلطان وقوصرة النوافذ والمسافات الفاصلة بين شرفة النساء فكلها مزخرفة ببلاطات من الخزف الإزنيقي الملون تحت طبقة مزججة. اقتلع جزء من البلاطات الخزفية من مقصورة السلطان إبان الحرب العثمانية الروسية في عام 1293/ 1877- 1878 ونقل إلى موسكو، لكنه أُعيد في الفترة ما بين 1982- 1984. زخرفت حجرة الإنشاد والقبة بتشكيلات من الأزهار الملونة. المنبر، بزخرفته الهندسية الفخمة، والمحراب، بفجوته متعددة الأضلاع، وسقفه ذي المقرنصات، يعتبران من أرقى النماذج العثمانية في الحفر في الرخام.  
  
خضع مسجد السليمية للترميم في الفترة ما بين 1954- 1971، وما يزال يستخدم حتى اليوم مكاناً للعبادة. المدرسة الواقعة إلى جنوب شرق المسجد تستخدم اليوم متحفاً للفن التركي والإسلامي في إديرن. أما مدرسة أحاديث النبي إلى الجنوب الغربي فلم تعد مستخدمة.
artist: المعمار: خوجة معمار سنان آغا، أما الملحقات فبنيت على يد المعمار داؤود آغا.
keywords: إديرن؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ سليم الثاني؛ سنان؛ قرميد.

en.name: Selimiye Mosque.
description:
The Selimiye Mosque was built by the great Ottoman architect, Sinan, in an area called Kavak Meydanı or Sarıbayır. Considered as his masterpiece it is one of the most important buildings in the history of world architecture both for its design and its monumentality. The mosque, together with the two *madrasa*s on its southeast and southwest, is located within a courtyard measuring 190 m x 130 m. The row of shops (*arasta*) and recitation school (*darülkurra)* to the west of the courtyard were added to the complex by the architect Davud Ağa in the reign of Sultan Murad III (r. 982–1003 / 1574–95).  
The mosque consists of a rectangular, nearly square prayer hall and, on the north side, a courtyard with porticoes. There are three entrances to the courtyard: north, east and west. In the centre of the courtyard is a 12-sided fountain. Two of the bays of the portico for latecomers have panelled vaults, while the rest are covered with domes. Each corner of the prayer hall features a minaret nearly 71 m high with three balconies. The balconies of the minarets on the northeast and northwest corners are accessed by three separate staircases.  
The main feature which makes the Selimiye Mosque such a major work of architecture is the roof of the prayer hall. The monumental dome, 31.28 m in diameter, is carried on eight 12-sided pillars. The dome rises to 42.25 m in height. The zone of transition is made up of enormous squinches. The east and west pillars are supported by two buttresses each, concealed outside by the porticoes and galleries. Inside, the spaces between the walls and the pillars are adorned with galleries. In the Selimiye Mosque, Sinan abandoned the half-domes and secondary domed spaces he had used in his other buildings with centralised plans (with the exception of the half-dome covering the space with the *mihrab*); he thus solved the problem of the unity of the interior space. In the centre of the prayer hall is a loge for chanters (*muezzin mahfili*) with a fountain underneath it; the sultan's loge is in the southeast corner.  
The main outer walls of the building are covered with ashlar, while elements like the main portal, the *mihrab*, and the *minbar* are covered with marble.  
The walls of the domed space for the *mihrab*, the walls of the sultan's loge, the tympana of the windows and the spandrels of the women's gallery are decorated with underglaze-painted Iznik tiles. One section of the tiles in the sultan's loge was torn down during the Ottoman-Russian war of AH 1293 / AD 1877–8 and taken to Moscow. In the *muezzin mahfili* and the dome, the decoration consists of painted floral designs. These were restored in 1982–4. The *minbar*, with its rich geometric decoration, and the *mihrab*, which features a multi-sided niche covered with a *muqarnas* conch, are among the finest examples of Ottoman marble carving.  
The Selimiye Mosque underwent restoration in 1954–71 and continues to function as a place of worship today. The *madrasa* to the southeast of the mosque is used as the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Art of Edirne, while the school for traditions of the Prophet (*darülhadis)* to the southwest, is no longer in use.

The great Ottoman architect Sinan considered the Selimiye complex he built in Edirne for the Sultan Selim II as the masterpiece of his *usta* (master) period. The complex contains a mosque and two *madrasa*s with a *darülkurra* (recitation school) and an *arasta* (row of shops) added later. The dome of the mosque is 31.28 m in diameter and 42.25 m in height, rising on eight piers. The mosque is one of the most important buildings not only of Turkish architecture but also in the history of world architecture.
artist: Architect: Koca Mimar Sinan Ağa, with later additions by the architect, Davud Ağa.
keywords: Dome; centralised plan; floral decoration; tilework; Edirne; Sinan; Selim II

es.name: Mezquita Selimiye
description:
La mezquita Selimiye fue construida por el gran arquitecto otomano Sinan en un lugar llamado Kavak Meydani o Sarıbayır. Se considera su obra maestra y constituye uno de los edificios más importantes de la historia de la arquitectura mundial, tanto por su estructura como por su monumentalidad.  
La mezquita y sus dos madrasas, ambas en el lado sur, están dentro de un patio de 190 × 130 m. La fila de tiendas *(arasta)* y la escuela de recitación *(darülkurra)* que se alzan en el lado oeste son obra del arquitecto Davud Ağa, que las agregó al complejo durante el sultanato de Murad III (r. 982-1003 / 1574-1595).  
La mezquita comprende una sala de oración casi cuadrada y, al norte, un patio con pórticos y tres entradas –en los laterales norte, este y oeste– en cuyo centro hay una fuente de 12 lados. Dos de las crujías del pórtico para los rezagados poseen bóvedas de nervios y las demás están cubiertas por cúpulas. De cada esquina de la sala de oración se eleva un alminar de casi 71 m de altura y tres balcones. A los balcones de los alminares noreste y sureste se sube por tres escaleras independientes.  
El elemento principal que hace de esta mezquita una obra maestra es la cubierta de la sala de oración. La cúpula monumental, de 31,28 m de diámetro y 42,25 m de altura, reposa sobre ocho pilares dodecagonales. La zona de transición está compuesta por enormes pechinas. Los pilares este y oeste se apoyan en dos contrafuertes cada uno, que no se ven por fuera porque quedan ocultos por pórticos y galerías. En el interior, los espacios entre las paredes y los pilares están adornados con galerías. En la mezquita Selimiye, Sinan abandonó el principio de las semicúpulas y los espacios secundarios con cúpulas que había aplicado en otras construcciones de planta central, a excepción de la semicúpula que cubre la zona del *mihrab*; de esta forma resolvió el problema de la unidad espacial del interior. En el centro de la sala de oración hay una tribuna para los muecines *(muezzin mahfili)* con una fuente debajo. El palco del sultán se encuentra en la esquina sureste.  
Los muros exteriores principales del edificio están cubiertos con sillares, mientras que otros elementos, como el portal principal, el *mihrab* y el *minbar*, están revestidos de mármol.  
Las paredes del *mihrab*, el palco del sultán, los tímpanos de las ventanas y las enjutas de la galería de las mujeres están decorados con azulejos de Iznik pintados bajo vidriado.  
En 1293 / 1877, durante la guerra entre otomanos y rusos, fueron arrancada una parte de los azulejos del palco del sultán y llevada a Moscú. En la tribuna de los muecines y la cúpula, la decoración presenta motivos florales pintados, que fueron restaurados entre 1982 y 1984. El *minbar*, de elaborada decoración geométrica, y el *mihrab*, un nicho de varias caras cubierto con una concha de mocárabes, son dos de los máximos exponentes de la talla otomana en mármol.  
La mezquita se restauró entre 1954 y 1971 y hoy sigue siendo lugar de culto. La madrasa del sureste es actualmente sede del Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico de Edirne; sin embargo, la escuela de los dichos del Profeta *(darülhadis)* del lado suroeste ya no se usa.

El gran arquitecto otomano Sinan consideraba que el complejo Selimiye que construyó en Edirne para el sultán Selim II era la obra culminante de su época *usta* ('maestra'). El conjunto consta de mezquita, dos madrasas con una *darülkurra* ('escuela de recitación') y una *arasta* ('fila de tiendas') añadida más tarde. La cúpula, que descansa sobre ocho pilares, mide 31,28 m diámetro y 42,25 m de alto.  
Esta mezquita es uno de los edificios más importantes no sólo de la arquitectura turca, sino también de la historia de la arquitectura mundial.
artist: Arquitecto: Koca Mimar Sinan Ağa, con añadidos posteriores del arquitecto Davud Ağa.
keywords: Cúpula; planta central; decoración floral; azulejos; Edirne; Sinan; Selim II.

fr.name: Mosquée Selimiye.
description:
La mosquée Selimiyé a été construite par le grand architecte ottoman Sinan dans un lieu appelé Kavak Meydani ou Sarıbayır. Considérée comme son chef-d'œuvre, elle est une des plus importantes créations de l'architecture mondiale, tant par sa conception que par sa monumentalité. La mosquée et ses deux *madrasa*, au sud-est et sud-ouest, se dressent dans une cour de 190 x 130 m. La rangée de boutiques (*arasta*) et l'école de récitation (*darülkurra*) à l'ouest de la cour ont été ajoutées par l'architecte Davud Ağa sous le règne du sultan Mourad III (r. 982-1003 H / 1574-1595 J.-C.).  
La mosquée comprend une salle de prière presque carrée et, au nord, une cour à portiques. Trois entrées permettent l'accès à celle-ci, au nord, à l'est et à l'ouest. En son centre s'élève une fontaine à douze côtés. Deux des travées du portique des retardataires possèdent des voûtes lambrissées, les autres sont recouvertes de coupoles. De chaque angle de la salle de prière s'élève un minaret de près de 71 m de haut à trois balcons. Ceux des minarets nord-est et nord-ouest sont accessibles par des escaliers indépendants.  
Le principal élément qui fait de cette mosquée un chef-d'œuvre est le couvrement de sa salle de prière. La coupole monumentale de 31,28 m de diamètre et de 42,25 m de haut repose sur huit piliers à 12 faces. La zone de transition regroupe d'énormes trompes. Les piliers est et ouest sont soutenus chacun par deux contreforts dissimulés de l'extérieur par les portiques et les galeries. à l'intérieur, les espaces entre les murs et les piliers sont occupés par des galeries. Ici, Sinan a abandonné le principe des demi-coupoles et des espaces secondaires sous coupole qu'il avait utilisé dans d'autres chantiers à plan centralisé (à l'exception de la demi-coupole recouvrant la zone du *mihrab*) et ainsi résolu le problème d'unité du volume intérieur. Au centre de la salle de prière s'élève une tribune pour chantres (*muezzin mahfili*) au-dessus d'une fontaine. La loge du sultan se trouve dans l'angle sud-est.  
Les principaux murs extérieurs sont parés de pierre taillée, les éléments comme le portail principal, le *mihrab* et le *minbar* sont recouverts de plaques de marbre.  
Les murs de la zone du *mihrab* sous sa coupole, ceux de la loge du sultan, les tympans des fenêtres et les écoinçons de la galerie des femmes sont décorés de carreaux d'Iznik peints sous glaçure. Une partie des carreaux de la loge du sultan ont été enlevés et emportés à Moscou lors de la guerre russo-turque de 1293 H / 1878 J.-C. Dans le *muezzin mahfili* et la coupole, le décor consiste en motifs floraux peints, restaurés en 1982-1984. Le *minbar* à riche décoration géométrique et le *mihrab* à niche facettée et coquille à *mouqarnas* sont parmi les plus beaux exemples de la sculpture de marbre ottomane.  
La mosquée a bénéficié d'une campagne de restauration de 1954 à 1971 et sert toujours de lieu de culte. La *madrasa* du sud-est est devenue le Musée d'art turc et islamique d'Edirne. L'école pour l'étude des traditions du prophète (*darülhadis*) au sud-ouest n'est plus utilisée.

Le grand architecte ottoman Sinan considérait le complexe Selimiye, qu’il construisit à Edirne pour le sultan Sélim II, comme le chef-d’œuvre de sa période phare. Le complexe comprend une mosquée et deux *madrasa* avec une darülkurra (école de récitation) et une rangée d’*arasta* (échoppes) ajoutées ultérieurement. La coupole de la mosquée, de 31,28 m de diamètre et 42,25 m de hauteur, repose sur huit piliers. La mosquée est l’un des plus importants édifices non seulement de l’architecture turque mais aussi de l’histoire de l’architecture mondiale.
artist: Architectes : Koca Mimar Sinan Ağa, et additions ultérieures par Davud Ağa.
keywords: coupole ; plan centralisé ; décoration florale ; carreaux ; Edirne ; Sinan ; Sélim II

tr.name: Selimiye Camii.
description:
Mimar Sinan'ın Edirne'de Kavak Meydanı ya da Sarıbayır adı verilen alanda inşa ettiği ve “ustalık dönemi” eseri olarak nitelendirdiği Selimiye Camii, tasarımı ve anıtsallığıyla dünya mimarlık tarihinin en önemli yapıtlarından biridir. Cami, güneydoğu ve güneybatısındaki iki medreseyle birlikte, 190mX130m boyutlarında bir avlu içine yerleştirilmiştir. Avlunun batısındaki arasta ve darülkurra, külliyeye, Sultan III. Murad döneminde, Mimar Davud Ağa tarafından eklenmiştir.  
  
Cami, kareye yakın dikdörtgen planlı bir harim ve kuzeyindeki revaklı avludan oluşmaktadır. Avluya kuzey, doğu ve batı cephelerindeki üç açıklıktan girilmektedir. Avlunun ortasında, onaltıgen planlı bir şadırvan bulunmaktadır. Son cemaat yeri revak birimlerinden ikisi manastır tonozuyla, diğerleri kubbelerle örtülüdür. Harimin dört köşesine, yaklaşık 71m. yüksekliğinde, üçer şerefeli birer minare yerleştirilmiştir. Kuzeydoğu ve kuzeybatı köşedeki minarelerin şerefelerine üç ayrı merdivenle çıkılmaktadır.  
  
Selimiye Camii'ni dünya mimarlık tarihinin en önemli yapıtlarından biri yapan ana özelliği, ibadet mekanının kurgusudur. Mekanı örten 31.28m. çapındaki anıtsal kubbe, onikigen kesitli sekiz ayakla taşınmaktadır. Kubbenin yerden yüksekliği 42.25m.dir. Kubbeye geçiş, iri tromplarla sağlanmıştır. Doğu ve batıdaki ayaklar, dışta, revak ve galerilerle gizlenmiş ikişer payandayla desteklenmiştir. İçte, duvarlarla ayaklar arasında kalan boşluklar galerilerle değerlendirilmiştir. Sinan, Selimiye Camii'nde, mihrabın yer aldığı yarım kubbeli bölüm hariç, merkezi planlı diğer yapılarında uyguladığı yarım kubbe ya da kubbelerle örtülü ek birimleri terk etmiş, mekan bütünlüğü sorununu ortadan kaldırmıştır. Harimin ortasında, altında fıskiyeli havuz bulunan *müezzin mahfili*, güneydoğu köşesinde ise *hünkar mahfili* yer almaktadır.  
  
Yapının beden duvarları düzgün kesme taşlarla; taçkapı, mihrap, minber gibi unsurları ise mermerle kaplanmıştır.  
  
Mihrabın içinde yer aldığı yarım kubbeyle örtülü bölümün duvarları, hünkar mahfili duvarları, pencere alınlıkları ve kadınlar mahfili kemer köşelikleri, sıraltı teknikli İznik çinileriyle süslenmiştir. Hünkar mahfilindeki çinilerin bir bölümü, 1877-78 Osmanlı-Rus savaşında sökülerek Moskova'ya götürülmüştür. Müezzin mahfili ve kubbede, bitkisel desenli kalem işi süslemelere yer verilmiştir. Bu süslemeler 1982-1984 yılları arasında onarılmıştır. Zengin geometrik süslemeler içeren minberi ve mukarnaslı kavsarayla örtülü çokgen kesitli bir nişe sahip olan mihrabı, Osmanlı mermer işçiliğinin en güzel örneklerindendir.  
  
1954-1971 yılları arasında onarım geçiren Selimiye Camii, bugün halen ibadethane olarak işlevini sürdürmektedir. Güneydoğusundaki medrese Türk-İslam Eserleri Müzesi olarak kullanılmıştır.

Mimar Sinan'ın Sultan II. Selim için Edirne'de inşa ettiği ve ustalık dönemi eseri olarak nitelendirdiği Selimiye Camii, iki medrese ve bunlara sonradan eklenen arasta ve darülkurra ile birlikte bir külliye oluşturmaktadır. Selimiye Camii, sekiz destek üzerine oturan 31.28 metre çapında ve yerden 42.25 metre yükseklikteki kubbesiyle sadece Osmanlı mimarisinin değil, dünya mimarlık tarihinin de en önemli yapılarındandır.
keywords: Edirne; II. Selim; kubbe; merkezi plan; bitkisel bezeme; çini

en.name: Migration preparations from Lemnos island to Turkey
short_description: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.
holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
keywords: migration; population exchange
partner: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)

en.name: Stucco decoration and paintings in the Chapel of St. Anthony
description: While the stuccowork in Our Lady of the Scapular Chapel facing it is the work of the  Styrian practitioner, J. A. Quadrio, the Chapel of St. Anthony has stuccowork made later by an unknown author. Interwoven plants and ribbons frame eight medallions depicting the Life of St. Anthony of Padua, painted by Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, in around 1738.
artist: Stuccowork: unknown artist; painter: Ivan Krstitelj (Johann Baptist) Krstitelj Ranger (1700–1753)

en.name: Coach belonging to King João V
description:
A brilliant example of a royal ceremonial vehicle, the coach was built in Portugal during the first half of the 18th century. It is generally agreed that it was commissioned by King D. João V for his personal use. Its gilt carving is attributed to the sculptor José de Almeida whose brother, Felix Vicente de Almeida, was an architect and sculptor attached to the royal household. The coach clearly reflects the transition between the Louis XIV and Louis XV styles, although there is also an obvious Italian influence in the decoration. This is not surprising since José de Almeida studied in Rome under Carlo Monaldi. According to Max Terrier the coachwork may have been executed by Filipe Juvara, an Italian sculptor working in Portugal for King D. João V.  
The main features are the elegant curving lines and the Rococo-style rippling movement enhanced by the *bombé* shape of the side panels and doors, typical of Regency furniture during the period (1715–1723). The four side-sections of the body bear elegant carvings of female figures holding castles, attended by genii. The bodywork is covered by woodcarving and chiselled bronze finials, handles and springs, in the form of young women's heads, known as *espagnolettes*, much in vogue all over Europe at the time. According to Luciano Freire the paintings were executed by José da Costa Negreiros, a Portuguese painter and a disciple of André Gonçalves. On the other hand Luis Keil believes the painting could be attributed to the French painter, Pierre Antoine Quillard, (1701-33) a disciple of Antoine Watteau. Apparently, Quillard arrived in Lisbon to serve the Portuguese court where “he executed not only religious paintings but also portraits, palace interiors and coach panels”.  
The interior of the coach is lined with rich red velvet and the rear wheels are decorated with small carvings representing the 12 signs of the zodiac.

This coach was built in Portugal during the first half of the 18th century.  
Decorated in the rococo style with French and Italian influences, it has a closed body with elegant curving lines and glazed windows. The interior of the coach is lined with red velvet and the rear wheels are decorated with the 12 signs of the zodiac.
artist: José de Almeida (1700, Portugal–1769, Portugal); Felix Vicente de Almeida (n.d.–1785, Portugal); Filipe Juvara (1685, Messina, Italy–1735, Madrid, Spain); José da Costa Negreiros (1714, Portugal – 1759, Portugal); Pierre-Antoine Quillard (1701, Paris, France–1733, Lisbon, Portugal)
keywords: Coach; horse-drawn vehicle
materials: Wood, leather, bronze, glass, silk and velvet; wood: carved, painted and gilded; bronze: melted, soldered, gilded

pt.name: Coche de D. João V
description:
Este coche é um perfeito exemplar de uma viatura de cerimónia construída em Portugal, na primeira metade do século XVIII, mandado fazer pelo rei D. João V para seu uso pessoal. O trabalho de talha deste veículo, de uma qualidade notável, é atribuído ao escultor José de Almeida e ao seu irmão Félix Vicente de Almeida, arquitecto e entalhador da casa real. O coche pertence ao período de transição entre os estilos Luís XIV e Luís XV, embora com grande influência italiana na decoração, o que não é de estranhar, uma vez que José de Almeida estudou em Roma. Na opinião de Max Terrier, este projecto pode também ter sido executado por Filipe Juvara, (1685-1735) escultor italiano que trabalhou em Portugal para o rei D. João V.  
A principal característica deste veículo é a elegância das suas linhas sinuosas, num movimento ondulante, prenúncio do estilo *rocaille*, acentuada pelo tratamento das madeiras em *bombé*, os painéis laterais e as portinholas, típicos do mobiliário do período da Regência francês (1715-1723). Nos quatro cantos da caixa, é de realçar o excelente trabalho esculpido de graciosas figuras femininas, sustendo castelos, auxiliadas por pequenos “amores”. Em toda a estrutura do coche, incluindo maçanetas, puxadores e molas, esculpidas em madeira ou em bronze, encontram-se representadas cabeças de jovens mulheres, conhecidas como *espagnolettes*, muito em voga por toda a Europa, nessa época. De acordo com Luciano Freire, as pinturas terão sido executadas por José da Costa Negreiros, pintor português que foi aluno de André Gonçalves. Por outro lado, Luis Keil crê que esse trabalho pode ser atribuído ao pintor francês Pierre Antoine Quillard (1701-1733), discípulo de Watteau, que esteve em Lisboa ao serviço da coroa portuguesa e “pintou, além de quadros religiosos, cenas galantes, retratos, decorações de palácios e painéis de carruagens”.  
O interior do coche é estofado com um rico tecido de veludo vermelho e as rodas traseiras são decoradas com pequenas esculturas representando os doze signos do zodíaco.

Coche construído em Portugal, na primeira metade do século XVIII.  
A sua decoração é em estilo Rococó, de influência francesa e italiana. Possui uma caixa fechada de elegantes linhas curvas e janelas de vidro. O interior é estofado a veludo vermelho e na decoração das rodas apresenta os signos do zodíaco.
artist: José de Almeida (1700, Portugal – 1769, Portugal); Félix Vicente de Almeida (n.d., Portugal – 1785, Portugal); Filipe Juvara (1685, Messina, Italia – 1735, Madrid, Espanha); José da Costa Negreiros (1714, Portugal – 1759); Pierre-Antoine Quillard (1701, Paris, França –1733, Lisboa, Portugal).
keywords: Coche; veículo; veículo de tracção animal.
materials: Madeira, couro, bronze, vidro, seda e veludo. Madeira: entalhada, dourada e policromada; Bronze: fundido, soldado e dourado.
tags: Madeira, couro, bronze, vidro, seda e veludo. Madeira: entalhada, dourada e policromada

en.name: Astrolabe
short_description: This portable astrolabe consists of a suspension device with a 18cm diameter disk, divided up into degrees, and a handle. Two moving parts are used for measurements: the spider on the front, and the alidade (a flat ruler revolving round a point) on the back. The astrolabe remained in use as the primary tool for navigation until the 18th century. However, it was also used as an astronomical tool, to measure the height of stars from the horizon, or the angle separating one star from another.
keywords: Navigation tools; astronomy
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Astrolabe
short_description: Cet instrument portatif en cuivre comprend un appareil de suspension composé d’une poignée, d’un disque de 18 cm de diamètre dont le bord est divisé en degrés. Deux éléments mobiles servant aux mesures : sur la face, l’araignée ; sur le dos, l’alidade, qui est une règle plate tournant autour du centre. L’astrolabe reste le principal instrument de navigation jusqu’à la fin du XVIIIe siècle. Il est aussi un instrument de mesures astronomiques puisqu’il sert à mesurer la hauteur des astres au-dessus de l’horizon ou la distance angulaire entre eux.
keywords: Instruments de navigation; Astronomie
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
short_description: Postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. Intended for a relatively popular western market. Illustrates the social structures and costumes of the last days of the Ottoman empire. Great reformer Mahmud II in European-influenced dress.

en.name: *David with the Head of Goliath*
description: The painting shows the key moment in the Old Testament story of David depicting the head of the giant Goliath, killed with a slingshot by the young shepherd. The canvas belonged to Cardinal Scipione Borghese from at least 1613, in which year, following payment, it was framed. The work dates from the artist's second stay in Naples (1609–1610), when Caravaggio, fleeing Rome having been convicted of killing a man, nevertheless continued to maintain a relationship with Cardinal Scipione. The latter's influence on his uncle Pope Paul V, after the painting was sent by the painter as proof of penance, convinced the Pope to grant a pardon. During his return journey, Caravaggio was delayed on the Tuscan coast near Port'Ercole, and died of unknown causes in July 1610, never reaching Rome. The oldest sources already recognise the artist's self-portrait in Goliath's face, but opinion differs regarding the young hero. Some see a self-portrait of the artist as a young man. As usual, the composition, executed using dark colours, demonstrates a lively and acute drama simply through the expressiveness of the faces. On David's unsheathed sword we can see some letters that have been interpreted to represent the virtuous motto “*HumilitAS Occidit Superbiam*”.

Caravaggio innovatively painted himself as Goliath and sent the painting to Pope Paul V seeking pardon for the murder he had committed. The canvas may in fact be a double self-portrait, as David could be a portrait of the painter as a young man. The use of artificial light by Caravaggio has a moral function, probably expressing divine grace. It was at this time that Caravaggio’s artistic influence began to spread around the world.
keywords: Christian themes; self portrait; symbol

it.name: Davide con la testa di Golia
description: Il dipinto raffigura il momento saliente della storia di Davide raccontata nell'Antico Testamento: l'esposizione della testa del gigante Golia, ucciso dal giovane pastore a seguito del lancio di una pietra. La tela apparteneva al cardinale Scipione Borghese almeno dal 1613, anno nel quale, come risulta dai pagamenti, venne fornita di una cornice. L'opera viene datata al secondo soggiorno napoletano (1609-1610) dell'artista, periodo nel quale Caravaggio, fuggito da Roma a seguito della condanna per l'uccisione di un uomo, continuò comunque a mantenere rapporti con il cardinale Scipione. Questi esercitò la sua influenza presso lo zio Paolo V per la concessione della grazia e il dipinto, inviato dal pittore come prova di pentimento, convincerà il pontefice ad accordare il perdono. Durante il suo viaggio di rientro Caravaggio venne tuttavia fermato sul litorale toscano nei pressi di Port'Ercole, morendo per cause ancora sconosciute nel luglio 1610, senza poter raggiungere Roma. Già nelle fonti più antiche viene riconosciuto l'autoritratto dell'artista nel volto di Golia, mentre per quanto riguarda il giovane eroe, le ipotesi sono diverse; alcuni addirittura vi identificano un autoritratto in fattezze giovanili. Come di consueto la composizione, eseguita con colori cupi, risente di un'accesa drammaticità essenziale, resa unicamente con l'espressività dei volti. Sulla spada sguainata di Davide si leggono alcune lettere interpretate come la sigla del motto, esempio di virtù, “HumilitAS Occidit Superbiam”.

Caravaggio con un linguaggio innovativo dipinse il suo autoritratto nella testa di Golia e inviò l'opera al papa Paolo V come richiesta di grazia per l'omicidio che aveva commesso. La tela è anche stata interpretata come un doppio autoritratto, dove David potrebbe raffigurare il ritratto del giovane pittore. L'uso della luce artificiale è concepito da Caravaggio con intento morale, probabilmente espressione della “grazia divina”.  
In questo periodo l'influenza artistica di Caravaggio era diventata internazionale.
keywords: Tematiche cristiane; autoritratto; simbolo

ar.name: ثوب ملك خضاري
description:
ثوب ملك خضاري، يرجع أصله لمنطقة الخضر في مدينة بيت لحم، حيث تطرزه النساء باليد للمناسبات الخاصة فقط، ويمكن للعرائس فقط ارتدائه ليلة زفافهن. ثوب ملك من قماش الخضاري، وقماش أبو وردة. القبة مطرزة بقبة الملك التقليدية بقطبة اللف، وبها تطريز القوار والورود، مغطاة بقطعتين من قماش المخمل الأزرق مطرز عليها عصفور. الرقبة والأكتاف مصنوعة من قماش أحمر اللون، والأكمام مصنوعة من قماش هرمزي حريري بالإضافة إلى القماش الأصلي للثوب المطرز بساعة بيت لحم ويعلوه طائر. وتظهر البنايق من القماش الحريري ومثبتة على الثوب بواسطة عرق المناجل، وعليها في الأسفل تطريز على شكل ورود وزخارف نباتية، بالإضافة إلى بعض الصلبان. تتميز الأزياء الفلسطينية التقليدية بتركيز قوي على الزخرفة والألوان، وهي مطرزة ومشغولة من أجود وأغلى الأقمشة، كما تظهر في هذا الثوب بشكل خاص.  
تاريخ الحصول على القطعة: 1983 م.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن التاسع عشر
keywords: تقليدي، منسوجات فلسطينية، ثوب

en.name: Ikhdari Dress (*Malaq*)
description: This *malaq* dress originates in the Al-Khadir area of Bethlehem District, where women embroider it by hand. It is worn only by brides for their wedding day. This dress is made with *Abu Warda* fabric. It has a traditional *malaq* chest panel of flower pot motifs, bordered by two pieces of blue velvet fabric with a bird embroidered on them. The neck and shoulders are made of red fabric. The sleeves are made with silk *hirmizi* cloth in addition to the original fabric of the dress and are embroidered with a Bethlehem clock and a bird. The *banayeq* (side panels) are embroidered with clock and floral motifs in addition to multiple crosses. Traditional Palestinian costumes are characterized by strong emphasis on decoration and colour and are designed from the finest and most expensive fabrics, as shown by this dress.
keywords: Traditional costume; Palestinian textile; Dress; Clothing

en.name: *Dhiil*
description: The *dhiil* is a traditional Somali milk container, both practical and finely crafted, used mainly to collect and store milk from different livestock, and sometimes water. Traditionally made by Somali nomad women, the *dhiil* can be woven from the thorny *qabo* (a plant from the *Euphorbia* genus), as featured, or crafted from wood. Its construction involves peeling and softening the spiny *qabo* stems into long strips, which are then coiled and bound in a basketlike technique. The vessel has a hemispherical base that widens to a central ridge (*kelli*) before narrowing toward the top, capped with a fitted lid (*bugul*). Once woven, the *dhiil* is treated with *asal*, a dye and sealant made from red acacia bark (*qaroon*), giving it a rich colour and protective finish. The interior is traditionally smoked over *shilin* (wood) and cleaned carefully, a process that imparts a distinct smoky flavour to the milk. Milk is shared from the cup of the *dhiil*, called *harrubi*, in a tradition known as *waddagid* ("sharing").
place: Belonged to Mohamed family in Somalia; passed down through generations before being inherited by Salim Mohamed.
keywords: Dhiil, milk container, haroub

ar.name: ستارة باب الكعبة المشرفة في مكة المكرمة
description: يُمثل هذا الستار، والمعروف أيضًا باسم ستارة أو بُردة أو بُرقع والمزدان بالآيات القرآنية، أكثر الأجزاء تفصيلًا لقماش كسوة الكعبة التي تكسو الكعبة المشرفة بمكة. وقد ابتُكر هذا النموذج تحت رعاية الملك فهد بن عبد العزيز آل سعود، الذي اعتلى العرش في عام 1405 هجريًا/ 1985 ميلاديًا.

en.name: Curtain for the door of the Holy Ka‘ba in Makkah al-Mukarramah
description: This curtain, known as *sitara*, *burdah* or *burqa* and embroidered with qur’anic quotations, forms the most elaborate part of the *kiswah* textile cover which encloses the Holy Ka‘ba in Makkah. This example was made under the patronage of King Fahd ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Saud, who ascended the throne in AH 1405 / AD 1985.
keywords: Curtain; Door; Holy Ka'ba; Makkah al-Mukarramah; Textile; patronage; pilgrimage; hajj

en.name: Church and Tower of the Clergymen
description: With this church the architect, Nicolau Nasoni, provided Portugal with some new architectural features. Nasoni designed a narrow façade over a stairway; a “screen” placed in the middle of the hill. The body of the oval-shaped church then followed: it has double walls and passages that surround the chancel, giving access to the back of the building. Next are the service facilities, where the offices of the congregation and brotherhood were located. Nasoni gave up the idea of towers flanking the façade and built a single colossal bell tower at the extreme rear of the building.

An oval shaped Baroque church with an infirmary and offices. It is attached to a tall bell tower located at the back of the building. The interior has Late Baroque decorative stonework and gilded woodcarving.
artist: Architect: Nicolau Nasoni (1691–1773); woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), João Lopes da Maia [n.d.], Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)
history:
Construction of the Church of the Clergymen began in 1731. It was commissioned by the Brotherhood of the Clérigos, founded in 1707 as the result of a merger between three counterpart entities: The Brotherhoods of St. Peter, St Peter Nery and of Our Lady of Mercy. Because the brotherhoods constituted priests or secular clergymen, the order assumed the name of Brotherhood of the Clérigos or Clergymen.  
The façade of the church was built in 1745 and the stairway a bit later, in around 1753; by 1748 the building was almost finished. The Clergy's House was finished in 1759. It included offices and the infirmary. The Tower was erected more slowly, between 1757 and 1763.
keywords: Oval; Baroque church; tower, Porto
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Igreja e Torre dos Clérigos*
description: O edifício é de uma monumentalidade ímpar. A verticalidade da fachada, acentuada pelo grande embasamento que lhe serve de fundamento, e a impressionante torre sineira - uma verdadeira agulha quase gótica e catedralícia -, harmonizam-se com a invocação do templo a Nossa Senhora da Assunção, como que traduzindo em pedra as palavras que remetem para o movimento ascensional da Virgem, em direcção ao Céu. A genialidade de Nasoni empresta à igreja traços completamente inéditos na arquitectura portuguesa. Uma vez que houve que solucionar dificuldades de implantação e de fundação do edifício, que teria que vencer um grande desnível, instalando-se num terreno longitudinal, Nicolau Nasoni projectou uma fachada relativamente estreita e crescendo em altura. A esta grande entrada, sucede o corpo da igreja, de planta oval e com duplas paredes, com corredores de passagem em serventia rodeando a nave e dando acesso à parte posterior do edifício. A seguir, levantam-se as dependências utilitárias, autênticos escritórios das congregações e confrarias que aqui tinham assento, com maior sobriedade em termos de tratamento decorativo e seguindo, ao contrário do templo, um esquema arquitectónico tradicional, de paredes rectas. Por fim, Nasoni, que abdicava das torres ladeando a fachada, colocou a única e colossal sineira na face posterior do edifício.

Igreja de uma só nave, inscrita numa oval, com dependências anexas destinadas à congregação. Grande torre sineira na face posterior do edifício e interior com decoração barroca *rocaille* sobre pedra e talha dourada.
artist: Arquitecto: Nicolau Nasoni (1691–1773); entalhadores: Luís Pereira da Costa (activo c.1724), João Lopes da Maia [n.d.], Domingos Martins Moreira (activo 1746–1750).
history: As obras começaram logo em 1731, por encomenda da Irmandade dos Clérigos, que se constituíra em 1707, através da fusão de três entidades congéneres: a Confraria de S. Pedro, a Confraria de S. Pedro Neri e a Confraria de Nossa Senhora da Misericórdia. Por serem formadas por padres ou clérigos seculares, assumiu o nome de Confraria dos Clérigos. Em 1745, foi construída a fachada do templo e, pouco mais tarde, a escadaria (cerca de 1753), mas em 1748 a igreja já estaria quase concluída. A Casa dos Clérigos, como é chamada a parte, por assim dizer, burocrática do edifício, estava concluída em 1759, incluindo a secretaria e uma enfermaria. A torre foi construída mais lentamente, entre 1757 e 1763.
keywords: Oval; Nasoni; igreja barroca; torre, Porto.

en.name: Ewer and Wine Glass
description:
Part of the set that is kept in the Museum of Applied Art collection, these items were created at the end of the 19th century in one of the Czech glasshouses, the Gebrüder Feix Brothers, of Albrechtsdorf (Bohemia). The items are made of colourless glass, with ground decoration at the bottom in the form of stylized leaves. Each part of the set has a silver coating along the rim and filling the engraved emblem of the Obrenović dynasty with the motto, Tempus et Meum Jus – (translation from Latin: "Time and My Right").  
The Museum of Applied Art collections contain items from the legacy of the Obrenović dynasty, which with minor interruption reigned in Serbia from 1815 to 1903. The part of the set with a dynastic monogram comes from the last period of this dynasty's reign. A large part of the procurement for the Obrenović court came from Austro-Hungary, particularly utility items and sets primarily intended for formal banquets. Thus, in addition to German, French and Austrian glass, the Feix glass, known for its high quality and various decorative models, was also purchased for the Obrenović court. This factory's specialty was a type of crystal decorating, created by fine galvanic grinding technique, which filled the ground fields with enamel or, as with the coat of arms of the Obrenović dynasty on the Obrenović court set, by silvering.
artist: Gebrüder Feix in Albrechtsdorf Bohemian Glass Manufacture
keywords: Blown glass; Coat of arms; Court life; Crystal; Cut-glass decoration; Tableware; Feix Brothers; Bohemian glass manufacture; Silvering
materials: Blown crystal glass; cut, with silver rim; engraved and silver-plated royal coat of arms

en.name: The Sealed Fountain
description: One of the springs which feeds into Solomon's Pools at Artas. This watercolour shows a vaulted structure which is now known as the Spring House, in which water from 'Ain Farujeh is fed into the Lower Pool, which is the largest of the three reservoirs. The Spring House is situated in the eastern dam wall of the Lower Pool. Recent excavations and refurbishments have revealed the complex history of the pools over two millennia.
keywords: Solomon’s Pools, Artas, Bethlehem
materials: Watercolour and pencil on paper. Created in the studio from a pencil and ink sketch made on site.

en.name: Chair of Krste Petkov Misirkov
short_description: Misirkov’s book “On Macedonian Matters” lays the foundations of the modern Macedonian language and grammar. Being one of the central figures of the “Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society" in St. Petersburg, he largely contributed to issuing the periodical Macedonian and Russian-language publication, “Makedonski Golos” (“Macedonian Voice").

ar.name: قالب على شكل كبش.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن قالب على شكل كبش صنع من أجزاء متساوية من البدن وقطعة صغيرة تشكل رأس الكبش. هناك أربع حواف بارزة تعمل كمفاصل تظهر على الظهر وعلى الجزء العلوي من الرأس، وهناك أيضاً اثنتان تحت أرجل الكبش. أما قرون الكبش فتظهر بشكل واضح خلف أذنيه.  
  
يبدو أن هذا القالب قد استخدم خصيصاً لصناعة نوع خاص من الخبز أو الكعك للأطفال. وهناك قالب آخر على شكل فيل عثر عليه في نفس المكان.  
  
الكبش من الحيوانات المحببة للمسلمين، وورد ذكره عدة مرات في القرآن الكريم. القصة الرئيسية التي تذكر الكبش جاءت في سورة الصافات (رقم 37) في الآيات 102- 107. تذكر الآيات سيدنا إبراهيم الذي افتدى ابنه إسماعيل بكبش. كذلك فإن المسلمين يضحون بالأكباش، بالإضافة إلى حيوانات أخرى مثل الجمال والبقر والأغنام، في عيد الأضحى.  
  
يظهر الكبش أيضاً على الأرضيات الفسيفسائية في الكنائس البيزنطية في الأردن. كذلك فإن معظم الصناعات الحديدية في الفترة الإسلامية المبكرة كانت تصنع على أشكال حيوانات متعددة.
place: ربما تكون قد صنعت في سوريا.
keywords: أضحية؛ حديد؛ قالب؛ قصة سيدنا إبراهيم.

en.name: Ram mould.
description:
A ram-shaped mould made from two equal parts to form the body, and another small piece that forms the head. There are four hinged joints: one on its back, one on the top of its head and two at its feet. The horns of the ram are clearly visible behind the ears.  
The object seems to have functioned as a special kind of mould used for shaping bread or cake for children. Another mould in the shape of an elephant was found along with this one.  
The ram has particular significance for Muslims. It is mentioned several times in the Qur'an in for instance, *sura* 'Al Saffat' (chapter 37, verses 102–7), where the story of Abraham's sacrifice of his son Isaac is related and how ultimately Abraham sacrificed a ram in place of his son. Within the Muslim festival calendar is that of Eid Al-Adh'ha (Greater Bairam) when a ram is sacrificed, along with other animals such as a camel, a cow or a lamb.  
Rams are also a feature of the mosaic floors found in Jordanian Byzantine-period churches. The ram is also evident on the mosaic floor of the Umayyad palace, Qasr Hallabat. A number of Islamic-period metalwork pieces are made in the form of animals.

A cast iron mould shaped in the form of a ram from the Umayyad palace of al-Fudayn. It was found along with another mould in the shape of an elephant and they were probably meant to produce bread or cakes for children. Metalwork representing animals is common in early Islamic art.
keywords: Metal; mould; Ransom Story; Abraham

es.name: Molde en forma de carnero.
description:
Molde en forma de carnero realizado con dos piezas iguales que forman el cuerpo y otra pieza pequeña para la cabeza. Posee cuatro junturas articuladas: una sobre el lomo, otra en la parte superior de la cabeza y dos en las patas. Los cuernos del carnero son perfectamente visibles detrás de las orejas.  
Parece que el objeto sirvió como molde para hacer pan o bizcochos para los niños. Junto a este se encontró otro molde con forma de elefante.  
El carnero tiene un significado especial para los musulmanes. Es un animal que se menciona varias veces en el Corán, como por ejemplo en la sura 37, *Al-Saffat* (versículos 102-107), que relata la historia del sacrificio del hijo de Abraham, quien finalmente sacrificó un carnero en su lugar. En el calendario musulmán figura la Aid al-Adha o Gran Bairam, fiesta en la que se sacrifican un carnero y otros animales, como un camello, una vaca o un cordero.  
Los carneros también están presentes en los mosaicos de los suelos de las iglesias jordanas del periodo bizantino, así como en los del palacio omeya Qasr Hallabat. Se conservan varias piezas de metalistería con formas de animales fabricadas en el periodo islámico.

Molde de hierro fundido con forma de carnero del palacio omeya de al-Fudayn. Se encontró junto a otro molde con forma de elefante. Probablemente se usaran para hacer pan o bizcochos para los niños. La metalistería con formas animales fue común en el arte de los primeros tiempos del Islam.
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d.C.
keywords: Metal; molde; relato del rescate; Abraham.

fr.name: Moule en forme de bélier.
description:
Moule en forme de bélier réalisé en deux parties égales pour le corps et une petite pièce supplémentaire pour la tête. Il comporte trois points d'articulation : un sur le dos, l'autre au sommet de la tête, les deux derniers aux pieds. Le dessin des cornes est visible derrière les oreilles.  
Il s'agit sans doute d'un type de moule utilisé pour la confection de pains ou de gâteaux destinés aux enfants. Un autre moule en forme d'éléphant a été découvert à proximité.  
Le bélier revêt une signification particulière pour les musulmans. Il est mentionné à plusieurs reprises dans le Coran, par exemple à l'occasion du récit du sacrifice d'Abraham et de la manière dont celui-ci remplaça finalement son fils par un bélier (sourate XXXVII, “al-Saffat \[les Harmonies\]”, versets 102-107). Dans le calendrier des fêtes musulmanes figure l'Eid Al-Adh'ha (grand baïram), où l'on sacrifie un bélier et d'autres animaux comme un chameau, une vache ou un agneau.  
Les béliers sont présents dans l'iconographie des sols en mosaïque trouvés dans les églises jordaniennes de la période byzantine, ou dans celle du palais omeyyade de Qasr Hallabat, par exemple. Un certain nombre d'objets en métal de la période islamique sont en forme d'animaux.

Moule en fonte en forme de bélier du palais omeyyade d’al-Foudayn. Il fut découvert à proximité d’un autre moule en forme d’éléphant et ils étaient probablement utilisés pour la confection de pains ou de gâteaux destinés aux enfants. Le travail du métal représentant des animaux est commun dans le premier art islamique.
dates: IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: métaux ; moules ; Abraham

en.name: *Reposadero* or vat-base
description:
It has a cylindrical, hollow body with a straight base and a square-shaped rim, featuring a hole that would have served as a conduit for drainage. Both the base and the rim are slightly concave, the latter also has a whitish colour that could be interpreted as calcareous remains.  
  
The decoration is concentrated on the wall and consists of an epigraphic frieze between concave mouldings with marked edges. The central frieze is stamped with the inscription al-mulk with a six-pointed star positioned above the “m”.  
Functionally, the objects are known as *reposaderos* and served as supports for large water vats, which were both placed either in the courtyard or in domestic interiors. They preserved the water from impurities and kept it fresh, while also collecting any oozes liquid. By the spout of the *reposadero*, the water was transferred to basins or other vessels and could be used for washing hands or for human consumption. Furthermore, the stamped decoration, which repeats the word "*al-mulk*" or "the power", alludes to prophylactic practices of protection and praise of God.
dates: Second half of Hegira 6th century / AD 12th century
keywords: Water; Technology; Conservation; Household goods; Prophylactic practices

de.name: Deckenfresko: *Aufnahme des hl. Stephanus in den Himmel*
description: Die Fresken von Anras sind die frühesten selbständigen Arbeiten Martin Knollers und stehen noch ganz unter dem Einfluss seines Lehrers Paul Troger. Dargestellt ist im Langhaus die Aufnahme des Kirchenpatrons, des hl. Stephanus in den Himmel sowie die Auffindung seiner Gebeine. Die relativ kleinen Freskenfelder sind von gemaltem Stukko finto in Formen des frühen Rokoko umgeben, der ebenso von Knoller stammt.

en.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Acceptance into Heaven of St. Stephen*
description: The Anras frescos are the earliest independent works of Martin Knoller and are still wholly under the influence of his teacher Paul Troger. The nave fresco depicts the acceptance into heaven of the church patron, St. Stephan, as well as the discovery of his remains. The relatively small fresco panels are framed by “stucco finto” (painted stucco) in the forms of the early Rococo and are also the work of Knoller.

ar.name: الطيفور (صحن مقعّر).
description: طيفور بفوهة دائرية وحواف عمودية منحنية وشفة مثلثة. قاعدته محدبة قليلاً وساقه حلقية منحرفة؛ مطلي من الخارج بطلاء مزجج أحادي اللون عسلي. توجد في الداخل تقنية زخرفية خاصة تجمع مابين إفريز من وريدات صغيرة مختومة وزخارف تعتمد على تقنية الحبل اليابس *cuerda seca*، وتبدو فيها ألوان الطلاء المزجج المكوّنة من الأبيض والأخضر والبنفسجي والعسلي مفصولة عن بعضها البعض بشكل واضح بخطوط من المنغنيز. ويمثل الشكل المركزي شجرة حياة تتألف من ثلاثة زهور لوتس مرئية بشكل مسطح، ومتصلة فيما بينها بساق نباتية، ومحاطة بإفريز الوريدات المختومة. يُستكمل هذا التكوين بمخطط رباعي الأجزاء عند الحافة، يتكون من زوجين من الأشكال النباتية المتناوبة. ولموضوع شجرة الحياة أو شجرة الجنة مايماثلها في قطع الفخار العراقية ذات الانعكاسات المعدنية (البريق المعدني) التي تعود إلى القرن التاسع (Grube, 1976). قطعة مرمّمة.

طيفورٌ مزخرفٌ حسب تقنية الحابل اليابس. الشكل المركزي عبارة عن شجرة حياة مكونة من ثلاثة زهرات لوتس مرئية من الجانب ومرتبطة بواسطة ساق. أحيط المجموع بإفريز من الوريدات؛ وجرى إتمام الزخرفة بترتيب يضم أربعة أجزاء على الحافة، تتشكل من زوجين من الأشكال النباتية المتناوبة.
dynasty: الفترة الموحدية، النصف الثاني من القرن 6 الهجري / القرن 12 الميلادي
keywords: تجارة؛ فخار بتقنية الحبل اليابس cuerda seca.

en.name: Glazed bowl.
description: A bowl with a circular mouth, a curved vertical rim with a triangular lip, a hemispherical body and slightly convex base with diagonal foot-ring. The exterior is glazed in honey-coloured monochrome and the interior presents an unusual decorative style which combines a frieze of small stamped rosettes with the decoration in *cuerda seca* in which the white, green, purple and honey colours of the glaze are separated by lines of manganese. The central theme is the tree of life formed by three lotus flowers in cross-section joined by a stalk, surrounded by a frieze of stamped rosettes. The composition is completed by a design on the rim in four parts, consisting of two pairs of alternating plant motifs. The 'tree of life' or 'tree of paradise' theme already appeared in metallic lustre-ware in the earthenware of AH 3rd -century / AD 9th-century Iraq (Grube, 1976). The object has been restored.

Bowl decorated in *cuerda seca*. The central motif is a tree of life consisting of three lotus flowers seen from the side and joined by a stem, all surrounded by a rosette border. The decoration is completed by a four-part composition on the brim, formed by two pairs of alternating plant motifs.
dates: Hegira second half of 6th century / AD second half of 12th century.
keywords: cuerda seca; ceramic; trade
materials: Ceramic made from a coarse-grained straw and paste mix, modelled on a potter’s wheel, and fired in an oxidising atmosphere, glazed and decorated using the *cuerda seca* technique throughout.

es.name: Ataifor.
description: Ataifor con boca circular, borde vertical curvo con labio triangular, cuerpo hemisférico y base levemente convexa con pie anular diagonal. El exterior se reviste de vidriado monocromo melado y el interior presenta una particular técnica decorativa que combina un friso de pequeñas rosetas estampilladas con la decoración en cuerda seca total en la que los colores blanco, verde, morado y melado del vidriado se encuentran separados por trazos de manganeso. El tema central es un árbol de la vida formado por tres flores de loto vistas en alzado y unidas por un tallo, rodeado del friso de rosetas estampilladas. La composición se completa con un esquema cuatripartito en el borde, formado por dos pares de motivos vegetales alternados. El tema del “árbol de la vida” o “árbol del Paraíso” encuentra paralelos en reflejo metálico ya en la loza dorada iraquí del s. IX (Grube, 1976). Pieza restaurada.

El tema decorativo central de este ataifor es el “árbol de la vida”, formado por tres flores de loto vistas en alzado y unidas por un tallo, y rodeado por el friso de rosetas. La composición se completa con un esquema cuatripartito en el borde de dos pares de motivos vegetales alternados.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo VI H. / XII d. C.
keywords: Ataifor; Mértola; almohades; cerámica; cuerda seca; comercio

fr.name: Ataifor (plat creux).
description: *Ataifor* à bouche circulaire, bord vertical courbe et lèvre triangulaire, base légèrement convexe et pied annulaire diagonal. L'extérieur est recouvert d'une glaçure monochrome couleur miel ; l'intérieur présente une technique décorative particulière qui combine une frise de petites rosettes estampées et un décor à la *cuerda seca* et dans laquelle les couleurs blanc, vert, violet et miel de la glaçure se trouvent nettement séparées par des traits de manganèse. Le motif central est un arbre de vie formé par trois fleurs de lotus vues en plan et reliées par une tige, entourées de la frise de rosettes estampées. La composition est complétée par un schéma quadripartite sur le bord, formé par deux paires de motifs végétaux alternés. Le thème de l'arbre de vie ou arbre du Paradis trouve déjà des parallèles dans les faïences à reflets métalliques irakiennes du IXe siècle (Grube, 1976). Pièce restaurée.

Ataifor décoré selon la technique de la *cuerda seca*. Le motif central est un arbre de vie composé de trois fleurs de lotus vues de côté et reliées par une tige, le tout entouré d'une frise de rosettes. La décoration est complétée par une composition en quatre parties sur le bord, formée de deux paires de motifs végétaux alternés.
dates: Seconde moitié du VIe siècle H (du XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: céramique; cuerda seca ; commerce
materials: Céramique fabriquée dans une pâte jaunâtre peu compacte au tour rapide, cuisson en atmosphère oxydante ; glaçure ; décor à la cuerda seca totale.

pt.name: Tigela.
description: Tigela com boca circular, bordo vertical curvo com lábio triangular, corpo hemisférico e base levemente convexa com pie anular diagonal. O exterior está revestido com vidrado monocromo melado, apresentando o interior uma técnica decorativa que combina um friso de pequenas rosetas estampilhadas com a decoração em corda seca total em que as cores branca, verde, manganés e melada do vidrado se encontram separadas por traços de manganés. O tema central é uma árvore da vida formada por três flores de lotus vistas em alçado e unidas por um caule, rodeado pelo friso de rosetas estampilhadas. A composição completa-se com um esquema quatripartido no bordo, formado por dois pares de motivos vegetais alternados. O tema da “árvore da vida” ou “árvore do Paraíso” encontra paralelos na louça dourada iraquiana do século III AH / IX AH (Grube, 1976). Peça restaurada.

A composição completa-se com um esquema quatripartido no bordo, formado por dois pares de motivos vegetais alternados.

de.name: Ulrichsaltar
description: Das anonyme Altarbild des monumentalen Stuckmarmoraltares zeigt als zweiten Nebenpatron den heiligen Augsburger Bischof St. Ulrich, wie er reitend mit Kaiser Otto I. gegen die Ungarn in die Schlacht zieht und dabei die siegbringende  Kreuzreliquie hält.

en.name: Altar of St. Ulrich
description: The monumental scagliola marble altar is furnished with an anonymous painting depicting the second subsidiary patron the Holy Bishop from Augsburg – St. Ulrich – together with Emperor Otto I riding to battle against the Hungarians and thereby receiving the cross-relic which brings victory.

en.name: Statue of Cardinal Lavigerie
short_description: On the 23 November 1925, the French resident-general in Tunisia, Lucien Saint, organised a solemn gathering to commemorate 100 years since Cardinal Lavigerie's birth. The municipality of Tunis also received a statue of him brandishing a cross by the sculptor Élie-Jean Vézien, which they chose to put in Place Bab el-Bhar (at the entrance to the medina), a place of great importance to Tunisians. This choice of location angered the Tunisian population and triggered a protest from the students of the Zaytuna University, who considered this act an attack on their religious beliefs (it was placed close to the Zaytuna Mosque) and their traditions. The statue stayed there until Tunisian independence, when it was removed by the Mayor of Tunis.  Lavigerie was the Archbishop of Algiers and Carthage, and the founder of the Pères Blancs in 1868.
holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: French protectorate of Tunisia; missionaries in Tunisia
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Statue du cardinal Lavigerie
short_description: Le 23 novembre 1925, le résident général de France en Tunisie, Lucien Saint, commémore dans un rassemblement solennel le centenaire du cardinal Lavigerie. Par la même occasion, une statue de lui réalisée par le sculpteur Élie-Jean Vézien est offerte à la municipalité de Tunis, qui décide de l’installer sur la place Bab el-Bhar (à l’entrée de la Médina), lieu extrêmement important car faisant partie du quotidien symbolique des autochtones. Elle représente le cardinal brandissant la croix. La décision d’installer cette statue suscite le mécontentement des Tunisois d’origine arabe et provoque une manifestation de la part des étudiants de l’université Zitouna qui considèrent ce geste comme une atteinte à leurs croyances religieuses (car elle est placée à proximité de la mosquée Zitouna) et un mépris pour leurs traditions. La statue ne sera retirée qu’après l’indépendance de la Tunisie, par décision du maire de l’époque. Lavigerie était archevêque d’Alger et de Carthage, fondateur des Pères blancs en 1868.
keywords: Protectorat français en Tunisie; Missionnaires en Tunisie
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey* (painting)
short_description: This 1861 oil on canvas by B. de Moynier shows the Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey in front of the throne in the great hall of the Palais du Bardo, his right hand on the Tunisian constitution (which he has just proclaimed), his left holding his sword. He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold stripe and a short black coat with a gold belt and epaulets, in addition to the Nichan al-Amen medal and a green sash with a double red stripe. On his chest the Nichan al-Dam, the Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (classe majeur) medals can be seen, as well as a Légion d'Honneur and Nichan al-Iftikhar on a sling. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.
holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
keywords: Oil on canvas; B. de Moynier; Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey
materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Tableau de peinture *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey*
short_description: Tableau de peinture à l’huile sur toile réalisé en 1861 par le peintre B. de Moynier, il représente le bey Mohamed Sadok Pacha devant le trône de la grande salle du Bardo, la main droite posée sur la constitution tunisienne, qu’il venait de promulguer, la main gauche tenant son épée. Avec sa tenue officielle, un pantalon rouge orné de bandes dorées et d’un demi-manteau noir avec des épaulettes et une ceinture dorée, il porte au cou le Nichan Ahd el-Amen et son ruban vert à double liseré rouge. Sur sa poitrine, le Nichan ad-Dam, la plaque de la Légion d’honneur et celle de la classe majeure du Nichan al-Iftikhar ; en écharpe, le grand cordon de la Légion d’honneur et celui du Nichan al-Iftikhar. Œuvre témoin d’une intense activité diplomatique entre le palais du Bardo et les chancelleries occidentales.

de.name: Kath. Filialkirche St. Johann Nepomuk und Asamhaus
description: Der relativ schmale, in Vestibül, Gemeinde- und Altarraum unterteilte Kirchenraum liegt eingekeilt zwischen den Hauswänden und empfängt daher nur durch die Fassade, am Chor vom Hof aus sowie zuoberst am Gewölbeansatz sein Licht, was die Asams geschickt für die Inszenierung ihrer skulpturalen und malerischen Arrangements zu nutzen verstanden. Der Gemeinderaum ist einer zweistöckigen Hofkirche entsprechend organisiert, indem ihn eine vorspringende, elegant gekurvte Galerie mit Balustrade umgibt. Er ist eine Art Zuschauerraum für das im Chor und am Gewölbe sich abspielende „theatrum sacrum“.

Zu Recht gilt die nach ihren Schöpfern, den Brüdern Asam, benannte kleine Kirche im Herzen der Münchner Altstadt als Wunderwerk des bayerischen Sakralbarock: Die prunkvolle Noblesse einer Hofkirche liefert das Ambiente für theatralisch mit Lichteffekten inszenierte skulpturale und malerische Arrangements römischer Prägung. Überdies wird die ebenso römisch beeinflusste und als Skulpturenbühne benutzte Kirchenfassade durch die prachtvolle Stuckfassade von Egid Quirin Asams Wohnhaus konterkariert.
artist: Egid Quirin Asam (1692-1750), bürgerlicher Bildhauer und Stuckateur

Architektur, Stuck und Skulptur: Egid Quirin Asam (1692-1750)  
Architektur und Deckenfresken: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686-1739)
history: Ab 1729 erwarb Egid Quirin Asam im Herzen der Münchner Altstadt mehrere benachbarte Grundstücke, um darauf sein privates Wohnhaus einschließlich Werkstatt zu errichten sowie ein Priesterhaus und mittig dazwischen eine private Kirche, die eine Familiengruft und ein Privatoratorium beinhalten sollte. Die zeitgleich 1729 erfolgte Heiligsprechung des Johann Nepomuk und dessen anschließende Erhebung zum Schutzpatron Bayerns veranlaßte das Patrozinium, weshalb am 16. Mai 1733, am Tag des Heiligen, die Grundsteinlegung erfolgte. Der romerfahrene Maler Cosmas Damian Asam half seinem Bruder bei Planung und Ausmalung der Kirche, die zwar am 1. Mai 1746 geweiht werden konnte, deren Ausstattung aber selbst 1750 beim Tod des Stifters noch unvollendet war.

en.name: Subsidiary Church of St. John Nepomuk and House of the Sculptor Egid Quirin Asam
description: The relatively narrow interior of the church, divided into the vestibule, the nave and the sanctuary, is enclosed by the walls of the houses on each side. For that reason, it only receives light through the façade, at the chancel beside the courtyard and at the base of the vaulted ceiling. The Asam brothers understood how to skilfully use the light to stage their sculptural and pictorial compositions. The nave is arranged like that of a two-storey court church with an overhanging, elegantly curved balcony and balustrade encircling it. It serves as a viewing platform for the “sacred theatre” playing out in the chancel and on the vaulted ceiling.

Named after its builders, the Asam Brothers, this little church in the heart of Munich’s historic district is rightly considered a marvel of Bavarian Baroque architecture. Its splendid grandeur, comparable to that of a court church, provides the right atmosphere for theatrically displaying its Roman-inspired sculptural and pictorial compositions through the effect of light. Furthermore, the equally Roman-inspired exterior of the church which features a sculptural arrangement, pales in comparison to the marvellous stucco façade of Egid Quirin Asam’s own house.
artist: Architecture, stucco and sculptures: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); architecture and ceiling frescoes: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)
history:
In 1729, Egid Quirin Asam acquired several neighbouring properties in the heart of Munich’s historic district upon which to build his private residence. This included a studio, a rectory and a private church between them. The church contains a family crypt and a private oratory.  
At the same time in 1729, the canonisation of St. John of Nepomuk and his subsequent elevation as the patron saint of Bavaria inspired Egid Quirin Asam to accept this saint for the patronage of his church. It is for this reason that the foundation stone was laid on 16 May 1733, St. John’s feast day.  
Cosmas Damian Asam, a painter educated in Rome, assisted his brother in the designing and painting of the church, which was consecrated on 1 May 1746. However, the furnishing of the church remained incomplete at the time of Egid Quirin Asam’s death in 1750.

en.name: Sedan chair
description: The sedan chair is a typical shape, with an S-curve back, a door at the front and a graceful roof. The slender gilt structural framework, which is curved and mobile, has moderate carved volutes and leaf and shell motifs. The door and sides are equipped with glazed apertures, which open by lowering. The remaining surfaces are light green with the edges painted with a dignified garland of multicoloured flowers. Painted on the upper panel of the chair-back is the Dubrovnik-based patrician Zamagna family’s coat of arms. The graceful roof, covered with black leather, secures with a decorative edging of brass. There are two fitments for the shafts on the sides. The interior has one seat located at the rear. Like the cushion, the seat upholstery is red silk damask. The curtains are white silk damask enhanced with haberdashery trimmings.

The sedan chair is a typical shape, with a graceful roof covered with black leather, a glazed door and sides, slender, curving mobile framework decorated with gilt carving, and light-green painted panels edged with a dignified garland of multicoloured flowers. On the upper panel of the chair-back is the painted coat of arms of the patrician Zamagna family. Like the cushion, the seat upholstery is red silk damask. The curtains are white silk damask enhanced with haberdashery trimmings.
