en.name: Headdress ornament.
description:
Made up of a nickel silver-plate disc with metal chains, Ottoman coins, charms and beads, this headdress ornament would have been worn as part of a bridal outfit, fixed to the top of a bonnet made of embroidered fabric, and shaped to fit the head. One of the charms is a French medal of Saint Joseph, and the other is the Hand of Fatima. The coins, except for one Spanish coin that shows the name of King Phillip V of Spain, are Ottoman, dated between AH 1180 and 1260 (AD 1766–1844). The coins in such headdresses had two functions, one simply about decoration, and the other as an indicator of the bride's wealth; her social status and the value of her dowry. The presence of the Christian saint's medal centred in the front section of the disk draws attention to the probability that this headdress may have belonged to a Christian bride! In Palestine, which is full of intermingling Christian and Muslim villages, this headdress is a good example of the cultural diversity of the Ottoman Middle East. Other European coins popular in Middle Eastern jewellery include coins depicting the Austrian Empress Maria Theresa.  
  
The brides of Ramallah (a predominantly Christian town) would have worn headdresses such as this one for their wedding celebrations. A woman would be free to either add more coins or to take some off for personal use, for home improvements for example. Many of these headdresses were passed down through generations, and when gold coins came into fashion, many of the silver coins were replaced.

A Christian saint’s medal attached to the front of this ornament reveals that it belonged to an Arab Christian bride from the Ottoman period in Palestine. It would have been worn as part of the bridal outfit of a lady from Ramallah. The silver coins are Ottoman from between AH 1180 and 1260 (AD 1766–1844).
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
keywords: Women; coinage; coin; numismatics; Jewellery; costume; traditional costume; marriage; daily life
materials: Nickel silver-plate with metal chains and coins, and glass and stone beads.
tags: Nickel silver-plate with metal chains and coins, and glass and stone beads.

es.name: Adorno de tocado.
description:
Este adorno de tocado, hecho con una lámina de plata niquelada, cadenas de metal, monedas otomanas, amuletos y abalorios, se luciría como parte de un traje de novia, sujeto a la parte superior de una capota en bordado y ajustada a la cabeza. Uno de los amuletos es una medalla francesa de san José y el otro, la mano de Fátima. Las monedas son otomanas, de los años 1180-1260 / 1766-1844, excepto una española con una inscripción en que se menciona al rey Felipe V. Las monedas de estos tocados tenían dos funciones: decorar y mostrar la riqueza de la novia, su estatus social y el valor de su dote. Este tocado, por la medalla del santo cristiano que cuelga en la parte frontal del disco, debió de pertenecer a una novia cristiana y es un buen ejemplo de la diversidad cultural del Oriente Próximo otomano, en este caso Palestina, donde se entremezclaban localidades cristianas y musulmanas. Otras monedas europeas populares en la joyería de Oriente Próximo son las que representaban a la emperatriz austriaca María Teresa.  
Las novias de Ramala (ciudad de predominio cristiano) llevarían un tocado como este el día de su boda. Las mujeres podían añadir más monedas o coger alguna para sus gastos, como por ejemplo arreglos en la casa. Muchos de estos tocados pasaron de generación en generación, y las monedas de plata fueron sustituidas por otras de oro cuando estas se pusieron de moda.

La imagen de un santo cristiano en la parte frontal de este tocado indica que perteneció a una novia árabe cristiana de la Palestina del periodo otomano. Formaría parte del traje de novia de una mujer de Ramala. Las monedas de plata son otomanas, datadas entre 1180 y 1260 / 1766-1844.
holder: Galería de Arte y Museo Kelvingrove, Museos de Glasgow.
dates: Siglo XII de la Hégira / XIX d. C.
keywords: mujeres; monedas; joyería; joyería; indumentaria; numismática
materials: Lámina de plata niquelada, cadenas de metal, monedas, vidrio y abalorios de piedra.
tags: Lámina de plata niquelada, cadenas de metal, monedas, vidrio y abalorios de piedra.

fr.name: Ornement de coiffure.
description:
Composé d'un disque de maillechort, de chaînettes métalliques, de pièces de monnaie ottomanes, de porte-bonheur et de grains divers, cet ornement de coiffure de mariage se fixait au sommet d'un bonnet en tissu brodé adapté à la forme de la tête. L'un des porte-bonheur est une médaille de saint Joseph d'origine française, l'autre une “main de Fatma.” Les pièces de monnaie – sauf une au nom du roi d'Espagne Philippe V – sont ottomanes et datées d'entre 1180 et 1260 H / 1766-1844 J.-C. Elles remplissaient deux fonctions, l'une purement décorative, l'autre d'indication de la richesse de la mariée, de son statut social et de l'importance de sa dot. La présence d'une médaille chrétienne au centre du disque fait penser que cet ornement a pu être destiné à une mariée chrétienne. Cet ornement est un bon exemple de la diversité culturelle du Moyen-Orient ottoman, en particulier en Palestine, où les villages pouvaient être chrétiens ou musulmans. Parmi les autres pièces de monnaie européennes populaires dans les bijoux moyen-orientaux figurent celles à l'effigie de l'impératrice Marie-Thérèse d'Autriche.  
Les jeunes mariées de Ramallah (ville à dominante chrétienne) portaient ce type d'ornement de coiffure pour leurs noces. La femme était libre de l'enrichir de pièces ou, au contraire, d'en prélever pour son usage personnel, par exemple pour l'aménagement de sa maison. Un grand nombre de ces coiffes passaient de génération en génération et lorsque les pièces d'or devinrent à la mode, elles remplacèrent souvent celles d'argent.

La médaille d’un saint chrétien accrochée sur le devant de cet ornement révèle qu’il appartenait à une jeune mariée arabe chrétienne de la période ottomane en Palestine. Il s’agit sans doute d’un accessoire de parure de mariée portée par une femme de Ramallah. Les pièces d’argent sont ottomanes et datées d’entre 1180 et 1260 H (1766-1844 J.-C.).

en.name: *The Suffragette 1d Weekly*
short_description:
‘The Suffragette’ was the weekly newspaper of the Woman's Social and Political Union (WSPU), the leading militant organisation campaigning for women’s suffrage in the United Kingdom. This wood block printed advertisement features the patron saint of the Suffragettes, Joan of Arc carrying the banner of the WSPU.  
  
Hilda Dallas was a member of the Suffrage Atelier, which was formed in 1909 to encourage artists to promote 'the enfranchisement of women, by means of pictorial publication'. Its activities also included training non-professional artists in printing techniques. The low cost, low tech method of wood block printing, as used in this poster, was cheap, quick and easy to learn.
artist: Artist: Hilda Dallas; issuer: W.S.P.U. (Women's Social and Political Union)
keywords: Print; advertising; politics; propaganda; poster; women; suffragette; printing

ar.name: مبخرة
description: المبخرة مكونة من ثلاثة أجسام لسنوريات ، ربما أسود وهي مصنوعة بطراز شائع في العصر السلجوقي: الرؤوس مدورة والآذان مثلثية ومدببة والفم نصف مفتوح والعينين مثقوبتين. والأجسام الثلاثة متصلة بعنصر ذو تجويف في المركز. و هناك ثقوب مرئية خلف السنويات وبدقة على الرؤوس الثلاثة ومجمعة في الجزء السفلي للعنق. وتفاصيل العمل المخرم على الجزء السفلي للقطعة لا تلتزم بطراز نموذجي خاص مثلا باستخدام النباتات أو الأشكال الهندسية كما في عناصر معاصرة أخرى ولكنها مرتبة ضمن أطر مربعة ومستطيلة الشكل. والثقوب الدقيقة والمجموعة معا كانت مهمتها أساسية في القطعة لخروج الدخان. والمباخر بشكل القطة هي  جزء من الأنواع المميزة لإنتاج المعادن الإيرانية في العصر السلجوقي. ولكن في أغلب الأحيان تمثل القطعة حيوانا واحدا كاملا. وإن تشكيل ثلاثة أجسام سنورية في القطعة هنا ليس فريدا كليا حيث أن أمثلة أخرى موثقة تتميز بتجويف في مركز العنصر الذي يربط الأجسام، والذي يحتوي البخار البخور أو المادة التي ستحرق(أنظر متحف اللوفر، MAO 357).  لكن في بعض الأحيان، في المنطقة الوسطى، يوجد عناصر مثقبة دائرية التي تضاف ويوضع فوقها شكل طائر. إن الأسود، حيوانات الوشق والفهود هي أيضا أشكال كثيرة الاستخدام في الفن الإسلامي حيث أنها مميزة للأيقونية الملكية أو البيئات التي تمثل البلاط حيث أن ترمز للقوة والشجاعة والسلطة. وإن جودة الصنعة للقطعة والقيمة العالية للبخور كسلعة تجرية خلال العصور الوسطى كان يعني أن القطعة تعود لعائلة ثرية.

en.name: Incense burner
description: The incense burner is composed of three feline bodies, probably lions, made in a style common in the Seljuk age: the heads are roundish, the ears are triangular and pointed, the mouth is semi-open and the eyes are pierced. The three bodies are connected by an element with a cavity in the centre.  Holes are visible in the back of the felines, precisely on the three heads and clustered at the lower part of the neck. The openwork detail on the lower part of the object does not adhere to a particular patterned style, for example geometric or vegetable as in other contemporary items, but is arranged within square and rectangular frames. The precise and grouped holes were functional to the object to let out smoke. Cat-shaped incense burners are part of a typology characteristic of Iranian metal production at the time of the Seljuk dynasty. Most of the time, however, the object depicts one single animal. The articulation of three feline bodies in the object here is not entirely unique, as other documented examples feature a cavity at the centre of the element connecting the bodies, which acommodates incense or essences to be burned (see Musée du Louvre, MAO 357). Sometimes, however, in this central area, perforated circular elements are inserted and topped by a bird figure (see The Israel Museum, 64.9.3692). Lions, lynxes and cheetahs are also frequent motifs in Islamic art, as they are characteristic of royalty iconography or court environments as they symbolise strength, courage and power. The craftsmanship quality of the piece and the high value of incense as a commercial good during the Middle Ages indicate that it was intended for a wealthy family.
holder: Museum of Civilisations/ Museum of Oriental Art
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art (EIAC)

it.name: Brucia incenso
description: Il brucia incensi è composto da tre corpi felini, probabilmente leoni, resi secondo formule di stilizzazione particolarmente diffuse in età selgiuchide: le teste sono tondeggianti, le orecchie triangolari e a punta, la bocca semiaperta e gli occhi forati. I tre corpi sono raccordati tra loro tramite un elemento che presenta una cavità al centro.  Forature sono visibili nella parte posteriori dei felini, precisamente sulle tre teste e presso la zona inferiore del collo. La lavorazione a traforo, eseguita solo nella parte bassa dell’oggetto, non compone ornamenti particolari, ad esempio geometrici o vegetali come in altri esempi coevi, ma si dispone entro cornici quadrate e rettangolari. In tutti i casi, questi buchi erano funzionali alla fuoriuscita del fumo. Brucia incensi a forma di felino rientrano in una tipologia caratteristica della produzione dei metalli dell’Iran all’epoca della dinastia selgiuchide. Il più delle volte però l’oggetto rappresenta un solo animale. L’articolazione a tre corpi felini, come nel caso dell’oggetto in questione, è documentata anche da altri esempi in cui la cavità al centro dell’elemento di raccordo tra i corpi è destinata ad accogliere l’incenso o le essenze da bruciare (vedi Musée du Louvre, MAO 357). Talvolta invece in questa zona centrale si innestano elementi circolari traforati sormontati da una figura di volatile (vedi The Israel Museum, 64.9.3692). Leoni, linci e ghepardi, inoltre, sono motivi frequenti nell'arte islamica, in quanto caratteristici dell'iconografia della regalità o degli ambienti di corte, poiché simboleggiano la forza, il coraggio e il potere reale. La qualità della manifattura del pezzo, considerata in relazione al grande valore dell'incenso come oggetto commerciale nel medioevo, sta a indicare che esso fosse destinato ad una famiglia facoltosa.
holder: Museo delle Civiltà/Museo d’arte orientale „Giuseppe Tucci“
materials: Bronzo, decorazione a intaglio e a traforo

ar.name: تجليد كتاب
description: تجليد الكتاب الجلدي هذا مزين برسم باللكر من الذهب والفضة وهو مصنوع في القرن السادس عشر من قبل ورشة في البلاط الفارسي ويظهر التجليد الأهمية الكبيرة لفن تجليد الكتب في الثقافات الإسلامية. والرسم باللكر على الجلد يصور مشهدا فردوسيا :حيث يوجد طائر يطير بين الغيوم في السماء ويجلس على شجرة والشجيرات المحيطة. ويصارع فهد حيوانا آخر في اليسار ويقاتل نمر غزالا إلى اليمين ويوجد تنينين يتبارزان تحت الشجرة .إن الحيوانات الأسطورية والخيالية مثل ذات الرأس البشري وجسم حيوان ووحيدات القرن الأسطورية والتنانين مع الغيوم وطيور الكركي في السماء تبين التأثير الصيني على هذا العمل الفني.وتقنية الرسم باللكر أيضا أصلها من الصين ولكن تجليد الكتب باستخدام اللكر هو اختراع فارسي من أواخر القرن الخامس عشر في إيران بينما عندما اندمج تذهيب الكتب وتجليدها يتحول الغلاف الواقي إلى عمل مصور فني. والحيوانات المتصارعة هي صور من مراحل قبل الإسلام والتي تشير للجنة . إن دقة وحيوية الرسم تجعل من الغلاف مثالا بارزا لرسوم تجليد الكتب الفارسية.
dates: القرن الحادي عشر الهجري / القرن السادس عشر الميلادي

en.name: Book binding
description:
This leather book binding is decorated with gold and silver lacquer painting. Made in a 16th-century Persian court workshop, the binding demonstrates the immense importance of book art in Islamic cultures. The lacquer paintings on leather depict a paradisal landscape: bird fly amongst the clouds in the sky and sit in the tree and surrounding bushes. A cheetah fights another animal to the left, a tiger battles a deer on the right, and two dragons duel beneath the tree.  
Mythic and fantastical animals such as the phoenix, qilin, and dragons, along with the clouds and cranes in the sky, reveal the Chinese influence on this artwork. The lacquer painting technique also originated in China. Lacquer book binding, however, is a Persian invention from late 15th-century Iran where illumination and book bindery merge, turning the protective cover into a work of pictorial art. The fighting animals are a pre-Islamic motif, which can indicate Paradise. The delicacy and vividness of the painting make this cover an outstanding example of Persian book binding paintings.
keywords: Bookbinding; Chinese influence

en.name: Annunciation to Mary, so-called "Angelic Salutation"
description: In 1764, the graceful wooden sculpture and its counterpart, the pietà, were created as processional statues for the Rosary Brotherhood that had been installed in the abbey church. On a small console, a realistically coloured, life-sized group of sculptures rests with an unobtrusive, yet room-filling presence. The depiction of Mary's humble posture, as Archangel Gabriel is dancingly gliding in, achieves a supreme compositional density.

en.name: Reliquary Chest of St. João de Brito
description:
The Portuguese established trading posts along the coasts of India and China where merchants could trade and store their merchandise, extending their authority into the hinterland. While the traditional political structures of local chieftains remained, the elite profited by reselling European wares. In addition to trade, the Portuguese sought to spread Christianity among the local Asian populations with Franciscan, Dominican and later Jesuit missionaries preaching to the indigenous peoples. The Christian missionaries learned the native languages, familiarised themselves with the indigenous cultures and even their religions; in this effort, the Jesuits were extremely dedicated. St. João de Brito was sent as a member of the Jesuit Order to the mission of Maduré, in India, in 1673. His aim was to convert the higher castes, in order to better establish Christianity in the region. He became a *pandaraswami*, an Indian ascetic. One of his converts, Prince Tadaya Theva upon becoming Christian, was rejected by one of his wives. She complained to her uncle, the Raja of Marava, who had the Jesuit executed in Orbyur, India, in 1690.  
This chest, with a pyramidal lid engraved in low-relief, features scenes of St. João de Brito's life and martyrdom. The bas-relief on the top features the saint in Indian dress, with sandals and a staff. Several winged cherubs in chiselled silver flank the lid. The body of the chest presents two sculpted winged angels on each side in true Baroque expression. Four elaborate feet in gilded silver hold the main body. Commissioned by King Pedro II of Portugal as a royal homage to the Jesuit saint, the Portuguese coat of arms is seen in the centre testifying to the royal provenance.  
The presence of the *Agnus Dei* on the top may have been a later addition by the Jesuits, who used it on special occasions as a Eucharistic tabernacle for the veneration of the Blessed Sacrament.

Commissioned by King D. Pedro II, this Reliquary Chest is engraved in low-relief with scenes of St. João de Brito’s life and martyrdom. The bas-relief on the top features the saint in Indian dress, with sandals and a staff.

Santa Casa de Misericórdia, Lisbon / Museum of São Roque

pt.name: *Arca Relicário de São João de Brito*.
description:
Os Portugueses estabeleceram entrepostos comerciais ao longo das costas da Índia e da China, onde os mercadores negociavam e armazenavam os seus produtos, estendendo a sua actividade pelo interior dos territórios. Enquanto as tradicionais estruturas políticas dos chefes locais se mantinham conservadoras, a classe mercantil aproveitava com a venda de objectos no mercado europeu. Além do comércio, os portugueses procuravam espalhar o Cristianismo entre as populações da Ásia, através dos missionários franciscanos, dominicanos e, mais tarde, com os jesuítas. Os missionários cristãos aprendiam as línguas nativas, familiarizavam-se com as culturas locais e até com as suas religiões. Neste aspecto, os jesuítas eram extremamente dedicados. São João de Brito foi enviado pela Companhia de Jesus para a missão do Maduré, na Índia, em 1673. O seu objectivo era converter as castas superiores, para facilitar o desenvolvimento do Cristianismo naquela região indiana. Para isso, trajava-se de *pandaraswami,* um asceta indiano. Um dos seus convertidos, o príncipe Tadaya Theva, foi denunciado pela mulher junto do tio desta, o Rajá de Marava, que mandou executar o jesuíta em Orbyur, na Índia, em 1690.  
Esta arca, com uma tampa ligeiramente piramidal, apresenta baixos-relevos em prata, com cenas da vida e do martírio do santo missionário. O baixo-relevo, no topo, apresenta o santo vestido com o seu traje indiano tradicional, com sandálias e cajado. Vários querubins alados, em prata cinzelada, ladeiam a arca. O corpo da peça apresenta, de cada lado, dois anjos de asas abertas, de grande expressão barroca. Quatro pés ricamente elaborados, em prata dourada, sustentam a peça. Foi esta arca encomendada pelo rei D. Pedro II para homenagear a figura de S. João de Brito. O brasão de armas real, ao centro, testemunha a proveniência da peça. A presença de um “Agnus Dei”, no topo, deve-se, provavelmente, a um acrescento posterior feito pelos jesuítas, que cedo utilizavam esta arca como sacrário eucarístico, em ocasiões solenes.

Encomendada pelo rei D. Pedro II, esta Arca Relicário apresenta baixos relevo em prata cinzelada com cenas da vida e do martírio de S. João de Brito. O baixo-relevo, no topo da arca, apresenta o santo com o seu traje indiano, com sandálias e bastão.

en.name: The Kevorkian Hyderabad Carpet
description:
This carpet is known as the “Kervorkian Hyderabad Carpet” due to the fact that it was owned by Kervorkian, who was a famous Islamic art dealer and collector. This wool and cotton pile-woven carpet is nearly sixteen metres long and might have been created for the palaces of the Deccani sultans who ruled in Hyderabad during the 17th century.  
This carpet, which symbolizes the tradition of paradisical iconography in Islamic art, features a garden composition that includes geometric lozenges with a variety of vegetal motifs arranged in a mirrored composition. At the centre, a polylobed shape represents an abstracted fish pond decorated with multi-coloured fish. The rug presents a reach palette of colours (yellow, brown, blue and green) with a majority of vivid red, characteristic of that production.  
The border, which recalls manuscripts illuminations of the same period, is also highly decorated with repeated polychromic arabesque cartouches and foliated motifs.  
Carpet production in India during the Mughal period and the Deccan sultanate, especially during the 17th century, demonstrate the transfer of motifs and patterns from the cultural and commercial exchange with Iran, the Middle-East and Europe.
keywords: Deccan sultanates; Floral motifs; Hyderabad

en.name: TAORMINA
description:
The seat of Siculians or Sikels, of whom there remains in witness a necropolis of the 8th century BC, the city was founded and inhabited in the 4th century BC by a group of Greek refugees  
from nearby Naxos. At the time of the Romans it was enriched by prestigious monumental buildings, of which some conspicuous vestiges remain.  
In the 7th century the Byzantines  
added further fortifications to the Hellenistic walls (Castles of Monte Tauro and Castelmola), and established the capital of the *thema* in the city when Syracuse fell into the hands of the  
Muslims (878). This permitted them, thanks to the inaccessibility of the site and to its powerful defensive structure, a strenuous resistance to the Arab Conquest. In fact, the Reconquest by  
the Christians in 909 followed the first capitulation of 902 under the blows of Amir Ibrahim Ibn Ahmad and in 962, after an assault lasting seven months, the final occupation by the Muslims.  
The survivors were deported as slaves to Yemen and acquired by the Fatimid Caliph of Bagdad, al-Mansur. The city changed its name to *al-Muâizziya* to celebrate the Fatimid Caliph al-  
Muâizz and the conquerors started their reconstruction in the south where the Cusene and Porta Saraceni Quarters have been identified. The construction of a tower in the area of the Roman  
forum is also attributed to the Arab period (the pre-existence of Palazzo Corvaja). This presided over the Giarafi (âcanalâ) Quarters, where the hydraulic conduits of the imperial age converged,  
which the Muslims had wisely enriched, with irrigation outlets in the surrounding land to encourage cultivation of the fields.  
The Normans conquered it in 1079 after an ingenious assault,  
carried out by the means of stockades, ephemeral *donjons* and innovative war machines, which completely isolated the sharp relief on which the settlement stood. Further, the city  
having been taken, the built-up area was restricted to the original town, justifying this contraction by the improvement of the defensive strategy, by way of a smaller walled circle, which was  
easier to control and maintain.  
Having been the seat of Parliament at the beginning of the 15th century during the Vice Regency of the house of Aragon, the State-owned city was sold  
several times by the Spanish court.  
Excluded from all commercial traffic, the city was opened in the 19th century to the tourist industry, thanks to the renown that travellers and  
*vedutisti* had bestowed on it, from the second half of the 18th century.

en.name: *Marija Terezija Oršić (nee Wintershofen)*
description:
By birth from a Styrian baronial family, Maria Theresia Wintershofen was extremely well educated. She married Count Antun Oršić (1670/6–1706), a descendant of an old Croatian baronial family who was a cavalry captain and first served in the War of Spanish Succession and then fought against the Turks in Hungary. Maria Theresia and Count Oršić married when they were both very young, before 1695. Soon after, in 1700, he sued her for adultery and for allegedly casting spells on him. Granted a divorce, he took away their three children.  
An unknown, probably Croatian painter has bestowed on this portrait of Maria Theresia something unusual and mysterious, somehow reflecting her strange destiny. The portrait magnificently illustrates various details of female aristocratic dress at the end of the 17th century, notably the influence of French fashion seen in the cap (*fontange)* which is highly decorative and made of ruffled white lace and red ribbons threaded with silver. The colourful dress she wears was typical of the 17th century, richly endowed with pearls and lace. She also wears a small watch, hung on a red ribbon from her waist, accentuating her high social position.

ar.name: قطعة حلي مطلية بالمينا
description: ابتُكرت قطعة المجوهرات الرائعة تلك في جايبور، بولاية راجاستان، وهي مركز مشهور بإنتاج الأعمال المطلية بالمينا في عهد المغول. وقد اشتهر تصميمها- الذي يتخذ شكل طاووسين يطوقان بأجنحتهما تصميمًا زهريًّا في المنتصف- في العديد من الثقافات في الشرق والغرب. وفي العالم الإسلامي حيث كان من السائد إبراز الأفكار المتعلقة بالجنة والحياة الأبدية.

en.name: Enamelled jewellery ornament
description: This magnificent piece of jewellery was created in Jaipur, Rajasthan, a famous centre for the production of high-quality enamel work in Mughal times. Its design – two peacocks flanking a central floral motif – was popular in many cultures, east and west. In the Islamic world it was understood to evoke notions of paradise and eternal life.
keywords: Jewellery; enamel; floral decoration; bird; symbol

ar.name: لوح من الخشب.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن لوح مستطيل من الخشب يزخرفه شريطان ضيقان يحصران بينهما شريطاً عريضاً. يزخرف الشريطين الضيقين كتابة بالخط الكوفي تحتوي على البسملة وآية الكرسي (الآية رقم 255 من سورة البقرة) وعبارة "حسبي الله." ويزخرف الشريط الأوسط العريض رسومات هندسية تقسمه إلى سبعة أقسام مربعة، ويزخرف كل مربع رسومات نباتية وعناصر مجنحة وأشكال بيضاوية وأوراق نباتية ثلاثية الفصوص. ويزخرف كل من المربع الثالث والخامس عقد مفصص يحوي زخارف نباتية بداخله وفي المثلثين المحصورين بين منحناه الخارجي وزاويتي المربع. ويتضح في أساليب زخرفة وحفر هذه القطعة سيطرة الطابع الهليني بما في ذلك تجسيم العناصر الزخرفية والأشكال البيضاوية والأوراق الثلاثية والفروع النباتية. كما يظهر في هذه القطعة التأثير الساساني من خلال ما تحويه من عناصر مجنحة وعقود مفصصة.  
  
وكانت الألواح الخشبية تستخدم في تزيين المساجد والمنازل، كما استخدمت كأجزاء من الدكك والمقاعد التي اشتهرت بصناعتها مصر وخاصة الفسطاط في العصور الإسلامية المبكرة. وازدهرت صناعة هذه الألواح وتطورت في العصرين الفاطمي والمملوكي، وقد عثر على كثير من الألواح في الفسطاط حيث كانت تستخدم لحماية جدارن القبور الصغيرة من تسرب الأتربة منها إلى الموتى.

قام الفن الإسلامي عند نشأته على أكتاف الفن الهيلنستي، والفن الساساني، ثم بدأ بعد ذلك يفرض شخصيته الإسلامية، حتى أصبح للفن الإسلامي أساليبه الخاصة في هذا الميدان. وتمثِّل هذه القطعة امتزاج الفنون الثلاثة فيها.
keywords: حفر بارز؛ خشب؛ خط؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ لوح.

en.name: Wooden panel.
description: A rectangular wooden panel decorated with two narrow borders flanking a broad central band. The two narrow borders are ornamented with an epigraphic inscription in *kufic* script, which consists of the *bismillah (In the Name of God)* and the 'Throne' verse (2: 255) as well as the expression '*Hasbi Allah*' ('Allah is sufficient for me'). The broad central band is ornamented with geometric motifs, which divide it into seven square-shaped sections. All sections are decorated with vegetal decorations, winged motifs, oval forms and tri-lobed leaf designs. The third and fifth squares hold a lobed arch, within which is vegetal decoration and, flanking the triangular areas between the outer curvature of the arch and the corners of the square-shaped section, are further vegetal motifs. Both the decorative style and the carving of this piece portray a Hellenic stamp, seen in the relief carving of decorative motifs, the oval shapes, the tri-lobed leaves and the vegetal stems. The panel also displays Sassanid influences seen in the winged motifs and lobed arches.
Islamic art came into being on the shoulders of Hellenistic and Sassanid arts and then developed its own Islamic character. This piece demonstrates the blending of the three artistic styles.
keywords: high relief; wood; inscription; vegetal decoration; panel

es.name: Tablero.
description:
Tablero rectangular decorado con dos bordes estrechos que enmarcan una ancha banda central. En los bordes se lee una inscripción en letra cúfica compuesta por la *basmala* ("En el nombre de Dios") y la aleya 255 o "del Trono" de la sura 2, así como la expresión *hasbi Allah*, 'Allah me colma'. La franja central está decorada con motivos geométricos que la dividen en siete partes, todas ellas con decoración vegetal, motivos alados, formas ovales y hojas trilobuladas. El tercer y quinto cuadrados presentan sendos arcos lobulados cuyo vano y albanegas están cubiertos de decoración vegetal.  
Tanto los motivos decorativos (óvalos, hojas trilobuladas y tallos) como la talla en relieve tienen una impronta helenística, aunque es patente también la influencia sasánida en los motivos alados y los arcos lobulados.

El arte islámico tomó como punto de partida el arte helenístico y el sasánida para después desarrollar sus propias características. Esta pieza es un ejemplo de la mezcla de los tres estilos artísticos.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico
dates: Siglo III de la Hégira / IX d. C.
keywords: Incrustación; inscripción decorativa; motivos vegetales; perfume; perfumero; cobre.

fr.name: Panneau de bois.
description: Panneau de bois rectangulaire composé d'un large bandeau encadré de deux minces bordures présentant l'inscription en style coufique d'une *bismillah* (“Au nom de Dieu”), le verset “du Trône” (sourate “de la Vache”, verset 255) et l'expression “Hasbi Allah”, “Allah me comble”. Le bandeau central est orné de motifs géométriques qui le divisent en sept parties carrées. Chacune est décorée de motifs végétaux, d'ailes, d'ovales et de feuilles trilobées. Les troisième et cinquième carrés contiennent un arc brisé sur fond de décor végétal. Le style décoratif et la sculpture révèlent une influence hellénistique, en particulier dans les motifs, les ovales, les feuilles trilobées et les tiges végétales. Le panneau présente également quelques influences sassanides dans les motifs en aile et les arcs brisés.

L'art islamique s'imposa en s'appuyant sur les arts hellénistiques et sassanides et développa par la suite son caractère islamique spécifique. Ce panneau de bois montre le mélange des trois styles artistiques.
dates: IIIe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe siècle J.-C.).

en.name: *Friedrich Wilhelm IV, King of Prussia, in his study at the imperial palace, Berlin*
Textiles
description: These textiles were part of the famous Alhambra wall hangings that decorated different Alhambra rooms. Each is from a different Nasrid king: Yusuf I (textile 1607), Muhammad III (textile 1606) and Muhammad V (textile 1719).
keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
materials: Silk and metallic threads; lampas weave

ar.name: دار الحدّاد.
description:
ينفتح القصر عند نهاية درب شكل قديماً ممرّاً خاصّاً. وبعد المرور بثلاثة دهاليز متعرجة نصل إلى الصحن المحاط من جهاته الثلاث بأروقة تحملها أعمدة مصنوعة من حجر الكذّال وتيجان حفصية تزيد القمريات من ارتفاعها.  
أثث الجانب الرابع من الباحة بثلاث مشاك تمتد حتى تبلغ ارتفاع الأروقة المعمّدة. يزين مقعدان من الأحجار قاعدة المشكاتين الجانبيتين، في حين يخترق باب خلفية المشكاة الوسطى، في حين يمتد في الطابق الأرضي رواق على الجهات الأربع. ترتكز الأعمدة، المجمعة في وحدات مكونة من ثلاث أعمدة في الأركان، على قواعد مقطوعة الزوايا. ويوصل بينها وبين الأعمدة درابزين من الخشب المبروم الذي يستخدم كحاجز.  
وعلى خلاف التقسيم المعتاد في القصور، لاينفصل فضاء الخدمة عن سكن السادة، وإنما يتوزع على جهتي قاعة الاحتفالات التي تقع في مواجهة المدخل، حيث تحتل قاعة جهة مقببة تستخدم مكانا للمؤن، ومن الجهة الأخرى تتواجد قاعة تحتوي على بئر وتؤدي إلى باحة صغيرة يطل عليها المطبخ والمراحيض، بالإضافة إلى حمام مجهز بقنوات تنقل الماء الساخن من غرفة المواقد.  
تتواجد أهم صالة في القصر في الجهة الغربية من الطابق الأرضي؛ وتمثل تصميماً غير موجود في مكان آخر، يضم قاعة ذات تقعّر وسطي تجانبها أربع حجيرات جانبية، تحتفظ الحجيرة الشمالية بالموقد الوحيد الذي يحمل تأثيراً تركيّاً في مدينة تونس، يبدأ من عقد بحواش مهدّبة وينتهي متوجاً بسلّة مخروطيّة.  
أما السقوف من الخشب المنقوش والملون والجبس المنقوش بمهارة فتم استلهامهما من الطراز الأندلسي.

يحمل القصر اسم سعيد الحداد، أحد أغنى صناع الشاشية الأندلسية. شيد المبنى في الجنوب الغربي لأسواق تونس في القرن 10 للهجرة (القرن 16 للميلاد)؛ ورمم من قبل المعهد الوطني للتراث.  
أصالة تصميمه، ومقاييس كتله وغنى زخرفه المعماري، المطبوعة بالتأثيرات الأندلسية والتركية، جعلت من القصر أحد أجمل المباني التاريخية لمدينة تونس العتيقة؛ ويحتضن اليوم قسم التنمية المتحفية (المعهد الوطني للتراث).
keywords: حجيرة؛ خشب منحوت؛ جبس منقوش؛ تأثير أندلسي؛ تأثير عثماني؛ عمارة القصور؛ موقد.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Dar al-Haddad.
description:
The entrance to the palace is at the end of a blind alley which was once a private passage. After negotiating three off-set hallways one comes into the courtyard, which has porticoes on three sides. The *kadhal* columns have Hafsid capitals and are raised by imposts.  
The fourth side of the courtyard has three elongated niches of the same height as the porticoes. Two stone benches sit in the lateral niches, while the central niche has a doorway.  
A first-floor gallery runs around the four sides of the courtyard. In each corner, groups of three columns stand on canted plinths. A turned-wood balustrade running between the columns provides safety.  
Contrary to the usual layout in palaces, the service areas are not separate from the main rooms but are situated on either side of the great hall opposite the entrance. On one side is a vaulted room which served as a provisions store. On the other is a room with a well, leading into a small courtyard off which one enters the kitchen, the latrines and a *hammam* with underground pipes carrying hot water from a furnace.  
The largest room in the palace is on the west side of the first floor. Its layout is unique; a hall with a sunken area in the centre flanked by four small bedrooms. The north chamber possesses the only Turkish-influenced fireplace in the Tunis Medina. It consists of an arch with lambrequins beneath a conical chimney. The ceiling of sculpted and painted wood and the finely carved stuccos take their inspiration from the Andalusian tradition.

Named after a wealthy *fez* maker, Saïd al-Haddad from al-Andalus, this palace was built to the southwest of the Tunis *suq*s in the AH 10th / AD 16th century and later restored by the National Heritage Institute. The originality of its design, the scale of the structures and its rich architectural decoration, marked by Andalusian and Turkish influences, make it one of the most beautiful historical buildings in the Tunis Medina. It is now home to the Museum Development Division of the National Heritage Institute.
keywords: Palace architecture; chimneys; bedrooms; sculpted wood
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Dar al-Haddad.
description:
El palacio se encuentra al fondo del callejón sin salida que antaño era un pasadizo privado, cerrado por varias puertas. Después de tres vestíbulos en codo *(driba)*, se llega al patio, rodeado de pórticos en tres de sus lados. Las columnas en *kadal* con capiteles hafsíes están rematadas con impostas.  
El cuarto lado del patio está marcado por tres rehundimientos alargados que llegan a la altura de los pórticos. Dos bancos de piedra rellenan la base de estos nichos, mientras una puerta se abre en el nicho central. En la planta superior, una galería une los cuatro lados. Las columnas, triples en los ángulos, descansan sobre basas achaflanadas. Una barandilla de madera torneada une las columnas y sirve de antepecho.  
A diferencia de la distribución habitual de otros palacios, el espacio de servicio no está separado de las habitaciones de los señores; se distribuye a ambos lados de la sala de protocolo, que se encuentra frente a la entrada. En un lado hay una sala abovedada que se usaba como despensa; en el otro, una sala con pozo comunica con un pequeño patio al que daban la cocina y las letrinas, así como un *hammam* con canalizaciones subterráneas que se abastecía de agua caliente desde una caldera.  
La sala más importante del palacio se encuentra en el lado oeste del primer piso. Presenta una planta desconocida en otros palacios, que incluye una sala con un rehundimiento central flanqueado por cuatro pequeñas salas laterales. En la del lado norte se encuentra la única chimenea otomana conocida en la medina de Túnez. Está coronada por una campana cónica y se abre en un arco polilobulado con lambrequines. Tanto los techos de madera esculpidos y pintados como los estucos delicadamente cincelados son de inspiración andalusí.

El palacio, que debe su nombre a un rico fabricante de *shashiya* andalusí, Sayid al-Haddad, fue edificado al suroeste de los zocos de Túnez en el siglo X / XVI y restaurado por el Instituto Nacional del Patrimonio.  
La originalidad de su planta, la armonía de sus volúmenes y la riqueza de su decoración arquitectónica, marcadas por influencias andalusíes y turcas, lo convierten en uno de los monumentos históricos más bellos de la medina de Túnez. Acoge en la actualidad la División de Desarrollo Museográfico (Instituto Nacional del Patrimonio).
dates: Siglo IX de la Hégira / siglo XV d. C.
keywords: arquitectura palatina; chimenea; sala pequeña; madera esculpida
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Dar el-Haddad.
description:
Le palais ouvre au fond de l'impasse qui était jadis un passage privé. Après trois vestibules en chicane, on aboutit à la cour, entourée de portiques sur trois côtés. Les colonnes en *kadhal* à chapiteaux hafsides sont surhaussées d'impostes.  
  
Le quatrième côté de la cour est meublé de trois niches allongées atteignant la hauteur des portiques. Deux banquettes de pierre garnissent la base des niches latérales, alors qu'une porte perce le fond de la niche centrale. à l'étage, une galerie court sur les quatre côtés. Les colonnes, groupées par trois aux angles, reposent sur des bases à pans coupés. Une balustrade en bois tourné relie entre elles les colonnes et sert de garde-fou.  
  
Contrairement à la répartition habituelle dans les palais, l'espace de service n'est pas séparé de l'habitation des maîtres, mais se répartit de part et d'autre de la salle d'apparat qui fait face à l'entrée. D'un côté, une salle voûtée servait de salle à provisions, de l'autre une salle contenant le puits donne accès à une courette sur laquelle s'ouvraient la cuisine et les latrines, ainsi qu'un hammam avec des canalisations souterraines acheminant l'eau chaude à partir d'une chaufferie.  
  
La plus importante salle du palais se trouve du côté ouest de l'étage. Elle présente un plan inconnu ailleurs, et comprend une salle à défoncement central que flanquent quatre chambrettes latérales. La chambrette nord offre l'unique cheminée d'influence turque dans la médina de Tunis. S'ouvrant dans un arc à lambrequins, elle est coiffée d'une hotte conique. Les plafonds en bois sculpté et peint, les stucs finement ciselés sont d'inspiration andalouse.

Du nom d'un riche fabricant de chéchias andalou, Saïd el-Haddad, le palais, édifié au sud-ouest des souks de Tunis au Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.), a été restauré par l'Institut national du patrimoine.  
L'originalité de son plan, l'échelle des volumes et la richesse du décor architectural, marquées par les influences andalouses et turques, en font l'un des plus beaux bâtiments historiques de la médina de Tunis. Il abrite aujourd'hui la Division du développement muséographique (Institut national du patrimoine).
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Architecture palatiale; cheminée; chambrette; bois sculpté.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

de.name: Fassade
description: Die Fassade, deren Türme, Giebel und Wappen erst um 1900 fertiggestellt bzw. ergänzt worden sind, zeigt den Einfluss des Salzburger Doms wohl am deutlichsten. Das Äußere ist in der typischen strengen Gliederung des süddeutschen Frühbarock gehalten. Türme und Fassadenmitte bilden eine Einheit. Die zwei Portalbögen, die von Doppelpilastern getrennt werden (vgl. München, St. Michael), nehmen außen bereits den Aufbau der Langhauswände vorweg.

en.name: Façade
description: The façade, whose towers, gables and escutcheons were first completed in 1900, i.e. supplemented, most clearly show the influence of the Salzburg Dome. The exterior is maintained in the strict arrangement typical of South German Early Baroque. The towers and the centre of the façade form a unit. The two portal arches, separated by double pilasters (cf. St. Michael’s Church, Munich) already anticipate the configuration of the interior nave walls.

en.name: Lancia D50
description: Two fuel tanks mounted outside the bodywork, separately from the body of the car, are among the special features of this car; these were put in place as designer Vittorio Jano wanted to achieve good aerodynamic profiling. At 620 kg unladen, it was also one of the lightest single-seaters at the time; for comparison, the new Mercedes W 196 weighed 690 kg. It made its racing debut at the 1954 Spanish Grand Prix, with Alberto Ascari at the wheel, fresh from a one-year contract with Lancia. The first victory came with Ascari at the 1955 Turin Grand Prix and then at the Naples Grand Prix in the same year. Further accolades would follow: Juan Manuel Fangio drove the D50 to his championship at the 1956 Formula 1 race. This model can travel at 280km/h thanks to its eight-cylinder V-shaped engine, which provides 260 horsepower at 8,000 revolutions per minute and displaces 2,488 cubic centimetres.
keywords: Historic Car; Engine; F1
materials: Steel, copper, leather, paint; assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting
tags: assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting

ar.name: تمثال فارس.
description:
هذه القطعة تمثل فارساً ملتحياً ذا سحنة آسيوية تركمانية على رأسه خوذة وله شعر طويل مضفور. وقد التف حول قدم الحصان الأمامية اليمنى ثعبان، وارتفع باتجاه الفارس من الجهة اليسرى، ونرى الثعبان يفتح فمه ليعض الفارس، ولكن الفارس يصدّه بترسه ويشهر سيفاً مستقيماً إلى الأعلى جاهزاً للنيل من الثعبان. يوجد عمود مجوف تحت بطن الحصان يقصد منه على الأغلب تثبيت التمثال قائماً. كما زيّن الحصان بزمام أزرق اللون ونافر قليلاً. يلتف شريط الزمام المزخرف حول فمه، ويتدلى تحت عنق الحصان وعبر جسمه وينتهي عند أسفل فخذيه بطرة.  
  
القطعة مطلية بطبقة زجاجية من اللونين السكري والأزرق. إذاً نستطيع مقارنتها بالأسلوب "اللقبي" من بلاد الفرس الذي استعمل أيضاً في الرقة. الصناعات بالأسلوب "اللقبي" عادة تتضمن الزبادي والصحون الفاخمة، وتتمركز هذه الصناعات في مدينة كاشان في إيران على الأغلب. لونت الزخرفة النافرة بالألوان الأزرق والأصفر والأخضر والبنفسجي والزهري، لكي تتميز عن اللون الأبيض أو السكري في الخلفية.

تماثيل فخارية، أطلق عليها اسم "فرسان الرقة"، وهي عبارة عن قطع مميزة من الفخار السوري، المطلي بالكروم، والمصقول، والتي يتَّضح من خلالها تأثُّر الذوق الفني، والصناعات المحلية، بالوضع السياسي والنظام العسكري.
keywords: إعادة توطين؛ باريس؛ حصان؛ حلب؛ خزف؛ الرقة؛ فارس؛ فخار.

en.name: Equestrian figurine.
description:
A figurine of a bearded horseman with Asian Turkoman facial features, long braided hair and a helmet. Around the right front hoof of the horse is a snake that is climbing towards the rider from his left. The snake is shown opening its mouth to bite the rider through his armour, but he repels it with his shield. He carries a straight sword lifted into the air, ready to strike. There is a grooved cylindrical column coming out of the stomach of the horse that probably supported the statue, keeping it upright. The horse wears blue reins that are executed in relief. The reins continue around the horse's mouth and hang in front of its neck, then, like a harness, run across the sides of the horse's body down to the lower part of its hind legs.  
The object is glazed in off-white and blue and, therefore, can be compared to the laqabi-style ware of Persia, also known to have been produced in Raqqa. Laqabi ware is often seen as luxury bowls and dishes with moulded decorations. Production probably centred on the city of Kashan in Persia. Raised areas were often coloured in bright- blue, yellow, green, purple and pink to differentiate them from the white or off-white background.

Known as the 'Horseman of Raqqa', this masterpiece of Syrian polychrome underglaze sculptural ceramics clearly displays the influence of the Central Asian military elite on artistic taste and local production.
keywords: Earthenware; ceramics; horse; polychrome; Raqqa; Aleppo; Paris; Salim ‘Adil ‘Abd al-Haqq; M. E. de Lorey

es.name: Figurita ecuestre.
description:
Figurita de hombre barbado a caballo, de rasgos faciales turcomanos, pelo largo trenzado y casco. Alrededor de la pezuña derecha del caballo se ve una serpiente que está trepando hacia el jinete por su izquierda. La serpiente tiene la boca abierta para morder al jinete, pero él la rechaza con el escudo. Blande en el aire una espada de filo recto, listo para asestar el golpe. Del vientre del caballo sale una columna cilíndrica estriada, probablemente destinada a mantener derecha la estatuilla. Las riendas del caballo son azules y están en relieve; rodean el hocico del caballo y le cuelgan de la parte anterior del cuello; después se prolongan por los costados del animal a modo de arnés y bajan hasta la parte inferior de las patas traseras.  
La estatua presenta un vidriado en colores hueso y azul, por lo que se asocia al estilo *laqabi* persa, que también se producía en al-Raqqa. Entre los objetos de este estilo hay numerosos platos y cuencos de lujo con decoración moldeada. La producción se concentraba, posiblemente, en la ciudad de Kashan (Persia). Las zonas en relieve solían ser de color azul brillante, amarillo, verde, morado y rosa, lo que las diferenciaba del blanco o el hueso del fondo.

Esta obra maestra siria de la cerámica escultórica bajo vidriado, conocida como “jinete de al-Raqqa”, muestra claramente la influencia que tuvo la élite militar de Asia central en el gusto artístico y la producción local.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: Barro cocido; cerámica; caballo; policromía; al-Raqqa; Alepo; París; repatriación; Salim Adil Abd al-Haqq

fr.name: Figurine équestre.
description:
Figurine équestre représentant un cavalier barbu et casqué dont le visage présente des traits turcomans caractéristiques. Sa longue chevelure est tressée. Près du sabot avant droit de sa monture, un serpent monte vers lui. Le reptile ouvre la gueule comme pour mordre l'homme à travers son armure, mais celui-ci le repousse de son bouclier. Il porte une épée droite qu'il tient en l'air, prêt à frapper. La colonne cannelée qui sort du ventre du cheval avait probablement pour fonction de maintenir droite la statuette. Le cheval est harnaché de rênes bleues traitées en relief qui se poursuivent autour de la bouche, entourent le cou puis, comme un harnais, se poursuivent sur les flancs et descendent jusqu'au bas des pattes arrière.  
La sculpture est vernie en blanc cassé et bleu, ce qui évoque donc le style *laqabi* perse, dont on sait qu'il était également pratiqué à Raqqa. Parmi les objets de ce style figuraient nombre de luxueux plats et coupes à décor moulé. Leur production était vraisemblablement centrée autour de la ville de Kashan en Perse. Les parties en relief étaient souvent colorées en bleu, jaune, vert, pourpre et rose, ce qui avait pour effet de les faire ressortir sur le fond blanc cassé.

Connu sous le nom de “Cavalier de Raqqa”, ce chef-d'œuvre de la céramique syrienne polychrome sculpturale à décor sous glaçure montre clairement l'influence de l'élite militaire issue d'Asie centrale sur la production et le goût artistique locaux.
dates: VIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Terre cuite ; céramiques ; chevaux ; polychromie ; Raqqa ; Alep ; Paris ; rapatriement ; Salim ‘Adil ‘Abd al-Haqq ; M. E. de Lorey

cs.name: *Alegorie prosperity Moravy pod dobrou vládou Leopolda I (doktorská teze Karla Josefa Rodena)*
description:
Námětem grafického listu je alegorie země Moravy. Mapa ve formě zeměkoule – tedy moravského světa je obklopena nebeskými mocnostmi, zástupci stavu (duchovenstvo, šlechta, města) a alegorickými figurami. Vlevo poklekající žena se zrcadlem je personifikací *Prudentie* (obezřetnosti – předvídavosti). *Fortitudo* (statečnost – pevnost) reprezentuje ženská figura s masivním sloupem a herákleovskou lví kůží na hlavě spolu s opět ženskou postavou personifikující *Moderatio* (umírněnost – sebeovládání) s přesýpacími hodinami. Symbolicky pozdvižená ruka s váhami nad Moravou patří *Justitii* (spravedlnosti). Důstojnou postavu muže s parukou, opírajícího se jednou rukou o fasces a druhou o sochu Pallas Athény, můžeme interpretovat jako alegorii *Bonum consilium* – dobré rady a zároveň vzdělanosti. Podobně jako v případě nebeských mocností zajišťují představitelé stavu spolu s personifikacemi státně politických ctností rozkvět země pod vládou císaře Leopolda I. (1657–1705), jehož monogram *LI* tvoří střed celého listu. Výsledky dobré vlády naznačují rohy hojnosti s plody země, ale i  
s atributy vzdělanosti nebo kameny se symboly planet, kterým odpovídají stříbro a železo, zajišťující bohatství země.  
V centru kompozice je na křídlech říšského orla nesen obraz zázračné brněnské Panny Marie Svatotomské, jedné z hlavních záštit Moravy, doprovázené dalšími patrony země: věrozvěsty Cyrilem a Metodějem vlevo a sv. Václavem vpravo. Upřesnění funkce nebeské sféry, kde se objevují symboly planet nesené anděly, je vysvětleno textem na nápisové pásce: „*Božská moc řídí nebeské světy*“. Neobvyklou formu znázornění Moravy ve formě zeměkoule objasňuje potom druhá část sentence objevující se jako mluvící páska na rozmezí nebeské a pozemské sféry: „*a císař otcovskou mocí-péčí moravský svět*.”  
Grafický list vznikl jako jedna z tezí, jimiž byla olomoucká univerzita proslulá. Po složení zkoušek bylo povinností absolventa zúčastnit se veřejné disputace, jejíž teze byly vytištěny jako návěstí. Některé z nich byly vyryty dle předloh domácích malířů ve slavných augsburských dílnách. Univerzitní prostředí melo značný vliv na vývoj barokní kultury na Moravě.

Teze je typickým příkladem barokní symboliky. Vedle hlavních patronů země zachycuje personifikace ctností–dobré vlády, jež jsou předpokladem rozkvětu země.

en.name: *Allegory of the Prosperity of Moravia under the Beneficent Reign of Leopold I*
description:
An allegory of Moravia: a map in the shape of the globe, i.e. the Moravian world, is surrounded by celestial powers, representative of the states (clergy, nobility, towns) and allegorical figures. The woman with a mirror kneeling on the left personifies *Prudentia* (deliberation or foresight), while *Fortitudo* (courage or resolution) is represented by a female figure with a massive column and a Heraclean lion-skin on her head, close to another female figure with an hourglass embodying *Moderatio* (temperance or self-discipline). The symbolically raised hand with the scales over Moravia belongs to *Justitia* (Justice). The dignified man with a wig, with one hand on a *fasces* (a bundle of white birch rods) and the other on a statue of Pallas Athene, may be interpreted as an allegory of *bonum consilium* – good advice – as well as education. The celestial powers testify to the prosperity of the land under Emperor Leopold I (1657–1705), whose monogram *LI* is the centre piece of the print. The fruit of his beneficent reign is indicated by cornucopias, as well as by the attributes of education, and stones with planetary symbols corresponding to silver and iron, the wealth of the country.  
At the centre, the imperial eagle supports a picture of the miraculous Virgin Mary of St. Thomas, accompanied by patron saints Cyril and Methodius on the left and St. Wenceslas on the right. The function of the celestial sphere carried by angels is specified by the words: “Divine power rules the celestial worlds” on a band. The peculiar manner of representation, with Moravia as a globe, is elucidated by the second part of the sentence, at the interface of the heavenly and earthly spheres: “and the emperor rules the Moravian world with fatherly, powerful care”. The print originated as part of an Olomouc University thesis. After taking exams, graduates had to participate in public debates, the theses of which were printed as announcements. Some of them were engraved after templates by Moravian painters in the renowned Augsburg workshops.

As well as the principal patron saints of the land, the print presents personifications of good government, considered to be a prerequisite of the country’s prosperity.

en.name: The lateral altars of the Chapterhouse

The two lateral altars were installed during the reigns of King João V (r.1706–1750) and King José I (r.1750–1777). One is dedicated to the Death of Christ the other to Our Lady of Good Death.

description: الزبدية مصنوعة من صلصال أصفر برتقالي محمر ومغطاة من الخارج ما عدا بضعة بقع بدهان فخاري (تبطيني) بلون أبيض غير شفاف وجزئيا يغطي هذا الزجاج الذي يعطي لون الكريم الأبيض. وهناك فقط آثار من طلاء فخاري تحت القاعدة والسطح الداخلي له نفس الخلفية ذات لون الكريم الأبيض والذي يظهر في مقابلها شكل طائر له جسم أخضر ومنقار بني فاتح وعصابة العنق والساقين وأسفل الذيل مزينة ببقع بنية داكنة وعصابات وحدود عليها نقاط بيضاء. يتألف التزيين الإضافي من ثلاث زهرات بطراز خاص بشكل قلائد/ رصائع دائرية بلون بني وبني فاتح مع نقاط بيضاء على الطائر وأيضا صور نبات وحالقات (كلابات نباتية) بلون بني داكن والذي لطخ فوق خلفية في أماكن عديدة .وهناك دائرة غير كاملة حول داخل الزبدية على بعد ثلث المسافة من القعر. والزبدية قد كسرت وتم إصلاحها مع بعض الترميم في مواقع غير مهمة. والتزجيج وبطانة الفخار مفقودة من أكثر الإطار.

en.name: Bowl with Design of Bird and Flowers
description: A bowl made of reddish-buff clay, covered on the exterior, except for a few spots, with matt-white slip and, partially covering this, with glaze giving a creamy color. There are only traces of slip under the foot. The interior has the same cream-colored background, against which appears in profile a bird, having a green body and light brown beak, neck band, legs, and lower tail, decorated with dark brown spots, bands, and borders lightened with white dots. Additional decoration consists of three stylized flowers in the form of circular medallions, in brown and light brown with white dots as on the bird, as well as plant and tendril motifs in dark brown. This dark brown color has smeared over the background in several places. There is an incised circle around the interior of the bowl about one-third of the way up from the bottom. The bowl has been broken and mended, with some restoration in unimportant locations. Glaze and slip are missing from most of the rim.
dates: Hegira Late 2nd to late 5th / AD 10th–11th century

en.name: Jug
description: The red slip - Armenian bole, introduced in workshops in Iznik in around 1560 – was used on this jug with a striking artistic force. The stylized tiger stripes – which together with the three spots comprise the classical chintamani pattern – hover all over the body of the jug like surrealistic lips. This pattern is found in variations on Turkish textiles and tiles.

en.name: Ford Model-T popcorn car
description: This extraordinary truck popularised popcorn, an American movie snack. The Columbia Buddy Company converted one of three Ford Model-Ts into a popcorn vending machine on wheels. Besides fresh buttered popcorn made with the original popcorn equipment, this crimson red vehicle would sell ice-cold sodas and roasted peanuts. Special-purpose vehicles were not unknown, as model-Ts were also transformed into ambulances and fire trucks. The popcorn wagon presented a unique marketing and entertainment opportunity within a charming circus-like aesthetic.

en.name: Palace of the Raïs
description:
The buildings of Bastion 23 are reached by following the Avenue of 1st November, a broad artery with tall buildings that contrast with the low houses of the Casbah. The Bastion is on the right, past a traffic circle with a beautiful sculpture, Horses of the Sun, in its centre. In the extension facing the sea stands a statue of Raïs Hamidou, famous pirate of Algiers, by the Algerian sculptor Rédha Cheikh Bled.  
Bastion 23, also called the Palace of the Raïs, owes its name to the fact that it corresponds to the location of a battery or bastion of the defence system of Algiers, Toppanet Sebaa Tebaren (Battery of Seven Taverns), listed as number 23 after the French reorganisation. Behind this bastion is a set of several houses and three palaces built by Ramdane Pacha and Mustafa Pacha in the 10th / 16th century. The only complex from the Ottoman era not destroyed in this area, it is a testament to the survival of the old city that extended to the sea.  
It is the site of beautiful residential architecture of the Casbah, with large impressive entryways, vast patios with marble colonnades and terraces designed for their vantage points. Carefully restored in the 1990s, the palaces display elegant decor, with ceramics of diverse origins and carved woodwork: elaborately worked balustrades, magnificent ceilings with rosettes or fruits painted in relief, and elaborate shelves in the Algerian style.  
These buildings are characterised by the ingenuity of the hydraulic and heating systems of the *hammam* (baths), by the ventilation system of chimneys and by the kitchen wells.  
The palaces are part of a complex spanning more than 6,000 square metres. Two streets lead to more modest houses, probably previously owned by pirates or fishermen. One of them has a *sabât*, or roofed passageway. Within the walls are masonry benches for rest or conversation. At the corner of the two streets is the battery (bastion) terrace that lent its name to the neighbourhood.  
Currently, apart from the three palaces reserved for tourist visits, the other houses are the seat of administration of the Arts and Culture Centre. One can tour the complex via a narrow path at the foot of the building that runs along the beach below.

fr.name: Le Bastion 23 (palais des Raïs)
description:
On accède à l’ensemble du Bastion 23 en longeant l’avenue du 1er-Novembre, large artère aux hauts immeubles contrastant avec les maisons basses de la Casbah. L’ensemble se trouve sur la droite, après un rond-point au centre duquel a été érigé un bel ensemble sculpté, les Chevaux du Soleil. Dans le prolongement se dresse, face à la mer, la statue du raïs Hamidou, célèbre corsaire d’Alger, réalisée par le sculpteur algérien Rédha Cheikh Bled.  
Le Bastion 23, également appelé palais des Raïs, doit son nom à ce qu’il correspond à l’emplacement d’une batterie ou bastion du système défensif d’Alger, Toppanet Sebaa Tebaren (batterie des sept tavernes), répertoriée au numéro 13, puis 23 après le réaménagement français. En arrière de ce bastion se trouve un ensemble de quelques maisons et de trois palais construits par Ramdane Pacha et Mustapha Pacha au Xe/XVIe siècle. Seul îlot de l’époque ottomane à ne pas avoir été détruit dans cette zone, il témoigne de la continuité de la médina qui se prolongeait jusqu’à la mer.  
On y retrouve l’architecture des belles demeures de la Casbah avec des entrées aux dimensions imposantes, de vastes patios à colonnades de marbre et des terrasses aménagées en belvédères. Ayant été l’objet d’une restauration soignée dans les années 1990, les palais présentent une élégante décoration de céramiques de diverses provenances et de boiseries sculptées : balustrades richement ouvragées des étages, magnifiques plafonds aux motifs peints en relief, rosaces ou fruits et étagères ouvragées de style algérois.  
Ces palais se caractérisent par l’ingéniosité du système hydraulique et de chauffage des hammams, ainsi que par le système d’aération des cheminées et des puits des cuisines.  
Ces palais font partie d’un ensemble s’étendant sur plus de 6 000 mètres carrés. On y trouve deux rues menant à des maisons plus modestes, ayant sans doute appartenu à des corsaires ou à des pêcheurs. L’une d’elles comporte un *sabbat* ou passage couvert. Dans les murs, des banquettes en maçonnerie offrent des lieux de repos ou de conversation. À l’angle des deux rues se trouve la terrasse qui fut l’emplacement de la batterie et qui a donné son nom au quartier.  
Actuellement, en dehors des trois palais réservés aux visites touristiques, les autres maisons sont le siège de l’administration du Centre des arts et de la culture.  
On peut faire le tour de l’ensemble par un étroit chemin, au pied de l’édifice, qui longe la plage en contrebas.

ar.name: سقف (قطعتان).
description:
قطعتان من سقف مسطّح ينتمي للمصنوعات الخشبية التي ترجع لفترة المدجنين، مصنوعٍ من الخشب الكستنائي بطريقة آلفارج *alfarje*. تتكون الزخارف من أشكال هندسية مع عناصر تتقاطع مشكّلة تشبيكات، وهي عبارة عن أشكال تشبه الزلّيج (القاشاني المغربي) الذي كان يُُصنع خلال نفس الفترة. للقطعتين أرضية ملساء مع تعددية في الألوان يتميز من بينها أحمر الزنجفر والتلونات المذهبة.  
  
تم صنع هاتين القطعتين من أجل قاعة من قاعات قصر الأبرشية. وبفضل نوعية العمل، نتعرف فيهما على"شغل التشبيك" الذي نفّذه صانع واحد؛ وهما – القطعتان - تقدمان في كل الأحوال تشابهاً مع السقوف التي أنجزت من أجل الكاتدرائية القديمة (سي فيلها) في كويمبرا خلال الأعمال التي قام بها د. جواو غالفاو. كان هذا الأسقف الذي حكم أسقفية كويمبرا ما بين 1460 و 1481 أول من نال لقب الأسقف - الكونت الذي مُنح في عام 1472 من طرف د. ألفونسو الخامس (ملك ما بين 1438-1481) بعد أن تم توحيد مقاطعة الكونت دارغانيل وأبرشية كويمبرا.

تحفظ هاتين الكسرتين اللتين تنتميان إلى سقف من الخشب مصنوع على شاكلة الفرش، والمحصل عليهما من قصر أبرشية كويمبرا، في متحف المدينة. يتكون الزخرف من أشكال هندسية مع عناصر تتشابك وتشكل تشبيكات، وهي أشكال قريبة من الزليج المصنوع خلال نفس الفترة.
place: قصر الأبرشية (حاليا متحف ماشادو دي كاسترو الوطني) كويمبرا.
keywords: آلفارج؛ تشبيكات هندسية؛ سقف؛ قصر الأبرشية؛ كويمبرا؛ مدجّنون.

en.name: Ceiling (two fragments).
description:
Two fragments of a flat ceiling, a work of Mudéjar carpentry in chestnut wood with *alfarje* work (an Iberian decorative style). The decoration is geometric in nature, with intersecting elements forming a lattice, with similar motifs to those used to decorate *azulejos* (glazed tiles) from the same period. The background of the fragments is smooth, with polychromy, notably vermilion red and shades of gold.  
These fragments were made for one of the rooms of the Episcopal Palace. The quality of the workmanship suggests 'lacework' by the same master or, at least, great similarity to the ceilings made for the Sé Velha cathedral of Coimbra during the campaign of work undertaken by João Galvão. This Bishop, who was in charge of the diocese of Coimbra between 1460 and 1481, was the first to use the title Bispo-Conde or Count Bishop, granted in 1472 by Dom Afonso V (r. 1438–81), for the union of the county of Arganil with the bishopric of Coimbra.

These two wooden fragments of *alfarje* ceilings from the Episcopal Palace of Coimbra are kept in the town’s museum. The decoration is geometric with elements combining to form interlacing patterns, similar to those produced on tiles from the same period.
place: Episcopal Palace (today the Machado de Castro National Museum), Coimbra.
keywords: ceiling; Episcopal Palace; Coimbra; Mudéjar; alfarje, geometric patterns

es.name: Dos fragmentos de techumbre.
description:
Dos fragmentos de techo plano, obra de carpintería mudéjar en madera de roble tallada. La decoración es geométrica, con elementos que se entrecruzan formando lacerías, motivos que se asemejan a los que decoran azulejos producidos en el mismo periodo. Tiene fondo liso, con policromía donde destacan el rojo cinabrio y los tonos dorados.  
Estos fragmentos fueron ejecutados para una de las salas del Palacio Episcopal. La calidad del trabajo revela una "obra de lazo" del mismo maestro o, por lo menos, muy próxima a la de las techumbres realizadas para la Sé Velha de Coimbra durante la campaña emprendida por João Galvão. Este obispo, que regentó la diócesis de Coimbra entre 1460 y 1481, fue el primero en usar el título de obispo-conde, concedido en 1472 por D. Afonso V (r. 1438-1481) al unir el condado de Arganil a la mitra de Coimbra.

De los techos del antiguo Palacio Episcopal de Coimbra se conservan en el museo de la ciudad dos fragmentos en madera tallada. La decoración es geométrica, con elementos que se entrecruzan formando lacerías, motivos que se asemejan a los de azulejos producidos en el mismo periodo.
place: Palacio Episcopal (hoy Museo Nacional Machado de Castro) de Coimbra.
keywords: diseño géométrico

fr.name: Plafond (deux fragments).
description:
Deux fragments de plafond plan, ouvrage de menuiserie mudéjare en bois châtain travaillé en *alfarje.* Le décor est constitué de figures géométriques, avec des éléments qui s'entrecroisent formant des entrelacs, motifs proches des *azulejos* fabriqués à la même époque. Présentent un fond lisse, avec polychromie, dont se détachent le rouge cinabre et les tons dorés.  
Ces fragments ont été réalisés pour une des salles du Palais de l'Évêché. Par la qualité de l'ouvrage, ils désignent des “ouvrages d'entrelacs” d'un seul maître, présentant en tout cas des similarités avec les plafonds exécutés pour l'ancienne cathédrale (Sé Velha) de Coimbra durant les travaux entrepris par D. João Galvão. Cet évêque, qui a gouverné le diocèse de Coimbra de 1460 à 1481, fut le premier à prendre le titre d'évêque-comte, accordé en 1472 par D. Afonso V (r 1438-1481), en raison de l'union du comté d'Arganil avec l'Évêché de Coimbra.

Ces deux fragments de plafond en bois travaillé en *alfarje* provenant du palais de l'Évêché de Coimbra sont conservés au musée de la ville. Le décor est constitué de figures géométriques, avec des éléments qui s'entrecroisent formant des entrelacs, motifs proches des *azulejos* fabriqués à la même époque.
place: Palais de l’Évêché (aujourd’hui Musée national Machado de Castro), Coimbra.
keywords: plafond ; Palais de l’Évêché ; Coimbra ; mudéjar ; alfarje ; motif géométrique

pt.name: Tecto (dois fragmentos).
description:
Dois fragmentos de tecto plano, obra de carpintaria mudéjar em madeira de castanho com trabalho de alfarge. A decoração é de cariz geométrico, com elementos que se entrecruzam formando laçarias, motivos que se assemelham aos produzidos nos azulejos do mesmo período. Apresentam o fundo liso, com policromia, destacando-se o vermelho cinábrio e os tons dourados.  
  
Estes fragmentos foram executados para uma das salas do Paço Episcopal. Pela qualidade do trabalho que apresentam, denunciam “obra de laço” do mesmo mestre, ou, pelo menos, grande proximidade com os tectos executados para a Sé Velha de Coimbra durante a campanha emprendida por D. João Galvão. Este Bispo, que governou a diocese de Coimbra entre 1460 e 1481, foi o primeiro a usar o título de Bispo-Conde, concedido em 1472 por D. Afonso V (r. 1438-1481), pela união do condado de Arganil à Mitra de Coimbra.

Dos tectos do antigo Paço Episcopal de Coimbra conservam-se no museu da cidade dois fragmentos em madeira com trabalhos de alfarge. A decoração é de cariz geométrico, com elementos que se entrecruzam formando laçarias, motivos que se assemelham aos produzidos nos azulejos do mesmo período.
holder: Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro.
place: Paço Episcopal (hoje Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro), Coimbra.
keywords: tecto; Paço Episcopal; Coimbra; mudéjar; alfarge, padrão geométrico

en.name: Saint Georges
description:
This stained glass was commissioned from the artist Yoki by the Association “Semper Fidelis” to commemorate the entry of the canton of Fribourg into the Swiss Confederation in 1481. Although officially presented to the Fribourg cantonal authorities, this piece of glass art was designed for the Musée du Vitrail (now Vitromusée Romont), which opened in 1981 as part of the celebrations for the 500th anniversary of the canton joining the Swiss Confederation. For a long time it was exhibited in the attic of the museum, where a special opening was created to display it.  
  
This glass in concrete depicts St. George in armor and nimbus, riding a white horse, holding a spear in both hands and piercing the mouth of the dragon lying at his feet, which turns its head to look at him.
keywords: banner; shield; horse; dragon; George; religion; cross; soldier; lance

en.name: Chrysler Windsor Deluxe
description:
This black-lacquered car is viewed as iconic in Chrysler history. Produced between 1939 and the 1960s, the Chrysler Windsor fulfilled each and every desire of Americans after the second world war.  
  
As a more luxurious model compared to the New Yorker, this full-sized sedan from 1951 embraced the changing times with a redesign. The cigarette lighter, map lights and safety-padded dashboard would breathe new life into the steadfast car.  
  
With great popularity among political leaders and celebrities, this model belongs to the state cars owned by the third ruler of Qatar, Sheikh Abdullah Bin Jassim Al Thani. While the fashionable fins endured as a lasting feature, the Windsor remains a remarkable car in collections beyond the United States.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Sedan; Four-Door; Royal Collection; Family Heirloom; Customised; Classic Cars

en.name: Pera Palace Hotel
short_description: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
