en.name: Fragment of silk lampas with geometric pattern
description:
Since the 12th century, Granada has been the leading centre of the Pyrenees for the production of high quality silk. This costly golden-thread silk lampas dated to the 14th century could be used as interior decoration in one of the Granada palaces. A very similar fabric is known to be used for interior decoration in the famous Alhambra Palace.  
The geometric pattern includes favourite Muslim motifs: octagonal stars and rosettes, braids, stylized plant elements. Historians suppose the common origin of the textile décor with that of Nasrid architecture and, first of all, with the carved and mosaic ornamental panels of Alhambra.  
Quite rare is the motif of paired heraldic birds sitting in the tree branches. It may be hypothetically considered as an image of Simurg (Senmurv), the holy King of the birds in the folklore of Iranians and Turks. The literate Muslims of Nasrid Spain were well versed in the key narratives of the Near and Middle East culture due to Arabic translations of books, particularly of Abu l-Qasim Ferdowsi's poem Book of Kings ("*Shahnama*").
keywords: Fabrics; Silk; Lampas; Islamic Spain; Granada; Nasrid
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and Amelia del Valle y Serrano, in Oriental garment
names: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquesa de Cerralbo, y Amelia del Valle y Serrano, con atuendo oriental
description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and her daughter Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicious thanks to the typical Turkish costume, the apparently easy pose and the scenography and the absolute harmony with the idea of aesthetic orientalism.
keywords: Portrait; women; souvenir; memorabilia; orientalism

en.name: Holy Trinity Monument
description:
Votive pillars are a town planning-cum-sculptural brief that is typical of Central Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries. They relate broadly speaking to two major historical events of the time: the Turkish threat; defeat and withdrawal, and the plague. The Turkish preoccupation, i.e. victory over the Turks, is symbolised by a depiction of the Immaculate Virgin at the top of a central pillar. Monuments erected to protect from or commemorate the plague depict the Holy Trinity at the centre of the composition and the patron saints of the plague at the base. One of the best-known and most influential examples of the latter is the monument to the Holy Trinity in Graben, Vienna, the planning and construction for which some of Vienna's most prominent sculptors took part.  
The core of the Osijek monument consists of a massive pedestal on which there rests a smooth pillar. The Holy Trinity is at the top. The ground plan of the pedestal is expanded by protuberances of four large volute brackets with pedestals on which stand four statues arranged around the pillar. The saints, traditionally held to be sovereign against the plague, are St. Charles Borromeo and St. Francis Xavier, St. Roch and St. Sebastian, and additionally, a recumbent figure of St. Rozalia. As is often the case with stone monuments in the open-air, the Osijek Column's sculptural saints are suffering from environmental damage. Moreover, partial alteration of the sculptures during restorations of the past makes their original formal and stylistic features difficult to discern. Still, it is clear that a well-trained sculptor who had thoroughly mastered the contemporary Baroque artistic vocabulary was responsible. In 1784, statues of the *Immaculate Virgin*, *St. Catherine*, *St. John Nepomuk* and *St. Joseph* were transferred from Osijek's two city gates and placed around the perimeter of the monument.

Placed at the centre of the main square of the Baroque fortress in Osijek, the Plague Column is Croatia's best-preserved example of a monument designed to ward off or commemorate the end of the plague. Such monuments were a characteristic feature of Central European towns in the 17th and 18th centuries.
history: Marija Ana Petraš, widow of the commander of the fort in Osijek general and vice-marshal Maksimilijan Petraš, initiated the erection of the monument and financed it as was recorded on the occasion by “*Pestis Syrmiensis*”. In 1784, four statues were taken from Osijek's two city gates to furnish the outer perimeter of the monument.
keywords: Osijek, votive monument, plague pillar or column, sculpture
tags: Osijek, votive monument, plague pillar or column, sculpture

en.name: *Truth*
description:
Sitting on rough-surfaced rock the figure of the smiling maiden holds an image of the sun in her right hand. She represents “Truth” according to Cesare Ripa's famous *Iconologia*, an encyclopaedic repertoire illustrating the personifications of abstract concepts, widely used by artists during the Baroque period to represent allegorical figures. A recent study has also shown that the marble figure of the maiden is a faithful sculptural representation of a painting by Correggio, *Allegory of Virtue*, which was in Rome at the time, incomplete, as part of the Pamphilj Collection. According to ideas expressed by the artist in his preparatory drawings, the statue was to be part of an imposing group showing a moral theme, *Truth Unveiled by Time*. It was intended to be overseen by an old man with a scythe, the symbol of Time, intent on lifting the cloth to reveal the radiant beauty of the maiden. The work was conceived during the pontificate of Innocent X Pamphilj (1644–1655). It was a particularly difficult time in the artist's life when he was unjustly accused of causing structural instabilities in Saint Peter's, resulting in the demolition of the bell towers that he had designed. Bernini, who never completed the sculptural group, arranged for the statue to remain at his home as a warning to his descendants. The different ways in which the marble is finished represent an important example of Bernini's extraordinary technical skills. The well researched contrast between the crystalline finish of the figure and the “non finish” of the rocks is also evident in the detail of the foot resting on the globe.  
The typically Baroque practice of using a metaphor of the personal to illustrate a universal warning is particularly noteworthy.

Bernini carved the sculpture for himself at a difficult time in his career (during the pontificate of Innocent X Pamphilj, 1644–1655) when he was accused of causing structural problems at St. Peter’s bell tower. The group, which was never finished, was to include the figure of Time. Bernini left the sculpture as an eternal warning to his heirs, with whom it remained until 1924.
keywords: Personification; Iconologia; allegory; marble; movement

it.name: *La Verità*
description:
La figura della fanciulla sorridente, seduta su una roccia dalla superficie scabra, mostra nella mano destra l'immagine del sole. Essa rappresenta la “Verità” secondo la celebre *Iconografia*  di Cesare Ripa, repertorio di carattere enciclopedico, in cui erano illustrate le personificazioni di concetti astratti, molto usato dagli artisti in età barocca per la rappresentazione di figure allegoriche. Uno studio recente ha inoltre evidenziato come la figura marmorea della fanciulla rappresenti in scultura la ripresa fedele da un dipinto di Correggio, l'*Allegoria della Virtù*, la cui versione incompiuta si trovava anche a quel tempo a Roma nella collezione Pamphilj. Secondo il pensiero espresso dall'artista nei disegni preparatori, la statua doveva costituire parte di un imponente gruppo scultoreo raffigurante un tema di carattere morale, *la Verità svelata dal Tempo*. Essa sarebbe stata infatti sovrastata da un vecchio con la falce, simbolo del “Tempo”, intento a sollevare il drappo per rivelare la radiosa bellezza della fanciulla. L'opera fu concepita dall'artista in un periodo particolarmente difficile della sua vita, durante il pontificato di Innocenzo X Pamphilj (1644-1655), quando fu ingiustamente accusato dei dissesti statici verificatisi nella fabbrica di San Pietro, culminati nell'abbattimento di uno dei campanili da lui stesso progettati. Bernini, che non portò mai a compimento il gruppo scultoreo, dispose che la statua rimanesse nella sua dimora come monito ai suoi discendenti. Essa rappresenta un importante esempio della straordinaria capacità tecnica dello scultore nel differenziare il trattamento della superficie marmorea. Il ricercato contrasto tra la finitura cristallina della figura e il “non finito” delle rocce emerge anche nel dettaglio del piede appoggiato alla sfera terrestre.  
Di notevole rilievo è anche l'uso, tipicamente barocco, della metafora per illustrare una vicenda che dalla dimensione personale assurge a valore di monito universale.

Bernini scolpì l'opera per sè stesso in un momento difficile della sua carriera (al tempo del papato di Innocenzo X Pamphilj, 1644-1655). Egli era stato accusato di aver causato problemi strutturali a un campanile di San Pietro. Il gruppo, mai terminato, avrebbe dovuto includere la personificazione del Tempo. Bernini lasciò la scultura come un eterno monito ai suoi discendenti, presso i quali rimase fino al 1924.
keywords: Personificazione; Iconologia; allegoria; marmo; movimento

en.name: Carpet
description:
Field: The field is of a reddish hue and depicts motifs of interwoven green ribbons that form elongated hexagons. Inside of these upright pineapples framed on serrated palms are housed.  
Border: The carpet consists of two borders: the interior consists of green and white motifs upon a dark background; The exterior features calligraphic elements and flowers upon a blue background.  
Naturally coloured wool is used for the warp and weft. The wool knots utilise blue, green, red, yellow and white hues.  
The carpet is of a Gothic-Moorish type in which Gothic motifs predominate in the field, while Mudejar styles persist in the valances. The outer border resembles the pseudo-*kufic* inscriptions of the Admiral series, but much more schematic.  
A similar carpet is reproduced in the painting 'The Annunciation' which is currently housed in the Prado museum and dated to around 1500 CE. The painting is composed by the unnamed artist 'Master of the Sisla'.  
The current dimensions do not reflect the original size of the carpet, since it is composed of numerous fragments due to several successive restorations. It is the first in a series that is inspired by contemporaneous fabrics.  
The carpet comes from the Weisberger Collection.
materials: Warp: Wool, Weft: Wool, Spanish knot [Density: 2500 knots/dm2 ]
tags: Warp: Wool, Weft: Wool, Spanish knot [Density: 2500 knots/dm2 ]

es.name: Alfombra
description:
Campo: De color rojo, muestra una decoración de cintas de color verde entrelazadas, formando hexágonos alargados, de posición ascendente, en cuyo interior se alojan piñas enmarcadas sobre palmas dentadas.  
Marco: Rodeada en todo su perímetro por dos cenefas separadas por líneas: la interior, con elementos indefinidos en verde y blanco sobre fondo oscuro; la exterior presenta elementos de carácter caligráfico y flores sobre fondo azul.  
Para la urdimbre y la trama se utiliza lana en su color. Los nudos se realizan en azul, verde, rojo, amarillo y blanco.  
Alfombra de tipo gótico-morisca: en el campo predominan los motivos góticos, mientras que en las cenefas persisten motivos de recuerdo mudéjar. La cenefa exterior recuerda a las inscripciones seudocúficas de la serie del Almirante, pero mucho más esquemática.  
Una alfombra similar aparece reproducida en una Anunciación del Maestro de la Sisla del Museo del Prado, fechada hacia 1500.  
Las dimensiones actuales no reflejan el tamaño original de la alfombra, puesto que ésta está compuesta por numerosos fragmentos, después de sucesivas restauraciones.  
Es la primera serie que se inspira en los tejidos coetáneos a ella.  
Antigua colección Weisberger.
materials: Urdimbre: Lana. Trama: Lana. Nudo español [densidad de nudos 2500 por dm2]
tags: Urdimbre: Lana. Trama: Lana. Nudo español [densidad de nudos 2500 por dm2]

en.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
short_description: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics.Ssingle-volume Qur’ans like this one became increasingly popular and were completed in large numbers. This example – which appears to have remained unfinished judging by the empty title cartouches above the chapters, begins – as is customary – with a lavishly decorated double page, showing – on the right - the first chapter ‘Al-Fatiha’ and – on the left - the beginning of the second chapter ‘Al-Baqara’. Both texts are contained within broad geometric borders and framed with colourful illuminations with vegetal detailing. The remainder of the all in all 114 chapters of the Holy Qur’an are written in black naskhi and red detailing, with 15 lines to each page. As was customary, the verse markers are rendered as golden circles and each page is confined within delicate gilt borders. Colourful medallions in some of the margins mark important subdivisions of the text.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
artist: Calligrapher Ali Shukri, known as Nadherzadeh
keywords: naskhi
materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather

de.name: Marinus-und-Anianus-Altar (Hochaltar)
description: Der Hochaltar ist Zielpunkt des Raumgefüges, wobei sein mächtiges Säulenretabel selbstbewusst über die ihm als Rahmen zugedachte Pilasterarkade hinausgreift. In Ergänzung der innerhalb des Freskenprogramms thematisierten Martyrien der Kirchenpatrone zeigt das Altarblatt deren Glorie. Berühmte Musterbeispiele der Rokoko-Skulptur sind ihrer exaltiert-eleganten Posen und der versteckten Ironie wegen die Standfiguren: Bei den süddeutschen Bistumspatronen wittert der Korbinian beigesellte Bär das Fischattribut des Ulrich, und beim heiligen Kaiserpaar wendet Heinrich II. sich eifersüchtig von seiner des Ehebruchs beschuldigten Gemahlin Kunigunde ab, während diese beleidigt die ihr auferlegte Tugendprobe durch beiläufiges Antippen einer glühenden Pflugschar mit entblößtem Fuß absolviert.
artist: Altar und Skulpturen: Ignaz Günther (1725-1775); Altarblatt: Joseph Hartmann

en.name: Marin and Anian Altar (High Altar)
description: The high altar is the focal point of the spatial sequence, with its mighty columned retable confidently expanding over the pilaster arcade intended as its frame. In addition to the thematised Martyrdom of the church patrons within the fresco cycle, the altar piece displays their glory. Famous examples of Rococo sculpture are the standing figures due to their exalted, elegant poses and hidden irony: near the south German diocesan patrons, the Corbinian associated bear senses the fish attribute of Ulrich. In regard to the holy imperial couple, Heinrich II turns away jealously from his wife, Kunigunde, because she was accused of adultery. Insultingly, she absolves the test of virtue imposed on her by casually tapping a smouldering ploughshare with her bare foot.
artist: Altar and Sculptures: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); Altar piece: Joseph Hartmann
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Sunbeam Grand Prix
description: In 1923, Sunbeam boss Louis Coatalen recruited the renowned Fiat engineers Bertarione and Becchia. They developed three cars for the 1924 Lyon Grand Prix, including this highly original No. 3. The No. 3 features two overhead camshafts, a roller crankshaft, a Rootes compressor, a dry sump, four-wheel servo brakes and a low-slung chassis. Although it failed to win in the 1924 Grand Prix de l'A.C.F, the two-litre Sunbeam has to its credit a very long line of successes in all kinds of events, including Grands Prix, world and class records and hill climbs.
keywords: Early racing; steel body; aluminium panels; Grand Prix

ar.name: جامع الصالح طلائع.
description:
يعتبر هذا الجامع آخر جامع أنشئ في العصر الفاطمي في مصر، وقد اشتمل على مميزات معمارية قلّ أن تتوفر في جامع فاطمي آخر.  
  
بني الجامع على ارتفاع 4 م من منسوب الشارع، وجُعل في أسفله حوانيت. ويطلق على هذا النمط من المساجد اسم "المساجد المعلقة"، وهو يعتبر أول مثال لجامع معلق في مصر. وقفت الحوانيت على الجامع، واستخدم ريعها لصيانته وتجديده. وقد اتبع هذا النظام من الوقف بعد ذلك في العصر المملوكي، فعلى سبيل المثال هو متبع في مدرسة الأشرف برسباي في القاهرة (بنيت عام 827 هـ / 1424 م).  
  
للجامع أربع واجهات مبنية من الحجر، ويظهر في الأجزاء السفلى من واجهاته الشمالية والجنوبية والغربية واجهات الحوانيت التي تقع أسفله. الواجهة الرئيسية للجامع هي واجهته الغربية، وتتكون من خمسة عقود تكوّن رواق المدخل الذي يتقدّم المبنى، وهو ترتيب يظهر لأول مرة في المساجد في مصر، واقتبس من جامع أبي فتاتة في سوسة في تونس (بني عام 226 هـ / 841 م). وزخرف صدر رواق المدخل بحنيات تتوجها عقود مزخرفة بأشكال محارية مشعة وأفاريز نقش في داخلها آيات قرآنية كتبت بالخط الكوفي المزخرف تشبه زخارف واجهة الجامع الأقمر الفاطمي. ويعلو الحوانيت إفريز يتكون من أشكال مربعة مزخرفة بتنوع ظهر مثلها بعد ذلك في مدرسة الصالح نجم الدين أيوب (بنيت عام 647 هـ / 1249 م) في العصر الأيوبي، وتدل هذه الزخرفة على تقدم زخارف الحفر في الحجر في العصر الفاطمي.  
  
المبنى مستطيل الشكل أبعاده 53.50 × 27 م، يتوسطه صحن مكشوف يوجد أسفله صهريج مياه، ويحيط بالصحن أربع مسطحات مسقوفة بها صفوف من الأعمدة تشكل أروقة. وأهم هذه المسطحات هو مسطح القبلة المكون من ثلاثة أروقة ذات عقود ترتكز على أعمدة رخامية. زخرفت حافات العقود من الداخل والخارج بكتابات من آيات قرآنية بالخط الكوفي المزهر، وهذه الزخرفة ظهرت سابقاً في الجامع الأزهر والجامع الأقمر. كما يوجد في جدار القبلة الذي يحتوي على المحراب شبابيك حديثة من الجص يحيط بها إفريز جصّي كتب فيه بالخط الكوفي آيات قرآنية. ويحتفظ متحف الفن الإسلامي في القاهرة بشباك جصّي أصلي من الجامع القديم. يوجد على يمين المحراب منبر خشبي يحتوي على حشوات هندسية مجمّعة بها زخارف نباتية محفورة، وهو من أعمال الأمير بكتمر في عام 699 هـ / 1299 م في عصر السلطان المملوكي الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (حكم ثلاث مرات في الأعوام 693 – 694هـ / 1294 – 1295م، و 698 – 708 هـ / 1299 – 1309 م، و 709 – 741 هـ / 1309 – 1340 م).  
  
تشير بعض المصادر التاريخية إلى أن الصالح طلائع بنى هذا الجامع ليدفن فيه رأس سيدنا الحسين - حفيد سيدنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، إلا أن الخليفة الفاطمي الفائز بنصر الله رفض وقال "لا يكون إلا داخل القصور الزاهرة." وبني المدفن داخل القصر الكبير الفاطمي، ويوجد اليوم بقايا من المدفن بجوار جامع سيدنا الحسين في حي الحسين في القاهرة.  
  
ويقوم المجلس الأعلى للآثار حالياً (عام 2005 م) بتنفيذ مشروع شامل لترميم الجامع.

هو آخر جامع بُني في العصر الفاطمي، ويقع خارج أسوار القاهرة الفاطمية، في مواجهة "باب زويلة". كما أنه أول جامع يرتفع عن مستوى الطريق، في مصر، وجُعل في أسفله حوانيت للصرف من ريعها على صيانته وتجديده. وتشبه زخارف رواق المدخل وكتاباته، تلك التي في واجهة جامع الأقمر.
artist: الصالح طلائع بن رزيك، وكان قد تولى الوزارة عام 549 هـ / 1154 م في عصر الخليفة الفاطمي الفائز بنصر الله (حكم في الفترة 549 – 555 هـ / 1154 – 1160 م).
keywords: رواق مدخل؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ عمارة دينية؛ مسجد معلق.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: Salih Tala’i Mosque.
description:
Al-Salih Tala'i Mosque is considered the last mosque built in the Fatimid period in Egypt. It includes distinctive architectural features that are scarcely found in any other Fatimid mosque.  
The mosque was built 4 m above street level and a series of shops were built below it. This mode of mosque-building was known as a 'suspended mosque'; the building is thought to be the first example of a suspended mosque in Egypt. The shops were endowed (*waqf*) to the mosque, the revenue from them going towards its maintenance and renovation. This system of *waqf* was imitated subsequently in the Mamluk period in, for example, al-Ashraf Barsbay Madrasa in Cairo (built AH 827 / AD 1424).  
The mosque has four facades, all of which are built of stone. On the lower parts of the northern, southern and western facades are shops located beneath the mosque. The principle (western) façade of the mosque consists of five arches forming an entrance arcade, which precedes the building. This is an arrangement that appears here for the first time, and which was borrowed from the Mosque of Abi Fatata in Sousse, Tunisia (built AH 226 / AD 841). The front of the entrance colonnade is decorated with niches, crowned with arches of radial-shell form and friezes, within which are Qur'anic verses carved in decorative *kufic* script; all of which is similar to the facade decoration of the Fatimid Mosque of al-Aqmar in Cairo. Above the shops is a frieze consisting of squares which are carved with a variety of decorations, the like of which appears later in the Madrasa of al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub also in Cairo, built during the Ayyubid period in AH 647 / AD 1249. The decorative scheme indicates the development in carved decoration on stone during the Fatimid period.  
The building is rectangular in shape, measuring 53.50 m x 27 m. At the centre of the mosque is an open courtyard, and below the courtyard is a water cistern. The courtyard is surrounded by four roofed areas with rows of columns forming colonnades. The most important of these is the *qibla* sanctuary, consisting of three aisles of colonnades with arches resting on marble columns. The edges of the arches are decorated on the inside and outside with verses from the Qur'an carved in floriated *kufic* script, a decorative innovation that had appeared before in al-Azhar Mosque and in al-Aqmar Mosque, both of which are also in Cairo. Furthermore, the *qibla* wall, which contains the *mihrab*, is also characterised by stucco coloured-glass windows that are not original and which are surrounded by a stucco frieze on which Qur'anic verses are inscribed in *kufic* script. These decorative features were entirely new to Egyptian architecture. The Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo preserves an original stucco window from the old mosque.  
To the right of the *mihrab* is the wooden *minbar*, which contains assembled geometric panels with carved vegetal decoration. This is one of the works commissioned by Amir Boktomor in AH 699 / AD 1299, during the reign of the Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun.  
Some of the historical sources indicate that al-Salih Tala'i built this mosque to bury within it the head of Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad. However, the Fatimid caliph, al-Fa'iz bi Nasr Allah, refused to entertain the idea, and insisted that it should not be placed anywhere except within the Palaces of Zahira, thus, he built the tomb within the Great Fatimid Palace. Today what remains of the tomb is to be found beside the Mosque of Sayyida al-Husayn, in the district of al-Husayn, in Cairo.  
In 2005 the High Council of Antiquities undertook the implementation of a comprehensive restoration project for the mosque.

The last mosque to be built in Egypt in the Fatimid period, it lies outside the south Fatimid walls of Cairo opposite Bab Zuwayla. It is the first mosque in Egypt built above street level to allow the presence of shops beneath it to provide revenue for the mosque's upkeep and renovation. The decorations of the entrance arcade and its epigraphy resemble those on the facade of al-Aqmar mosque.
artist: Al-Salih Tala’i ibn Ruzik, who occupied the position of vizier in the year AH 549 / AD 1154 during the reign of the Fatimid caliph al-Fa’iz bi Nasr Allah (r. AH 549–55 / AD 1154–60).
keywords: Entrance colonnade; epigraphic inscription; vegetal decoration; religious architecture; suspended mosque.
partner: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Supreme Council of Antiquities

es.name: Mezquita de al-Salih Talai.
description:
La mezquita de al-Salih Talai se considera la última mezquita fatimí construida en Egipto. Presenta peculiares rasgos arquitectónicos que apenas se encuentran en otros templos fatimíes. Se levantó a 4 m de altura con respecto al nivel de la calle y debajo de ella se construyeron tiendas. Este tipo de mezquita se denomina "mezquita suspendida" y este es el primer ejemplo que se conoce en Egipto. Las tiendas eran un *waqf* para la mezquita y los beneficios que se obtenían en ellas se destinaban a mantenimiento y renovación. El sistema de *waqf* siguió vigente en época mameluca, por ejemplo en la madrasa de al-Ashraf Barsbay de El Cairo (827 / 1424).  
La mezquita tiene cuatro fachadas, todas de piedra. En la parte inferior de las fachadas norte, sur y oeste hay tiendas. La fachada principal (oeste) consta de cinco arcos que forman un pórtico de entrada al edificio. Es aquí donde aparece esta disposición por primera vez, inspirada por la mezquita de Abi Fatata de Susa (Túnez), construida en 226 / 841. Flanquean la arcada zonas rehundimientos en forma de nicho con decoración lobulada y frisos tallados con versículos coránicos en letra cúfica; todos estos elementos recuerdan a la decoración de la mezquita de al-Aqmar (El Cairo). Sobre las tiendas se aprecia un friso compuesto por cuadrados con diversos motivos ornamentales tallados, similares a los que más tarde aparecerían en la madrasa de al-Salih Naym al-Din Ayyub (también en El Cairo), construida en época ayyubí (647 / 1249). El esquema decorativo pone de manifiesto el desarrollo que experimentó la decoración tallada en piedra durante la época fatimí.  
El edificio es de planta rectangular (53,5 × 27 m) con patio central, bajo el cual hay un aljibe. El patio está rodeado por tres pórticos y la sala de oración de tres naves paralelas al muro de la *qibla* cuyas arcadas descansan sobre columnas de mármol. El extradós de estos arcos está adornado, por ambos lados, con aleyas del Corán talladas en escritura cúfica florida, decoración que sólo se había empleado antes en las mezquitas de al-Azhar y al-Aqmar (ambas en El Cairo). Además, el muro de la *qibla* se distingue por sus ventanas de estuco con vidrieras (aunque no son las originales), rodeadas por un friso también de estuco con aleyas en letra cúfica. Estos elementos ornamentales eran una total novedad en la arquitectura egipcia. En el Museo de Arte Islámico de El Cairo se conserva una ventana de estuco original de la antigua mezquita.  
A la derecha del *mihrab* está el *minbar* de madera, de tableros con decoración vegetal tallada. Se trata de una de las obras realizadas por orden del emir Buktumur en 699 / 1299, en tiempos del segundo sultanato de al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (698-708 / 1299-1309).  
Fuentes históricas indican que al-Salih Talai mandó construir esta mezquita para enterrar en ella la cabeza de al-Husayn, nieto del profeta Muhammad. No obstante, el califa fatimí al-Faiz bi-Nasr Allah rechazó la idea e insistió en que el único lugar digno para ella era el palacio al-Zahira, por lo que ordenó construir la tumba dentro del gran palacio fatimí. Hoy se conservan vestigios de la tumba junto a la mezquita de Sayyidna al-Husayn, en el barrio cairota de al-Husayn.  
En 2005, el Alto Consejo de Antigüedades de Egipto emprendió un completo proyecto de restauración de la mezquita.

Esta mezquita, la última fatimí de Egipto, se halla fuera de la muralla sur de El Cairo fatimí, enfrente de la Bab Zuwayla. Es la primera mezquita egipcia que se construyó por encima del nivel de la calle para poner tiendas debajo que produjeran beneficios destinados a su mantenimiento. La decoración de la fachada de entrada y su epigrafía recuerdan las de la mezquita de al-Aqmar.
artist: Al-Salih Talai ibn Ruzik, que ocupó el puesto de visir en el año 549 / 1154 durante el reinado del califa fatimí al-Faiz bi-Nasr Allah (r. 549-55 / 1154-60).
keywords: columnata de la entrada; inscripción epigráfica; decoración vegetal; arquitectura religiosa; mezquita suspendida.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

fr.name: Mosquée d'al-Saleh Tala’i.
description:
Cette mosquée est probablement la dernière construite en égypte au cours de la période fatimide. Elle présente des caractéristiques architecturales quasi spécifiques.  
Elle a été construite à 4 m au-dessus du niveau d'une rue que longe une série de boutiques. Elle serait le premier exemple égyptien de cette disposition appelée “mosquée suspendue”. Les boutiques, mentionnées dans la charte *waqf* de la mosquée, servaient à financer son entretien et sa rénovation. Ce système de *waqf* fut repris par les Mamelouks par exemple dans la *madrasa* d'al-Achraf Barsbay (827 H / 1424 J.-C.).  
L'ensemble compte quatre façades, toutes en pierre. La principale (ouest) compte cinq arches formant une arcade en projection par rapport au bâtiment. Cette disposition apparaît ici pour la première fois et a probablement été empruntée à la mosquée de Sousse en Tunisie (226 H / 841 J.-C.). Le devant de la colonnade d'entrée est décoré de niches surmontées d'arcs en forme de coquille radiante et de frises sculptées de versets du Coran en écriture de style coufique décoratif, l'ensemble étant similaire au décor de la façade de la mosquée fatimide d'al-Aqmar au Caire. Au-dessus des boutiques, la frise composée de carrés sculptés de divers motifs décoratifs est semblable à celle qui sera apposée plus tard sur la *madrasa* d'al-Saleh Najm al-Din Ayyoub, également au Caire, et construite sous les Ayyoubides en 647 H / 1249 J.-C. Ce type de décor marque un état du développement de la décoration en pierre sculptée de la période fatimide.  
La construction de forme rectangulaire mesure 53,50 x 27 m. Au centre se trouve une cour ouverte créée au-dessus d'une citerne d'eau. Elle est entourée de quatre zones couvertes à colonnades. La plus importante, celle de la *qibla*,consiste en trois nefs à colonnades de marbre soutenant des arcs. Ceux-ci sont décorés sur leurs faces et leur intrados de versets du Coran sculptés en style coufique fleuri, innovation décorative déjà apparue cependant à la mosquée al-Azhar et la mosquée d'al-Aqmar, toutes deux au Caire. Le mur de la *qibla*, dans lequel s'ouvre le *mihrab*,se caractérise par des fenêtres en stuc à verres de couleur (non originales) prises dans une frise en stuc sur laquelle sont gravés des versets coraniques en style coufique. Ces éléments décoratifs étaient alors entièrement nouveaux pour l'architecture égyptienne. Le Musée d'art islamique du Caire conserve une fenêtre en stuc d'origine qui a appartenu à cette mosquée.  
à droite du *mihrab* s'élève le *minbar* en bois composé d'un assemblage de panneaux à motifs géométriques de décor végétal sculpté. Il s'agit d'un travail commandé par l'émir Boktomor en 699 H / 1299 J.-C. sous le règne du sultan mamelouk al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, qui régna à trois reprises (693-694 H / 1294-1295 J.-C. ; 698-708 H / 1299-1309 J.-C. ; 709-741 H / 1309-1340 J.-C.).  
Certaines sources historiques rapportent qu'al-Saleh Tala'i a édifié cette mosquée pour y enterrer la tête d'Hussein, petit-fils du prophète Muhammad. Cependant, le calife fatimide al-Fa'iz bi Nasr Allah s'y opposa et ordonna que la relique soit conservée dans le palais d'al-Dahira et construisit à cet effet un tombeau dans le Grand Palais fatimide. Aujourd'hui les vestiges de ce tombeau se trouvent sous la mosquée de Sayyidna al-Hussayn dans le quartier d'al-Hussayn au Caire.  
En 2005, le Haut Conseil des Antiquités a entrepris une restauration complète de la mosquée.

Dernière mosquée construite en Égypte durant la période fatimide, elle est située à l'extérieur du mur d'enceinte méridional du Caire, face à Bab Zouwayla. C'est la première mosquée construite en Égypte au-dessus du niveau de la rue, permettant ainsi, en dessous, l'installation d'échoppes destinées à procurer des revenus pour l'entretien et la rénovation de la mosquée. Les décorations de l'entrée en arcade et son épigraphe ressemblent à celles de la façade de la mosquée al-Aqmar.
artist: Al-Saleh Tala'i ibn Ruzik, vizir en l'an 549 H / 1154 J.-C. sous le règne du calife fatimide al-Fa’iz bi Nasr Allah (r. 549-555 H / 1154-1160 J.-C.).
keywords: entrées à colonnade ; inscriptions épigraphiques ; décoration végétale ; architecture religieuse ; mosquées suspendues
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: Covered al-Buzuriyya Market
description: During the Mawlid (Feast of the Birth of Prophet Muhammad), people from all over Damascus rush to buy the first gift of this occasion, the *Mulabbas*, distinguishing the capital from other Syrian cities. This sweet, made of roasted almonds coated with sugar, is linked to the emotional history of the people of the capital because it is white, symbolising new birth, as in the birth of the Prophet. Many shops in the historic Buzuriyya market in Damascus are filled with sweets and chocolates in preparation for Mawlid al-Nabawi. According to one of its makers, the *Mulabbas* industry in Damascus dates back more than 150 years, and its main sales area is centred in the historic Buzuriyya Market.

en.name: Artillery piece – Half-cannon – Muzzleloader
description:
Although the military armaments industry of India and China flourished more than it did in Europe in the early 15th century, developments in Europe took advantage later in the century – the Portuguese learning armament techniques. During the 16th and 17th centuries with their arrival in China, the Portuguese were able to profit from their ability to help the warring factions in the Chinese Empire. In Japan, the Shogun authorities learned about guns from the Portuguese in the 16th century.  
This half-canon dates to the 17th-century. Cast in bronze, it has a caliber of 13.8 cm and a length of 3.62 m; it weighs over 3026 kg. It uses iron canon balls of 8.2 kg.  
The object displays the coat of arms of the city of Macao in China, below which is a rampant lion with a Marquis' crown. Engraved in a frame is the following inscription: “ANT. TELES DE MENEZES Govºr DA INDIA A MANDOU FAZER NO ANO DE 1640” (“ANTONIO TELES DE MENEZES GOVERNOR OF INDIA ORDERED IT TO BE MADE IN 1640”).  
Holding in its breech the name of the Caster “M\[anu\]el TAVARES BOCARRO”, as a personal touch, the cascable ending is in the shape of a lotus flower. Manuel Tavares Bocarro, son of Pedro Dias Bocarro also a gun founder, was the leading officer of the gun foundry of cannons in the Chunambeiro, Macao, during the mid-17th century. The cannons he produced were famous worldwide; two of them are in the Tower of London.
A bronze half-cannon muzzleloader from the first half of the 17th century, used to attack and defend fortresses.
keywords: Half-cannon; Bocarro; bronze; military object; arms; armours; weapon; firearm

pt.name: *Peça de Artilharia - Meio Canhão – Carregamento pela Boca*
description:
Embora a indústria do armamento militar, no início do século XV, conhecesse um maior florescimento na Índia e na China relativamente à Europa, nos finais do século XV, o desenvolvimento europeu levou a dianteira, com a aprendizagem pelos portugueses das técnicas de fabrico de armamento. Durante os séculos XVI e XVII, com a sua chegada à China, os portugueses lucraram com a sua capacidade de ajudar as facções beligerantes no Império chinês. No Japão, foi com os Portugueses que, no século XVI, os *xoguns* tomaram contacto com as armas de fogo.  
Este meio canhão, datado do século XVII, é fundido em bronze, tem o calibre de 13,8 centímetros, mede 3,62 metros de comprimento, pesa mais de 3026 quilos e lançava balas de ferro de 8,2 quilos.  
A peça ostenta o brasão de armas da cidade de Macau, na China. Por baixo, apresenta um leão rampante, encimado por uma coroa de marquês. Numa moldura, tem gravada a seguinte inscrição “ANT. TELES DE MENEZES Govºr DA INDIA A MANDOU FAZER NO ANO DE 1640”.  
Na culatra, tem inscrito o nome do fundidor, “Mel TAVARES BOCARRO”. Como toque pessoal, a cascavel termina na forma de uma flor de lótus. Manuel Bocarro, filho de Pedro Dias Bocarro, também ele fundidor no seu tempo, foi o responsável pela fundição de canhões em Chunambeiro, Macau, durante a primeira metade do século XVII. Os canhões por ele fabricados eram famosos em todo o mundo; dois deles encontram-se na Torre de Londres.
Meio canhão, manufacturado em bronze, de carregamento pela boca, da primeira metade do século XVII, usado no ataque e na defesa de fortalezas.
keywords: Meio canhão, Bocarro, bronze.

en.name: Pharaoh Rameses II in the act of killing enemies with his spear
names: Il faraone Ramses II trafigge un nemico con la lancia
short_description: The print reproduces the drawing, today at the University Library of Pisa, realised by Giuseppe Angelelli. Angelelli’s painting is used for Table LXXXIII of the Historical Monuments which shows one of the engraved paintings from the southern wall of the temple of Abu Simbel, celebrating King Ramses piercing his enemy with a spear. This is a traditional scene that has been reproduced on numerous Egyptian monuments from early historic periods to show the supremacy of the Pharaoh above all foreign people. The enemies of the Egyptians are characterised by libic hair and dresses. An error was made by the copier in the spear used by Rameses, possibly reproduced within Angelelli’s painting because of the Director of the Commission wanted to correct the hieroglyphical text above.
holder: Egyptian Museum (original drawing: Library of Pisa University)
keywords: Campaign in Egypt; Egyptomania; archaeology; Leopoldo II; Charles X; scientific expedition; university; museums; collection; collector; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; epigraphy; travelling artist; Italian painters; Thebes; botany

en.name: Cairo to Bagdad
description: Photographic album belonging to British soldier Eric Blackwell (–1940) documenting the first successful motor crossing of the desert from Damascus to Baghdad in 1919. Carried out by a military convoy of ten Model T Fords and some 15 men under the command of Lt Col Keeling, the aim was to set up a chain of whitewashed stone markers to aid pilots of an air mail service between the eastern Mediterranean and India, cutting out the lengthy sea route via Suez, Aden and Bombay. Stops along the route included Abu Kamal, Ana, Ramadi and Fallujah before reaching Baghdad, with onward travel documented to Babylon, Basra, Bombay, Aden and Suez. The crossing predates by four years the Nairn brothers' runs in 1923, which led to the establishment of the Nairn Transport Company and the overland mail service between Damascus and Baghdad.
keywords: Great Britain; Army; Officers; Photograph; World War; 1914-1918; Campaigns; Automobile travel; Middle East; Air mail; Gelatine silver prints; albums

en.name: Carpet
description:
Even though the manufacture of Arraiolos carpets has been documented since the late 16th century, the earliest surviving examples are from the first third of the 17th century. In essence, these early pieces reveal a marked similarity to oriental carpets, especially those from Iran, but also from Turkey. Although there are no Turkish carpets in Portuguese collections, other documentary and iconographic sources confirm the presence of them in Portugal, especially during the first half of the 16th century. Just as with paintings, where representations of carpets of Turkish and Iranian origin have been recognised, some Arraiolos carpets bear testimony to the consumption habits of old, attesting to their presence in, and influence upon Portuguese artistic production. Such is the case with this example, whose composition recalls those of the “small-pattern Holbein”-type carpets, made in Anatolia.  
Despite that today it appears yellowish, the profusely decorated border was originally red and would have contrasted vividly with the blue field, where large palmettes form orthogonal lines, alternated with miniscule birds, which frame small rosettes.
keywords: carpet; Arraiolos; 17th century; Portugal; embroidery; Arraiolos stitch; Slavic cross-stitch; *ponto de Arraiolos*
materials: Linen and wool; embroidered; oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as *ponto de Arraiolos*)
tags: oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as ponto de Arraiolos)
partner: National Museum of Ancient Art ‒ MNAA

en.name: The port of Brăila
short_description: In 1829, an annex to the peace treaty of Edirne, that was concluded after the Russo-Ottoman war of 1828-1829, concerned the Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia. One of its provisions was that the Sublime Porte had to give back to Wallachia the three cities situated on the left bank of the Danube, which it had conquered in the 15h-16th centuries. Among these was Brăila, a port on the Danube annexed by the Ottomans at around 1540. After 1829 measures were taken by the local authorities for the modernization of Brăila. The port subsequently developed thanks to the growth of Wallachian commerce as a consequence of the fact that by the treaty of Edirne the Ottoman Empire granted the freedom of commerce to the Romanian Principalities. In 1838 Brăila was given the status of free port (with no or few customs duties).

en.name: Benedictine Abbey of St. Aignan in Tihany
description:
The one-nave church has a horizontal, elevated sanctuary with a crypt underneath. The main façade, embraced by two towers, is decorated with statues of the Virgin Mary and St. Aignan (by an unknown master from Veszprém, 1754) and floral ornaments. The main gate shows the initials of Archabbot Ágoston Lécs (“ALAT”: Augustinus Lécs Abbas Tihaniensis) with his coat of arms above it.  
The richly carved furniture made for the church contrasted with the original modest, whitewashed walls (the murals seen today are 19th century).The furniture is an outstanding example of Hungarian Baroque wood carving, created by Sebestyén Stulhoff and his local assistants from Pápa and Veszprém (Stulhoff began work at Tihany Abbey in 1754). The altarpiece paintings are by artists from Pápa and Székesfehérvár.  
The opulently gilded, high-standing main altar (1757) is framed by columns and crowned with a baldachin. Statues of Benedictine saints (St. Benedict, St. Scholastica) and the saints of the Árpád dynasty (St. Stephen and St. Ladislaus) can be seen in the column niches. On the main moulding decorated with vases, the statue of the Virgin Mary stands amidst a group of angels. The main altarpiece painting by János Novák from Sopron in 1822 – the *Apotheosis of St. Aignan*, with Tihany Abbey and its surroundings in the background – is a copy of the 18th-century original by an unknown master.  
Abbot Sámuel Vajda had the Altar of Mariazell installed in 1762, and the Altar of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in 1771. On top of the Mariazell Altar *God Enthroned* looks down from a cloud surrounded by adoring angels. The sacred statue is placed in a silver-gilt, vaulted “sanctuary”, which stands in front of an arched superstructure that resembles red marble. The original clothed figurine of the Virgin Mary was replaced with one made in Tyrol in 1889. The altarpiece, carved by József Hubert from Pápa, was gilded and painted by József Cordelli from Székesfehérvár.  
The statues on the Altar of the Sacred Heart of Jesus are also the works of József Hubert, and were painted and gilded by master Ambrosio from Székesfehérvár. At the centre, Jesus with a Crown of Thorns points at his gaping wound, his heart revealed. He is framed by a large heart composed of 12 flames and a smaller heart; underneath are the figures of Our Lady of Sorrows and a pelican feeding its young with its own blood. On either side of the altar, statues of saints display their affection towards Jesus (St. Augustine, St. Peter, St. Barbara and St. Paul).  
The opulently carved pulpit from 1715 depicts the Four Church Fathers (St. Ambrose, Pope Saint George, St. Jerome and St. Augustine) and their attributes, as well as those of the Four Evangelists (angel, ox, lion and eagle), the Eye of Providence, the figure of St. Paul the Apostle and allegorical figures of Faith, Hope and Love, all in high relief.  
The altarpieces of St. Benedictine and St. Scholastica were painted by János Stern in 1759 (on one, St. Benedictine blesses the poisoned chalice that was given to him, on the other, the soul of St. Scholastica ascends to heaven in the shape of a dove). The Altar of St. Benedictine is decorated with the statues of his disciples, St. Maurus and St. Placidus. The Altar of St. Scholastica is adorned with the figures of female Benedictine abbots, St. Gertrude and St. Walburga.  
The carved pews were completed in 1760. The organ screen and the organ case are the works of József Huber, and József Cordelli did the painting and gilding in 1765; the paintings on the sides represent St. Cecilia playing the organ and King David playing the harp. The original 18th-century organ was restored in 1993.  
The furniture in the vestry is carved and partly painted (1768–mid-1770). The frescoes in the vault depict the *Sacrifice of Melchizedek, Samuel with the Prelate Heli, Zachariah and the Angel Gabriel*, the *Crucifixion*, and the *Lamb of God*. The Baroque paintings in the crypt were painted by Ambrosio Dornetti. The 11th-century crypt was re-painted in the 19th century, and renovated and restored in 1955.  
On the western facade of the monastery, a gate with a stone surround is similar to the main gate of the church. The refectory, on the ground floor of the southern wing, is decorated with murals illustrating Benedictine saints and saints of the Árpad dynasty framed with stuccoes. The library is on the first floor.

The Church and Monastery were built in the 18th century on the foundations of a former church and monastery founded by King Andrew I in 1055. The one-nave Baroque church was dedicated to the Virgin Mary and St. Aignan; their statues (dating from 1754) are visible on the two-tower facade of the church. The interior of the church was designed by local craftsmen: the master joiners Sebestyén Stulhoff and József Hubert made the richly carved furniture, Ambrosio Dornetti painted the ceiling frescoes of the vestry and János Stern and József Cordelli painted and gilded the carved furniture.
artist: Benedictine Arch Abbey of Pannonhalma; Abbot Villebald Grassó (1716–1740); Abbot Lécs Ágoston (1740–1760); Abbot Sámuel Vajda (1760–1795); Hungarian Benedictine Congregation, Ordo Sancti Benedicti (OSB)

Painter-gilders: József Cordelli, János Stern; fresco painter: Ambrosio Dornetti; master joiners/wood carvers: Sebestyén (Sebastian) Stulhoff (1723–1779); sculptor: József Hubert; painters (main altar) János Novák; renovation: Győző Cziegler and other unknown masters
history:
The Benedictine Abbey of Tihany was founded by King Andrew I of the Árpád dynasty in 1055. It was built in honour of the Virgin Mary and St. Aignan, and for the salvation of his closer family and the royal dynasty. King Andrew and his son were buried in the crypt of the church. During the Ottoman wars the monks deserted the monastery and it was converted into a border stronghold. After the Ottomans had retreated, the Hungarian Benedictine order was unable to pay the Royal Chamber the 10 percent land-tax due on the land at Tihany, and the abbey was obtained by the Austrian Benedictine Order of Alternburg in 1702. The Benedictine Arch Abbey of Pannonhalma repurchased the Abbey of Tihany in 1716, but only the crypt remained relatively intact as the other buildings were blown up by Austrian imperial troops after the end of the Turkish wars.  
The reconstruction of the building complex in the Baroque style can be separated into three main phases. During the first phase in the 1720s, reconstruction of the church and the monastery commenced under the supervision of Abbot Villebald Grassó. In 1736, both the new church built on the medieval foundation walls, and the new monastery burned down. Reconstruction was resumed in 1737, but the Baroque building we see today was built later – under Abbot Ágoston Lécs in the 1740s – which marks the second reconstruction phase. In 1754, the church was consecrated for temporary use. The third phase of reconstruction marks the completion and interior furnishing, ending in 1778, with the consecration of the church. The Abbot at the time, Sámuel Vajda, was granted special permission by Pope Clement XIII to hold a celebration known as the Sacred Heart of Jesus (a celebration that became compulsory in the worldwide Roman Catholic Church in 1856).  
In 1786, when Emperor Joseph II dissolved the Benedictine order, only one monk was allowed to stay in the monastery to complete parish duties, and the 18th-century furniture in the library was sold. The Benedictines were only able to return to Tihany in 1802.  
In the late 19th century, Abbot Zsigmond Simon (1864–1891) entrusted Győző Cziegler with the renovation of the buildings, which by now were in poor condition. The altars were renewed and new murals and frescoes were painted (1889–1890). King Charles IV and Queen Zita spent their final days in Hungary under the roof of the monastery in Tihany (26–31 October 1921). The building complex was nationalised in 1950 and the monastery was converted into a workhouse; it finally became a museum in 1955. The books that were in the library have disappeared. The Benedictine order returned to Tihany in 1990, but the complex was only granted back to them in 1994. Today it functions as the Benedictine Abbey Museum. Between 1992 and 1996, the interior of the church was thoroughly restored. Reconstruction of the monastery resumed in 1996.

ar.name: قلعة معان.
description: كانت قلعة معان واحدة من محطات قوافل الحج الشامي. تتخذ القلعة شكلاً مربعاً طول ضلعه 24 م، وترتفع جدرانها الباقية إلى ما يزيد عن 9 م، ويخترقها فتحات ضيقة لإطلاق السهام.  يفتح المدخل في منتصف الجدار الشرقي، وتعلوه بعض الزخارف المحفورة في الكتل الحجرية والتي أقيم فوقها سقاطة.  يلاحظ أن نوعين من الحجارة استخدما في هذا الجدار والمدخل الذي فتح فيه.  تتألف الزخارف المنقوشة في الحجر من كتابة وضعت بين عنصرين زخرفيين في الأعلى والأسفل، وتذكر اسم السلطان العثماني سليمان القانوني بصفته راعٍ للبناء.  يتألف العنصر الزخرفي العلوي  من نجمة ثمانية تكونت من تقاطع مربعين يتوسطها قرص دائري، وعلى جانبي النجمة توجد الزخارف التي تتكون من أشكال نباتية ونماذج هندسية.  يؤدي المدخل إلى فناء مستطيل أبعاده 19 م X 8 م يحيط به من جانبين عشر غرف بما فيها إيوانان متعامدان.  يتكرر هذا التوزيع للغرف في الطابق الثاني الذي زوِّد بممر عرضه 1 م.

قلعة معان، محطة على طريق الحج؛ تبعد نحو 200 كم عن عمَّان جنوباً. وهذه الآبدة منشأة مُربَّعة. لأسوارها كوى إطلاق سهام، مع بوابة دخول وسط الجدار الشرقي. الزخارف الحجرية الكائنة فوق البوابة مباشرة، تحيط بنقش يُؤكِّد أن السلطان العثماني سليمان القانوني هو المؤسِّس (في عام 937 هـ/1531م). في أعلى الجدار، فوق المدخل، ثمة نافذة بارزة كاشفة. جرى استخدام نمطين مختلفين من أنماط العمارة الحجرية، لبناء الجدار الشرقي، ممّا قد يشي بإصلاحات وتعديلات طرأت على البوابة والطبقة العليا.

en.name: The Fortress at Ma’an.
description:
A station on the pilgrimage route in southern Jordan, the fortress at Ma'an lies about 200 km south of Amman along the desert highway. The monument is a square structure measuring 24 m x 24 m with a maximum preserved height that exceeds 9 m.  
The walls are provided with plain slit windows, with the entrance gateway located in the middle of the eastern wall articulated by stone decorations immediately above it. At the top of the wall, directly above the gateway, a machicolation (a projecting window) is placed. Two different types of masonry were used to construct the eastern wall which might indicate some repairs and modifications to the gateway and the upper storey. The stone decoration consists of an inscription placed between two decorative devices at the top and the bottom of it. The inscription cites the name of the Ottoman Sultan Suleyman the Magnificent as the founder. The upper device consists of an eight-pointed star formed by two intersecting squares with a concave decorative disc in the centre. On both sides of the star and in the centre of the concave disk additional elements of floral and geometric designs are added.  
At the ground level 10 rooms, including two centrally placed *iwan*s, were organised symmetrically on both sides of a rectangular internal courtyard measuring 19 m x 8 m. This arrangement is repeated on the first floor which, in addition, was provided with a walkway that is 1 m long.

The Ma’an fortress is a station on the pilgrimage route, about 200 km south of Amman. The monument is a square structure. Its walls have slit windows, with the entrance gateway located in the middle of the eastern wall. Stone decorations immediately above it surround an inscription that cites the Ottoman Sultan Suleyman the Magnificent as the founder (in AH 937 / AD 1531). At the top of the wall above the gateway, a projecting window is placed. Two different types of masonry were used to construct the eastern wall, which might indicate repairs and modifications to the gateway and the upper storey.
artist: Sultan Suleyman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–74 / AD 1520–66).

es.name: Fortaleza de Ma’an
description:
El alcázar de Ma’an, una de las paradas de la ruta de peregrinación del sur de Jordania, se encuentra junto a la carretera del desierto. El monumento es una estructura cuadrada (24 × 24 m) de la que se conserva una altura máxima de algo más de nueve metros.  
Las fachadas presentan saeteras normales. En el centro de la fachada oriental está la puerta, que tiene un adorno de piedra justo encima. En la parte superior del muro, sobre la puerta, hay un matacán. En la construcción de esta fachada se emplearon dos tipos de mampostería, lo que podría indicar que en la entrada y en la planta superior se realizaron reparaciones y alteraciones. El adorno de piedra consta de una inscripción colocada entre dos elementos decorativos, uno arriba y otro abajo. La inscripción cita el nombre del sultán otomano Suleyman el Magnífico como fundador del edificio. El adorno superior es una estrella de ocho puntas formada por la intersección de dos cuadrados con un disco cóncavo en el centro. A los lados de la estrella y en el centro del disco se ven otros ornamentos geométricos y florales.  
En la planta baja de la fortaleza hay diez salas –entre ellas dos *iwan* centrales– dispuestas simétricamente a los dos lados de un patio interior rectangular (19 × 8 m). Esta distribución se repite en la primera planta, que cuenta, además, con un pasillo de un metro de ancho.

La fortaleza de Ma’an, 200 km al sur de Ammán, fue una etapa en la ruta de la peregrinación. Presenta una estructura cuadrada y tiene saeteras en los muros. Sobre la entrada, en medio del muro este, hay adornos en piedra que rodean una inscripción que menciona al sultán otomano Suleyman el Magnífico como fundador del edificio en 937 / 1531. Encima del muro de entrada hay un matacán. En la construcción del muro este se usaron dos tipos de mampostería, lo que podría indica que se realizaron reparaciones y alteraciones en la puerta de entrada y en la planta superior.

fr.name: Forteresse de Ma’an.
description:
étape sur la route du pèlerinage de Jordanie méridionale, la forteresse de Ma'an s'élève en bordure de la route du désert, à 200 km environ au sud d'Amman. Elle se présente sous forme d'une construction carrée de 24 x 24 m dont la hauteur maximale des murs subsistants excède les 9 m.  
Les murs sont percés de simples meurtrières. La porte d'entrée, implantée au milieu du mur est, est ornée en sa partie supérieure d'ornements en pierre sculptée. Au-dessus, à l'aplomb de la porte, se projette une bretèche. Deux types de maçonnerie différents ont été utilisés pour ce mur, ce qu'expliquent certaines réparations et modifications apportées à l'entrée et à l'étage supérieur. Le décor en pierre consiste en une inscription prise entre deux éléments ornementaux horizontaux. Elle cite le nom du sultan ottoman Soliman le Magnifique, fondateur de la forteresse. L'ornement supérieur est une étoile à huit branches constituées par deux carrés sécants entourant un disque concave. Des deux côtés et au centre du disque ont été ajoutés divers éléments décoratifs géométriques et floraux.  
Au rez-de-chaussée, 10 salles, dont deux *iwan* en position centrale, sont disposées symétriquement des deux côtés de la cour intérieure rectangulaire de 19 x 8 m. Ce plan se retrouve à l'étage dont les pièces sont entourées d'une desserte de 1 m de large.

C’est une construction carrée aux murs percés de meurtrières, la porte d’entrée étant située au milieu du mur est. Le décor en pierre au-dessus de la porte consiste en une inscription qui cite le nom du sultan ottoman Soliman le Magnifique comme fondateur (en 937 H /1531 J.-C.). Au-dessus, à l’aplomb de la porte, se projette une bretèche. Deux types de maçonnerie différents ont été utilisés pour la construction du mur est, ce que pourraient indiquer certaines réparations et modifications apportées à l’entrée et à l’étage supérieur.

en.name: Qur'an
description: This small manuscript is of note for its extensive documentation and equally for its extensive illumination. Its colophon states that it was copied by al-Hasan ibn Juban ibn ‘Abdallah al-Quwani (‘from Konya’) in the *madrasa* (theological school) of Sa‘ad al-Din Kubak in the city of Konya, in eastern Turkey, in AH 678 / AD 1278. Somewhat unusually, the illuminator is also named, one Mukhlis ibn ‘Abdallah al-Hindi (‘from India’). The manuscript now includes seven double-pages and one single page of illumination, all in a palette of mainly blue and gold. (The single-page frontispiece with which the manuscript now opens was probably originally a double-page composition.) Throughout the text, the name of Allah (God) is written in gold ink.

en.name: Microscopic photo-jewel, containing a microscopic photograph of Napoleon III
description: Stanhopes are an optical device that integrate a powerful magnifying lens and image to enable the viewing of microphotographs without additional tools. They first became popular following their launch at the 1859 International Fair in Paris by René Dagron. He mounted these into optical jewellery and novelties, including miniature binoculars.  One very rare variety of these stanhopes is those where the glass lens is also facetted as an artificial gem. This example held by National Museums Scotland is one of a selection in the Museum’s collections that are the only known surviving examples of these gemstones still in their original settings. The stone is in fact the glass lens and a viewing hole in the reverse of the setting allows the viewer to see the portrait.
keywords: Glass artistry; scientific glass

ar.name: طبق بقاعدة
description: نُسب هذا الطبق المسطح ذو الحافة في الماضي إلى "مجموعة جرجان"، وهو يرتكز على ثلاثة أرجل على شكل أبو الهول المتوج. يُظهر الحقل المركزي رسماً لفيل يحمل هودجاً مع شخصية تحجب وجهها، على الأرجح سيدة. هذا الموضوع ليس غريباً، ويشير إلى العلاقات السياسية والثقافية المكثفة مع جنوب آسيا في ذلك الوقت. ربما يكون إشارة إلى قصة بهرام غر وعروسه الهندية سابنود، من الشاهنامه.

en.name: Footed dish
description: Attributed to the “Gurgan hoard” in the past, this rimmed flat dish rests on three feet shaped as crowned sphinxes. The central field shows the depiction of an elephant carrying a palanchin (*hawda*) with a veiled figure, most likely a lady. Such theme is not unusual, and speaks of the intense political and cultural contacts with South Asia at that time. It may be an allusion to the story of Bahram Gur and Sapinud, his Indian bride, from the *Shahnameh*.
keywords: Dish; Kashan; Muhammad ibn Abi Tahir; Ceramics; Figural motifs; Women depiction; Calligraphy; human representation; inscription

en.name: *Dallah* (Coffee pot), *Mezallah*; serving stage smallest pot
description: This copper *dallah* goes back to a type allegedly first used in 17th-century Baghdad, and by the 19th century, there were several production centres in the Arabian peninsula. Its design cleverly reflects its functional needs. The broad base ensures stability on the fire or in the sand, whilst the large spout prevents too much coffee sediment from reaching the cup. The lid is purposely weighted to avoid it opening during the pouring process. Throughout the Near and Middle East coffee lay at the heart of social rituals and hospitality, while providing sustenance during chats, debate and political discourse in the many coffee houses in the region. In this light, the quality of the coffee served was an important indicator of both the wealth of the host and status of the guest. In continental Europe, the fashion for coffee was at its height in the 17th and 18th centuries, with coffee houses the preferred meeting places for intellectuals and artists. In Britain, meanwhile, tea soon overtook coffee in popularity, even though certain religious organisations tried to promote coffee houses for the poor in order to steer them away from public houses that primarily sold alcohol.
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
keywords: dallah; coffee pot

en.name: Les tombeaux des rois de Touggourt
description: The constructions are square, topped by domes and aligned in a picturesque way. One of these, larger than the others, contains a courtyard and several other structures. The tombs in the cemetery are rectangular, surmounted by plaster masonry blocks. The style is spare, of austere design, with no ornamentation.

fr.name: Les tombeaux des rois de Touggourt
description: Les constructions sont carrées, surmontées de coupoles et alignées d’une façon assez pittoresque. L’une d’elles, plus grande que les autres, renferme une cour et plusieurs dépendances. Dans ce cimetière, les tombeaux sont de forme rectangulaire, surmontés de blocs de maçonnerie en plâtre. Le style est dépouillé, le décor sobre, sans aucune ornementation.

en.name: Renault 16 TX
description: When it was released in 1965, the R16 revolutionized the world of sedans with its two-volume five-door body and a rear hatch. The original design is due to Philippe Charbonnaux, who created the first style office at Renault in 1960 with the release of the R8. The first model was followed in 1973 by the TS and in 1976 by the TX with five-speed gearbox, four iodine headlights, rear wiper, centrally locking doors, etc. The R16 remained in production from 1965 to 1980, resulting in 1,851,502 cars produced.
keywords: Family car; French design; steel body; front-wheel drive

en.name: Ewer
description:
During the Middle Ages, handwashing had a profound significance, linking hygiene, spirituality, and socialisation. This importance is attested to by the profuse production of ceramic and metal ewers and is also reflected in literature and poetry. Generally, stories and inscriptions, whether on the objects themselves or in architecture, refer to this act of purification in both secular and religious settings.  
  
In relation to this cultural importance, ewers were not only found in religious spaces for ritual ablution prior to prayer but also played a role in secular spaces. At the entrances to domestic and palatial premises, as a sign of hospitality and generosity, the *tacas* (small openings in the walls) probably held containers of perfumed water to welcome visitors. In addition, banquets and receptions were preceded by a washing ritual that not only emphasised hygiene, but also power and social hierarchy.  
  
Furthermore, pieces such as this one have led to historiographical debate about their place of production, ranging from al-Andalus to Sicily, or even the Asian Levant.
keywords: Ritual religioso, ritual secular, hospitalidad, espiritualidad, etiqueta social
tags: Ritual religioso, ritual secular, hospitalidad, espiritualidad, etiqueta social

es.name: Aguamanil
description: Jarra periforme con pie troncocónico y boca atrompetada, con asa en S y pico vertedor alargado, terminado en boca zoomorfa (cabeza de felino). La decoración grabada se estructura a partir de medallones y cartuchos formados por cenefas de roleos. El pie presenta una serie de medallones enmarcando figuras de aves y cérvidos. Cada lado del galbo muestra un felino enmarcado en medallón, mientras que bajo el pico vertedor se entrecruzan dos medallones más. Aquí aparecen un pavo real y un felino. En el extremo superior de dicho marco aparece un cartucho epigráfico en caligrafía cúfica. El paso al cuello está marcado por una moldura sogueada.

en.name: *St. Mary the Magdalene*
description:
St. Mary the Magdalene is kneeling in front of the crucifix, next to her are a skull and an open book. She looks at the angels holding a chalice and a crown of thorns, symbols of the Passion of Christ and pointing to heaven.  
The painting shows a skilled thecnique and brilliant colours both deriving from the deep knowledge of the local pictorial tradition (the Carraccis, Guido Reni) together with that of Venetian and Roman contemporary painting.  
The picture is still in the original stucco framing. The cartuche above mentions the date 1757, when the painting and its pendant were put in the oratory and the chaplain Biagi paid for them. The coat of arms above the painting says “INVENI QUEM DILIGIT ANIMA MEA = TENUI EUM”.

Saint Mary Magdalene kneels in front of the crucifix with her attributes next to her. She looks at the angels above, holding a chalice and a crown of thorns, the symbols of the Passion of Christ. The painter, Gaetano Gandolfi, looks at the Bolognese painting of the seventeenth-century and at the contemporary Roman and Venetian schools.
holder: Oratory of the Blessed Virgin of the Intercession (Beata Vergine del Suffragio)
keywords: Religious/liturgical painting; Altarpiece; Academic art; Gaetano Gandolfi; *St. Mary the Magdalene*; Pendant; Christian themes; symbol

it.name: *Santa Maria Maddalena*
description: Il dipinto raffigura Santa Maria Maddalena inginocchiata davanti al Crocifsso con accanto fra le altre cose il teschio, il libro aperto. Lo sguardo della santa è rivolto verso gli angeli che tengono in mano il Calice e la Corona di Spine simboli della Passione di Cristo e le indicano la via verso il Regno dei Cieli. Il dipinto è eseguito con tecnica sicura e dei bei chiaroscuri e da notare è la bella resa dei colori in particolare il giallo intenso della veste che derivano da una approfondita conoscenza della tradizione locale dai Carracci, a Guido Reni assieme alla contemporanea pittura veneta. La piccola pala, canonica nell'impaginazione compositiva, si impone tra i risultati della scuola pittorica locale coniugando gli insegnamenti della Clementina con la grande tradizione grafica del passato bolognese e le influenze dei maestri della pittura romana tra cui Pompeo Batoni. Il dipinto è ancora oggi nella sua collocazione originaria, racchiuso in una incorniciatura in stucco su cui è apposta un cartiglio da cui si apprende che l'opera e il suo pendant furono collocati nella cappella dell'Oratorio nel 1757 e commissionate a proprie spese dal cappellano dell'epoca di nome Biagi. Sopra il dipinto vi è uno stemma nel quale si legge la scritta “INVENI QUEM DILIGIT ANIMA MEA = TENUI EUM”. Il dipinto è stato restaurato in occasione della mostra sul Settecento emiliano (Bologna 1979) da A. Gialdini Santunione nel 1978.

Lo sguardo della santa è rivolto verso gli angeli che tengono in mano il Calice e la Corona di Spine simboli della Passione di Cristo. Il pittore, Gaetano Gandolfi guarda alla pittura bolognese del Seicento e alla contemporanea pittura romana di Pompeo Batoni oltre che a quella veneziana.

en.name: The female surgery division of the Italian hospital in Tunis
short_description:
Prior to the establishment of the French protectorate on Tunisia in 1881, Italian doctors operated in Tunisia. The Bey had frequently employed Italian physicians. Some were born in Tunisia, of Jewish families from Livorno, others had arrived in Tunisia as political exiles in the first half of the 19th century. The largest contingent of Italian doctors, however, migrated to Tunisia after 1881.  
In 1890, the Italian community opened a hospital with about 100 beds. Italian physicians worked in the hospital as volunteers and indigent patients were treated for free. The initial funding for creating and running the hospital came from the Italian community; the Italian state contributed to pay the expenses for the construction of a new facility in 1900 and partly subsidized the hospital activities.
tags: Comitato Della Camera Italiana Di Commercio Ed Arti

en.name: Coffee preparer and his utensils
description:
The coffee cook usually sits next to the fireplace. The embers might be in a portable fire bowl (*mawqid* or *manqal*), or in a chimney with a smoke outlet built into the guesthouse wall (*fkhayriyya, bakhura, nafila, tafiyya*).  
The making and serving of bitter coffee follows certain rules and traditions, among them that the coffee cook serves himself first and drinks in front of the guests. The explanation given for this tradition is that the *qahwaji* wants to control both the quality and temperature of the coffee.  
The order in which guests receive their coffee was traditionally fixed, but is not necessarily followed today. The highest-ranking or eldest man received his coffee first, followed by the men sitting to the right of this person to the end of the row, then beginning again with those persons to the left of the highest-ranking person to the last one, who was often seated near the door. During funeral services, and in Damascus today, the coffee will be served counterclockwise from right to left, regardless who sits where.

en.name: Alfa Romeo 2600 Sprint Zagato
description: Introduced in 1961, the Alfa Romeo 2600 was the top-of-the-range model, available at the time in Sedan, Sprint (coupe designed by Bertone) and Spider (Touring) versions. They had a new in-line six-cylinder engine with twin camshafts. Zagato presented their vision of the 2600 Coupe at the end of 1962. This prototype featured completely innovative lines compared to Alfa Romeo's offering. The final version of 1965 was not unlike the Lancia Flaminia Sport Zagato, presented a few years earlier. Despite good performance and Zagato's signature, production of the model remained confidential: from 1965 to 1967, only 105 examples were produced.
keywords: Italian; aluminium body; sports coupe; handcrafted

en.name: Le donjon du Manar
description:
The Manar dungeon is part of the *ksar* (fort) of the same name. It is a signal tower (or fire tower) erected at the edge of the cliff that protects the city to the east and overlooks the Fredj Valley. The excavated section revealed the floor plan of a square room that measured 20 metres per side, whose upper part had collapsed. Its facades are carved up to their full height with tall vertical niches with circular bases, covered by half-domes Eastern and Sassanid-inspired shell-covered cupolas that the Fatimids would use to decorate the porch of their mosque in Mahdia, and which would also be used in the Cuba Palace in Palermo. The facades overlooking the valley are preceded by a 1.50 metre deep front section.  
The storeys were ascended by straight sections of a ramp that turned around a central core consisting of stacked parts. The keep, or dungeon, consists of two rooms, one above the other. The lower room, covered with a cloister vault arch, served as a prison or storeroom. The upper room had a cross-shaped layout achieved by hollowed-out niches with flat backs. It would have been covered by a dome whose remnants can be found in the corners. A round path ran around the building. The courtyard opens onto an oratory.

fr.name: Le donjon du Manar
description: Le donjon du Manar fait partie de l’ensemble du *ksar* du même nom. C’est une tour à signaux (ou tour à feux) dressée au bord de la falaise qui protège la ville à l’est et qui surplombe l’oued Fredj. La partie fouillée a révélé le plan d’une salle carrée de 20 m de côté dont la partie supérieure s’est effondrée. Ses façades sont défoncées, sur toute leur hauteur, de hautes niches verticales à base circulaire, couvertes par des demi-coupoles en coquille d’inspiration orientale et sassanide que les Fatimides reprendront pour orner le porche de leur mosquée à Mahdia et qui se retrouvera aussi au palais de la Cuba à Palerme. Les façades qui surplombent l’oued sont précédées d’un avant-corps de 1,50 m de profondeur. On montait aux étages par des rampes tournant en sections droites autour d’un noyau central constitué de pièces superposées. Le donjon est formé de deux salles superposées. La salle inférieure, couverte d’une voûte en arc de cloître, servait de prison ou de magasin. La salle supérieure, de plan cruciforme obtenu par des défoncements en forme de niches à fond plat, devait être recouverte d’une coupole dont on retrouve les vestiges de trompes d’angle dans les coins. Un chemin de ronde faisait le tour du bâtiment. La cour donne sur un oratoire.

en.name: Marasali prayer rug
description: A Caucasian Marasali prayer rug woven in 1253 Hijra (1838 AD) with the quintessentially Azeri flaming buta motif. The main, and very dark blue, field of this pile carpet is occupied by rows of multi-coloured pear-shaped leaf motifs with serrated edges.  These motifs are better known as flaming butas (also botehs or Paisley pattern motifs), and are here alternately coloured across the horizontal rows, creating uniformly coloured diagonal rows on the vertical axes from bottom right to top left. A geometrical arch is positioned at the top end of the centre filed creating the distinctive prayer-niche design of the prayer rug. To the left of the arch’s tip is discretely woven the date of manufacture using red knots. In Arabic letters and numbers it states “year 1253” in the Islamic calendar. The border shows a row of “bird motifs”, resembling bunches of red grapes, on an ivory background. These bird motifs are one of the key distinguishing features of Marasali carpets, and have evolved from clearly rendered abstracted birds bending to peck at the ground to the form you see on the border of this carpet, which looks more like a bunch of grapes with a leaf at its base.
keywords: prayer niche; prayer rug; Paisley Pattern; boteh; buta; flaming buta; bird; inscrption; date
materials: Silk warp and weft; wool pile

en.name: Fort of the Andalusians
description:
This monumental fort occupies an end point in the north-west of the enclosure which allows it to survey and control the town, the port and the harbour of Bizerte. Its construction was begun by the Pasha of Algiers, ‘Alj ‘Ali, on the basis of a design mapped out by a Sicilian engineer, and, after having been conquered by the Spanish, its construction was then completed by them, hence its name. This fort was built in the shape of a five-point star, but, following a series of modifications, it stands today as a 13-sided polygon, made in part from pounded earth with a freestone facing. The fort is pierced by a single entrance door, which faces the town and is preceded by a porch, opening out onto a round arch crowned with merlons, and defended by a pole-axe. This gate leads into a polygonal courtyard; a ramp that runs along the side of this courtyard offers access onto the fort’s platform, the level of which is indicated on the outside by a large, semicircular moulding. This latter, which serves as an artillery platform, is protected by a parapet 1.9 m. high pierced with tiny arches.  
**The Andalusian Quarter**  
The Andalusian Quarter is a suburb that lies outside the city walls, lying north-east of the *medina*. Begun by the Moriscos around 1018/1610, it grew lengthwise along a stretch 450 m. in length and was 130 m. at its widest point. This Quarter possesses a more or less regular layout: it is arranged around a main thoroughfare which runs across it from north to south, and has its own mosque, the Mosque of the Andalusians.

es.name: Fuerte de los Andalusíes
description:
Este monumental fuerte ocupa el extremo noroeste del recinto, lo que permite que desde él se pueda controlar y supervisar la ciudad, el puerto y la ensenada de Bizerta. Si bien fue el pachá de Argel Alsh Alí quien comenzó la construcción de este fuerte, según el plano establecido por un ingeniero siciliano, se terminó a manos de los españoles, quienes habían venido a luchar contra él. Este fuerte tenía la forma de una estrella de cinco brazos, aunque después de varias modificaciones, se presenta hoy en día con la forma de un polígono de trece lados, construido parcialmente en tierra batida y con una acera de piedra tallada. El fuerte sólo tiene una puerta de entrada orientada hacia la ciudad y precedida por un porche abierto bajo un arco de medio punto, coronado por merlones y defendido mediante una trampa. Esta puerta se abre sobre un patio poligonal. Una rampa que recorre todo el largo del lado sudeste del patio da acceso al terraplén del puerto, cuyo nivel está señalado, en el exterior, por una gruesa moldura semicircular. Este terraplén servía de plataforma para la artillería, por lo que aparece protegido mediante un parapeto alto de 1,90 m y abierto con saeteras.  
**El barrio de los Andalusíes**  
El barrio de los Andalusíes es un arrabal extramuros que se extiende en el noroeste de la medina y que fue edificado por los moriscos hacia 1018/1610. Se desarrolla a lo ancho y tiene una extensión de unos 450 m de largo y 130 m de ancho. Este barrio presenta un trazado más o menos regular, organizado alrededor de la arteria principal que lo atraviesa de Norte a Sur, incluyendo su propia mezquita, llamada la mezquita de los Andalusíes.

fr.name: Fort des Andalous
description:
Ce fort monumental occupe un point culminant, au nord-ouest de l’enceinte, ce qui lui permettait de contrôler et de surveiller la ville, le port et la rade de Bizerte. Sa construction fut commencée par le pacha d’Alger Eulj Ali, d’après un plan établi par un ingénieur sicilien, et achevée par les Espagnols qui venaient de le battre, d’où son nom. Ce fort avait la forme d’une étoile à cinq branches mais, par suite de plusieurs modifications, il se présente aujourd’hui sous la forme d’un polygone de 13 côtés, bâti en partie en terre pilonnée avec un parement en pierre de taille. Le fort est percé d’une seule porte d’entrée, orientée vers la ville et précédée d’un porche, ouvrant sur un arc en plein cintre outrepassé, couronné de merlons, défendu par un assommoir. Cette porte ouvre sur une cour polygonale; une rampe courant le long du flanc sud-est de cette dernière donne accès au terre-plein du fort dont le niveau est signalé, à l’extérieur, par une grosse moulure semi-circulaire. Ce dernier, servant de plate-forme d’artillerie, est protégé par un parapet haut de 1,90 m percé d’archères.  
  
  
**Le quartier des Andalous**  
  
Le quartier des Andalous est un faubourg extra-muros qui s’étend au nord-est de la médina. Edifié par les Morisques vers 1018/1610, il se développe en longueur sur une étendue de 450 m de long et une largeur maximale de 130 m. Ce quartier présente un tracé plus ou moins régulier; il s’organise autour d’une artère principale le traversant du nord au sud et qui a sa propre mosquée appelée la mosquée des Andalous.
