en.name: Beni-Isguen Dam
description:
The great Beni-Isguen Dam is also known as *ahbas* and this name has spread to the whole surrounding region. Upstream of the *qsar*, it is built over the bed of the N'tissa Wadi, spanning one of the narrowest gaps between the two hills that flank the palm grove.  
The dam is 430 m long, 8 m high, 3 m wide at its base and 1 m wide at the top. It is divided into two main parts.  
Firstly, the spillway and distributor, which is 77 m wide and runs down on a slightly diagonal path; 74 vertically set stones break the power of the water current and allow the *umanas* (flood water management commission) to measure the height of the floods from the level at each stone. At the top of the spillway a post (*sham'a* or candle) of predetermined height indicates a dangerous flood level. If the water rises to this height, an immediate alert is given to evacuate the whole palm grove and the *qsar* area further downstream.  
The second part of the dam is the natural reservoir which feeds the ground water. Two wells dug out at the level of the dam accelerate and ease the feed to the ground water and so reduce the effect of evaporation caused by the extensive surface area of the stored water, especially during hot weather.

The great Beni-Isguen dam is situated upstream of the *qsar* in the bed of the N'tissa Wadi. It consists of two parts; the spillway, along which are set stones for measuring the water level and to give the alert in case of dangerous floods; and the reservoir in contact with the ground water via two wells.
keywords: dam; *ahbas*; spillway; water; reservoir.

es.name: Presa.
description:
La gran presa de Beni Izguen es llamada también *ahbas* y este nombre ha acabado denominando a toda la zona cercana. Está situada en el lecho del N’tissa, aguas arriba del *qsar*, en uno de los puntos donde más se aproximan las dos colinas que delimitan el palmeral.  
Con una longitud de 430 m, un grosor de tres metros en la base y uno en su parte superior, y una altura media de 8 metros, la presa está subdividida en dos partes principales.  
La primera, de 77 metros, adopta la forma de aliviadero y distribuidor, ligeramente inclinado en sentido longitudinal. A lo largo del cuerpo de este aliviadero, 74 piedras encajadas verticalmente frenan la velocidad de la corrientes de agua y permiten a los *umana* (comisión de gestión de las aguas de crecida) evaluar la importancia de las crecidas según la piedra alcanzada por el nivel del agua. En el límite superior de este aliviadero, un hito con una altura determinada, localmente llamado *shama* (‘vela’), indica el nivel de las crecidas peligrosas. Si el agua alcanza la cima de este testigo, se da rápidamente la alerta para evacuar todo el palmeral y parte de la extensión del *qsar*.  
La segunda parte de la presa constituye la reserva natural que permite el abastecimiento de la capa freática. Se trata de dos pozos excavados a la altura de la presa, que facilitan y aceleran el alimento de la capa freática y disminuyen así, teniendo en cuenta la extensión de la superficie de las aguas almacenadas, los efectos de la evaporación, sobre todo en época de altas temperaturas.

La gran presa de Beni Izguen está situada más arriba del *qsar*, en el lecho del río N’tissa. Consta de dos partes principales: el distribuidor, a lo largo del cual las piedras encajadas permiten medir el nivel del agua y, en caso de crecida peligrosa, dar la alerta; y la reserva natural, en contacto con la capa freática por medio de dos pozos.
dates: Siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.
keywords: Presa; ahbas; aliviadero; agua; alberca

fr.name: Barrage
description:
Le grand barrage de Beni Isguen est également appelé *ahbas* et son nom s'est étendu à toute la zone environnante. En amont du *ksar*, il se situe sur le lit de l'oued N'tissa au niveau d'une des plus courtes distances entre les deux collines qui limitent la palmeraie.  
D'une longueur de 430 m sur une largeur de 3 m à la base et de 1 m au sommet, avec une hauteur moyenne de 8 m, le barrage est subdivisé en deux parties essentielles.  
La première est en forme de déversoir et de distributeur, légèrement incliné dans le sens de la longueur sur 77 m. Le long du corps du déversoir, 74 pierres plantées verticalement brisent la vitesse du courant des eaux et permettent aux *oumanas* (commission de gestion des eaux de crue) d'apprécier l'importance des crues selon la pierre atteinte par le niveau de l'eau. A la limite supérieure de ce déversoir, une borne d'une hauteur déterminée et localement appelée *cham'a* (bougie) indique le niveau des crues dangereuses. Si l'eau atteint le sommet de ce témoin, l'alerte est rapidement donnée pour évacuer toute la palmeraie et une partie de l'extension du *ksar*.  
La deuxième partie du barrage constitue le réservoir naturel qui permet l'alimentation de la nappe phréatique. Il s'agit de deux puits creusés au niveau du barrage qui facilitent et accélèrent l'approvisionnement de la nappe et diminuent ainsi l'effet d'évaporation, étant donné l'étendue de la surface des eaux stockées surtout en période hautes températures.

Le grand barrage de Beni Isguen est situé en amont du *ksar*, dans le lit de l'oued N'tissa. Il se partage en deux étendues importantes : le déversoir le long duquel sont plantées des pierres qui permettent de mesurer le niveau de l'eau et, en cas de crue dangereuse, de donner l'alerte ; et le réservoir en contact avec la nappe phréatique par le biais de deux puits.

ar.name: منمنمة فارسية  مثبتة  كصفحة البوم
description: تخلد اللوحة ، المؤرخة في عام 1065 هـجري (1654 / 1655 ميلادي) ، ذكرى لقاء حدث سنة 1618 ميلادي بين الشاه عباس الأول (حكم 996-1038 هجري/ 1587-1629 ميلادي) والسفير الهندي .نعلم أنه في وقت لاحق من هذا العام استقبل الحاكم الصفوي كلاً من مبعوث الحاكم المغولي جهانجير (حكم في الفترة 1014-1037 هجري / 1605-1627 ميلادي) خان علم ,ومبعوث السلطان محمد قطب شاه غولكوندا (حكم في الفترة 1020-1035 هجري / 1612-1626 ميلادي) ، وهي إمارة في منطقة ديكان.بنى شيخ عباسي لوحته ، التي عُرفت منها ثلاث نسخ معاصرة أخرى، على أحد أعمال بيشانداس (أو إحدى النسخ العديدة).رافق بيشانداس السفارة وصوّر الشاه والسفير مع حاشيتهما جالسين في غابة. منذ أن أرسل شاه عباس الثاني (حكم 1052-1077 هجري/ 1642-1666ميلادي) سفيراً إلى جولكوندا في عام 1065هجري (1654/55ميلادي) ، لا يمكن استبعاد أن تكون منمنمة شيخ عباسي  هدية دبلوماسية. إذا كان هذا الافتراض صحيحًا ، فلا بد أنها رسمت بعد وفاته لتخليد ذكرى الاجتماع بين عباس الأول وسفير غولكوندا. في أعمال شيخ عباسي ، تلعب الإشارات إلى الهند دورًا بارزًا. يصور في نصف أعماله تقريبًا رجالًا ونساءً هنودًا. يمكن أيضًا إثبات أنه استعمل زخارف من اللغة البصرية الهندية وكان على دراية بتقنيات الرسم الديكاني.

en.name: Persian miniature mounted as album leaf
names: Shah ʿAbbas receiving an Indian ambassador
description:
Dated Hegira 1065 (AD 1654/55), the painting commemorates a meeting between Shah ʿAbbas I (r. Hegira 996 - 1038 / AD 1587-1629) and an Indian ambassador in 1618. We know that later in this year the Safavid ruler received both the envoy Khan ʿAlam of the Mughal ruler Jahangir (r. Hegira 1014-1037 / AD 1605-1627) and that of Sultan Muhammad Qutb Shah of Golconda (r. Hegira 1020-1035 / AD 1612-1626), a principality in the Deccan.  
  
Shaykh ʿAbbasi based his composition, of which three other contemporary versions are known, on one of Bishandasʼs work (or one of the numerous copies). Bishandas accompanied the embassy and portrayed the shah and the ambassador together with their entourage seated in a forest clearing. Since Shah ʿAbbas II (r. Hegira 1052-1077 / AC 1642-1666) sent an ambassador to Golkonda in the year 1065 (1654/55), it cannot be ruled out that Shaykh ʿAbbasʼs miniature painting was intended as a diplomatic gift. If this assumption is correct, it must be a posthumous rendition of the meeting between ʿAbbas I and the ambassador from Golconda.  
  
In Shaykh ʿAbbasisʼs oeuvre, references to India play a prominent role. Almost half of his works depict Indian men or women. It can also be shown that he took up motifs from Indian iconography and was even familiar with Deccani painting techniques.

en.name: Winston Churchill waving his hat atop his walking stick in front of the Zunfthaus zur Meisen
description:
Winston Churchill waves to a cheering crowd packed into the cathedral square in Zurich after giving a speech on 19 January 1946. Churchill visited Switzerland again from 23 August to 20 September 1946 when he travelled from Geneva via Lausanne and Bern to Zurich where he gave his famous speech on Europe at the University of Zurich. Although by then he was leader of the opposition, and was on a private visit to Switzerland, Churchill received an enthusiastic welcome befitting a statesman.  
Everywhere he went, photographers treated Churchill’s trip through Switzerland like a state visit. The Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) agency covered his visits to Lausanne and Zurich. The Swiss National Museum acquired the archives of PDL and Actualités Suisses Lausanne (ASL) in 2007. Combined they number around six million images in the form of negatives, prints, and slides. Covering the years from 1937 to 1999, they record the most significant developments during the era of analogue press photography.

en.name: Garrafilla
description:
Milk glass carafe with pronounced shoulders, cylindrical neck and flat, circular lid. Enamelled decoration with floral garlans, with the inscription “Viva la Constancia”. Small, enamelled bouquets of flowers and golden stars can be seen scattered on the surface of this deposit. Golden contours cast silhouettes on each profile.  
The most common enamelled repertoire during the reign of Carlos IV are naturalist floral decorations, floral garland with inscriptions and landscapes with pastoral images. These bouquets of flowers are inspired by the German floral bouquets of Meissen, which were in vogue in Europe during this period.  
As is the case with porcelain, the enamel on the glass is combined with gold decoration on the edging and contours in order to enhance the contours and give the piece both greater elegance and sumptuousness.  
The Real Fábrica de Cristales de San Ildefonso employed numerous components in order to obtain the milk glass:  
1.- In accordance with Venetian formulae, with lead and tin.  
2.- Or mixing calcined animal bones: a formula written by Johan Kunckel, in the well-known “Art Vetraria” of the 18th Century, by Antonio Neri.  
The discovery of this enamel technique in the Real Fábrica de Cristales dates back to 1791, when Patricio Sanz, thanks to the contributions of the famous book on the Art of Glassmaking by Neri, and the book on the art of enamel painting by Monsieur Montany, discovered the secret of fixing the colours to the surface of white glass using fire, in imitation “from China".  
The enamel used to decorated glass are very similar to those used on ceramic. They should be vitrifiable, consisting of colouring agents, generally metal oxides and fluxing agents. In other words, vitrifiable compounds which function both as a vehicle and setter for the colourants to the glass. They require annealing in a furnace at a temperature of 400ºC.
holder: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja
Museo de Artes Decorativas de Madrid
artist: Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja
keywords: Royal Glass Factory; enameled and gilded technique; milk glass; XVIII century
partner: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja

es.name: Garrafilla
description:
Garrafilla de vidrio blanco de leche, con hombros pronunciados, cuello cilíndrico y tapón circular aplastado. Decoración esmaltada con orla lazada, cobijando la inscripción “Viva la Constancia”. Pequeños ramos florales esmaltados y estrellitas doradas aparecen salpicados por la superficie del depósito. Filetes dorados siluetean los perfiles.  
Los repertorios esmaltados más comunes durante el reinado de Carlos IV son decoraciones florales naturalistas, orlas florales con inscripciones y paisajes con escenas bucólicas. Estos ramos florales se inspiraban de los ramos florales alemanes de Meissen, tan de moda durante esa época en Europa.  
Como en la porcelana, los esmaltes sobre el vidrio se combinaban con decoración dorada para adornar los rebordes y perfiles (también llamados filetes) con el fin de realzar así los contornos y dar mayor prestancia y suntuosidad a la pieza.  
En la Real Fábrica de Cristales de San Ildefonso se emplearon distintos componentes para obtener el vidrio blanco de leche:  
1.- Según fórmulas venecianas, con cal de estaño y plomo.  
2.- O mezclando huesos de animales calcinados: fórmula escrita por Johan Kunckel, en el célebre tratado de Antonio Neri “Art Vetraria”, del siglo XVIII.  
El descubrimiento de esta técnica esmaltada en la Real Fábrica de Cristales se remonta a 1791, cuando el maestro Patricio Sanz, gracias a las aportaciones del célebre libro sobre el Arte de Vidriería de Neri, y el libro sobre el arte de pintar esmalte de Monsieur Montany, descubre el secreto de fijar, por medio del fuego, los colores a la superficie del cristal blanco, a imitación “de la China”.  
Los esmaltes que se utilizan para decorar los vidrios son muy similares a los de la cerámica. Deben ser vitrificantes, y estar compuestos por sustancias colorantes, generalmente óxidos metálicos y fundentes, es decir, compuestos vitrificantes que hacen de vehículo y fijador de los colorantes sobre el vidrio. Requieren un recocido en un horno, a unos 400 º C.
holder: Museo de Artes Decorativas de Madrid
artist: Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja

en.name: Egyptianising necklace
short_description: Gold fringe necklace in the  form of cast alternating lotus flowers and buds. Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on 19th French jewellery. As was typical, this necklace is not derived from an original, but a more free creation based on patrern books.
keywords: Egyptianising; Egyptomania; floral decoration; lotus

en.name: Triumphal Arch, Vác
description: A Triumphal Arch with a single archway that rests on simple pillars, and which was designed using pure geometrical shapes. An attic can be seen above the indented cornice, and eagles on the frieze are depicted holding a festoon. The use of the eagle, a symbol of the Roman emperors, refers to both Queen Maria Theresia and her family, and her husband German Emperor Francis I of the Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty (1745–1765). On the south side of the triumphal arch that faces the city, the inscription reads: “AETERNAE DOMUI” (“To the Eternal \[Habsburg\] House”). On the attic the portraits of the Queen and her husband are visible in *tondo*s (circular engravings in high relief). The inscription on the northern side of the triumphal arch, which faces in the direction of arrival into the city, reads: “FRANCISCO I. ROM. IMP. M. THERESIAE / AUG. HUNG. BOH. REGI PIIS FELICIBUS INVICTIS / JOSEPHO ROM. REGI NOBILISSIMO CAESARI LEOPOL- / DO / M. ANNAE M. CHRISTINAE REGIIS PRINCIPIBUS OB / VACII PRAESENTI EORUM MAJESTATE TRIDUUM BEA- / TUM CHRISTOPHORUS S.R.E. CARDINALIS A MIGAZZI / EPISCOP. VAC. SECUNDO ARCUM HUNC IMAGINIBUS / AUGUSTAE DOMUS INSIGNEM DICAVIT ANNO / MDCCLXIV.” (“Frances I. Rom\[an\] Emp\[eror\] M. Theresia \[Her\] Majesty Queen \[of\] *Hungariae Bohamie* \[Czech\] Pious and Fortunate Conqueror Joseph King \[of\] the Romans most celebrated Caesar Leopold / M\[aria\] Anna \[and\] M\[aria\] Christina Royal Princesses / to pay honour for the three days of lasting happiness while staying in Vác of their Highnesses / Cardinal \[of\] S\[acrae\] R\[omanae\]. E\[cclesiae\] Christoph Migazzi Bishop of Vác dedicated \[this\] \[triumphal\] arch decorated with the images of their Highnesses in the year \[of\] MDCCLXIV \[1764\].”) The *tondo*s on this side contain portraits of archdukes Joseph and Leopold as well as the portraits of archdukes Ferdinand and Maximillian.

The Triumphal Arch in Vác is a unique edifice in the corpus of 18th-century Hungarian architecture of this type, and the first such arch to be built from stone in Central Europe. The second was built in Innsbruck a year later at the request of Queen Maria Theresia (1740–1780). It was based on the “Roman style” of the Triumphal Arch in Vác, which differed from the Late Baroque style on account of the direct influence of Antique forms and features.
artist: Architectural design: Isidore Ganneval (1730–1786); stonemason: Matthias Chmelik; sculptor: Joseph Bechert
history: Queen Maria Theresia (1740–1780) and her family visited Pest and Vác in 1764. For the occasion and to pay homage, Christoph Anton Migazzi Bishop of Vác and Archbishop of Vienna (1756–1757; 1761–1785), ordered the construction of the triumphal arch. It was designed by Isidore Ganneval – a student of Niccolò Servandoni – who introduced early Classical architecture to Migazzi’s court and subsequently to Hungary. His architecture, which was directly influenced by Antique forms and features and based on pure geometrical shapes, was one of the most modern styles in contemporary Europe. Master builders in Central Europe, many of whom held onto local traditions, did not even react to the new style for several decades. Stonemason, Matthias Chmelik, and sculptor, Joseph Bechert, worked on the construction.
keywords: Triumphal arch, dynastic representation, festivals, portraiture, Isidore Ganneval, Matthias Chmelik, Joseph Bechert, Queen Maria Theresia, German Emperor Francis I of the Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty, Christoph Anton Migazzi, Archduke Joseph, Archduke Leopold, Archduke Ferdinand, Archduke Maximillian, Vác
partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

de.name: Kath. Pfarr-, Benediktinerabtei- und Wallfahrtskirche Mariae Himmelfahrt
description: Die vom kurfürstlichen Hofarchitekten und Bernini-Schüler Enrico Zuccalli entworfene zweigeschossige  Fassade, eine Paraphrase von Berninis Louvre-Projekt, mit Nischenfiguren der Apostel von Ägid Verhelst, umschließt mit raumgreifenden barocken Kurvungen einen durchfensterten und laternenbekrönten Kuppelbau, der sich machtvoll darüber erhebt. Der zwölfeckige Zentralbau, sowie der sich im Osten anschließende Chor besitzen einen zweigeschossigen Umgang, der zum Teil noch aus der Zeit des gotischen Vorgängerbaues stammt. Im Inneren befindet sich über dem Eingangsportal eine überreich mit Stuck verzierte Orgelempore. Die Wandflächen weisen jeweils eine flache, von Rocaillekartuschen bekrönte Nische mit Altar auf, darüber leitet eine hohe Fensterzone in die Kuppel über. Die üppigen Stuckdekorationen mit kapriziösem Rocaille-, Muschel- und Blattwerk werden Johann Georg Üblher und Franz Xaver Schmuzer zugeschrieben. Der ellipsenförmige Chor im Louis-Seize-Stil steht mit seiner rational-kühlen Marmorausstattung im Kontrast zum Hauptraum und nimmt den dreiteiligen Hochaltar mit dem mittelalterlichen Gnadenbild auf. Im Sockelgeschoss der Chorrotunde sind vier vergoldete, holzgeschnitzte Reliefs von Roman Anton Boos mit Szenen aus dem Leben Christi angebracht.

Zu einem vielschichtigen Meisterwerk vereinigen sich eine prächtige Rokoko-Ausstattung und die barocke Architektur der Wallfahrtskirche St. Maria, welche die Architekten Enrico Zuccalli und Joseph Schmuzer auf der Basis eines bestehenden mittelalterlichen Zentralbaues geschaffen haben. Die Schnitzaltäre Johann Baptist Straubs und das riesige Deckenfresko Johann Jakob Zeillers bilden Höhepunkte der Innenausstattung, die mit dem kühlen Louis-Seize-Stil des Chores kontrastiert.
dates:
1710-1726 Fassade und Chorneubau  
1744-1753 Fertigstellung des Kuppelbaus  
1769-1790 Ausstattung des Chores
artist: Äbte Placidus II. Seitz (reg. 1709-1736), Benedikt III. Pacher (1739-1759), Bernhard II. von Eschenbach (reg. 1759-1779), Othmar II. Seibold (1779-1787), Alphons Haffner (1787-1803)

Architektur: Enrico Zuccalli (um 1642-1724); Joseph Schmuzer (1683-1752)  
Fresken: Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710-1783); Martin Knoller (1725-1804)  
Stuck: Johann Georg Üblher (1700-1763); Franz Xaver Schmuzer (1713-1775)  
Seitenaltäre: Johann Baptist Straub (1704-1784)  
Chorreliefs: Roman Anton Boos (1733-1810)  
Fassadenskulpturen: Ägid Verhelst (1696-1749)
history: Das Benediktinerkloster wurde 1330 von Kaiser Ludwig dem Bayern als Votiv gestiftet und 1370 geweiht. Unter Abt Placidus II. Seitz begann man mit umfassenden Veränderungen des Klosterbaues, und 1710 erfolgte die Grundsteinlegung für den Kirchenumbau auf der Basis des bestehenden mittelalterlichen Zentralbaues. Enrico Zuccalli fertigte die Entwürfe und begann zunächst mit der Neuerrichtung der Fassade, deren Türme noch heute unvollendet sind. 1726 erfolgte die Weihe des Hochaltars. Nach einem verheerenden Brand im Jahr 1744, der einen großen Teil der Ereuerungen zerstörte, wurden die Bauarbeiten ab 1745 unter der Leitung des Wessobrunner Baumeisters Joseph Schmuzer fortgeführt.

en.name: Catholic Benedictine Abbey and Pilgrimage Church of St. Mary
description: The two-storey facade is a paraphrase of Bernini's Louvre-project and was designed by Enrico Zuccalli, the electoral court architect and Bernini scholar. The niche-figures of the apostles are by Ägid Verhelst, these are enclosed within voluminous Baroque curves and a fenestrated and lantern-crowned dome construction which soars mightily above them. The dodecagonal central-plan building and the easterly attached new chancel have a two-storey ambulatory, which originates partly from the era of the Gothic construction. On the inside, a lavishly stucco-decorated organ loft is located over the entrance portal. The wall spaces have in each case a shallow niche with an altar, crowned with *rocaille*\-cartouches, above which high windows lead the eye to the dome. Luxuriant stucco decorations with capricious *rocaille*, *coquillage* and foliage are ascribed to Johann Georg Üblher and Franz Xaver Schmuzer. The elliptical-shaped Louis XVI chancel, with its rational-coolish marble work, forms a contrast to the main room and includes the three-part high altar with the medieval miraculous picture. Installed at the basement-level of the chancel rotunda, four gilded, wood carved reliefs by the Roman Anton Boos illustrate scenes of the Life of Christ.

The Baroque architecture of the pilgrimage church of St. Mary and its splendid Rococo decoration add up to a complex masterpiece, created by the architects Enrico Zuccalli and Joseph Schmuzer, and based on an existent medieval central-plan building. Carved altarpieces of Johann Baptist Straub and the large ceiling fresco by Johann Jakob Zeiller crown the interior decoration which contrasts with the coolish Louis XVI style of the chancel.
dates: 1710–1726: façade and new construction of the chancel; 1744–1753: completion of the domed structure; 1769–1790:  furnishing of the chancel
artist: Abbots Placidus II Seitz (gov. 1709–1736), Benedikt III Pacher (gov. 1739–1759), Bernhard II. von Eschenbach (gov. 1759–1779), Othmar II. Seibold (gov. 1779–1787), Alphons Haffner (gov. 1787–1803)

Architecture: Enrico Zuccalli (c. 1642–1724), Joseph Schmuzer (1683–1752); frescos: Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710–1783), Martin Knoller (1725–1804); stucco: Johann Georg Üblher (1700–1763), Franz Xaver Schmuzer (1713–1775); side altars: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784); reliefs in the chancel: Roman Anton Boos (1733–1810); niche figures on the facade: Ägid Verhelst (1696–1749)
history: The Benedictine Abbey was founded as votive by Emperor Ludwig (Louis) the Bavarian in 1330 and was consecrated in 1370. Under Abbot Placidus II Seitz large scale changes to the monastery buildings were initiated, and in 1710, the ceremonial laying of the cornerstone for the church’s reconstruction based on the existent medieval central-plan building took place. Enrico Zuccalli prepared the architectural plans and set to work on the construction of the new facade with its to-date unfinished towers. The high altar was consecrated in 1726. After a disastrous fire in 1744, which destroyed the greater part of the alterations, as of 1745, construction continued under the direction of the Wessobrunn master builder Joseph Schmuzer.
keywords: Fresco; stucco; sculpture; *rocaille*; *coquillage*
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: الجامع الكبير في المهديّة.
description:
ينتظم الجامع في مستطيل عميق (55 م x 75 م)، ويدعّمه من الجانبين برجان مستديران، كانا يستعملان لتجميع مياه الأسطحة. ويبدو أنّ الجامع لم يكن يتوفر على مئذنة، وأنّ الأذان كان يتمّ من أعلى أحد هذين البرجين. تتقدم المدخل الرئيسي كنّة تعرفها العمارة الدينيّة المغاربيّة للمرّة الأولى. يعلو هذه الكنّة ذات النِّسب المعماريّة المتناسقة عقداً دائريا متجاوزا تحمله، على مستوى الخط الأعلى، مشاكٍ تتخذ شكل محراب؛ أمّا في القسم السفلي فالواجهات المختلفة مغطاة بمشاكٍ قعرها مسطّح. وقد أعلنت هذه الزخارف التي استخدمت كنموذج لإنشاء الأبنية الفاطميّة وأثبتتها وبشكلٍ أساسي الواجهة الجانبية للجامع الكبير في صفاقس، عن الزخارف التي سوف تميّز الفترة الزيريّة. كما أنّ هيئة هذه الكنّة تذكّر بأقواس النصر الرومانيّة.  
تُفضي كنّة المدخل إلى فناء داخلي محاط بأربعة أروقة تغطّي غرفةً عند الزوايا، وهي مفتوحة على الصحن بواسطة عقود منكسرة تحملها دعامات عند الرواق الشمالي؛ وعقود دائرية ومتجاوزة في الأروقة الأخرى، وتستند على أعمدة تحمل تيجانا.  
يؤدي الرواق الجنوبي الشرقي إلى قاعة للصلاة تتكون من تسع بلاطات وثلاثة أساكيب؛ يتقاطع فيها البلاط الأوسط مع بلاط جدار القبلة ويشكلان تصميما يأخذ شكل حرف التاء "T " اللاتيني. وعند تقاطعهما يحددان فضاءا مربعا تغطيه قبّة ترتكز على أعمدة متعدّدة الفصوص، وتأوي محراباً شكله وزخارفه الحاليّة هي نسخة من محراب القرن 5 هجري/ 11 ميلادي. يتألف هذا المحراب من مشكاة نُحتت جدرانها بأثلام ذات مقطع نصف دائري، وتنتهي كل واحدة منها بصدفة. وتغطي مشكاة المحراب قبيبة فتحتها موجّهة نحو قاعة الصلاة بعقد حدوي تحمله أعمدة صغيرة تكللها تيجان من الطراز الزيري. وقد كان لجامع المهدية الكبير تأثير على هندسة بعض المساجد الفاطميّة في مصر، وعلى الأخص جامع الحكم وجامع الأقمار في القاهرة.

شيد المسجد الكبير للمهدية من طرف الخليفة المهدي؛ وخضع إلى العديد من التعديلات، قبل أن يعيد بناءه المهندس الفرنسي أ. ليزين مابين عامي 1961 و 1965. يبدو أن المسجد لم يكن يتوفر على منارة؛ وكان النداء إلى الصلاة يتم من أعلى أحد أبراجه. وقد ألهم المسجد الكبير للمهدية بعض المساجد الفاطمية في مصر مثل مسجد الحاكم ومسجد الأقمار في القاهرة. وترجع جمالية هذا الجامع إلى بساطة أشكاله، وحصانة مواده وغياب أي زخرف زائد.
dates: بداية أعمال البناء عام 303 هجري/ 916 ميلادي.
history: تمّ بناء الجامع على أرض خارجة عن محورها ولكنّها رُدمت ورُفعت فوق مستوى البحر، كما أدخلت على البناية عدّة تعديلات في العهد الزيري بعد سقوط جدار القبلة، وأجريت أعمال أخرى خلال العهد العثماني، في القرن 11 هجري/ 17 ميلادي. وقد أعيد تشييد الجامع بين عامي 1961- 1968، باستثناء الكنّة والرواق الشمالي اللذين يشكلان حاليا الأجزاء الأصلية المتبقية.
keywords: جامع؛ عمارة؛ الفترة الفاطمية؛ العهد الزيري؛ كنّة.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Great Mosque of Mahdiyya.
description:
This mosque was built on a rectangular plan measuring 75 m x 55 m. It is flanked by two round towers which served to catch the water running from the terraces. It seems the mosque did not have a minaret. The call to prayer was probably proclaimed from one of the towers. In front of the main entrance stands a porch claimed to be the first to figure in Maghrebin architecture. Harmoniously proportioned, this porch is roofed with a round horseshoe arch with *mihrab*\-shaped niches placed high up on either side. Lower down, the different faces of the porch are ornamented with flat-backed niches. This decoration, a main feature of Fatimid monuments (best exemplified by the lateral façade of the Great mosque at Sfax) was carried over into the early Zirid period. This porch is reminiscent of the triumphal arches built by the Romans.  
This entrance porch leads into a courtyard surrounded by four galleries with a room at each corner. These are supported by arches and pillars rising from the courtyard on each side. Pointed arches for the north gallery simply rest on pillars whilst the three other galleries have round horseshoe arches and columns with capitals. From the southeast gallery one comes into the prayer-hall which has nine naves and three bays. The central nave and the transept form a T-shape. At their intersection is a dome supported on multifoil columns, under which a reproduction of the AH 5th-/ AD 11th-century *mihrab* has been built. This comprises a niche with fluted walls, each flute terminating in a shell motif. A *cul-de-four* on top of the niche is bordered by a horseshoe arch positioned on small corner columns incorporating Zirid capitals. The Great Mosque at Mahdiyya was the inspiration for several Egyptian mosques, notably al-Hakim and al-Aqmar mosques in Cairo.

The Great Mosque of Mahdiyya was built by the caliph al-Mahdi. It was modified on several occasions before being rebuilt by the French architect A. Lézine between 1961 and 1965. The mosque does not appear to have had a minaret, with the call to prayer being made from the top of one of its towers. The Great Mosque of Mahdiyya inspired a number of mosques in Fatimid Egypt, such as al-Hakim Mosque and al-Aqmar Mosque in Cairo. This monument owes its beauty to the simplicity of its forms and materials, as the absence of any superfluous decoration.
history: The mosque was built on a fairly tangential piece of land which was in-filled and reclaimed from the sea. Several re-workings of the original building have taken place, mainly during the Zirid period after the collapse of the *qibla* wall. Other works were carried out during the Ottoman era in the 11th / 17th century. The mosque was rebuilt between 1961 and 1968. Only the porch and the north gallery are authentic.
keywords: Mosque; architecture; porches
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Mezquita Mayor
description:
Esta mezquita presenta una planta rectangular (75 x 55 m) con una proporción de tres por dos, y está flanqueada por dos torres redondas que servían para la recuperación de las aguas pluviales desde las terrazas. La mezquita no parece haber tenido alminar; por tanto, la llamada a la oración se haría sin duda desde lo alto de alguna de las torres. La entrada principal está precedida por un porche, considerado el primero en la arquitectura religiosa magrebí. Este porche, de proporciones armoniosas, está coronado por un arco de medio punto, flanqueado, a la misma altura que el registro superior, por nichos en forma de *mihrab*. En la parte baja, sus diferentes caras presentan nichos de fondo plano. Esta decoración –que había servido de modelo para los monumentos fatimíes, como indica sobre todo la fachada lateral de la Mezquita Mayor de Sfax– anunciaba ya la de época zirí. El aspecto general del porche evoca los arcos de triunfo romanos.  
El porche de entrada da a un patio rodeado por cuatro galerías, con una habitación en cada ángulo; la del lado norte presenta arcos apuntados sostenidos por pilares, mientras los arcos de las demás son de medio punto y descansan sobre columnas coronadas por capiteles.  
Desde la galería sureste, se entra a la sala de oración, compuesta por nueve naves y tres tramos; la nave central y la galería paralela al muro de la *qibla* adoptan una disposición en forma de T. Su intersección está rematada por una cúpula colocada sobre columnas yuxtapuestas, delante de un *mihrab* cuya forma y decoración actuales reproducen el *mihrab* del siglo V / XI. Está constituido por un nicho semicircular de fondo acanalado, con cada acanaladura rematada en forma de concha. Una bóveda de cascarón remata el nicho, que se abre a la sala con un arco de herradura apoyado sobre pequeñas columnas coronadas con capiteles de tipo zirí.  
La Mezquita Mayor de Mahdia ha servido de inspiración para algunas mezquitas fatimíes de Egipto, sobre todo las de al-Hakim y al-Aqmar, en El Cairo.

La mezquita fue edificada por el califa al-Mahdi. Objeto de varias modificaciones, fue reconstruida por el arquitecto francés A. Lézine entre 1961 y 1965. La Mezquita Mayor de Mahdiya no parece haber tenido alminar; la llamada a la oración se hacía desde lo alto de alguna de sus torres. Ha sido fuente de inspiración para algunas mezquitas fatimíes de Egipto, como las de al-Hakim o al-Aqmar en El Cairo. El monumento debe su belleza a la simplicidad de sus formas, la nobleza de sus materiales y la ausencia de decoración superflua.
dates: 303 de la Hégira / 916 d. C. (inicio de las obras)
history: La mezquita fue construida sobre un terreno relativamente irregular, que fue terraplenado y ganado al mar. El edificio ha sido objeto de varias modificaciones, sobre todo en la época zirí, como consecuencia de la caída del muro de la *qibla*. Otras obras fueron llevadas a cabo en época otomana, en el siglo XI / XVII. La mezquita fue reconstruida entre 1961 y 1968. Del conjunto original sólo permanecen el porche y la galería norte.
keywords: mezquita; época fatimí; época zirí; arquitectura; porche
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Grande Mosquée de Mahdia.
description:
Présentant un plan rectangulaire (75 x 55 m) plus profond que large, cette mosquée est flanquée de deux tours rondes qui servaient à récupérer les eaux des terrasses. La mosquée ne semble pas avoir eu de minaret ; l'appel à la prière se faisait sans doute du haut de l'une des tours. L'entrée principale est précédée d'un porche attesté pour la première fois dans l'architecture religieuse maghrébine. De proportions harmonieuses, ce porche est surmonté d'un arc en plein cintre outrepassé, flanqué, au niveau du registre supérieur, de niches en forme de *mihrab*. En bas, les différentes faces sont meublées de niches à fond plat. Ce décor, qui avait servi de modèle pour les monuments fatimides, et attesté essentiellement par la façade latérale de la Grande Mosquée de Sfax, annonçait ceux de l'époque ziride. L'allure de ce porche n'est pas sans rappeler les arcs de triomphe romains.  
  
Le porche d'entrée dessert une cour entourée de quatre galeries, abritant une pièce aux angles et donnant sur le patio par des arcs brisés soutenus par des piliers au niveau de la galerie nord. Ceux des autres galeries sont en plein cintre outrepassé et reposent sur des colonnes surmontées de chapiteaux.  
  
à partir de la galerie sud-est, on pénètre dans la salle de prière composée de neuf nefs et trois travées, la nef axiale et le transept adoptant une disposition en T. Leur intersection est surmontée par une coupole posée sur des colonnes polylobées et abritant un *mihrab* dont la forme et le décor actuels reproduisent le *mihrab* du Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.). Il est constitué d'une niche à parois creusées de cannelures à section semi-circulaire s'achevant chacune par une coquille. Un cul-de-four surmonte la niche et donne sur la salle par un arc en fer à cheval soulagé par des colonnettes d'angle sur lesquelles sont posés des chapiteaux de type ziride. La Grande Mosquée de Mahdia a inspiré certaines mosquées fatimides d'égypte, surtout la mosquée d'al-Hakim et la mosquée al-Aqmar au Caire.

La Grande Mosquée de Mahdia fut construite par le calife al-Mahdi. Objet de plusieurs modifications, elle a été reconstruite par l'architecte français A. Lézine entre 1961 et 1965. La mosquée ne semble pas avoir eu de minaret ; l'appel à la prière se faisait du haut de l'une de ses tours. La Grande Mosquée de Mahdia a inspiré certaines mosquées fatimides d'égypte comme la mosquée al-Hakim et la mosquée al-Aqmar du Caire. Ce monument doit sa beauté à la simplicité de ses formes, la franchise des matériaux et l'absence de tout décor superflu.
dates: Début de la construction : 303 de l’Hégire / 916 J.-C.
dynasty: Fatimo-ziride (début de la dynastie : 297 H / 910 J.-C.).
history: La mosquée fut construite sur un terrain relativement désaxé qui a été remblayé et entièrement gagné sur la mer. L'édifice a fait l'objet de plusieurs remaniements, essentiellement à l'époque ziride à la suite de l'effondrement du mur de la *qibla*. D'autres travaux furent menés à l'époque ottomane, au XIe siècle H (XVIIe siècle J.-C.). La mosquée a été reconstruite, entre 1961 et 1968. Seuls le porche et la galerie nord sont actuellement authentiques.
keywords: Mosquée; époque fatimide; époque ziride; architecture; porche.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: House of Castril – Provincial Archaeological and Ethnological Museum
description: The house belonged to the family of don Hernando de Zafra, who was secretary to the Catholic Monarchs. Possibly built by Hernando de Zafra’s grandson after 1539, the façade, worked in stone, is an ample discourse on the possibilities of the Renaissance language imported from Italy. This is a mixture, or a kind of anthology, with motifs of *grutescos*, *candelieri*, heraldry and symbolic forms, which tell us much about the skill of the sculptors in Granada and of the culture of their patrons. Several of the interior spaces lead off the central Renaissance patio, most of them covered with *alfarjes* decorated with geometric forms, which in some places echo Renaissance coffered work. The most outstanding ceiling is the one over the staircase; here we find a magnificent rectangular *armadura* of five sections, with *limas Moamares*. The whole ceiling is covered with interlocking strapwork of ten-strand knots with the *almizate* decorated with three pinecone-shaped *muqarnas*. The outlines are marked in white, red and black and the centre of the stars are gilded. A highly stylised plant motif completes the decoration.

es.name: Casa de Castril – Museo Arqueológico y Etnológico Provincial
names: Casa de Castril - Museo Arqueológico y Etnológico Provincial
description: Propiedad de la familia de don Hernando de Zafra, secretario de los Reyes Católicos, posiblemente fue construida por su nieto a partir de 1539. La fachada, tallada en piedra, constituye un amplio discurso acerca de las posibilidades del lenguaje renacentista llegado de Italia. Allí se mezclan, en una especie de álbum, motivos de *grutescos*, “candelieri”, heráldicas y formas simbólicas que nos hablan de la capacidad de los escultores granadinos y de la cultura de los mecenas de la obra. En el interior un patio renacentista sirve de distribuidor de espacios, la mayor parte cubiertos con *alfarjes* decorados con formas geométricas que en ocasiones se aproximan a los *artesonados* renacentistas. Lo más destacable del interior es la techumbre de la escalera. En ella encontramos una magnífica *armadura* rectangular de cinco paños con *limas moamares*. El conjunto está totalmente apeinazado con lazo de diez, con el *almizate* decorado con tres piñas de *mocárabe*. Los perfiles se marcan en blanco, rojo y negro, y el centro de las estrellas está dorado. Se completa con ornato vegetal muy estilizado.

en.name: *The Empress' boulevard*
short_description: Painted in 1865, this canvas was one of many the artist created depicting "the new boulevard of Algiers". This boulevard, built by the opera house where Saint-Saëns was performing at the time, was the architect Frédéric Chassériau's (the painter's uncle) first significant work. It was inaugurated in 1839 by Napoléon III and the Empress Eugénie, after whom it it was named, and marked the beginning of Algiers' new, European-style urbanisation programme, which affected both the city and its surroundings. Although these changes did bring the city's inhabitants a number of comforts, they also resulted in the irrevocable destruction of a number of very important monuments from the Ottoman era.

fr.name: *Le boulevard de l'Impératrice*
short_description: L’artiste peignit à plusieurs reprises « le nouveau boulevard d’Alger », notamment en 1865. Ce boulevard, érigé tout près de l’opéra où le musicien Saint-Saëns se produisit, est la première grande réalisation de l’architecte Frédéric Chassériau, l’oncle du peintre ; inauguré par Napoléon III et l’impératrice Eugénie dont il porta le nom, il annonce le nouveau programme urbanistique à l’européenne qui s’inscrit intramuros et extramuros à partir de 1839, un programme qui tout en apportant des commodités techniques évidentes n’en effaçait pas moins irrémédiablement de très nombreux monuments de l’ancien Alger ottoman.
keywords: Orientalisme; cité traditionnelle; espace urbain traditionnel; cité colonielle

en.name: Cup with a curved stem
short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, and was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The Crystal cup with curved stem and appliqued aquamarine glass flowers and leaves dates from the second half of the 19th century. Baroque repertory inspired its form and use of floral decoration. A tendency toward abstract form is noticeable.

en.name: Tamentit
description: A thousand-year-old oasis on the road to Reggane, Tamentit (literally “beside the spring” in Berber) is a community and complex of *ksour* (groups of earthen houses). It is well-known for having been a very important and influential cultural, spiritual, literary and theological centre. Before Adrar became capital of the Touat region, Tamentit served as the centre of gravity in an area including both the Gourara to the north and Tidikelt to the east. It is a land that had long been a junction for trade caravans, a place for travellers, an essential thoroughfare and an asylum for refugees, as well as a centre of scholarship.

fr.name: Tamentit
description: Oasis millénaire implantée sur la route de Reggane, Tamentit (littéralement “à côté de la source” en berbère) est une concentration de *ksour* ayant connu un rayonnement culturel, spirituel, littéraire et théologique très important. Avant Adrar, aujourd’hui capitale du Touat, c’était Tamentit qui faisait office de centre de gravité de la région, incluant tout aussi bien le Gourara au nord que le Tidikelt à l’est, contrée qui a toujours été un carrefour caravanier, un lieu de transit, un passage obligé et une terre d’asile pour les réfugiés, tout autant qu’un centre d’érudition.

de.name: Kartuschenteppich
description: Neben dem Berliner Teppichfragment existiert ein weiteres, etwas größeres im Metropolitan Museum of Art New York. Beide Fragmente zählen zu den herausragendsten Beispielen frühsafawidischer Teppichkunst. Beide Fragmente zusammen lassen das Design eines Kartuschen-Teppichs deutlich erkennen. In versetzter Reihung wechseln sich hochrechteckige Kartuschen mit leicht ovalen Medaillons ab. Um den Größenunterschied beider Motive auszugleichen sind die Medaillons oben und unten mit schildförmigen Anhängern verziert. Beide Motive berühren sich in ihrer senkrechten und waagerechten Mittelachse. Die Flächen zwischen den zwei Hauptmotiven sind mit je zwei halbkreisförmigen Lanzettblättern gefüllt. Die Besonderheit des Teppichs liegt in der subtilen Zeichnung der Einzelmotive, seiner Farbvielfalt sowie der Farbkomposition. Jede Farbfläche wird durch eine anders farbige Kontur von der nächsten getrennt. Auch der Teppichgrund, der normalerweise einfarbig ist, wechselt hier in jedem Feld seine Farbe. Das Spiel mit 20 unterschiedlichen Farben und Farbtönen gelingt perfekt. Die Knüpftechnik und der sehr kurze Flor lassen die Farb- und Motivgestaltung, teilweise sind die Konturen nur einen Knoten breit, exakt hervortreten. Kartuschen-Teppiche sind häufig in der timuridischen Miniaturmalerei belegt, jedoch sind keine Teppiche aus dieser Zeit erhalten. Aufgrund der Verwendung vereinzelter Jufti-Knoten wird die Provinz Chorasan in Nordostiran als Herstellungsgegend vermutet.
holder: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum
materials: Baumwolle, Seide, Wolle; geknoteter Florteppich; asymmetrischer Knoten, Jufti-Knoten

en.name: Cartouche carpet
description: In addition to this Berlin carpet fragment, a second, somewhat larger one exists in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. Both fragments are considered among the most outstanding examples of early Safavid carpet art. The two fragments together allow the design of a cartouche carpet to be clearly recognized. In staggered rows, tall rectangular cartouches alternate with slightly oval medallions. To even out the size difference of the two motifs, the medallions are adorned at top and bottom with shield-shaped additions. The two motifs touch at their vertical and horizontal central axis. Each of the areas between the two main motifs is filled with two semicircular lancet leaves. The special character of the carpet lies in the subtle drawing of its individual motifs, its variety of colour and its colour composition. Each colour area is separated from the next by a differently coloured outline. The carpet ground, which is normally in one colour, also changes its colour in each field. The interplay of twenty different colours and colour shades succeeds perfectly. The knotting technique and the very short pile allow the colour and the motif design to emerge precisely – some of the outlines are only one knot wide. There is frequent evidence of cartouche carpets in Timurid miniature painting, but no carpets from this period have been preserved. Because of the use of individual Jufti knots the province of Khorasan is presumed to be the area of production.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Fragment; F.R. Martin, Metropolitain Museum; Jufti knot
materials: Cotton, silk, wool; knotted pile carpet; asymmetrical knot, Jufti knot
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: *An Elephant*; *An indian Ox*; *An Antelope*
short_description: In 1891 Filippo Palizzi donated more than 300 paintings to the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in order to describe his entire career through his artworks. All of them are cited in the Chronological List of 1853, which includes 12 studies depicting exotic animals done in The Jardin des Plantes in Paris. The series is considered the preparatory base for the amazing painting *Dopo il Diluvio. Uscita degli animali dall’Arca* (*After the Flood. The Animals Exiting the Ark*), commissioned by King Vittorio Emanuele II for the Museum of Capodimonte and presented in 1867 at the Universal Exposition in Paris. Other animals, like the Indian ox, the antelope and the dromedary were depicted in the Jardin des Plantes in Paris with the same aim.
keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist painting; Italian painters; exoticism; artistic exchanges; France; international exhibitions; universal exposition; travel; imaginary trips; travelling artist; natural sciences
partner: MIBACT | National Gallery of Modern Art (GNAM)

en.name: Basto del Diavolo (Urban Gate)
description:
The so-called "Basto del Diavolo" (Devil’s packsaddle), located at the intersection of Via Appia Antica and Via di Vallericcia, is probably the Roman Porta Urbica (Urban Gate) built in the Republican period and which provided access to the Forum of Aricia. It consists of an arch in *opus quadratum* with armilla (a second set of ashlars) incorporated on a wall on the sides. The Eastern face shows signs of the 19th century’s restorations. During the excavations of 1980, *basolato* (a type of Roman paving) of Via Appia Antica was found under the arch and later interred again.  
(Bibliography: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

it.name: Porta Urbica (Basto del Diavolo)
description:
Il cosiddetto “Basto del Diavolo”, collocato all’incrocio tra via Appia Antica e via di Vallericcia, probabilmente coincide con la Porta Urbica di accesso al Foro aricino. Presenta una struttura ad arco in opera quadrata con armilla a blocchi radiali disposti per taglio e per testa, di età repubblicana (II sec. a.C.), inquadrata da muratura di pietrame. Il fronte orientale mostra una facies riferibile ai restauri dell’800. Sotto l’arco è conservato il basolato della via Appia Antica, venuto alla luce negli scavi del 1980, oggi interrato.  
(Bibliografia: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

ar.name: وعاء
description:
تتزيّن هذه الأطباق والأوعية والمزهريات الخزفية بشريط كتابي بالخط الكوفي. وعلى عكس خصائص الفن الإسلامي الذي يتجنب الفراغ إلا أننا نجد الفراغ (أسطح غير مزخرفة )في هذه الأعمال الفنية، وهذا يُعتبر تقليد فني مناقض لخصاص زخرفة الفن الإسلامي .  
  
نشأ الخط الكوفي في مكة والمدينة (عام 625 ميلادي) كأحد أقدم أشكال الخط العربي في الإسلام، حيث تتمدّد الحروف في أشكال هندسية لتشبه بعضها البعض.

en.name: Bowl
description:
This clay bowl is decorated with *kufi* calligraphy on the inner neck edge. While in Islamic pottery, one may expect an abundance of floral or geometric patterns, *kufic* ceramics feature a band of letters creating a central void.  
  
*Kufi* script originates from Mecca and Medina (625 AD) as one of the earliest forms of calligraphy in Islam, with its letters stretching to resemble one another.  
  
This plate originates from Iran and embodies a two-fold function. At first sight, the abstract script appears as a decorative design. The second sight reveals a hidden message to decode. The inscription on this bowl would read: “Planning before work protects you from regret; prosperity and peace.”
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Kufic; Ceramic; Pottery
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

The Virgin Mary and John the Evangelist standing beside the cross, as well as Mary Magdalena kneeling at its foot, are shown in lamentation expressed through gestures of grief.

ar.name: قنديلا مسجد.
description:
قنديلا مسجد من الزجاج بجسم بصلي الشكل وحافة بارزة نحو الخارج، وهما مطعمان بالمينا ومذهبان. الجسم مزين بكتابة كبيرة الحجم، أما العنق فتطوقه حليات دائرية تتضمن شعاراً على شكل كأس، وهي تتناوب مع زخرفة كتابية. تذكر الكتابات حول الجسم أن القنديلين قد تم صنعهما لصالح سيف الدين شيخو العمري، وهو أحد أمراء السلطان الناصر حسن البارزين، وقد وصل إلى منصب كبير القواد في البلاط ثم أصبح أحد الأمراء الكبار قبل اغتياله عام 759/ 1357. تحوي الحليات الدائرية حول العنق والجزء الأسفل من الجسم شعاراً على شكل كأس هو رنك شيخو، ويدل على أنه كان حامل الكأس. العنق مزين بالسورة 24، الآية 35، والمعروفة بسورة النور "الله نور السماوات والأرض، مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري".  
كانت القناديل المملوكية، بزخارفها التي ابتعدت عن التصوير، واعتمدت على الكتابات القرآنية، مخصصة للمباني الدينية، ومن هنا يأتي اسم "قنديل المسجد"، إلا أن هذا لم يمنع من وجود قناديل من الشكل نفسه مخصصة للاستعمالات الدنيوية. يعتبر هذان القنديلان جزءاً من مجموعة من القناديل التي تم تصنيعها على الأرجح لصالح مسجد شيخو عام 750/ 1349، أو للخانقاه التي بناها بعد المسجد مباشرة عام 756/ 1355، والواقعة أسفل قلعة القاهرة.

زوج من المصابيح، مصنوعة من الزجاج المصقول والمطلي بالمينا، استُخدمت كمصابيح في مسجد. زيَّنت أجسام المصابيح ميداليات، يظهر فيها رمز كأس، وهي رمز يعود إلى سيف الدين شيخو العمري، الذي كان ساقياً للسلطان الناصر محمد.
dates: منتصف القرن الثامن/ منتصف القرن الرابع عشر.
keywords: رنك؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ شعار؛ قطعة ذات استعمال ديني.

en.name: Two mosque lamps.
description:
Two glass mosque lamps with globular body and flared neck, decorated with enamel and gilt. Around the body is a bold inscription, while roundels exhibiting a cup emblem alternating with calligraphy surround the neck. The inscriptions around the body of both these lamps state that they were made for Sayf al-Din Shaykhu al-‘Umari, a prominent amir for Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad. Shaykhu achieved the status of commander-in-chief of the palace and then Great Amir before being assassinated in AH 759 / AD 1357. The roundels around the neck and the underside of body contain a cup motif, the blazon of Shaykhu, indicating that he held the post of cup-bearer. The neck is inscribed with the Qur’anic verse 24:35, known as the ‘Light’ verse: ‘God is the Light of heavens and the earth; the likeness of His Light is a niche, wherein is a light, the light in a glass, the glass as it were a glittering star’.  
Mamluk lamps with their non-figurative decoration, and inscriptions of Qur’anic verses, were mostly intended for religious buildings, hence the term ‘mosque lamp’. However, there are some lamps of the same shape from this period that would have been used in a secular setting. These lamps are part of a group of extant lamps probably made for the mosque Shaykhu commissioned in AH 750/ AD 1349, or for the sufi hostel (*khanqa*) he had built soon after in AH 756/ AD 1355, situated at the foot of the Citadel in Cairo.

A pair of glass mosque lamps decorated with enamel and gilt. Around the body are medallions containing the cup emblem, the heraldic symbol belonging to the patron Sayf al-Din Shaykhu al-‘Umari, who was cup-bearer for Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.
dates: Hegira mid-7th century/ AD mid-14th century.
keywords: Calligraphy; blazons; emblems; religious object; Mosque interior decoration; coat of arms

es.name: Dos lámparas de mezquita
description:
Dos lámparas de mezquita de cuerpo globular y cuello ensanchado, decoradas con esmalte y dorado. Rodea el cuerpo una inscripción en gruesos caracteres, mientras que en el cuello alternan la caligrafía y medallones con una copa heráldica en su interior. Las inscripciones alrededor del cuerpo de ambas lámparas informan de que fueron hechas para Sayf al-Din Shayju al-Umari, importante emir del sultán al-Nasir Muhammad. En 759 / 1357, poco después de que Shayju alcanzase el rango de comandante en jefe del palacio y, más tarde, gran emir antes de ser asesinado. Los medallones del cuello y la parte inferior del cuerpo presentan un motivo en forma de copa; se trata del blasón de Shayj e indica que era el copero. En el cuello se lee la azora 35, o "de la Luz", de la sura 24 del Corán: “Dios es la luz de los cielos y la tierra, su luz es comparable a una hornacina donde hay una luz encendida, la luz está en un recipiente de vidrio, como si fuera una estrella titilante”.  
Las lámparas del periodo mameluco con versos coránicos inscritos y sin decoración figurativa se fabricaban principalmente para edificios religiosos, de ahí que se conozcan como “lámparas de mezquita”, aunque algunas con esta misma forma tenían un uso secular. Estas dos lámparas forman parte de un grupo hecho para la mezquita que Shayju mandó construir en el año 750 / 1349 o para el albergue sufí (*janqa*) que levantó poco después, en 756 / 1355, a los pies de la ciudadela de El Cairo.
dates: Mediados del siglo VII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.
keywords: caligrafía; blasones; emblemas; objetos religiosos

fr.name: Deux lampes de mosquée.
description:
Deux lampes de mosquée en verre à corps globuleux et col évasé, décorées d'émail et de dorure. Une inscription en caractères épais court tout autour de la panse, tandis que sur le col des rosettes à emblème de coupe alternent avec une calligraphie. Les inscriptions de ces deux lampes précisent qu'elles ont été fabriquées pour Sayf al-Din Cheikhu al-Umari, éminent émir auprès du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad. Il accéda à la fonction de commandant en chef du palais puis de Grand Émir avant d'être assassiné en 759 H / 1357 J.-C. Les rondeaux autour du col et sous la panse contiennent un motif de coupe, blason de Cheikhu qui occupait la fonction d'échanson. Le col porte la sourate XXIV, 35 du Coran, connue sous le nom de verset de la “Lumière” : “Dieu est la lumière des cieux et de la terre. Cette lumière ressemble à un flambeau, à un flambeau placé dans un cristal…” (trad. Kasimirski).  
Les lampes mameloukes à décor non figuratif et inscriptions de versets du Coran étaient la plupart du temps destinées à des bâtiments religieux, d'où leur nom de “lampes de mosquée”. Cependant, certaines lampes de la même forme datant de cette période ont pu servir à un usage séculier. Elles font partie d'un groupe de lampes subsistantes sans doute fabriquées pour la mosquée édifiée par Cheikhu en 750 H / 1349 J.-C., ou pour la résidence de soufis (*khanqa*) qu'il fit construire en 756 H / 1355 J.-C. au pied de la citadelle du Caire.

Paire de lampes de mosquée à décor émaillé et doré. Autour du corps se trouvent des médaillons contenant l'emblème de la tasse, le symbole héraldique appartenant au commanditaire Sayf al-Din Cheykhu al-Umari, qui était échanson du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.
dates: Milieu VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (milieu XIVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Calligraphie ; blasons ; emblèmes ; objets religieux

en.name: *Visitation*
description:
After studying locally in Langenargen, Maulbertsch went to Vienna where he was a pupil of Peter van Roy at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and where, in 1750, he won first prize in the academic painting competition. In 1758, he became an ordinary member of the Academy and was later a counsellor. Although both his home and workshop were in Vienna, his activities covered the entire Habsburg empire extending beyond its boundaries. Primarily a fresco painter, he was constantly overburdened with commissions from churches and secular patrons. His oeuvre includes several altarpieces, sketches and panel paintings, historical-mythological pictures, genre paintings and portraits, but also graphic works and etchings. In the course of his rich career, he traced a great arch of development from Late Baroque through Rococo to Neo-Classicism. He died in Vienna on 8 August 1796, while preparing his last great work, the fresco for Szombathely Cathedral.  
János Szily, the Bishop of the newly founded Szombathely diocese, commissioned Maulbertsch to decorate the salon of his personal residence in 1782. Almost 10 years later in 1791, he turned to Maulbertsch again for the altarpieces of Szombathely Cathedral. For the high altar, the Bishop ordered a picture representing the Visitation of Mary by Elizabeth, on the side altars the patron saints of Szombathely, St. Martin and St. Quirinus. In accordance with the pictorial practice at the time, the painter made some sketches which reflected his employer's requests and concepts, and sent them to Szombathely for approval. Some of these sketches have survived. The composition of the Pannonhalma sketch shows differences from the final version. On the altarpiece – executed in 1792 and gravely damaged during the World War II – Mary stands on the left, while in this sketch she stands on the right at the top of a stairway. Maulbertsch mentioned this modification in a letter he wrote to Bishop Szily in April 1792.

Maulbertsch's later works clearly show the influence of Neo-Classicism, as seen here and in several other of the painter's major works in Hungary (for example in Vác, Győr, Pozsony (Bratislava), Pápa, Eger and Szombathely). This sketch is a version of the recently restored, large-size, Szombathely High Altar painting, which was torn to pieces at the end of the Second World War.
place: Commissioned by János Szily, Bishop of Szombathely
keywords: Visitation; Rococo; Neo-Classicism; altarpiece; religious object; religious orders; Benedictine; Anton Franz Maulbertsch; Bishop János Szily; St. Martin; St. Quirinus; St. Elisabeth; Szombathely; Pannonhalma; Christian themes

de.name: Inneres
description: Die an sich schlichte Folge von Langhaussaal und Chorrechteck wird durch Abschrägungen der Ecken akzentuiert und belebt. Die kräftige Arkade über Wandpfeilern, die Langhaus und Chor trennt rahmt perspektivisch den pompösen Hochaltar. Die im Verhältnis zur Wölbungsfläche recht kleinen Fresken ergeben noch keinen „Heiligenhimmel“, sondern bleiben auf abgegrenzte Bereiche beschränkt. Die übrigen Flächen wurden weder durch Fresken noch Stuck gefüllt. Während im Chor die Heilige Familie dargestellt ist, zeigen die Bilder im Langhaus Szenen nach der Auferstehung Jesu, im Rang durch polychrome und monochrome Malweise unterschieden.

en.name: Interior
description: The simple sequence of the nave and choir rectangle is accentuated and given life by slanted corners. The powerfully built arcade-above-pilaster piers between nave and choir provide a perspectival frame for the ostentatious high altar. The extremely small frescos do not form a “heaven of the saints” being restricted to delimited areas. The remaining surfaces are neither filled with frescos or stucco. While the Holy Family is depicted in the choir the pictures in the nave feature scenes of the Resurrection of Jesus, distinguished in rank by the monochrome and polychrome execution.
place: View towards the choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

en.name: Church of Santa Catalina
description:
This church must have been built in the second half of the 14th century on the site of an older mosque, since the base of the present tower corresponds to an Islamic building that can be dated between the 9th and 10th centuries. It is a work of cut stone in alternating headers and stretchers, square on the outside and inside, and a spiral staircase around a central cylindrical core. It follows, therefore, the design of the *alminares* of Seville from the Emirate’s period.  
The new Mudéjar church followed the usual scheme of these buildings: three naves separated by four pillars, which are cruciform in section, and a deep sanctuary of three bays. The sanctuary has ribbed vaulting, while the roof of the central nave is formed of wooden structures of *armadura de par y nudillo*, with the side aisles covered by a single pitched structure. The armadura enriches its *almizate* in a decoration of knotwork and pendentives of *muqarnas*.  
The church has three doors: the main door is at the foot of the church and is made of brick with interlaced multifoil arches framed in *alfiz*. This design is exceptional in the Mudéjar churches in Seville, since it clearly derives from Almohad designs, which other contemporary churches in the Aljarafe area follow. A similar design was likely to have been used for the doorway in the north front as well, judging by the elements that can still be seen around what today is a doorway with a lintel. The doorway in the south aisle is a simple pointed brick arch.  
Nowadays, of these three original doors, only the last mentioned is visible from the outside, since the others have been hidden by other additions through time; the main door was hidden by a new gable wall where, in 1930, a doorway from the disentailed Church of Santa Lucia was inserted. This new façade also concealed some blind openings made of brick with multifoil arches framed in *alfiz*, which today are only visible from the choir loft. The door that was added is of cut stone, with both its design and the sculptural motifs so similar to those on the door of the church of Santa Marina that it can be presumed that it was made by the same craftsmen. A number of small stone statues are placed under canopies on either side, and above the keystone is the figure of the Eternal Father. The doorway is finished with corbels of roll-shaped modillions with a central band.  
The Mudéjar work of the tower is erected on top of the remains of the original *laminar*. From the outside, it has blind multifoil arches framed in *alfiz*, and sunken panels that must have been decorated with *sebka* motifs, which partially disappeared during the restoration carried out in 1881. The belfry has a horseshoeshaped opening on each side, framed in *alfiz*, and crowned with a crenellated parapet.  
Similar to the multifoil arches of the tower are those which exist on the façade and which, in the form of semicircular apses, correspond to an addition adjoining the north wall. Only the first of these belongs to the original building, the second is from the early part of the 20th century. An important Mudéjar element in this church is the chapel, added in around 1400 to the south wall, which is in use at present by the Society of the Hermandad de la Exaltación. This is a structure, which, following the model of the Muslim *qubba* is square with a vault on *trompas*, decorated with strapwork and incrusted with pieces of vitrified ceramic.

es.name: Iglesia de Santa Catalina
description:
Este templo debió de levantarse en la segunda mitad del siglo XIV en el solar de una antigua mezquita, pues el arranque de la torre actual corresponde a una obra islámica fechable entre los siglos IX y X. Se trata de una fábrica de sillares dispuestos a soga y tizón, con planta cuadrada al exterior, mientras en el interior se desarrolla una escalera de caracol alrededor de un machón cilíndrico. Responde, pues, al esquema de los llamados *alminares* sevillanos de tiempos del emirato.  
El nuevo templo mudéjar siguió el esquema habitual en tales construcciones: tres naves separadas por cuatro pilares de sección cruciforme y una profunda cabecera constituida por dos tramos. Esta se cubre con bóvedas nervadas, mientras las naves lo hacen con estructuras de madera, en forma de *armadura de par y nudillo* en la central, y en colgadizo en las laterales. Dicha *armadura* enriquece su *almizate* con decoración de lazo y con piñas de *mocárabe*.  
El templo cuenta con tres ingresos. El principal se sitúa a los pies, está fabricado en ladrillos y se organiza por arcos polilobulados entrelazados y enmarcados por *alfiz*. Tal solución es excepcional en los templos mudéjares sevillanos, pues deriva de esquemas claramente almohades, que también siguen otros templos coetáneos de la comarca del Aljarafe. Un esquema similar debió ofrecer la portada abierta en el muro septentrional, a juzgar por los elementos aún visibles en torno al hueco adintelado hoy existente. La portada correspondiente a la nave meridional está constituida por un sencillo arco apuntado, fabricado en ladrillo.  
Actualmente, de estos tres primitivos ingresos, solo el último de los comentados resulta visible desde el exterior, pues los anteriores quedan ocultos tras unas fábricas que se han ido adosando con el transcurso del tiempo. El principal quedó oculto al anteponérsele un nuevo hastial, donde se colocó en 1930 la portada procedente de la desamortizada iglesia de Santa Lucía. Esta nueva fachada ocultó, además, unos vanos fingidos fabricados en ladrillo y constituidos por arcos polilobulados enmarcados por alfiz, hoy solo visibles desde la tribuna del coro. La portada añadida es de cantería, y tanto su esquema compositivo como sus motivos escultóricos ofrecen tan estrecha relación con los correspondientes a la portada de la iglesia de Santa Marina que se han llegado a considerar obra del mismo taller. Unas pequeñas imágenes de piedra se disponen bajo doseletes a ambos lados, y sobre la clave se sitúa la figura del Padre Eterno. Rematan la portada canes en forma de modillones de rollo con banda central.  
La fábrica mudéjar de la torre se asentó sobre los restos del primitivo *alminar*. Exteriormente presenta arcos ciegos polilobulados inscritos en *alfiz* y unos paños rehundidos que originalmente debieron ocupar motivos de *sebka*, en parte desaparecidos durante la restauración llevada a cabo en 1881. El campanario ofrece en cada frente un hueco túmido enmarcado por *alfiz* y está coronado por un andén con merlones de gradas.  
Similares a los arcos polilobulados de la torre son los existentes en la fachada que, con forma de ábsides semicirculares, corresponden a una dependencia adosada al muro septentrional. Sólo el primero de los dos pertenece a la fábrica primitiva; el segundo es de comienzos del siglo XX. Un elemento mudéjar importante en esta iglesia es la capilla adosada hacia 1400 al muro meridional y que actualmente ocupa la Hermandad de la Exaltación. Se trata de una estructura que, según el modelo de la *qubba* musulmana, presenta planta cuadrada y bóveda sobre *trompas*, y está decorada con motivos de lacería, en los que se incrustan piezas de cerámica vidriada.

ar.name: بورتريه منمنمة للحاكم القاجاري فتح علي شاه
description: البورتريه المنمنمة لفتح علي شاه وقعت من قبل باقر وهو رسام يستخدم المينا متعدد الأغراض والذي أنتج أعمالا عالية الجودة للسلالة الحاكمة القاجارية وقد وقّع البورتريه المنمنمة كعبد ولد في بيت باقر والذي أكد على دوره كحرفي المشغل الملكي. وفي هذه المنمنمة يصور فتح علي شاه كشاب نسبيا ذو لحية  قصيرة وحاجبان متصلان. ويرتدي ملابس غنية ويضع العديد من العقود والأساور وقبعة أستراخان طويلة مزينة بحلية والتي ربما كانت غنيمة من الكنور المغولية في دلهي. وإلى يسار البورتريه يوجد عنصر تزيين بشكل دمعة الذي يحمل النقش :"" فتح علي شاه قاجار"".

en.name: Portrait miniature of the Qajar ruler, Fath ‘Ali Shah
description: This miniature portrait of Fath ‘Ali Shah was signed by Baqir, a versatile enamel painter, who produced high-quality work for the Qajar dynasty. He signed the miniature portrait as ‘the slave born in the household Baqir’, which stressed his role as a craftsman in the royal workshop. In this miniature Fath ‘Ali Shah is portrayed as a relatively young man, with a short beard and continuous eyebrows. He is richly dressed and wears several necklaces, armbands and a tall astrakhan hat decorated with an aigrette, possibly booty from the Mughal treasury in Delhi. To the left of the portrait there is a teardrop-shaped cartouche, which bears the inscription: ‘Fath ‘Ali Shah Qajar’.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
keywords: miniature; gold; enamel; Iran; Qajar; crown; portrait
materials: Gold sheet, painted with opaque and translucent enamels
tags: Gold sheet, painted with opaque and translucent enamels

en.name: Bottle
description: On its a globular body, this bottle features a honeycomb pattern that was common to glass vessels produced in the Near East throughout late antiquity and the Islamic period until the end of the 13th century. Numerous examples of patterned bottles can be found in all major collections of Islamic glass. They can be distinguished by the details of their pattern, their necks, and their applied parts as well as by their measurements and the glass colours used. The deep blue colour of this bottle is quite unique, as surviving bottles of this type are most often colourless, light green, or yellow.
materials: Glass, transparent deep blue; pattern moulded, blown in the half-post technique, applied thread decoration, tooled, worked on the pontil
tags: pattern moulded, blown in the half-post technique, applied thread decoration, tooled, worked on the pontil

en.name: İsa Bey Hammam
description:
It is not known for certain whether or not this building, to the southwest of İsa Bey’s Mosque, belonged to İsa Bey. Today there is no building inscription, but it is thought that an inscribed slab found in the garden of a nearby house and moved to Selçuk-Efes Museum might belong to this building. The inscription describes a *hammam* commissioned by Hoca Ali during the rule of İsa Bey in October-November 1364. Because of this, some researchers suggest that this hammam was not commissioned by İsa Bey. We do not have much information about the name Hoca Ali that is mentioned in the inscription; probably an important person of İsa Bey’s period, Hoca Ali’s gravestone dated 1378 is located in the courtyard of İsa Bey Mosque.  
Its environs and interior have been cleaned with the excavation work in the recent years. The building has a plan layout common to the 14th and 15th centuries. Adjoining the *hammam* on the east are the remains of a row of chambers, which are supposedly shops with no organic connection to the *hammam*, although examples of shops adjoining the sides of some Turkish *hammam*s are known. On the south is a low arch opening into the *külhan* under the water depot.  
The chambers adjoining the western facade, however, must be later additions. In some Turkish *hammam*s there are special sections called “keçelik” that were constructed for the manufacture of felt. It is thought that of the sections added later, the one on the north might be a “keçelik”.  
The walls of the *soyunmalık* on the northern side are preserved only at ground level. With two of the four columns still standing, the *soyunmalık* has traces of a star-shaped fountain in the centre of the marble floor. Apart from the *soyunmalık*, the rest of the *hammam* is quite well preserved. The visitor passes from the *soyunmalık* to the corridor, *ılıklık*, and *sıcaklık* respectively. The *sıcaklık* consists of four *iwan*s forming a cross with a dome in the centre and four *halvet*s in the corners, each covered by a dome. Light coming through the wells in the domes, now without the glass jars, though, creates an exotic play of light and shadow inside. The water depot adjoins the southern wall of the *sıcaklık*. As seen in most *hammam*s, there is a small window on the wall between the *sıcaklık* and the water tank for the purpose of cleaning and maintenance.

es.name: Hammam de İsa Bey
description:
No se sabe de cierto si el edificio situado al sureste de la mezquita de İsa Bey perteneció a este *bey*, puesto que no hay ninguna inscripción. Se cree, sin embargo, que una losa grabada que se halló en el jardín de una casa cercana y conservada ahora en el Museo de Selçuk-Éfeso pudo estar en el edificio. En ella se menciona un *hammam* que hizo construir Hoca Ali durante el mandato de İsa Bey, en octubre-noviembre de 1364. Algunos estudiosos, a la luz de esta inscripción, sostienen que la construcción no se debió a İsa Bey. No sabemos gran cosa del Hoca Ali citado; seguramente figura de relieve en la época de İsa Bey, su lápida, fechada en 1378, se encuentra en el patio de la mezquita de İsa Bey.  
Las excavaciones de los últimos años han despejado los alrededores y el interior del *hammam*. El edificio sigue un modelo de planta usual en los siglos XIV y XV; en el lado oriental, contiguas al baño, están las ruinas de una fila de espacios que, se supone, fueron tiendas no pertenecientes al cuerpo del baño; hay ejemplos, de hecho, de tiendas añadidas a los laterales de algunos *hammam*s. En el lado sur está el arco bajo que da al *külhan* bajo el depósito de agua. Las habitaciones del lado oeste parecen también haber sido añadidas más tarde. En el de la parte norte, podríamos identificar un antiguo *keçelik*, ya que se han encontrado estas dependencias reservadas a la fabricación de fieltro en varias *madrasa*s.  
Las paredes del *soyunmalık*, en el lado norte, solo se conservan hasta la altura de una planta baja. En esta sala, de la que permanecen en pie dos de sus cuatro columnas, hay restos de una fuente en forma de estrella que estaba en el centro del suelo de mármol. El resto del baño está muy bien conservado. Desde el *soyunmalık* se pasa a un pasillo, al *ılıklık* y al *sıcaklık*. El *sıcaklık* está formado por cuatro *iwan*s en cruz con una cúpula en el centro y cuatro *halvet*s en los rincones, todos con cúpula. La luz que entra por las claraboyas de las cúpulas, actualmente sin vidrios, crea un exótico juego de luces y sombras en el interior. El depósito de agua está pegado a la pared sur del *sıcaklık*. Como en la mayoría de los *hammam*s, hay una ventanita en la pared del *sıcaklık* para poder hacer la limpieza y el mantenimiento del depósito.

ar.name: رسم تشكيلي لفيل عليه راكب وعروس
description: أصول الفن التشكيلي للحيوانات يمكن أن يعود لأوائل المخطوطات البوذية في آسيا الوسطى ولاحقا كانت تدخل للرسوم الفارسية وبعد ذلك أصبحت  متشربة في الجوهر الفني لشمال ووسط الهند في القرن السادس عشر ومثل هذه الصور تبين بشكل بارز البشر والحيوانات الحقيقية والغريبة (ديفز) (شياطين ) أو ملائكة مجتمعة  في فسيفساء متداخلة ومع ذلك لحيوانات واضحة مثل الخيول ،الإبل والثيران. وفي الموروث الهندي  مثل هذا التشكيل يمكن أن يكون قد مثّل مبدأ غامضا لمقولة الوحدة الداخلية لكل الكائنات . والتفسيرات الأخرى تقول بسيادة السماوات على العالم الطبيعي ويعكس سلطة الملك على مملكته وشعبه.

en.name: A composite elephant with rider and groom
description: The origins of composite animals may date back to early Buddhist manuscripts of Central Asia. Later, they were introduced into Persian painting and subsequently became infused with the artistic essence of Northern and Central India in the sixteenth century. Such images prominently depict humans, real and whimsical animals, *divs* (demons) or angels, combined into mosaics of intertwined yet recognized animals such as horses, camels, and oxen. In Hindu tradition, such compositions may have represented the mystical doctrine of the internal unity of all beings. Other interpretations suggest the sovereignty of the heavens over the natural world, mirroring the power of a king over his realm and its people.

en.name: Paço dos Duques de Bragança
description:
The Old Palace is set on the right bank of the River Cávado and, as can be seen by its 16th-century iconography, it defended the old bridge. In 1510, it was set into the walls and was the last redoubt. Most of the work on the residence was carried out by order of D. Fernando, the 9th Count of Barcelos and Marquis of Vila Viçosa, as well as his son, also called Fernando, who later plotted against D. João II and was killed as a result of this in 1483.  
Works were continually being carried out, as can be seen by the letter from the Duke of Bragança; D. Jaime, to the Archbishop of Braga in 1530 indicating that the count wanted to enlarge his residence.  
All that remains today is the artificial platform and the central part of the building with cross-beam windows, serving as clear proof that work was still being carried out some time between 1530 and 1540.  
Various archaeological pieces have been placed around the building and nearby there is the Manueline pillory with its head in the form of a cage.

ar.name: مصحف مخطوط للقرآن الكريم
description: تتميز هذه المخطوطة القرآنية التي كتبها محمد شكري، بصفحة مزدوجة مُذهبة ذات زخرفة بديعة. وباقي النص مكتوب بخط النسخ الأسود مع وجود تفاصيل باللون الأحمر وعلامات الآيات باللون الذهبي. وتتألف كل صفحة من 15 سطرًا. كما كُتبت عناوين السور باللون الأبيض على خلفية ذهبية مزخرفة. وحُددت الصفحات بأُطُر ذهبية ذات زخارف هندسية.

en.name: Holy Qur’an manuscript
description: This Qur’an manuscript, written by Muhammad Shukri, has a richly ornamented and gilt, opening double page. The remaining text is in black *naskhi* script, with red detailing and golden verse markers, 15 lines to each page. Chapter headings are written in white on a gilt and decorated ground. They are enclosed in golden frames with geometric decoration.
keywords: Muhammed Shukri; Naskhi; Ottoman religious manuscripts; Ottoman calligraphy; religious manuscript

en.name: Entrance to the Citadel
description:
Although the entrance arch is nowadays more or less semicircular in shape, this gate previously had a surmounted or horseshoe arch, which was destroyed in 1887. Fortunately, there remained a stereotype of the original entrance made by a Polish citizen who had visited Elvas earlier. Apparently, it was an arch without any frame or *alfiz*.  
This set of circumstances suggests that there was an entrance system which, in chronological terms, may correspond to the periods of the emirs and *caliph*s (3rd/9th - 4th/10th centuries).

es.name: Arco do Miradeiro o Porta da Alcáçova
description:
La llamada Porta da Alcáçova (Puerta de la *Alcazaba*) o Arco do Miradeiro (Arco del Mirador) se compone de una puerta de entrada recta, flanqueada por dos torres cuadrangulares y macizas. En su construcción se usaron grandes sillares graníticos, provenientes probablemente de una construcción de época romana o tardorromana. Aunque actualmente el arco de la entrada sea un semicírculo más o menos perfecto, esta puerta tenía un arco de herradura, destruido en 1887. De esa entrada original se conserva, afortunadamente, un negativo fotográfico hecho por un ciudadano polaco que había visitado Elvas. Aparentemente, se trata de un arco sin marco o alfiz.  
Este conjunto de indicios apunta a un sistema de entrada que, en términos cronológicos, puede corresponder a los periodos emiral y califal (siglos III/IX-IV/X).
