ar.name: عنصر معماري مأخوذ من حمام.
description: القطعة عبارة عن عنصر معماري من الجص يمثل جزءاً من حمام، ويتكون من كوّة ذات عقد مدبب تحمل موضوعاً تصويرياً رسم بألوان مائية سوداء وحمراء على أرضية بيضاء ونفذ بالأسلوب المعروف باسم "الفريسكو." ويمثل الرسم شاباً - قد يكون أميراً - جالساً يمسك بيده كأساً، ويرتدي جلباباً تزينه حليات من زخرفة نباتية حمراء اللون، وحول عضديه شريطان، وعلى رأسه عمامة ذات طيات. ويظهر حول رأس هذا الشاب هالة كاملة الاستدارة ربما قصد بها الدلالة على أهميته. ويضع الشاب حول ظهره وشاحاً يخرج طرفاه من تحت إبطيه وينثنيان إلى أسفل معلقين في الهواء. ويتدلى من رأس الشاب خصلتان من الشعر إحداهما في الخلف والأخرى في الأمام. ويؤطر الكوة إطار على شكل عقد من حبات مستديرة. ويشبه هذا الرسم الجداري الرسومات التي وجدت في سامراء بالعراق، وذلك من حيث الأشكال والزخارف المتكررة وأشكال الرؤوس والهالة المستديرة والإطار على شكل عقد، وأيضاً من حيث الأسلوب البعيد عن الواقعية والميل إلى الطابع الزخرفي والتأثر بالتقاليد الفارسية. والصور المائية الفاطمية المرسومة على الجص لا تختلف في الشكل والأسلوب والموضوع عن الصور المنفذة على الخزف بالبريق المعدني التي تنسب إلى ذلك العصر. ويمكن دراسة الموضوع التصويري في هذا العنصر المعماري بالمقارنة بأمثلة شبيهة من العصر الفاطمي منفذة على الخزف وعلى بعض القطع الخشبية وعلى الكثير من المنسوجات. كما يمكن اعتبار استخدام الصور كعنصر زخرفي من مميزات التحف الفنية التطبيقية في العصر الفاطمي (أنظر ET 70 ).
كانت الحمامات من الأبنية المهمة في العالم الإسلامي، وذلك نظراً لأهميتها في التطهُّر والنظافة. وقد شاع استخدام التصوير في زخرفة الحمّامات، ومنها هذه الصورة المائية على الجصّ.
keywords: جص؛ حمام؛ زخرفة آدمية؛ صور آدمية؛ عنصر معماري؛ فريسكو.

en.name: Frescoed architectural fragment from a bathhouse.
description:
A frescoed architectural fragment that once formed part of a bathhouse, consisting of a niche with a pointed arch. The imagery within the niche portrays a figure, executed in black and red watercolours against a white background, executed in the fresco technique. The subject is a seated youth – who might have been a prince – and who holds a cup in his hand. He is wearing a loose robe-like garment, which is decorated with red vegetal motifs. His upper arms are encircled by two bands, and his head is covered by a pleated turban. A complete circular halo appears around the youth's head, perhaps to emphasise his status. He wears a scarf placed around his back, the two ends emerging from under his armpits and then left hanging down, suspended in mid-air. Two parts of the youth's hair can be seen beneath the turban, one in the front and the other at the back.  
The niche is framed by an arch composed of bead-like roundels. The fresco itself resembles paintings found in Samarra, Iraq in terms of both the figures; the shape of the heads and the circular halo, for instance, as well as in the repetitive decorative motifs; the frame in the form of an arch, for example. In addition the implementation of style is far from realistic, and leans more towards the decorative, with clear Persian influences. The Fatimid frescoes are not too different in form, style, or thematic content from depictions executed on metallic lustre ceramics, which were being produced in Egypt during this period. It is possible to study the pictorial representation on this architectural fragment by comparing it to similar Fatimid-period examples executed on various media: ceramics, some wooden pieces and on many textiles. Furthermore it is interesting to consider the role of painting itself as a distinctive decorative component of the applied arts during the Fatimid period.
Baths were buildings of importance in the Islamic world due to their role in purification and hygiene. The walls of bathhouses were commonly decorated with frescoes, like the example we see here.
keywords: Stucco; bathhouse; figurative representation; fresco
materials: Fresco: stucco-painted with watercolour in red and black.
tags: Fresco: stucco-painted with watercolour in red and black.

es.name: Fragmento de fresco de unos baños.
description:
Fragmento de fresco procedente de unos baños realizado en un nicho de arco apuntado. En él, con la técnica del fresco, se ha pintado una figura con acuarelas negra y roja sobre fondo blanco. Se trata de un joven sentado, que podría ser un príncipe, con una copa en la mano. Se cubre con un turbante y va vestido con una prenda amplia parecida a una túnica y ornada con motivos vegetales en color rojo; en la parte superior de los brazos se ven unas bandas. Alrededor de la cabeza aparece también una aureola circular, tal vez para destacar su estatus. Lleva un largo pañuelo que le rodea la espalda y cuyos extremos sobresalen de las axilas y quedan suspendidos en el aire. El turbante deja asomar el cabello del joven sobre la frente y en la nuca.  
El nicho se ha delineado con un arco decorado con círculos como cuentas de collar. El fresco recuerda a las pinturas encontradas en Samarra (Irak), tanto por la figura, la forma de la cabeza y la aureola como por los motivos decorativos repetidos y el arco que sirve de marco. Además, el estilo no es en absoluto realista, sigue ciertas convenciones y denota claras influencias persas.  
Los frescos fatimíes no se diferencian mucho en forma, estilo o temas de las representaciones que aparecen en las cerámicas de reflejo metálico que se fabricaron en Egipto durante este periodo. Para estudiar la representación pictórica de este fragmento, puede compararse con ejemplos similares del periodo fatimí efectuados sobre otros materiales, como cerámica, madera y telas. Además, es importante destacar el papel de la pintura como un elemento característico de las artes decorativas durante el periodo fatimí.

Los baños públicos tenían una gran importancia en el mundo islámico por las exigencias de purificación e higiene. Las paredes de los baños solían decorarse con pinturas al fresco como la de este fragmento arquitectónico.
dates: Siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.
keywords: Estuco; baños públicos; representación figurativa; elemento arquitectónico; fresco.
materials: Acuarelas roja y negra sobre estuco.
tags: Acuarelas roja y negra sobre estuco.

fr.name: Fragment de fresque de hammam.
description:
Fragment architectural en forme de niche à arc brisé peinte, qui faisait jadis partie d'un hammam. Il est décoré d'une figure exécutée à l'aquarelle rouge et noire sur fond blanc selon la technique de la fresque. Elle représente un jeune homme assis – peut-être un prince – qui tient une coupe dans sa main droite. Il est revêtu d'une grande robe à motifs végétaux de couleur rouge. Deux cercles entourent la partie supérieure de ses bras. Il est coiffé d'un turban plissé d'où dépassent des cheveux à l'avant et sur la nuque. Une auréole encercle sa tête, peut-être pour signaler son rang. Une écharpe aux extrémités flottantes est passée sous ses aisselles.  
La niche est encadrée par un arc composé de petits cercles évoquant des perles. La fresque rappelle des peintures découvertes à Samarra (Irak) tant pour le personnage que la forme de la tête, l'auréole, la répétition de motifs décoratifs et le cadre en arc. Par ailleurs le style n'est pas vraiment réaliste, ce qui dénote d'évidentes influences perses. Les fresques fatimides sont assez proches par leur forme, leur style et leur thématique de représentations ornant des céramiques à décor lustré produites en égypte au cours de cette période. La figure de ce fragment peut se comparer à d'autres exemples fatimides figurant sur divers médias : céramiques, bois sculptés et nombreux textiles, même si la peinture est un art décoratif aux qualités spécifiques au cours de la période fatimide.

Les hammams étaient des bâtiments d'importance dans le monde islamique en raison de leur rôle dans l'hygiène et la purification du corps. Les murs des bains publics étaient communément décorés de fresques, comme l'exemple que nous voyons ici.
dates: Ve siècle de l’Hégire (XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Stuc ; hammam ; représentation figurative ; éléments architecturaux ; fresques
materials: Peinture au plâtre et aquarelle rouge et noire.
tags: Peinture au plâtre et aquarelle rouge et noire.

en.name: *Crucifixion*
description:
The Dominican Monastery of St. Domingos de Benfica, founded in 1399 on the outskirts of Lisbon, was rebuilt in the second quarter of the 17th century during the government of Friar João de Vasconcelos (1624–1632). During this period Manuel Pereira was commissioned to make a series of sculptural devotional images among which were the *Crucifixion* and *Our Lady of the Rosary* – both located over the aisle altars – and *Saint Dominique of Gusmão* and *St. Peter the Martyr* in the main arch niches.  
Portuguese Manuel Pereira studied in Rome and lived in Spain where he received important commissions from the Madrid court, which at the time was the capital of the Iberian monarchy (1580–1640). Pereira worked in stone, wood and alabaster, and using these materials he conceived mainly devotional sculptures that visually imparted the values inherited from the Trent Council through the dual rhetoric of *docere* and *delectare* (to teach, to move and to delight), aimed at heightening the inner conversion of the Christian. Manuel Pereira's sculptures are characterised by their dynamic composition, combined with the delicate treatment of the surfaces, which in their smallest details irradiate light, delivering a deep and intense psychology. These aesthetic values are present in the polychrome wooden sculptures of the *Immaculate Conception* in Toledo, *St. Ignatius of Loyola*, *St. Francis Xavier*, *St. Aloysus Gonzaga* and *St. Francis of Borja* commissioned by the Church of São Roque in Lisbon. One can include the *Crucifixions* in Cartuja de Miraflores in Burgos and St. Domingos de Benfica in Lisbon, where the realism and inner drama are remarkably intense. In the São Roque Benfica *Crucifixion,* based on an engraving by Pontius from a painting by Peter Paul Rubens, Pereira's Christ hangs lifeless and heavy from the cross, His face contorted, exhaling His last breath and His eyes closing slowly in agony.

The epitome of Manuel Pereira's sculpture lies in his Crucifixions among which this one, in the Church of St. Domingos de Benfica, is remarkably intense. Based on a composition by Rubens, Christ's heavy, lifeless body hangs from the cross, creating a deep and intense psychological tension that visually imparts the values inherited from the Trent Council through the dual rhetoric of *docere* and *delectare* (to teach, to move and to delight), which in this context suggests that the body is elevated to eternity through the inner drama of the Passion.
holder: Church of St. Domingos de Benfica
place: Largo de São Domingos de Benfica, Lisbon
Church of St. Domingos de Benfica, Lisbon
artist: Roman Classicism, Portuguese and Iberian Baroque sculpture
keywords: Painted wood sculpture; Roman Baroque; Iberian Baroque; Realism; dramatic gesture

pt.name: *Cristo Crucificado*
description:
Fundado em 1399, o Mosteiro dominicano de São Domingos de Benfica, no aro de Lisboa, conheceu nova e definitiva edificação no segundo quartel do século XVII, durante o governo do prior Frei João de Vasconcelos (1624-1632). Deste período, data a encomenda de uma série de imagens devocionais a Manuel Pereira, entre as quais se destaca este *Cristo Crucificado*, juntamente com uma *Nossa Senhora do Rosário*, ambos colocados nos altares do topo do transepto, e *São Domingos de Gusmão* e *São Pedro Mártir*, nos nichos do arco triunfal da igreja.  
Escultor português de formação romana, Manuel Pereira fixou-se em Espanha, onde executou encomendas para a corte de Madrid, então capital da monarquia ibérica (1580-1640). Trabalhou em pedra, madeira e alabastro, materiais que utilizou sobretudo em esculturas devocionais que materializavam plasticamente os valores tridentinos. Para deleite e conversão interior dos cristãos, concebeu imagens caracterizadas pelas suas composições dinâmicas, articuladas com o delicadíssimo tratamento das superfícies, capazes de captar, nos mais ínfimos pormenores, as reverberações da luz e de criar poderosas e densas figuras psicológicas, valores plásticos especialmente significativos nas esculturas de madeira policromada, como a *Imaculada Conceição*, em Toledo, *Santo Inácio de Loyola*, *São Francisco Xavier*, *São Luís de Gonzaga* e *São Francisco de Borja*, para a Igreja de São Roque, de Lisboa. No vórtice desta expressividade psicológica, estão os *Cristos Crucificados*, da Cartuxa de Miraflores e de São Domingos de Benfica, em Lisboa, obras em que o realismo da execução e o dramatismo interior se conjugam com a maior mestria. Na composição da imagem do *Cristo Crucificado* de Benfica, - baseada numa gravura de Pontius, segundo uma pintura de Peter Paul Rubens -, o escultor atinge a sua expressão máxima, ao modelar o corpo pendente em tensão do madeiro da cruz, enquanto o rosto se contrai quando exala o último suspiro e os olhos se cerram lentamente em agonia.

A escultura de Manuel Pereira tem o seu expoente nos *Cristos Crucificados*, entre os quais se destaca o de São Domingos de Benfica. Baseado numa composição de Rubens, Cristo em agonia pende em tensão da cruz, elevando o corpo até à vida eterna através do drama da Paixão, retratado de forma realista.

ar.name: شباك
description:
القطعة عبارة عن شباك من الجص يحتوي على زخارف مفرغة مملوءة بالزجاج الملون. تقع زخارف الشباك في جزأين مستطيلين: سفلي وعلوي. تتكون زخرفة الجزء السفلي وهو الأكثر ارتفاعاً من عقد مدبب بداخله زخارف نباتية بينها أشجار سرو وزخارف تمثل بعض العناصر المعمارية ذات الطابع العثماني مثل القباب والمآذن. وتتكون زخرفة الجزء العلوي من كتابة بخط النسخ نصها "يا محمد." وقد كتب هذا النص على أرضية من زخارف هندسية وزهور محوّرة ملونة تمتاز بالبساطة.  
  
ظهرت الشبابيك الجصية في مباني العصور الإسلامية المبكرة، واستخدمت في جامع عمرو بن العاص وفي الجامع الأزهر في العصر الفاطمي، وانتشر استخدامها في العصرين المملوكي والعثماني. ويحتفظ متحف الفن الإسلامي في القاهرة بالعديد من الشبابيك الجصية ذات الزخارف المتنوعة التي تعطي منظراً جميلاً عندما تسقط عليها أشعة الشمس أو تتعرض للإضاءة الاصطناعية، ومن أجملها الشباك الذي يحمل رقم سجل 9886.

عُرفت الشبابيك الجصية في مختلف العصور الإسلامية، وفي مختلف العمائر. ومن خلالها ينفذ ضوء الشمس مُخفَّفاًً إلى داخل المبنى، وتمثِّل هذه القطعة أحد هذه الشبابيك، وعند تزويد فتحاتها بالزجاج الملوَّن، تعطي تأثيراً جمالياً بديعاً.
keywords: جص؛ خط النسخ؛ زجاج معشق؛ زجاج ملون؛ شباك.

en.name: Window.
description:
A window made of stucco, which contains pierced decoration filled with coloured glass. The decorations of the window are placed in two rectangular sections: one, larger, at the bottom and the other, smaller, at the top. The decoration in the lower section is composed of a pointed arch, within which are vegetal motifs including cypress trees, and decorative architectural components such as domes and minarets, which bear a strong Ottoman imprint. The upper section is composed of an inscription in *naskhi* script, which reads: 'Oh Muhammad'.This inscription is written against a background of geometric decoration and stylised-coloured flowers distinguished by their simplicity.  
Stucco windows appeared in buildings in the early Islamic era and were used in Amr ibn al-'As Mosque and in al-Azhar Mosque, during the Fatimid period. In the Mamluk and Ottoman periods stucco coloured-glass windows were used more generally. The Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo has a number of stucco coloured-glass windows in the collection that are embellished with a variety of decorations, which invests in them a special beauty particularly when the sun shines through them or when they are exposed to artificial light. Among the most beautiful is that with the registry number 9886.

Stucco windows were known in different Islamic periods and were used in different buildings to filter the sunshine and soften its glare. When their pierced patterns were covered with coloured glass, the aesthetic effect was exquisite.
keywords: Stucco; naskhi script; glass; coloured glass
materials: Stucco, pierced and fitted with coloured glass.
tags: Stucco, pierced and fitted with coloured glass.

es.name: Ventana.
description:
Ventana de estuco que presenta decoración calada cuyos huecos están tapados con vidrios de colores. Los adornos de la ventana están dispuestos en dos secciones rectangulares: uno vertical, mayor, en la parte inferior y la otra encima de ella. La decoración de la parte inferior contiene un arco apuntado que enmarca motivos vegetales como cipreses y elementos arquitectónicos ornamentales como cúpulas y alminares, de inconfundible impronta otomana. La sección superior contiene una inscripción en letra *nasji* que reza "Oh Muhammad", escrita sobre un fondo de decoración geométrica y estilizadas flores de colores que destacan por su sencillez.  
Las ventanas de estuco surgieron en edificios de comienzos de la era islámica, como las mezquitas de Amr ibn al-As y al-Azhar, ambas fatimíes. En las épocas mameluca y otomana, el uso de vidrios de colores en las ventanas de estuco se extendió notablemente. El Museo de Arte Islámico de El Cairo cuenta en sus fondos con varias ventanas de estuco con vidrieras que les otorgan una gran belleza, sobre todo cuando el sol brilla a través de ellas o se las expone a la luz artificial. Destaca también la ventana con el n.º de inventario 9886.

Las ventanas de estuco se usaron en distintas etapas de la era islámica para filtrar la luz del sol y suavizar su resplandor. Cuando los huecos se cubrían con vidrios de colores, se lograba un efecto estético exquisito.
dates: Siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.
keywords: Estuco; escritura nasji; vidrieras; vidrios de colores.
materials: Estuco, calado y decorado con vidrios de colores.
tags: Estuco, calado y decorado con vidrios de colores.

fr.name: Fenêtre.
description:
Fenêtre en stuc à décor percé orné de morceaux de verre de couleur. La composition du décor se répartit en deux parties rectangulaires, la plus petite occupant le haut du châssis. Le décor de la partie inférieure est inclus dans un arc brisé meublé de motifs végétaux, dont des cyprès, et des éléments architecturaux comme des coupoles et des minarets, d'influence fortement ottomane. La partie supérieure comprend une inscription en style *naskhi* disant “ô Muhammad” et se détachant sur un fond d'ornements géométriques et de fleurs de couleur stylisées remarquables par leur simplicité.  
Les fenêtres en stuc apparaissent au début de la période islamique et figurent déjà dans la mosquée Amr ibn al-'As et la mosquée al-Azhar, d'époque fatimide. Ces fenêtres ornées de verre de couleur se développèrent au cours des périodes mamelouke et ottomane. Le Musée d'art islamique du Caire en possède un certain nombre aux décors variés illuminés par les rayons du soleil ou par un éclairage artificiel. Le plus bel exemplaire porte le numéro 9886.

Les fenêtres en stuc étaient courantes à différentes époques islamiques et étaient utilisées dans divers bâtiments pour filtrer le soleil et adoucir son éclat. Quand leurs motifs découpés étaient couverts de verre coloré, l'effet esthétique était sublime.
dates: Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Stuc ; écriture naskhi ; verre de couleur ; vitrail
materials: Stuc percé, décoré de verre de couleur.
tags: Stuc percé, décoré de verre de couleur.

en.name: *Edward Jenner*, Marble Group by Giulio Monteverde
names: *Edoardo Jenner*, gruppo in marmo di Giulio Monteverde
short_description: Giulio Monteverde was an Italian sculptor who started carving wooden crucifixes and then moved on to sculpture during his years at the Academy of Fine Arts in Genoa. In 1865 Monteverde moved to Rome to study at the Academy of St. Luke. The sculpture of Edward Jenner (1749-1823) represents the British physician and naturalist inoculating for the first time, on his own son, the smallpox vaccine that he invented. This work was initially rejected by the Academy of St. Luke, entrusted with selecting works of art for the International Exposition in Vienna, and then exhibited in it thanks to an influential friend of the artist. The plaster cast of Jenner won the gold medal in Vienna. The engraving celebrates Monteverde's deeds. Chroniclers report that in 1878 the marble version of the group sculpture was awarded a huge prize at the International Exhibition in Paris: a gold medal and a hearty public welcome.
keywords: Medicine; health; vaccination; epidemics; disease; life expectancy; social changes; scientific development; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; Positivism; celebration of science; international exhibitions; universal exposition

en.name: Cup with serpentine stem
short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The motif of glass filaments worked with pincers to look like crests, typical of the 17th century objects is used also in the ruby-red glass cup with snake-shaped stem of neo-baroque inspiration and dating from the second half of the 19th century. Its form is inspired by snake goblets common in Venice and Germany in the 17th century.

en.name: *One Thousand and One Nights: Arabic fairytales tanslated by Galland, illustrated by the best French artists…*
names: *This edition of the One Thousand and One Nights is a beautiful new volume of eleven hundred and twenty pages* \[…\] *subscriptions available in all bookshops: published in 52 installments.*
short_description: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. en.name: Celestial Globe
description:
This precisely executed globe, made of two hemispheres, is the sixth earliest surviving celestial globe. The maker’s name is given twice on the globe. The first, and shorter inscription, states that the globe was made by Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn ‘Ali al-Tabari. His name appears again in the longer five-line inscription, where he omits the name of his grandfather and his nisbah, but emphasizes instead his trade as an astrolabe-maker, al-asturlabi. And indeed the globe does reflect the work of a professional instrument maker.  
  
The long inscription, situated near the south pole of the instrument, states that its maker, Muhammad ibn Mahmud based it on the illustrations in the AH 4th / AD 10th-century astronomer al-Sufi’s *Kitab suwar al-kawakib al-thabitah* (‘Book of the Fixed Stars’), adapting it to take account of the 200-year lapse of time and rectifying errors of placement and spelling and that the maker had written the identifications of the various constellations of the Zodiac, fixed stars, lunar mansions, and of some non-Zodiacal constellations as well. These show certain discrepancies with al-Sufi’s figures, and, further away from the ecliptic, the star-positions are increasingly misleading. And, although the maker does not say so, he would also have been responsible for calibrating the globe, a necessary condition of its being used for astronomical purposes.
holder: Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
artist: maker Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn ‘Ali al-Tabari al-Astralubi
materials: Brass, incised and inlaid with silver
tags: Brass, incised and inlaid with silver

en.name: Great Mosque of Aleppo
description:
The Great Mosque, built by the Umayyads on the grounds of a Byzantine cathedral, stands at the heart of Aleppo. Restored and rebuilt over the centuries, the only Atabeg vestiges extant are a few arches in its eastern courtyard and the splendid minaret, founded by the *qadi* Ibn al-Khashshab during the rule of the Atabeg, Aq Sunqur in 483/1090. Frequently compared to classical architecture, the minaret of the Great Mosque is actually more stylistically linked to the 5th- and 6thcentury AD churches west of Aleppo, such as Qalb Lozeh or Qal’at Sim’an. In this respect, it may represent a continuity of Syrian Late-Antique architecture.  
This minaret is one of the great masterpieces of medieval Aleppo. Towering to a height of more than 45 m the square shaft, broken up with cornices and inscriptions into six zones, has four decorated with pilasters, foliate arches and continuous mouldings. The stone-carved inscriptions found along the minaret's friezes offer a variety of angular and cursive designs, including some of Syria’s best examples of Atabeg *kufic* calligraphy. On the highest level the *basmala* “in the name of God …”, and the dedication to the Seljuq Sultan Mahmud bin Malik Shah. On the next level down there is a dedication to the Seljuq Atabeg of Aleppo, Aq Sunqur. The third level has  
a dedication to the *qadi* Ibn al-Khashshab, while the fourth holds a Qur’anic blessing to mosque builders in general. The ground level is undecorated, with only a cartouche naming the  
architect and date of construction: “Made by Hasan bin Mufarraj al-Samani in the year three and eighty and four hundred”, which corresponds to AD 1091.

de.name: Kath. Pfarrkirche hl. Veit
description: Im Gesamten wirkt die Kirche von Fulpmes, der erste vollständige Neubau von Penz, recht konservativ, mit der strengen Form eines tonnenüberwölbten, architektonisch straff und konsequent einheitlich gegliederten Saals sowie den noch recht kleinen Freskenfeldern. Der dezent eingesetzte, durchaus feine Stuck, der auch einige Freiflächen lässt, ist in den Formen des frühen Rokoko gehalten, mit noch wenig ausgeprägten Rocaillen; geschaffen wurde er von Anton Gigl, der einer Wessobrunner Stukkatorenfamile angehörte. Die Fresken des Augsburger Akademiedirektors Bergmüller illustrieren den Triumph des Katholizismus als Glaubensbekenntnis: im Chor die Verehrung des Lammes und der Eucharestie, dazu die Erztugenden Glaube, Liebe und Hoffnung, im Querhaus der Triumph des hl. Kreuzes sowie im Langhaus die Anbetung des Namens Jesu durch die Erdteile, die himmlischen Heerscharen und den Kirchenpatron. Die barocke Altarausstattung ist nur in Teilen original erhalten und wurde im 20. Jahrhundert größtenteils erneuert.

Der für eine Pfarrkirche weit und monumental wirkende Saalraum gehört dem Typus einer tonnengewölbten Wandpfeilerkirche an. Die Abseiten vor dem Chor sind querhausartig erweitert, wodurch sich im Grundriss ein lateinisches Kreuz ergibt. Durchgängiges Hauptmotiv ist die Pilasterarkade mit reinen Halbkreisbögen; in dieser Form wird auch der Eingang zum Chor als Torarkade ausgezeichnet. Breiten Raum nimmt der in dezenter Farbigkeit gehaltene Stuck ein, während die farbkräftigen Fresken in verhältnismäßig kleinen Feldern wie Öffnungen des Gewölbes wirken, die nur hier und dort den Blick in den Himmel eröffnen.
history: Fulpmes gehörte ursprünglich zur Pfarrei von Telfes im Stubaital. Als erste Kirche von Fulpmes gilt die spätmittelalterliche Sagererkapelle (heute Totenkapelle im Oberdorf). Mit der Einrichtung eines Benefiziats im Jahre 1745 wird auch der Neubau der Veitskirche betrieben. In den Jahren 1746/47 durch den in der Region berühmten kirchlichen Baudirektor Franz de Paula Penz geführt, konnte der Bau schon 1748 durch den Weihbischof von Brixen geweiht werden. Die Pläne stammen wohl von Josef Staph (wie auch in Wilten), die Ausführung oblag dem Innsbrucker Maurermeister Umhauser. Im selben Jahr 1748 erfolgte die Erhebung zur Kuratie. Die Ausstattung erfolgte zügig im wesentlichen 1747-50.

en.name: Catholic Parish Church of St. Vitus
description: Overall, the church in Fulpmes, the first complete building from Penz, appears extremely conservative, with the strict form of a barrel-vaulted, architecturally rigid and uniformly structured hall together with small fresco panels. The discreet, by all means delicate stucco is maintained in the form of the Early Rococo, with few pronounced rocailles, and is the work of Anton Gigl, a member of a family of stucco masons of the Wessobrun school. Bergmüller’s frescos illustrate the triumph of Catholicism as a confession of faith. In the choir, the Worship of the Lamb and the Eucharist, in the transept the Triumph of the Holy Cross, and in the nave the Worship of the name of Jesus. Only parts of the Baroque altar décor are original and were largely replaced in the 20th century.

The central hall, which appears broad and monumental for a parish church, is of the barrel-vaulted pilaster church type, with transept-like extended aisles before the choir. The main motif, continued throughout, is the pilaster arcade with pristine semi-circular arches. The stucco, in discreet colours, occupies a wide area, while the frescos in bold colours are situated in relatively small panels giving the impression of openings in the vault providing intermittent views of heaven.
artist: Architecture, construction supervision: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); plans: Joseph Stapf [n.d.]; altar statues: Josef Stapf; altar painting: Giuseppe Gru (c. 1715–c. 1775?); stuccowork: Anton Gigl (1700–1769); ceiling frescos: Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762)
history: Fulpmes originally belonged to the parish of Telfe in Stubaital. The first church in Fulpmes is considered to be the late medieval Sagererkapelle (today the Totenkapelle in Oberdorf). With the establishment of a beneficiary in 1745, the construction of the new Church of St. Vitus was instituted. Built in 1746/47 under the direction of the ecclesiastical building director Franz de Paula Penz, the building was consecrated as early as 1748. The plans originate from Josef Staph (as at Wilten); the execution was in the hands of the master mason Umhauser from Innsbruck. In the same year, 1748, it was elevated to the status of a parish district. The interior work was largely completed between 1747 and 1750.

en.name: Church of the Gesù, painted architecture of the high altar
description:
The church, based on a design in the Counter-Reformist style, has a wide nave with chapels that are intended to harmoniously combine the practical needs of preaching (larger spaces) with a sober, strict feel.  
Also for practical—as well as didactic—ends, the Jesuit Padre Andrea Pozzo created an illusory extension to the church, creating a prolongation of the choir behind the altar that contains a mock shrine modelled on Bernini's baldachin in St Peter's, and behind which there is a scene from the *Circumcision of Jesus*. The central space in front of the altar is covered by a mock cupola painted in perspective. It employs the solution used in Rome at Sant'Ignazio, but with greater sobriety in its architectural simplicity, and entirely free of figures. The artist's great skill and masterful perspective work are evident in the transitions, apparently forming a harmonious whole, between the real architecture of the nave and the mock pilasters and columns surmounted by capitals and trabeations in the painted area behind the altar. It should be noted that this use of painted perspective – undoubtedly dictated by economic need – at the time also assumed a symbolic significance inasmuch as true spiritual reality was sought beyond sometimes misleading appearances, to such an extent that the focal point enabling the illusion to be best appreciated is marked on the floor by a black disk, stressing—as confirmed by Padre Pozzo himself in his treatise *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum* (1693)—that there is only "one position to which the believer should strive".

For practical—as well as didactic—ends, the Jesuit Padre Andrea Pozzo painted a decorative scene that is one of the masterpieces of Baroque illusionistic art. A shortage of economic resources prompted the artist to create an illusory extension of the space in the church, creating a prolongation of the choir behind the high altar that contains a mock shrine, which stands before a representation of the *Circumcision of Jesus*.
artist: Andrea Pozzo (1642, Trento – 1709, Vienna) with the help of his Jesuit pupil, Antonio Colli (died, Rome, 1723)
history: The Church of the Gesù, now found right in the centre of the city on account of gradual urban expansion, dates back to the late 16th–17th/early 17th­–18th centuries, although there were Jesuits in the city from 1559. The church was expanded to its current form with the support of Olimpia Aldobrandini Pamphili, after her death in 1681 (between 1696 and 1700), according to the traditional Jesuit model already used in the Roman churches of the Gesù, Sant’Ignazio and Vallicella.
keywords: Perspective painting, *trompe-l'oeil,* illusionistic, fresco, Jesuit
tags: Perspective painting, trompe-l'oeil, illusionistic, fresco, Jesuit
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Chiesa del Gesù, Altare maggiore
description:
La chiesa è ad ampia navata unica con cappelle secondo una concezione di tipo contro riformato che si prefiggeva di armonizzare necessità pratiche di predicazione (ampiezza degli spazi) con un carattere di sobrietà e severità.  
Sempre per necessità pratiche, inoltre, ma anche con una finalità didascalica, il gesuita padre Andrea Pozzo realizzò un ampliamento illusorio dello spazio della chiesa rappresentando dietro l'altar maggiore un prolungamento del coro e al suo interno un finto tempietto, esemplato sul baldacchino beniniano di San Pietro, dietro al quale è rappresentata la scena della *Circoncisione di Gesù*. Inoltre il vano centrale antistante l'altare è coperto da una finta cupola dipinta in prospettiva secondo la soluzione già adottata a Roma in Sant'Ignazio, ma con un carattere di maggiore sobrietà nella semplicità architettonica non decorata da alcuna figura. Le grandi capacità tecniche e prospettiche dell'artista si rivelano nei brani di passaggio, apparentemente in armoniosa continuità, fra l'architettura reale della navata e le finte lesene e colonne sormontate da capitelli e trabeazione della zona dipinta dietro l'altare. Va infine sottolineato che tale ricorso alla prospettiva dipinta, sicuramente dettato da motivazioni di ordine economico, assumeva all'epoca anche un significato simbolico in quanto la vera realtà spirituale va cercata al di là delle apparenze a volte ingannevoli tanto che il punto focale che permette la corretta visione illusionistica è segnalato sul pavimento da un disco nero a sottolineare, come afferma lo stesso padre Pozzo nel suo trattato *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum* (1693) che solo "una è la posizione cui deve tendere il credente".

Per necessità pratiche ma anche con una finalità didascalica, il gesuita padre Andrea Pozzo eseguì una decorazione scenografica che si può annoverare tra i capolavori dell’arte illusionistica barocca. Infatti, a causa della mancanza di risorse economiche, l’artista realizzò un ampliamento illusorio dello spazio della chiesa rappresentando dietro l’altar maggiore un prolungamento del coro e al suo interno un finto tempietto, dietro al quale è rappresentata la scena della *Circoncisione di Gesù*.
artist: Andrea Pozzo (1642, Trento – 1709, Vienna) con l’aiuto del suo allievo gesuita Antonio Colli (morto a Roma nel 1723)
history: La chiesa del Gesù, oggi ubicata in pieno centro a causa del progressivo sviluppo urbano,  risale agli anni tra la fine del XVI e l’inizio del XVII secolo, benché i Gesuiti siano presenti nella cittadina fin dal 1559. La chiesa fu ingrandita nelle forme attuali con il contributo di Olimpia Aldobrandini Pamphili, dopo la sua morte (1681), tra il 1696 e il 1700, secondo il modello gesuitico tradizionale già sperimentato nelle chiese romane del Gesù, di Sant’Ignazio, della Vallicella, ecc.
keywords: Prospettiva dipinta ad affresco; gesuiti
partner: Provincia di Roma (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

ar.name: شاهدة قبر.
description:
شاهدة قبر هرميّة الشكل ذات درجات يعلوها موشور. نُحِتت عليها بشكلٍ بارز نقيشة كتابية بأحرف كوفيّة تَبسطُ النص التالي: " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وصلى الله على النبى / محمد وعلى آله وسلم تسليما كل نفس ذائقة الموت / هذا قبر عبد الله ابن محمد رحمه الله توفي يوم / الجمعة أول رمضان من سنة ثمانية وثمانين وأربعة."؛ وعلى جانبيه، يحمل الموشور النقش الكتابي التالي: "لله الحمد".  
إن وضع هذه الشاهدة سيء جدّاً ولا يمكن قراءة النقيشة الكتابية إلا بصعوبة شديدة.
شاهدة جنائزية هرمية الشكل وذات مدرجات مهشمة تهشما كبيرا، ويعلوها موشور. تعطي نقيشة كتابية بأحرف كوفية صعبة القراءة اسم المتوفى وتاريخ الوفاة، بالإضافة إلى الأدعية المعتادة تقربا إلى الله.
keywords: حجر رملي؛ حرف كوفي؛ علم الكتابات والخطوط؛ قطعة جنائزية؛ نقيشة كتابية.

en.name: Funerary stele of Abu ‘Abdallah ibn Khalifa.
description:
Funerary stele in the form of a pyramid, tiered and surmounted by a prism. Sculpted in relief, an inscription in *kufic* lettering reveals the following epitaph: 'In the name of God the Clement, the Merciful! May God bless the prophet / Muhammad! And his family and may he accord them complete salvation, as every soul tastes death \[Qur'an, XXI, 36\]. This is the tomb of ‘Abdallah son of Khalifa son of Muhammad, may God show him mercy, he died the day / *al-djumu'a* \[Friday\] first day of Ramadan of the year 488 \[September 1095\]'. On the lateral sides, the prism holds the following inscription: 'To God / the glory.'  
This stele is in a very bad condition, and the inscription is very difficult to decipher.

A very poorly preserved funerary stele in the form of a stepped pyramid topped with a prism. A barely legible inscription in *kufic* characters carved in relief gives the name of the deceased and the date of death, along with the habitual praise to God.
holder: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts
keywords: Funerary object; epigraphy; gravestone; sandstone; inscription; kufic

es.name: Estela funeraria de Abu Abd Allah ibn Jalifa.
description:
Estela funeraria de forma piramidal escalonada, rematada con un prisma. En una inscripción en caracteres cúficos, en relieve, se lee el epitafio siguiente: “¡En el nombre de Dios, el Compasivo, el Misericordioso! Que Dios bendiga al profeta / Muhammad y su familia y les conceda la salvación total, cada uno gustará la muerte \[Corán 21:35, trad. de J. Cortés). Esta es la tumba de Abd Allah ibn Jalifa ibn Muhammad, que Dios le tenga misericordia, falleció el / primer viernes de ramadán del año 488 \[septiembre de 1095\]”. En los laterales, el prisma lleva la inscripción siguiente: “A Dios, la alabanza”.  
La estela se encuentra en mal estado de conservación y resulta difícil descifrar el contenido de la inscripción.

fr.name: Stèle funéraire d’Abou Abdallah ibn Khalifa.
description:
Stèle funéraire de forme pyramidale à gradins surmontée d'un prisme. Sculptée en relief, une inscription en caractères coufiques déploie l'épitaphe suivante : “Au nom de Dieu le Clément, le Miséricordieux ! Que Dieu bénisse le prophète / Muhammad ! et sa famille et qu'il leur accorde le salut complet, toute âme goûte la mort \[Coran, XXI, 36\]. Ceci est la tombe d'Abdallah fils de Khalifa fils de Muhammad, que Dieu lui fasse miséricorde, il est décédé le jour / *el-djoumouaa* \[vendredi\] premier de *ramadan* de l'année 488 \[septembre 1095\]” ; sur les côtés latéraux, le prisme porte l'inscription suivante : “à Dieu / la louange.”  
  
Cette stèle est en très mauvais état, et l'inscription est très difficile à déchiffrer.

en.name: Saint Georges Maronite Cathedral
description: Designed by the Italian architect Giuseppe Maggiore in the neo-classical style, the Saint George Cathedral bears great resemblance to the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome. The Cathedral's nave is covered with a coffer roof with gilding and a double-wood frame decorated with golden leaves on a beige-coloured fond, and the walls are decorated with stucco and marble. The Archbishop of Beirut sits in the heart of the choir.
history: The Saint George Cathedral is the seat of the Maronite Archdiocese in Beirut. It was built between 1884 and Palm Sunday of 1894, using stone from the Roman columns of the Temple of Deir al-Qala'a in Beit Mery. The cathedral is built on the site of an earlier church, from 1755, which was also dedicated to Saint George.
keywords: Religion; Church; City Centre; Beirut

en.name: National Gallery of Modern Art in Rome
names: Galleria Nazionale di Arte Moderna, Roma
short_description: The Pavilion of Fine Arts, built for the 1911 International Exhibition in Rome and meant to become the permanent location of the National Gallery of Modern Art, was designed by the architect Cesare Bazzani (1873-1939). He also was responsible for the Department of Public Education and the layout of the Tiberine island. The Pavilion covered an area of 5000 square meters and was constructed in only 15 months. The building was designed in a sober classic style that merged perfectly with the environment and city landscape. The massive facade with the huge staircase and twin columns drew inspiration from ancient Roman architecture; the architect added to it more recent elements like Seicento festoons and the Borghese coat of arms with the eagle. The building celebrated the 50th anniversary from the Risorgimento (the unification of Italy) and affirmed the authority of the Italian state among the other countries.

en.name: Crystalware
description:
Prism-shaped travel trunk of varnished wood with metal trim. Housed in its two overlapping compartments is a collection of 44 blown glass, engraved and gilded pieces, decorated with floral motifs. The upper part of the set includes six stemmed glasses; two small bottles with lids; two small, lidded jars; two small glasses and a funnel. The middle portion features four medium-sized glasses, two large ones and two vinegar cruets with lids. Below these are two small stemmed glasses, two oil cruets, two flat-panelled salt cellars, a lidded jam jar and a tower salt cellar with a screw top. A total of 29 pieces are arranged on a tray lined with red fabric and moulded to fit each piece, an arrangement that has perfectly preserved the condition of both the glass and the gold that overlays the engraved decoration. Beneath the tray and within the lower compartment are 15 engraved but ungilded, square foot goblets. Originally there must have been 20 of these.  
  
All of these pieces, in their careful engraving and gilt finish, bear the influences of the foreign masters. The collection may be traced to the most prolific and highest-quality production period of the Royal Factory.  
  
Paloma Pastor Rey de Viñas identifies the set as a carrying case or travel glassware tote:  
  
…although rare, the so-called “carrying cases” were also made during this period. All the essentials for making an impromptu stop along the road were contained in these cases, including square foot goblets, glasses, dishes, vinegar bottles and even mugs. Pastor Rey de Viñas, Paloma, *La Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja. Historia, Repertorios decorativos y tipologías formales*, Madrid: Arte Segovia S.L., 1988: 70.)
place: La Granja de San Ildefonso, Segovia, Spain
artist: Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja (La Granja Royal Crystal Factory)
keywords: Crystalware; travel; gilded

es.name: Cristalería
description:
Caja de de viaje de madera barnizada, de forma prismática, con aplicaciones metálicas. Alberga en su interior —distribuida en dos compartimentos superpuestos— una cristalería de 44 piezas, realizada en vidrio soplado al aire, grabado y dorado, con decoración de motivos florales. El conjunto está integrado por seis copas, dos garrafitas con sus tapones, dos botecitos con tapadera, dos vasos pequeños y un embudo en un primer orden; cuatro vasos medianos, dos grandes, dos vinagreras cos sus tapas en un segundo orden; dos copas pequeñas, dos aceiteras, dos saleros planos, una dulcera con su tapa y un salero de torre con su tapadera de rosca en la parte baja. Todas estas piezas, un total de veintinueve, se recogen en una bandeja forrada de tela roja y cajeada con la forma de las piezas que ha permitido la perfecta conservación tanto del cristal como del oro que cubre la decoración tallada. Levantada la bandeja aparece el compartimento inferior con quince frascas talladas, pero sin dorar. Originalmente debieron de ser veinte.  
  
Se aprecia la influencia de los maestros extranjeros, sugerida por el cuidado grabado y posterior dorado de todas las piezas. Podemos datar el conjunto en el periodo más prolífico y de mayor calidad que se ha dado en La Real Manufactura.  
  
Su identificación como maletín o frasquera de camino viene recogida como tal en el libro "La Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja. Historia. Repertorios decorativos y tipologías formales" de Paloma Pastor Rey de Viñas (editado por Arte Segovia S.L. en el año 1998, pág. 70): "aunque escasos, también se realizaron durante esta época los denominados "maletines de camino", conteniendo en su interior frascas, vasos, copas, platos, vinagreras e incluso tazas, es decir, todo lo imprescindible para improvisar un alto en el camino”.
type: Vidrio y cristal; Ajuar de mesa
place: La Granja de San Ildefonso, Segovia, España
artist: Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja
keywords: Cristalería; viaje; dorado

en.name: Grand Hall
description: The most significant and artistically most important room in the building is the Grand Hall on the second floor, designed after the fire of 1785. Stucco decorations on the walls imitate grey marble with dark veins, while at one time those of the vault were painted light yellow. Architectural decoration powerfully articulates the surfaces.
place: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

en.name: A young algerian girl
short_description: Between the late 19th century and the 1930s, it became fashionable in the West to take photographs of children, either for publication as postcards or with "anthropological" aims. This photograph highlights the striking contrast between the hardships of poverty and the young girl's smile.

fr.name: Une petite Algérienne
short_description: De la seconde moitié du XIXe siècle aux années 1930, les photographes occidentaux prennent fréquemment des clichés d'enfants soit pour des cartes postales, soit dans un but "anthropologique". Ici le photographe a relevé le contraste saisissant entre la misère de cette fillette et son sourire.

en.name: A View of Street from Istanbul
short_description: The Abdullah Frères were a group of three Ottoman brothers of Armenian descent who were world-renowned photographers. They took pictures of scenic views and notable individuals, including sultans. Most of their photography was of the Ottoman Empire. In 1867, they sold their shop in Beyazid and moved to a more favourable location in Pera.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

en.name: Photograph of Bab al-Saraya
short_description: Bab al-Saraya was the eastern gate of the city. Whilst other gates were closed at dusk, this was the only gate that was kept open until evening prayer. Thus, it was also commonly known as *bab al-masla*, meaning the worshipper's gate. The official name, Bab al-Saraya, comes from its proximity to the Serail of the Amir Fakhr al-Din by the Sursuq market. It was also located near the Amir Mansur Assaf mosque on the sea front. The gate remained intact until it was destroyed by the French authorities during the mandate era, in 1927. The headquarters of an-Nahar, a famous Lebanese newspaper, now occupy the site.
keywords: Gate; Door; Portal; Bab; Beirut

en.name: Church of San Félix
description:
The town of Torralba de Ribota had an exclusively Christian population and was an important centre for the production of bricks and roof tiles. According to López Landa, the Bishop of Tarazona, don Pedro Pérez Calvillo, had the Mudéjar church built on a high flat spot overlooking the town in 1367 at a time when the war with Castile was still not completely over. This circumstance undoubtedly caused him to choose the architectonic typology of the fortified church, closely imitating the Church of the Virgin in Tobed. The pace of work was slow since a substantial part of it was still ongoing during the Bishopric of don Juan de Valtierra (1410–1433). It is precisely to this second decade of the 15th century that the upper choir and the west gable-end flanked by two towers corresponds, a work probably directed by the master Mahoma Ramí, once the second stage of San Pedro Mártir in Calatayud had been completed in 1414.  
The church has undergone numerous restorations during recent times, notably the one carried out by Fernando Chueca Goitia in the second half of the 20th century. The plan and structure correspond to what has been described already above in the Church of Tobed, although here the nave is shorter as it only has two spans. The interior plan of the two towers on the west front is interesting, as they have a cylindrical central core. This system, atypical in the Mudéjar of Aragon, is found only here and in the tower of the Mudéjar church in Quinto de Ebro. The church has conserved a magnificent series of painted Gothic altarpieces, which again offer evidence of the perfect coexistence of the Oriental and Occidental languages – the Mudéjar spatial one and the Gothic pictorial one.

es.name: Iglesia de San Félix
description:
La localidad de Torralba de Ribota estaba habitada solo por población cristiana y constituía un importante centro de fabricación de ladrillos y tejas. Según López Landa, la iglesia mudéjar, emplazada en un altiplano que domina el caserío, fue mandada edificar por el obispo de Tarazona don Pedro Pérez Calvillo en 1367, cuando la guerra con Castilla no se había apagado del todo, una circunstancia que motivó sin duda la elección de la tipología arquitectónica de iglesia-fortaleza, que sigue de modo muy directo a la iglesia de la Virgen en Tobed.  
Las obras avanzaron lentamente, pues una parte sustancial de las mismas se realizó durante el episcopado de don Juan de Valtierra (1410-1433). Precisamente a esta segunda década del siglo XV corresponden el coro alto y el hastial occidental flanqueado por dos torres, obra dirigida probablemente por el maestro Mahoma Rami, una vez terminada en 1414 la segunda etapa de San Pedro Mártir, en Calatayud. La iglesia ha sido objeto de numerosas restauraciones en nuestra época, destacando entre todas ellas la realizada por Fernando Chueca Goitia. Su disposición y estructura se corresponden con la ya descrita y visitada en la iglesia de Tobed, aunque aquí la nave es más corta, puesto que solo tiene dos tramos. Es interesante la disposición interior de las dos torres de la fachada occidental, que tienen un machón central cilíndrico. Este sistema, bastante atípico en el mudéjar aragonés, se halla solo aquí y en la torre de la iglesia mudéjar de Quinto de Ebro. La iglesia ha conservado una magnífica serie de retablos de pintura gótica, que permite constatar de nuevo la perfecta convivencia de los lenguajes oriental y occidental, el espacial mudéjar y el pictórico gótico.

ar.name: سيف منحني الحد (شمشير)
description:
يُنسب إلى الإمام سيف بن سلطان اليعربي الأول (قيد الأرض)  
من مقتنيات السلطان قابوس بن سعيد بن تيمور (طيب الله ثراه)  
  
يتميز نصل هذا السيف المصنوع من الفولاذ الدّمشقي، بأكثر التصاميم الزخرفية تعقيداً والتي تُعرف باسم "الأربعون خطوة"، ويظهر توقيع صانع السيف في خرطوش ذهبي يتوسط النّصل" عمل أسد الله 186"، وهو من صنع أسد الله الأصفهاني، أحد أشهر صانعي السيوف في العالم الإسلامي خلال القرن (11هـ/17م)، إضافة إلى عبارة "ملكية الشيخ سيف" أسفل منها، ونقش عبارة "شاه عباس سنة 5". أما المقبض المصنوع من العاج والمطعم بالذهب، فهو بنمط المقابض العربية.  
  
يُثبت نقش المُلكية على النصل بأن السيف لم يكن غنيمة حرب، وإنما تم تكليف الصانع بعملة، ومن المُرجح أنه قدّم كهدية إلى سيف بن سلطان اليعربي من بلاط الإمبراطورية الصفوية، التي رأت فيه إماماً مستقبليا لعُمان.

en.name: Saber (*shamshir*)
description:
Attributed to Imam Saif bin Sultan al-Yarubi I (*Qaid al-Ard’*)  
*Collections of Sultan Qaboos bin Said bin Taimur*  
  
The blade of this saber is by Asadallah of Isfahan, one of the most celebrated swordsmiths of Islamic civilisation in the Hegira 11th century / AD 17th century. It is made from Damascus steel and patterned with the most complex design, known as the “forty steps”. The swordsmith’s signature appears in the middle gold cartouche of the blade reading “the work of Asadallah 186”, and “property of Sheikh Saif” in the lower cartouche, as well as the inscription “Shah Abas year 5”.  
  
The blade’s inscription proves that the sabre was not taken as loot. Rather, the maker had been commissioned directly. The design and inscriptions make it likely that it was made for presentation to Saif, perhaps by the Safavid Court of Persia, who, in Hegira 1086 / AD 1675, saw him as a future leader of Oman.

en.name: *The Great Mosque of Algiers*
short_description: This painting was the first of Sintès' works to be bought by the museum on its opening in 1930. In actual fact it does not depict the mosque known as the "Great Mosque", but rather the "Djemâa ed-Djedid" (Jama'a al-Jadid) built in the 17th century in the style of the Turkish mosques from the city of Bursa. Here, the mosque appears overlooking the city's seafront ramparts, whilst the port neighbourhood's urban development does not appear to have begun.
keywords: Old Algiers; traditional urban space; colonial city; Orientalism

fr.name: *La Grande Mosquée d'Alger*
short_description: Il s’agit là de la première œuvre de Sintès acquise par le musée à son ouverture en 1930 ; en fait, elle ne figure pas le monument connu sous le nom de « Grande Mosquée », mais la « Djemâa ed-Djedid », qui fut édifiée au XVIIe sur le modèle des mosquées turques de la ville de Brousse : elle est ici représentée dominant les remparts en bordure de mer, alors que les remaniements urbanistiques du quartier de la Marine n’étaient pas encore commencés.
keywords: Veille Alger; espace urbaine traditionnel; cité colonielle; Orientalisme

en.name: Khanqa al-Farafra
description:
It was also founded by Dayfa Khatun in 634/1237 and intended for Sufi women. As such it is the only survivor of about a dozen medieval *khanqahs* in Aleppo. A *muqarnas* portal in the middle of a plain wall leads through a bent-axis vestibule to a squarish courtyard (10 x 11 meters) centered around an octagonal pool with a polylobed interior. A three-bay mosque with a central dome occupies the southern side, a spacious *iwan* faces it on the north, while the eastern and western sides are taken up by residential rooms arranged on two levels. The mosque is relatively plain except for a deeply recessed *mihrab* which is completely reveted in veined white marble and green diorite.  
Dhayfa Khatun’s architectural patronage reveals her inclination to learning and Sufism, while many contemporary chroniclers have recorded her justice and charity: “She was just to her subjects, very charitable and loving towards them. She removed various taxes in all the regions of Aleppo. She favoured jurists, ascetics, scholars and people of religion, and extended to them many charities”, records the Syrian historian Ibn al-Wasil (604–97/1208 98).

description: تنتمي المبخرة المسيحية لمجموعة التي نسبت أصلا لمناطق سوريا وفلسطين. وهذا التأريخ أكد أيضا بالنقش الفريد لطراز أولي من الخط الكوفي الذي يمكن ترجمته كالتالي: "" باسم الله ، صنعت من قبل يعقوب ابن اسحق من دمشق"".

en.name: Incense burner
description: The Christian incense burner belongs to a group that is normally ascribed to the Syrian and Palestinian area. This attribution is further confirmed by the unique inscription in early *Kufi* that can be translated as follows: “In the name of Allah (God), made by Yaqub, son of Ishaq from Damascus.”
keywords: Incense burner; Iran; Cast brass; Silver; Gold; religious object
materials: Cast and engraved bronze, later chain
tags: Cast and engraved bronze, later chain

en.name: Bottle
description: This square cobalt blue glass bottle with a rounded shoulder and cylindrical neck is composed of four swelling bands of glass. Made by a glassmaking process called marvering, taken from the French word, *marbre*, meaning "marble", this bottle presents fine white lines made with melted glass rods woven seamlessly into harmonious lines across the body. This glassmaking technique was particularly popular during the early Islamic period in Egypt, as evidenced by numerous examples of similarly decorated bottles excavated from Fustat, Egypt. Fustat, a centre of glass production during the early Islamic period, also served as the first capital of Egypt. Bottles like this were possibly made for the courtly elite to store precious ointments and perfumes.
keywords: Glass; Vessel; Mould-blown; Marvered; Abbasid; Umayyad

en.name: House of Zapata
names: House of Zapata – Residence of the Court of the Inquisition
description:
What is now the Court House, in its day was the residence of the Llerenaborn lawyer Luis Zapata, who was Counsellor to the Catholic Monarchs. Zapata was an active figure who played an important part in the politics of the kingdom. The palace was built during the first 30 years of the 16th century; it was then rented by the seat of the Holy Office or Inquisition in 1570, which later bought it and carried out a series of alterations. There is little left of the original 16th-century building that, at the time, was as notable as “*the best of the knights’ houses … and better than many noble ones*”. It had two entrance doors: one on the east side, which today is walled up, and about which there is only some data about its Hispano- Flamboyant Gothic style; and the north door, which gives on to the calle de la Corredera, and is the one used today. This north façade has two rows of semicircular arches on columns with twisted shafts and a cornice with pommels.  
We know from the register of visits of the Order that the palace had three patios in the 16th century, two of them with corridors, a yard, and two towers that had 34 rooms. The principal chamber of the palace of Luis Zapata, which the documents refer to as *Sala Dorada* or the Golden Chamber, was on the second floor. It had an oratory and very probably a Mudéjar ceiling.  
To have survived out of all of this is a square cloister with two floors of arcades in brick. The galleries of the lower floor have three stilted arches framed in *alfiz* on octagonal pillars, while the upper floor has four semicircular segmental arches also framed with *alfiz*.

es.name: Casa Zapata
names: Casa Zapata - Residencia del Tribunal de la Inquisición
description:
Lo que hoy es Palacio de Justicia fue en su día la residencia del licenciado Luis Zapata, natural de Llerena, y del Consejo de los Reyes Católicos. Fue un hombre activo que tuvo importantes intervenciones en la política del reino.  
El palacio, realizado durante el primer tercio del siglo XVI, pasó a ser sede del Santo Oficio, que primero lo alquiló, en 1570, y luego lo compró, veintiocho años después, llevando a cabo una serie de trabajos de acondicionamiento.  
Los restos que se conservan de la edificación del siglo XVI, de la que se llegó a decir que era “la mejor casa de caballeros... y mejor que la de muchos grandes”, son escasos. Contó con dos puertas de entrada, una en el lado oriental, que aparece hoy tapiada y de la que solo tenemos algunos testimonios acerca de su carácter gótico hispano-flamenco, y la septentrional, que es la que hoy sirve de acceso desde la calle de la Corredera. Esta fachada presenta dos alineaciones de arcos de medio punto sobre columnas de fustes torsos y una cornisa de bolas.  
Sabemos por los libros de visitas de la orden que en el siglo XVI el palacio tuvo tres patios, dos de ellos con corredores, un corral y dos torres que tenían treinta y cuatro habitaciones. La sala principal del palacio de Luis Zapata, que en la documentación se denomina “Sala Dorada”, estaba en la segunda planta, tenía un oratorio y es muy probable que se cerrara con una cubierta mudéjar.  
De todo ello solo nos ha llegado un claustro cuadrado de dos plantas con arquerías de ladrillo. Las galerías del primer piso están formadas por tres arcos peraltados encuadrados en *alfiz* sobre pilares octogonales, y la segunda planta, con cuatro arcos de medio punto rebajado, igualmente con *alfiz*.

en.name: Arraiolos rug
description:
Arraiolos rugs are one of the most typical forms of manufacture and those with the oldest tradition in the art of embroidery within Portugal. With its beginnings in the end of the 16th century, production reached its apogee in the 18th century, with its decline commencing in the 19th century, when the designs began to become broader and the size of the stitches, began to increase. The quantity of surviving examples allows us to recognise the recourse to various sources of inspiration in the conception of designs, which would themselves evolve throughout time.  
This rug, a piece of oriental influence which is thought to date to the 17th century, was most probably inspired by the so-called “wheel” carpets, a type associated with the “small-pattern Holbein”-type of Turkish carpets. It has a yellow field decorated with stylised flowers and the border is filled with flowers and birds of popular tradition, embroidered in faded pink (originally red), green, blue and yellow. Both the module constituting the base unit of the carpet’s design, as well as the alternated and bi-directional – horizontal and vertical ‒ manner in which it is repeated, forming a veritable grid, allowed it to be transposed into tile form. This is one reason why this type of carpet is also known as the “tile-pattern carpet”. Such is the proximity between the component parts of these forms of artistic creation.
holder: Museum of Portuguese Decorative Arts – Ricardo do Espírito Santo Silva Foundation
keywords: Portuguese carpet; embroidery; Arraiolos stitch; *ponto de Arraiolos*; 17th century
materials: Canvas, wool; wool embroidered on canvas; oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as *ponto de Arraiolos*)
tags: oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as ponto de Arraiolos)

ar.name: صحن أزرق وأبيض يعتمد على نموذج صيني
description: وجدت صناعة الفخار الصينية طريقها إلى الشرق الأوسط قبل الإسلام ولكن تأثيرها أخذ أهمية جديدة بعد وقت قصير من تأسيس الإمبراطورية العباسية في عام 750 وانتقلت العاصمة من سوريا إلى العراق. وظهرت الأشكال الصينية في منتجات القرن التاسع من الأفران في البصرة ، العراق وقلّد صانعو الفخار الجسم الأبيض بزيادة تعتيم زجاجهم بإضافة القصدير. وتأثير البضائع الصينية كان يتجلى بشكل أكبر في العصر المغولي عندما حكم الإلخانيون (1256-1353 ) وهم أقارب للمغول حكام الصين (سلالة يوان 1279-1368)  إيران ولكن لا شيء يقارن بالتأثير الشامل للبورسلين المستورد الصيني الأزرق والأبيض على الإنتاج الفارسي من الفخار. ومن حوالي عام 1600 فإن دفعة جديدة لتجارة البورسلين أتت من تأسيس الشركة الهولندية والإنجليزية لشرق الهند حيث أن كميات كبيرة من البورسلين كانت في طريقها إلى أوربا من الشرق الأدنى في سفنهم وقد فرغت في موانئ إيران واستجابة لتدفق البروسلين الصيني فقد قام  الإيرانيون بجهود كبيرة لتقليده .

en.name: Blue-and-white dish based on a Chinese model
description: Chinese pottery had found its way into the Middle East before Islam, but its impact took on new importance shortly after the founding of the Abbasid Empire in 750 and the move of the capital from Syria to Iraq. Chinese shapes appeared in the 9th-century products of the kilns at Basra, Iraq, and potters emulated the white body by increasing the opacity of their glazes by adding tin. The impact of Chinese goods was especially felt during the Mongol period, when the Ilkhanids (1256–1353)—relatives of the Mongol rulers of China (Yuan dynasty 1279–1368)—ruled Iran. However, nothing compares with the overwhelming influence of Chinese blue-and-white porcelain imports on Persian pottery. From around 1600, a new boost to the porcelain trade came from the founding of the Dutch and English East Indies companies. Large quantities of porcelain, on its way to Europe from the Far East in their ships, were off-loaded in the ports of Iran. In response to this influx of Chinese porcelain, Persian potters made great efforts to simulate it.
artist: Black square potter’s mark on base

ar.name: قلعة الحصن.
description:
تقع المنشأة بين مرفأ طرطوس ومدينة حمص، وتمتد على الجزء الجنوبي من الجبال الساحلية على ارتفاع 650م حيث يمكن منها مراقبة فتحة حمص، وهي الممر الرئيس بين المنطقة الداخلية لبلاد الشام الواقعة تحت سيطرة المسلمين، وبين الشريط الساحلي الذي يسيطر عليه الصليبيون.  
شغل الكلابيون الموقع عام 422/ 1031 حيث كان مقراً لحامية كردية، وعرف منذ ذلك الوقت باسم حصن الأكراد، إلا أن الشكل العام للموقع المحصن أخذ شكله النهائي بعد سيطرة الصليبيين عليه عام 504/ 1110، ولاسيما بعد تسليمه لفرسان القديس يوحنا المعروفين باسم الإسبتارية عام 537/ 1142. وقد بقي في حوزة الصليبيين لأكثر من 120 عاماً قبل أن يسقط في أيدي السلطان المملوكي الظاهر بيبرس عام 669/ 1271، ويدخل تحت الحكم المملوكي. تم ترميم القلعة وإعادة تحصينها لتصبح رمزاً للقوة المملوكية في المنطقة، ومقراً للحاكم المملوكي، وبقيت ذات صفة عسكرية حتى نهاية الفترة العثمانية عندما سكنت من قبل القرويين حتى فترة الانتداب. وقد تم ترميمها وإفراغها من السكان خلال القرن العشرين، وسميت قلعة الحصن خلال خمسينيات القرن العشرين.  
تقع القلعة على مرتفع بازلتي شبه منحرف يفصله عن الجبل في الجانب الجنوبي خندق صناعي، وتنقسم القلعة إلى منطقتين دفاعيتين متكاملتين. لقد تم تنظيم القلعة العليا، المبنية على نتوء صخري في وسط الموقع، حول فسحة سماوية مركزية، ولها سور مزدوج شبه منحرف، وهي تتضمن المباني الأكثر إثارة للإعجاب التي تم بناؤها خلال سيطرة الفرنجة، وتضم المجمع المعماري الديني المؤلف من كنيسة صغيرة وغرفة ورواقاً، ومقراً محصناً بني على الجهة الجنوبية، وهو يتألف من ثلاثة أبراج ضخمة تستعمل مركزاً للعمليات، ومقراً لإقامة الصفوة من الإسبتارية. وحول القلعة المرتفعة، تحوي الفسحة السماوية المنخفضة بقايا معمارية لمنشآت صليبية كالأسوار الغربية والشمالية، والإسطبل، والبركة على الجهة الجنوبية والمدخل المحصن على الجهة الشمالية.  
تظهر مساهمة المماليك واضحة في بناء القلعة إذ تشكل جزءاً أساساً فيها، وقد تم إنجاز أغلب الأعمال الهامة خلال الثلث الأخير من القرن السابع/ الثالث عشر، وأدى إلى تحسين كبير في الدفاعات التي بناها الإسبتارية، فقد تم إنشاء أسوار وأبراج جديدة على الواجهات الجنوبية والشرقية للفسحة السفلى تعلوها سلسلة ممرات مزودة بالسقاطات والرواشن (فتحات الرمي ومقصورات الرماة). وقد أدى استخدام المماليك للقلعة كمركز إداري محلي إلى تطوير المباني السكنية والقصر كمنزل الحاكم أعلى المقر المحصن، والغرف المزخرفة أعلى القلعة والحمام في الفسحة السفلى.

حصن الأكراد، وسُمِّي بهذا الاسم تيمناً بالأكراد الذين سكنوا القلعة خلال القرن الخامس الهجري/ الحادي عشر الميلادي، اعتُبر المكان ذا أهمية عسكرية ودفاعية، خلال فترة إحتلال الفرنجة، وخصوصاً من قبل الفرسان والقادة العسكريين الذين سكنوها. حافظ الفرنجة على هذا الموقع الإستراتيجي أكثر من 120 سنة، والذي اعتبر من أروع المباني العسكرية وأرقاها. واحتوى أيضاً على كنيسة صغيرة تعود للقرن السادس الهجري/ الثاني عشر الميلادي، والتي تظهر فيها معالم من العمارة الرومانية، وكذلك مبنى مقنطر يعود للقرن السابع الهجري/ الثالث عشر الميلادي، والمرتبط بالطراز القوطي الفرنسي.
dynasty: السلاجقة الكلابيون (422-504/ 1031-1110)؛ كونت طرابلس (4-537/ 10-1142)؛ فرسان القديس يوحنا- الأسبتارية (537-669/ 1142-1271)؛ .المماليك (669/ 1271- القرن السادس عشر)
artist: فرسان الأسبتارية والسلطان المملوكي بيبرس (58-676/ 60-1277)؛ بركة خان (6-678/ 7-1279)؛ المنصور قلاوون (78-689/ 79-1290)؛ الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (الذي حكم ثلاث مرات: 3-694/ 3-1294؛ 698-708/ 1299-1309؛ 9-741/ 10-1341).
keywords: إسبتاري؛ أكراد؛ الجبال الساحلية؛ سقاطة؛ صليبي؛ عمارة عسكرية؛ قلعة؛ كتابة.
