en.name: Tekke '*ensi*' rug
description: *Ensi* or *engsi* rugs are often treated by art historians as door hangings of a yurt, a traditional Turkmen nomadic tent. Covering the doorway of the tent *ensi* was supposedly destined to preserve the inside temperature from winter and summer extremes. There is also a different opinion that suggests treating *ensi* as a ritual rug used only for special social and cult occasions. *Ensi* is considered a complex kind of Turkmen rug in the aspects of design and iconography. Here in the middle of the carpet there is a cruciform composition of two broad stripes filled with small geometric elements. Small hooked motifs of various kinds also fill the four rectangular fields formed by the central "cross" and several stripes of border. Above the central field there is a stylized image of the tent or a *mihrab*. The design of the carpet is known as "*hatchli*" and is typical for Tekke, one of the major tribes of Turkmen. Ethnographic studies suggest the connection of a central cross-like pattern with the idea of rivers and canals, while a variety of smaller elements - with sheep and cattle, together with water make up the main resources of nomads' lives. The background of the carpet is dark ruby, other colours of the pattern include lighter shade of red, dark blue, brown and ivory white.
keywords: Rug; carpet; textile; ensi; Turkmen; Central Asia
materials: Wool (warp, weft and pile); asymmetrically knotted pile
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: The crown of king Carol I
short_description: Three years after obtaining its independence from the Ottoman Empire, Romania was declared a kingdom in March 1881. The coronation of prince Carol of Hohenzollern and his wife, Elisabeth, was settled for 10 May. Although the government wanted expensive and richly adorned crowns to be bought for the sovereigns, the king expressed his wish that his crown was made from the steel of a Turkish cannon captured by the Romanian army during the Independence War (the Russo-Ottoman war of 1877-1878), when Romania was Russia’s ally against the Ottoman Empire. Entirely of steel, the crown was made by the craftsmen working at the Army’s Arsenal. Queen Elisabeth’s crown was a smaller golden replica of the steel one and was made by an Austrian jeweler that had set up a workshop in Bucharest.

ar.name: مناظر صيد.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن لوحة فريسكو تقع في الشريط العلوي في الجدار الغربي لقاعة الاستقبال في قصير عمرة. تصوّر اللوحة منظراً يمثل مجموعة من الحمر البرية داخل منطقة مطوّقة يتم مطاردتها نحو شبكة لصيدها. يظهر بجانب الشبكة أشكال تشبه الدّمى تحمل مشاعل لإخافة الحيوانات وجعلها تتجه نحو الشبكة. يُشاهد في اللوحة، بين الحيوانات المسرعة، ثلاثة رجال يمتطون خيولاً مسرعة. الرجل الذي يظهر في أقصى يسار اللوحة (الناحية الجنوبية) يبدو كأنه سقط تواً عن صهوة حصانه.  
  
هناك منظر في الجدار الشمالي من الجناح الشرقي لقاعة الاستقبال يصوّر حيوانات محشورة تجز وتضرب بالرماح من قبل بعض الصيادين. يبدو أن هذا المنظر الأخير تكملة للمنظر الأول، فبعد مطاردة الحيوانات البرية وحشرها يتم صيدها وقتلها.

هذه اللوحة الفسيفسائية، موجودة في قاعة استقبال قُصيِّر عمرة، وتُصوِّر قطيعاً من حُمُر الوحش، يُساق عبر حظيرة مُسيَّجة إلى شبكة. مُنجزة بالاستناد إلى الإحساس بالحركة، كما في المشاهد الشرق أوسطية، تُبيِّن اللوحة أن الصيد رياضة، وتسلية ممتعة.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن 2 ﻫ/ 8 م.
keywords: صيد؛ فريسكو؛ لوحة جدارية جصية.

en.name: Fresco panel: ‘Hunting Scene’.
description:
A hunting scene that occupies the entire upper register of the western wall in the audience hall of Qusayr ‘Amra. The scene depicts a group of onagers within a fenced enclosure; they are being driven towards a net where they will be trapped. Alongside the fence are a number of puppet-like figures holding torches, apparently to scare the animals into the trap.  
  
In between the onagers (seemingly running at full speed) one can detect three men mounted on galloping horses; the horseman on the extreme left (south) side has just fallen off his horse. This scene, rendered with so much feeling for movement, savours strongly the hunting scenes in the mosaic pavements of Piazza Armerina in Sicily, and in Tunisia, for unlike Sassanid hunting scenes where the king appears as the central figure and the aim of the scene is to glorify the king and his prowess, the hunting scene at Qusayr ‘Amra depicts hunting as a pleasurable pastime and thus comes closer to the Mediterranean representation of hunting. What may well be a sequence to this scene is represented on the north wall of the eastern bay. The panel here depicts the trapped animals being speared and disembowelled by hunters, who are bare-footed and wear knee-length tunics with long, loose sleeves.

This fresco is in the audience hall of Qusayr ‘Amra and depicts a group of onagers driven through a fenced enclosure towards a net. Rendered with a sense for movement, similar to Mediterranean scenes, it shows hunting as a pleasurable pastime.
dates: Hegira first third of the 2nd century / AD first half of the 8th century.
keywords: Fresco; Hunting scene.

es.name: Fresco de escena de caza
description:
Escena de caza que ocupa todo el registro superior de la pared occidental del salón de audiencias de Qusayr Amra. La escena representa un grupo de onagros dentro de un cercado que están siendo dirigidos hacia una red donde quedarán atrapados. Al lado del cercado aparecen varias figuras que parecen marionetas y que portan antorchas, aparentemente para asustar a los animales y llevarlos hacia la trampa.  
En medio de los onagros (que parecen correr a gran velocidad) se distingue a tres hombres montados a lomos de caballos al galope. El jinete del extremo izquierdo (sur) se acaba de caer de la montura. Esta escena, que transmite una gran sensación de movimiento, recuerda en gran medida a las escenas de caza de Túnez o de los suelos de mosaico de Piazza Armerina (Sicilia). Es distinta a las escenas sasánidas de caza que ensalzaban al rey –que aparecía como protagonista– y sus hazañas, ya que aquí se muestra la caza como pasatiempo placentero, más al estilo mediterráneo. En el muro norte de la crujía oriental hay una escena que bien podría ser la continuación de esta; se trata de un panel que representa a los animales atrapados, ahora atravesados con lanzas y destripados por los cazadores, que están descalzos y visten túnicas hasta las rodillas, de largas y holgadas mangas.

Fresco del salón de audiencias de Qusayr Amra que representa a un grupo de onagros conducidos hacia una trampa a través de un cercado. Transmite sensación de movimiento; al igual que las escenas mediterráneas, representa la caza como un pasatiempo placentero.
holder: En su emplazamiento original, Qusayr Amra.
dates: Primer tercio del siglo II de la Hégira / primera mitad del siglo VIII d. C.
keywords: Fresco; escena de caza.

fr.name: Panneau de fresque, “Scène de chasse”.
description:
Scène de chasse occupant l'entière partie supérieure du mur occidental de la salle d'audience de Qousayr Amra. Elle représente un groupe d'onagres (apparemment) dans un enclos, poussé vers un filet où il sera piégé. Le long de la clôture, quelques figures grossièrement représentées tiennent des torches, sans doute pour effrayer les animaux.  
Au milieu de ces onagres qui se déplacent très vite, se repèrent trois hommes montés sur des chevaux au galop. Le cavalier à l'extrême gauche (sud) vient de tomber de sa monture. Cette scène pleine de mouvement rappelle fortement d'autres similaires observées en Tunisie ou sur les sols de mosaïque de Piazza Amerina en Sicile. à la différence des scènes de chasse sassanides qui montrent un roi occupant la place centrale d'une mise en scène à sa gloire, celle de Qousayr Amra décrit les plaisirs de la chasse et se rapproche des représentations méditerranéennes de cette activité. Sur le mur septentrional de la travée orientale figure ce qui pourrait être la suite de la première scène : les animaux piégés sont tués et éventrés à coups de pieux par des chasseurs pieds nus qui portent des tuniques descendant aux genoux et à longues manches flottantes.

Cette fresque se trouve dans la salle d’audience de Qousayr Amra et représente un groupe d’onagres conduits dans un enclos et poussés vers un filet. Rendue avec un sens accusé du mouvement, rappelant des scènes méditerranéennes similaires, elle décrit la chasse comme un loisir agréable.
dates: Premier tiers du IIe siècle de l’Hégire (première moitié du VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: fresques ; scènes de chasse

de.name: Hochaltar
description: Einem venezianischen Typus folgend verzichtet der Hochaltar auf ein Retabel zugunsten eines von Statuen flankierten Tabernakels, den ein Ziborium bekrönt. Die Marmorbildwerke der Ordensheiligen Scholastika, Gallus, Columban und Benedikt zählen zu den Meisterwerken ihres Schöpfers.
artist: Entwurf: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1652-1717); Skulpturen: Franz Anton Sturm (1690-1757)

en.name: High altar
description: Following a Venetian type, the high altar does not feature a retable, favouring a tabernacle flanked by statues and crowned with a ciborium. The marble statues of saints of the Benedictine Order, St. Scholastica, St. Gallus, St. Columbanus and St. Benedict, are masterpieces of the sculptor, Franz Anton Sturm, and rank among his best works.
artist: Design: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1652–1717); Sculptures: Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757)
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Church of Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres
description:
The church of Beja (1672) has a quadrangular nave covered by a tunnel vault; a narrower and lower chancel, a semi-circular apse – finished with a cupola and louvre – and a quadrangular addorsed sacristy, also covered with a vault.  
The church is an excellent example of a “total work of art” or *gesamtkunstwerk*, a sensibility often associated with Baroque interiors. The interior, a *theatrum* *sacrum*, holds within it the wood carvings of Manuel João da Fonseca and Francisco da Silva, which reflect the dialogue between the artistic schools of Lisbon and Évora. The ceiling compositions by Pedro Figueira, António de Oliveira Bernardes and João Pereira Pegado, who were influenced by the Beja masters, continue the artistic dialogue. Oliveira Bernardes' canvases and Gabriel del Barco's tile work represent the Mysteries of the Life of the Virgin, enhancing the theme of the Immaculate Conception.

The church of Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres in Beja lies close to the medieval city wall. Built in veneration of Our Lady, its importance was intensified by a miracle said to have taken place on a farm in Lisbon in the 16th century. Later, during the reign of King Pedro II, the church underwent renovation, turning it into one of the best examples of “plain” architecture and interior decoration in the Lower Alentejo. A remarkable example of a “Golden Church”, it is enriched with *azulejos*, gilded woodcarving, wall painting and canvases devoted to the Mysteries of the Life of Virgin, focusing on the co-existence of the Seven Sorrows and the Seven Joys of the Mother of God.
artist: Brotherhood of Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres

Woodcarvers: João de Touro Freitas [n.d.], António de Oliveira (1675–?), Manuel João da Fonseca [n.d.], Francisco da Silva (1684-?); painters: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732), Pedro Figueira [n.d.], João Pereira Pegado (1662–1732); tile painter: Gabriel del Barco (1649–1703?)
history: During the 16th century a door was opened in the medieval wall of Beja allowing access to the main square, near the *Corredoura* (a road used for horse racing). Our Lady of Pleasures Church was built in veneration of the Miracle of Our Lady and to eulogise the Seven Sorrows and the Seven Joys of the Mother of God, the importance of which was further intensified by a miracle said to have taken place on a farm near Lisbon. According to tradition, the Virgin appeared to a girl and asked her to tell her parents and neighbours that a chapel should be built close by. Thereafter, a series of other miracles aroused intense devotional outbreaks in the country and overseas territories, and these accelerated the construction of even more places of worship.
keywords: International Baroque, ceiling painting, *di sotto* *in sù*, illusionistic painting, *trompe l'œil*, *gesamtkunstwerk*, total work of art, architecture, Golden Church, António de Oliveira Bernardes, Immaculate Conception, Beja
tags: International Baroque, ceiling painting, di sotto in sù, illusionistic painting, trompe l'œil, gesamtkunstwerk, total work of art, architecture, Golden Church, António de Oliveira Bernardes, Immaculate Conception, Beja
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres
description: A igreja (1672) possui nave quadrangular coberta por abóbada de berço, capela-mor mais estreita e baixa, abside semicircular, com cúpula e lanternim, e sacristia quadrangular adossada, também coberta por abóbada. Trata-se de um brilhante exemplo de uma “obra de arte total” (*gesamtkunstwerk*), que corresponde a um modelo muito desenvolvido na arquitectura barroca. O interior, um *theatrum sacrum*, revestido pela talha dourada de Manuel João da Fonseca e Francisco da Silva, reflecte o diálogo das escolas artísticas de Lisboa e de Évora. As composições murais de Pedro Figueira, António de Oliveira Bernardes e João Pereira Pegado, que evidenciam o alto nível dos mestres bejenses, ampliam esse diálogo. As telas do mesmo Oliveira Bernardes e os azulejos de Gabriel del Barco representam os mistérios da vida de Maria, reforçando o tema da Imaculada Conceição.

A igreja de Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres foi construída junto à muralha medieval da cidade. Consagrada a Maria, reflecte uma devoção característica da época pós-tridentina, quando este culto atingiu o auge, após um milagre ocorrido em certa quinta de Alcântara, em Lisboa, no século XVI. Datando do reinado de D. Pedro II, constitui exemplo notável de uma “igreja de ouro”, em que a talha dourada anda a par de azulejos, de pinturas murais e a óleo sobre tela alusivos aos mistérios da vida da Virgem, que enaltecem as Sete Dores e as Sete Alegrias da Mãe de Deus.
artist: Irmandade de Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres.

Entalhadores: João de Touro Freitas [n.d.], António de Oliveira (1675–n.d.), Manuel João da Fonseca [n.d.], Francisco da Silva (1684-n.d.); pintores: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732), Pedro Figueira [n.d.], João Pereira Pegado (1662–1732); pintor de azulejos: Gabriel del Barco (1649–c. 1703).
history: A necessidade de tornar mais fácil o acesso à principal praça de Beja levou à abertura, no século XVI, de uma porta na muralha medieval, perto da Corredoura. Surgida junto a este postigo, a igreja de Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres evoca a devoção às Sete Dores e às Sete Alegrias da Mãe de Deus. Este culto intensificou-se em meados do século XVI, devido a um milagre ocorrido numa quinta de Alcântara, junto a Lisboa. De acordo com a tradição, a Virgem apareceu a uma menina e pediu-lhe para dizer aos pais e aos vizinhos que fizessem aí uma capela em sua honra. Construída a ermida, começaram as curas milagrosas, o que despertou um intenso movimento devocional. Em vários pontos do país e dos territórios ultramarinos, surgiram igrejas e capelas sob a mesma invocação.
keywords: Barroco internacional, pintura de tecto, *di sotto in sú*, pintura ilusionista, *trompe l'œil*, *gesamtkunstwerk*, obra de arte total, arquitectura, Igreja de Ouro, António de Oliveira Bernardes, Imaculada Conceição, Beja.
tags: Barroco internacional, pintura de tecto, di sotto in sú, pintura ilusionista, trompe l'œil, gesamtkunstwerk, obra de arte total, arquitectura, Igreja de Ouro, António de Oliveira Bernardes, Imaculada Conceição, Beja.

en.name: Medallion carpet with hunting animals
description:
This beautiful medallion carpet was woven in Iran, probably in the first half of the sixteenth century, during the reign of the Safavid dynasty. While it does not have any inscriptions linking it with a specific patron, place or date, the design holds many parallels with the arts of the book in early Safavid Iran.  
  
Despite its large scale, the carpet has a fine and complex design that rewards very close inspection. In its general layout, there are two lobed black medallions down the central axis, with four diagonal radiating oval pendants each, all set against a dark red main field. These medallions are then repeated by quarter-medallions in the four corners of the field, and by two half-medallions on either side. Each medallion is filled with a very refined radial design of yellow strapwork and large flowers, while each oval pendant is occupied by fluttering birds and Chinese-style cloudbands. Below this medallion superstructure, the red main field is a rich and varied garden landscape of trees filled with wildlife. There are trees with white blossoms, and others filled with ripe pomegranates. There are also leafy spiralling stems, with large lotus flowers. Among this greenery, the carpet is filled with animals and birds: there are resting pairs of spotted goats, lions and treetop birds. Predominantly though, the main field is full of hunting scenes: leopards killing horned goats, hawks killing long-legged water birds and lions killing stags. Down the central axis of the design, there are ornate Chinese style vases, formed of dragons, lions and peacocks, and lobed ponds full of fish.  
Beyond the main field, the main border features a reciprocal pattern, of an interlocking arcade in red versus black (or rather extremely dark blue indigo). On a slightly more condensed scale to the main field, this border also features hunting pairs: a snow leopard attacking a horned goat, and a lion pinning down a bull. A beautifully drawn pair of supernatural creatures confront each other in the dark blue arcading: a Chinese-style dragon opposite a long-tailed phoenix. Throughout the main and two minor borders, the design also features overlaid designs of leafy plant scrolls and Chinese cloudband motifs.  
  
[V&A online catalogue link](http://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O85144/the-chelsea-carpet-carpet-unknown/)
keywords: Iran; animals; birds; Safavids; hunting; hunters; medallions; trees; gardens
materials:
Wool; knotted pile; silk; warp and weft.  
Wool pile on silk foundation, depressed warps, asymmetrical knots open to the left.
tags: warp and weft. Wool pile on silk foundation, depressed warps, asymmetrical knots open to the left.

ar.name: إبريق.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن إبريق من النحاس المكفت بالفضة عليه زخارف وكتابات بخط النسخ نصها "المقر الأشرف العالي طبطق عز نصره." ويظهر على الإبريق شعارات (رنوك) تحمل رسم كأس يدل على وظيفة الساقي. ويظهر في أعلى بدن الإبريق شريط به ما يشبه دوائر بارزة رسم بداخل كل منها طائران متقابلان. وزينت فوهة الإبريق بزخارف نباتية، كما زوّدت بغطاء بمفصلين وبمصفاة وضعت في داخلها. وللإبريق مصب يزخرفه ثلاثة أشرطة يحمل أوسطها كتابة دعائية بخط النسخ، بينما يحتوي الشريطان الآخران على معينات رسم بداخلها زخرفة نباتية. ويرجع الاسم الذي يحمله الإبريق إلى الأمير طبطق، وهو من أمراء الملك الأشرف خليل الذي حكم في الفترة 689 – 693 هـ / 1290 – 1294 م. وكان طبطق حاكماً لمدينة قوص في صعيد مصر أثناء فترة الحكم الثالثة للسلطان الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (709 - 741هـ / 1309-1340 م).  
  
وقد ازدهرت صناعة الأباريق في إيران، ثم انتقلت إلى العراق ومنها إلى مصر في العصرين الأيوبي والمملوكي. وتعددت أشكال ووظائف الأباريق حيث استخدمت لصب الماء للاستحمام وغسل اليدين والوضوء. كما استخدمت الأباريق المميزة في تزيين قصور وبيوت الأمراء والسلاطين.

ترجع أهمية هذا الإبريق إلى جمال ودقة زخارفه، وأنه يحمل اسم الأمير طبطق، أحد أمراء السلطان الناصر محمد، ورنك الساقي (الكأس)، الذي يرمز إلى وظيفته، وقد عُرفت الأباريق في إيران، وانتقلت منها إلى العراق ومصر، وتعدَّدت أشكالها واستُخدمت في الاستحمام والوضوء وغسل الأيدي، في بيوت وقصور الأمراء.
keywords: إبريق؛ تكفيت؛ خط؛ خط النسخ؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ نحاس.

en.name: Ewer.
description:
A ewer made of copper and inlaid with silver. Decorated with ornamentation and inscriptions in *naskhi* script; the text reads: 'The honourable Excellency, Tabtaq. Glory to his triumph'. Blazons decorate the surface of the ewer, bearing depictions of a goblet, thereby alluding to the position of cupbearer. Adorning the upper section of the ewer's body is a decorative band featuring a series of prominent roundels inside each of which is depicted a pair of confronting birds. The mouth is decorated with vegetal motifs and is equipped with a two-hinge cover and a strainer, which sits inside the mouth. The spout of the ewer has three decorative bands: the middle one carries propagandistic inscriptions in the *naskhi* script, while the other two are adorned with diamond-shaped units filled with vegetal motifs. The name on the ewer dates back to Amir Tabtaq, one of the elite officers of al-Malik al-Ashraf Khalil, who ruled from AH 689–93 / AD 1290–4. Tabtaq was Governor of the City of Qus in Upper Egypt during the third reign of the Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. A.H. 709–41 / AD 1309–40).  
The crafting of ewers was an industry that flourished in Iran; it then transferred to Iraq and from there to Egypt, during the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods. The different forms of ewers and the roles that they played were manifold; they were used to pour water for bathing, for hand-washing, or for *wudu* (obligatory ablutions before prayer). However, ornamental ewers were used to decorate the palaces and houses of *amirs* and sultans.

The importance of this ewer stems from its fine decoration. It bears the name of Amir Tabtaq, a follower of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, and a cup blazon, the emblem of his post as cupbearer. Ewers came to Egypt and Iraq from Persia and took many shapes. They were used in palaces and houses for bathing, hand-washing and obligatory ablutions.
keywords: Ewer; inlay; inscription; naskhi script; epigraphic decoration; copper; blazon; propaganda

es.name: Aguamanil.
description:
Aguamanil de cobre con incrustaciones de plata decorado con distintos adornos e inscripciones en caligrafía *nasji* que dicen: "Su honorable Excelencia, Tabtaq. Gloria a su triunfo". La superficie del aguamanil presenta unos blasones en los que aparece representada una copa, símbolo del cargo de copero. La decoración de la parte superior del cuerpo consta de una banda con una serie de medallones en relieve en cuyo interior se muestran dos pájaros afrontados. La boca está decorada con motivos vegetales y provista de una tapa con dos bisagras y un filtro interior. El pitorro del aguamanil tiene tres bandas decorativas: en la del medio figuran inscripciones propagandísticas en caligrafía *nasji*, mientras que las otras dos presentan rombos con adornos vegetales en el interior.  
El emir Tabtaq, uno de los oficiales de elite de al-Malik al-Ashraf Jalil (r. 689-693 / 1290-1294), fue luego gobernador de la ciudad de Qus, en el Alto Egipto, durante el tercer sultanato de al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (709-741 / 1309-1340).  
La fabricación de aguamaniles floreció en Irán, después pasó a Irak y, de ahí, a Egipto durante los periodos ayyubí y mameluco. Las formas y las funciones de los aguamaniles eran diversas: se utilizaban para verter el agua para bañarse o lavarse las manos, o para el *wudu* (ablución obligatoria previas a la oración). No obstante, también se utilizaban como adorno en los palacios y las casas de emires y sultanes.

La importancia de este aguamanil radica en su decoración. Lleva el nombre de Tabtaq, emir del sultán al-Nasir Mohammad, y el emblema del cargo de copero. Los aguamaniles procedían de Irak y Persia y tenían muchas formas. Se usaban en palacios y viviendas para verter el agua del baño, lavarse las manos o hacer las abluciones.
keywords: Aguamanil; incrustación; inscripción; escritura nasji; decoración epigráfica; cobre; blasón; propaganda.

fr.name: Aiguière.
description:
Aiguière en cuivre à décor incrusté d'argent et inscriptions en style *naskhi* dont le texte se lit : “L'honorable Excellence, Tabtaq, Gloire à son triomphe”. Les blasons comportent un gobelet, ce qui désigne la charge d'échanson occupée par le propriétaire de l'objet. En partie supérieure, un bandeau décoratif présente une série de rondeaux en relief à décor d'oiseaux affrontés. L'embouchure décorée de motifs végétaux est dotée d'un couvercle à double charnière et d'un filtre interne. Le bec présente trois bandeaux décoratifs : celui du milieu est inscrit d'un texte de propagande en écriture *naskhi*, l'autre, orné d'éléments en pointe de diamant, est meublé de motifs végétaux. Le nom mentionné renvoie à l'émir Tabtaq, l'un des officiers d'élite de al-Malik al-Achraf Khalil qui régna de 689 à 693 H / 1290-1294 J.-C. Tabtaq fut gouverneur de la ville de Qous en Haute-égypte au cours du troisième règne du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. 709-741 H / 1309-1340 J.-C.).  
La fabrication d'aiguières était une activité florissante en Iran, d'où elle se transféra vers l'Irak puis l'égypte sous les Ayyoubides et les Mamelouks. Les formes et fonctions de ces objets étaient multiples : verser l'eau du bain, laver les mains et l'accomplissement du *woudou* (ablutions obligatoires avant la prière). Des aiguières purement ornementales décoraient également les palais et les résidences des sultans et des émirs.

L'importance de cette aiguière vient de sa décoration admirable. Elle porte le nom de l'émir Tabtaq, un disciple du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, et un blason à gobelet, symbole de sa charge d'échanson. Les aiguières arrivaient d'Égypte et d'Irak venant de Perse et avaient de multiples formes. On s'en servait dans les palais et les maisons pour verser l'eau du bain, se laver les mains et pour les ablutions obligatoires.
keywords: Aiguières ; inscriptions ; écriture naskhi ; décoration épigraphique ; cuivre ; blasons ; propagande

en.name: *Shéhérazade*
short_description: George Auriol, the typographer renamed after his creations, was a multitalented artist, and thus in his work he reflected many different influences of the late 19th century. As an artist and musician, he was interested in the different graphic movements, as is clear from this image: the theme is clearly "Oriental", but the composition of the piece borrows characteristics from Japanese aesthetics and Art Nouveau.
keywords: Orientalism; Art Nouveau

fr.name: *Schéhérazade*
short_description: George Auriol, typographe renommé pour ses créations, est un artiste polyvalent reflétant les influences diverses de la fin du XIXe siècle. Tour à tour dessinateur, chansonnier, il s'intéresse à divers mouvements graphiques comme en témoigne la composition de cette *Sheherazade*: influence orientale dans la thématique; composition empruntant au japonisme et à l'Art Nouveau.
keywords: Orientalisme; Art Nouveau

en.name: Colonial school in Paris, project of M. Maurice Yvon
names: *Longitudinal view; Plan of the first floor*
short_description: In 1885, the French diplomat Auguste Pavie brought thirteen young Khmers to Paris so that they could see France. This "Cambodian mission" was soon transformed into a colonial school which accepted young students of French, Cambodian or African origins in order to train the future civil servants of the colonies. Over first two, then three, years the students studied a variety of languages, French law, and ethnology. in 1895 the architect Maurice Yvon, son of an Orientalist painter, was appointed as the architect for a specialist school on 2 Rue de l'Observatoire. Insipired by "neo-Moorish" architecture, the resulting structure became a key example of "colonial art".
keywords: France; colonialism

fr.name: Ecole coloniale à Paris, projet de Mr M. Yvon.
short_description: En 1885, Auguste Pavie, diplomate français, fait venir à Paris treize jeunes Khmers pour que ceux-ci découvrent la France. Cette « Mission cambodgienne » se transforme progressivement en une École coloniale qui accueille de jeunes stagiaires d’origine française, cambodgienne ou africaine afin de former les futurs fonctionnaires des colonies françaises. En deux ans (puis trois), les élèves apprennent diverses langues et des notions de droit et d’ethnologie. En 1895, l’architecte Maurice Yvon, fils d’un peintre orientaliste, est chargé de bâtir une école spécifique au 2 rue de l’Observatoire. Le résultat, d’inspiration « néo-mauresque », devint une vitrine de « l’art colonial ».
keywords: France; colonisation

short_description: The Egyptian women of the 1919 Revolution – one of the most important Egyptian revolutions in modern times – which started due to objections to the practices of British occupation and the exile of symbols of Egyptian patriotism.

cs.name: Sv. Barbora
description:
V 60. letech byly oltáře doplněny o predelové obrazy J. Jablonského, usedlého

en.name: Tray (*sinija*)
description:
The term *sinija* (Tr. sini) refers to a large circular brass or copper tray, that functioned as a low table on which food and beverages were served.  
This large, circular plate is decorated with the court life theme. In the center of the composition is a large scene depicting the ruler on the throne, surrounded by courtiers, servants, musicians, and dancers, with small tables with jugs and cups. The central scene is encircled with small medallions with seated human figures in each of them. The background is filled with floral and vegetal patterns, as in the case of the next decorative band. In that band, there are twelve roundels with alternately combined court life scenes and inscriptions – verses from Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat and Ghazaliyat of Hafiz. Next to the raised sides and lobbed rim is the last decorative frieze, with medallions with, again, seated human figures and animals.

en.name: Historical Town
description:
Serpa is one of those towns where one can sense the continuity of human occupation, its long evolution over the centuries, marked by the coexistence and superimposition of successive historical settlements.  
The town’s past still remains somewhat unclear so that only fresh archaeological finds in the urban area can help to provide more precise information. Although the intense use made of the town’s spaces and the juxtaposition of everyday activities make it difficult to interpret the original urban fabric two main centres of activity can be identified.  
At one end of the town, at its highest point, is the Old Castle, as it has come to be known popularly, marking the oldest perimeter of the settlement. It was there that the first houses appeared, protected by a castle and its walls, and where there is now a small residential quarter of low houses and narrow winding streets. Indifferent to its neighbouring lay-buildings, the Parish Church of Santa Maria, believed to be a consecrated former mosque, stands proudly.  
At the other end of the town, the walls built by D. Dinis formed an enclosure that became the town’s residential and administrative centre from the 14th-15th centuries onwards.  
Although there is little doubt that cities reflect complex forms of social organisation, it is nonetheless commonplace to speak of the aristocratic features of the town of Serpa. With its many examples of erudite architecture and its noble houses proudly displaying their family crests, Serpa is also extremely rich aesthetically, in terms of the decorative air given to the walls of its “poor” inhabitants’ houses. It is after all, this town’s whitewashed houses that make it so full of light.

es.name: Conjunto urbano
description:
Serpa es uno de esos lugares donde ha dejado huella la continuidad de la ocupación humana, en una evolución de siglos marcada por la coexistencia y superposición de sucesivos estratos históricos.  
El pasado de la villa tiene, con todo, perfiles poco claros que solo los hallazgos arqueológicos en el área urbana podrán precisar. Pese a que la intensidad en el uso de los espacios y la yuxtaposición de vidas cotidianas dificultan la lectura del tejido urbano, se perciben claramente dos polos generadores principales.  
Por un lado, el popularmente conocido como Castelo Velho (Castillo Viejo), punto más alto del pueblo, representa su perímetro más antiguo. Allí, donde surgieron las primeras viviendas, protegidas por un castillo con sus murallas, se encuentra hoy un pequeño barrio de casas bajas, y calles estrechas y sinuosas. Indiferente a las construcciones seculares de sus inmediaciones se alza la iglesia mayor de Santa María, que se supone antigua mezquita sacralizada.  
Por otro lado, el recinto de murallas que mandó construir D. Dinis constituyó el foco congregador y regulador del entramado urbano a partir de los siglos XIV-XV.  
Puesto que las ciudades reflejan formas complejas de organización social, es un lugar común hablar de los rasgos aristocráticos de la villa de Serpa. Verdadero depósito de conjuntos arquitectónicos de carácter cultural, de casas hidalgas que orgullosamente ostentan blasones familiares, Serpa es también rica por la grandeza plástica de los alzados de las casas del pueblo “pobre”. Finalmente, es el blanco de la cal lo que vuelve a esta villa tan luminosa.

cs.name: Klášter benediktinů Rajhrad
description:
Konventní chrám byl obklopen čtyřmi kvadraturami. Před západním průčelím je prelatura, na jihu konvent a na protilehlé straně dva hospodářské dvory. Do kostelní novostavby byly začleněny rozestavěné západní věže z konce 17. století. Stavba se potýkala se statickými problémy bažinatého terénu. Santiniho projekt realizovali brněnský stavitel F. B. Klíčník. Ve výklencích stojí sochy sv. Vojtěcha a sv. poustevníka Vintíře. Štít mezi věžemi je ozdoben mozaikovým obrazem Neposkvrněného početí P. Marie (1895). Chrám trojdílného půdorysu  
s centralizujícím oktogenem má délku 79,5 m. Zmnožené triumfální oblouky umocňují hloubku podélného prostoru, dodávají mu rytmus a monumentalitu. Santiniho projekt kladl důraz na optické působení a počítal s malířskou složkou. Fresky J. J. Etgense (1726–1729) představují oslavení benediktinského řádu a jeho rozšíření v Evropě, Asii a Africe. Fresky nad kůrem znázorňují oslavu Boží zpěvným a hudebním uměním.  
K presbytáři chrámu přiléhá nad sakristií oratoř s oltářem sv. Benedikta. Byla vyzdobeny obrazy malíře J. Zeleného, rajhradského rodáka a prvního učitele Alfonse Muchy.

Klášter patří mezi nejstarší na Moravě a je zde jediným zástupcem řádu benediktinů. Měl velký význam pro rozvoj místní vzdělanosti a hospodářství. Santiniho projekt kladl důraz na optické působení, počítal s malířskou složkou. Fresky J. J. Etgense představují oslavení benediktinského řádu a jeho rozšíření v Evropě, Asii a Africe. Klášter je známý take svou obrazárnou. Sídlí zde Památník písemnictví na Moravě.
artist: Jan Blažej Santini-Aichl (1677 Praha – 1723 Praha), František Benedikt Klíčník (1677 Ivančice – 1755 Brno), Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vídeň), Jan Jiří Etgens (1691 Brno – 1757 Brno), Ignác Lengelacher (1698 Unter Paissenberg – 1780 Baden), Ondřej Schweigl (1735 Brno – 1812 Brno), Josef Winterhalder ml. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)
history: Klášter patří mezi nejstarší na Moravě a je zde jediným zástupcem řádu benediktinů. Vznikl kolem r. 1025 jako odnož kláštera v Praze-Břevnově na místě staršího osídlení. Až do 17. století si uchoval v podstatě románskou podobu (návrh přestavby A. Erna, 1670). R. 1721 byla v souvislosti se snahami o povýšení na opatství  zahájena přestavba, velká část původních staveb byla zbourána. K dokončení všech prací došlo až kolem r. 1840. Od r. 1540 zasedali rajhradští probošti v zemském sněmu. Klášter měl velký význam pro rozvoj vzdělanosti a hospodářství. Založil zde tradici vinohradnictví i pivovarnictví, zasloužil se o budování nemocnic, chudobinců, sirotčinců, od r. 1623 zde fungovala věhlasná škola. Klášter je známý rozsáhlou obrazárnou. Díla získal také ze zrušených klášterů i zámeckých sbírek. Proslulý je tzv. Rajhradský oltář (kolem 1420).

en.name: Benedictine Monastery, Rajhrad
description:
The monastery church was surrounded by four courtyards. In front of the west front is the prelature, in the south section the monastery, and opposite are two farmsteads. Unfinished west spires from the late 17th century were later incorporated into the church building. Structural engineers faced problems with the swampy terrain. Santini’s design was executed by the Brno builder F. B. Klíčník who reduced the number of neo-Gothic motifs, especially at the front. The niches contain statues of St. Vojtěch and the hermit, St. Vintíř. The gable between the spires features a mosaic of the Immaculate Conception (1895). The church, of a triplicate ground plan with a central octagon, is 79.5 m long. Triumphal arches accentuate the depth of the longitudinal space, endowing it with rhythm and monumentality. Santini’s design emphasised the optical effects relying largely on subsequent painting components. J. J. Etgens’s (1726–1729) frescos celebrate the Benedictine order and its spread throughout Europe, Asia and Africa in the first three centuries of its existence. Frescoes above the gallery represent the glorification of the Lord through singing and music.  
Above the sacristy, the church presbytery is adjoined by an oratory with an altar to St. Benedict. It was decorated with pictures by J. Zelený, a native of Rajhrad and the first teacher of the artist Alfons Mucha.

The monastery is one of the largest in South Moravia and the only one owned by the Benedictine order. It played a key role in local education and in the development of the economy. The frescos in the church, by the architect Santini, celebrate the Benedictine order and its spread throughout Europe, Asia and Africa in the first three centuries of its existence. The monastery is famous for its picture gallery. It also houses the Museum of Literature in Moravia.
artist: Jan Blažej Santini-Aichl (1677–1723, Prague), František Benedikt Klíčník (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno), Jan Jiří Etgens (1691–1757, Brno), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Paissenberg – 1780 Baden), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812, Brno), Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)
history: The monastery is one of the largest in South Moravia and the only one owned by the Benedictine order. It was established in around 1025 as a branch of a monastery in Prague-Břevnov, on a site of an old settlement. Until the 17th century it maintained a largely Romanesque appearance (reconstructed to a design by A. Erna in 1670). The reconstruction, triggered by efforts to promote the monastery to an abbey, started in 1721. The majority of the original buildings were demolished and the restoration was only completed in 1840. From 1540 onwards Rajhrad provosts held seats in the Provincial Assembly. The monastery played a key role in local education and in the development of the economy establishing the tradition of winemaking and beer brewing, and facilitating the construction of hospitals, workhouses and orphanages. After 1623 the monastery housed a prestigious school. It is famous for its large picture gallery which acquired art works from dissolved monasteries and chateau collections. Among the monastery’s valuable collection is the Rajhrad Altar (c. 1420).
keywords: Presbytery, *modello*, bas-relief
partner: Muzeum Brněnska, Museum of Literature in Moravia

en.name: One-handled Jug
description:
This one handled jug is a fine example of free-blown glassware. In the middle of the 1st century BC, glass-makers along the Syro-Palestinian coast discovered that molten glass could be inflated with air through a hollow blow-pipe. This invention of ‘free-blowing’ revolutionized the glass industry. It allowed vessels to be mass-produced thus rendering them less expensive and available to a wider market so that by the end of the 1st century AD free blown glass vessels were used widely throughout the Roman Empire. The majority were undecorated utilitarian pieces, used for storage and transport, and tablewares, like beakers and plates, but others were embellished with applied decoration. While still hot their bodies were rolled over loose glass chips of contrasting colours and then marvered flush with the wall of the vessel. Next, the pieces where reheated and further inflated and manipulated, so that when their necks were pulled out of their bodies the splashes also became elongated.  
The jug is light green in colour; its neck is flaring downwards and its shoulder is sloping. Strap handle is applied at the shoulder with a large downward claw to either side, drawn up vertically, then turned in at an acute angle and trailed onto neck below the rim. It is in an intact situation, but some soil-encrusted weathering, blowing striations, pinprick bubbles, partly flaked off dulling and a jagged pontil scars are also seen on the surface.
dates: AD Third or early fourth century
keywords: Glass in Asia Minor; Roman Period; casting; blowing; mould-blowing

en.name: Cup
description: This pale green glass cup belongs to a very small and rare group of lobed glass vessels with high-relief vegetal decoration. It is mould-blown and of a rounded form with a lobed rim, a short foot and an applied handle. It is decorated at the rim with flutes, giving it a flower shape when viewed from above. A band of alternating vegetal palmette motifs in moulded high relief wraps around its body. A manganese-purple ring handle topped with a flattened thumb-rest is applied to the body. Lobed bowls were most often made by Iranian potters and metalworkers using moulds to produce vessels of other shapes with similar vegetal decoration in relief. High-relief vegetal decoration and lobed rims were also created in glass and pottery prior to the fifth century AH / eleventh century AD using methods other than moulding, especially relief cutting. In view of its relationship to ceramic production, this glass cup was probably made during the Ghaznavid or Seljuk era (late fifth or the early sixth century AH / late eleventh or the early twelfth century AD).
keywords: Glass; Cup; Mould-blown; Ghaznavid; Saljuk
materials: Glass; mould-blown with applied and tooled decoration
tags: mould-blown with applied and tooled decoration

cs.name: *Únos Heleny*
description:
Paridův únos Heleny, krásné manželky spartského krále, je počátkem Homérovy Illiady, eposu o Trojské válce, jenž byl malířům častým zdrojem moralistních, historických i zábavných obrazů už od dob renesance.  
Drama události, která vedla ke zkáze Troje, je vyjádřeno především drobnopisným podáním pohybových akcí množství figur, které zaplňují plochu obrazu. Brutální krvavé scény jsou zcela opominuty, malíř příběh podává jako divadelní událost. Napětí scény zvyšuje zpřítomnění přírodních živlů – větru rozevívajícího prapory i šat Heleny, akcentované rumělkově červenou a opírajícího se do plachet prchajících lodí – a moře. Antikizujicí architektura přístavu s toskánskými sloupy a obelisky patřila k běžnému rejstříku dekorativní malby 18. století. Bojovník se vztyčeným štítem vlevo je parafrází Lisippova “Bojovníka Borghese”. Byl jedním ze základních studijních objetů na akademii. Protějšek obrazu tvoří Únos sabinek, příběh, jenž souvisí se založením Říma a jenž je podle Vergilia pokračováním Troje.  
Detailně propracované, narativní figurální kabinetní obrazy jsou typickou ukázkou vídeňského akademického malíře, který se spolu s Franzem Janneckem na tento druh mezi tehdejšími sběrateli oblíbených dekorativních obrazů specializoval. Poučením na nizozemské malbě 17. století a zejména rudolfínském manýrismu vytvořil osobitý malířský styl, zdůrazňující roztěkaným světlem a kontrastními barvami smyslové kvality povrchů a věcí.

Detailně propracovaný, narativní kabinetní obraz je typickou ukázkou vídeňského akademického malíře, který poučením na nizozemské malbě 17. století a zejména rudolfínském manýrismu vytvořil osobitý malířský styl, zdůrazňující roztěkaným světlem a kontrastními barvami smyslové kvality povrchů a věcí.

en.name: *The Rape of Helen*
description:
Paris's kidnap of Helen, the beautiful wife of the king of Sparta, opens Homer's *Iliad*, an epic of the Trojan War. For artists, it provided a frequent source of moral, historical and entertaining scenes from the renaissance onwards.  
The drama of the event that led to the destruction of Troy is conveyed in detailed rendering of multiple figures moving through the picture area. Brutal, gory scenes are omitted; the artist presents the event as a theatrical spectacle. The suspense of the scene is enhanced by the presence of the elements: the wind blowing the flags, Helen's vermilion-red attire and pushing the sails of fleeing ships, and the sea. The ancient architecture of the harbour, with Tuscan columns and obelisks, was standard in the repertoire of 18th-century decorative painting. The warrior with erect shield on the left paraphrases Lysippus's “Borghese Warrior”, a staple object of study at art academies. The counterpart picture of *The Rape of Helen* was *The Rape of the Sabines*, a legend associated with the foundation of Rome and, according to Virgil, the continuation of Troy.  
Detailed narrative cabinet pictures with a host of figures are typical of the oeuvre of this academic Viennese painter who, together with Franz Janneck, specialised in the kind of decorative paintings favoured by art collectors. Inspired by Dutch 17th-century painting and, in particular, by Rudolphine mannerism, Platzer coined an original style, highlighting the sensory qualities of surfaces and things with scattered light and contrasting colours.

A detailed narrative cabinet picture, typical of this academic Viennese painter. Inspired by Dutch 17th-century painting, in particular by Rudolphine mannerism, he coined an original style highlighting the sensory qualities of surfaces and things with scattered light and contrasting colours.

en.name: Wellhead
description:
Wellhead in the shape of an external octagonal and internal semicircular prism, made of sifted reddish clay on which various decorative motifs have been stamped and complemented with green glaze. On a circular and smooth base, a prismatic shape rises, which is reinforced by the moldings that vertically decorate each of the walls, ending at the top with lobed modillions. Two decorative motifs alternate on its eight fronts. The first consists of a decoration of quadrilobed flowers included in a rhomboidal pattern, in the manner of the sebka network, all glazed in green and bordering its contours with manganese oxide. The second has a trilobed arch, whose central lobe is a sharp pointed horseshoe arch, and which houses a decoration with a mirror pseudoepigraphic motif ending in palmettes that end in a twisted stem. It ends, under the mouth of the border, with two borders: the lower one with a stamped seven-point star decoration, on which three bands with incised zig-zag lines and a central one with knife-corded thread, and the upper one contains a inscription in florid Kufic, transcribed by Sahwki Zayed (2015) as *at-tawfiq*, "The Providence", repeated five times on each side of the octagon. The presence of this inscription is confirmed in numerous Almohad works, and is common in the Merinid and Mudéjar works, but not in the Nasrid works. Its upper edge, thickened on the outside and rectangular in profile, is octagonal and smooth.  
  
Such wellheads can be understood within the broader development of water management systems in al-Andalus. Methods and objects were introduced and disseminated to optimise the water usage, an essential resource that significantly shaped everyday life. As part of these innovations, systems for water collection, distribution, and storage were devised. Among these, wells played a key role in accessing underground water, and wellheads such as this one were installed both in public spaces and in domestic courtyards.
place: House No. 6, Ambrosio de Morales Street, Córdoba.
keywords: Water, dwelling, *cuerda seca* technique, stamped decoration
materials: Clay, kaolin, metal oxide; Stamping, engraving, firing, partial dry rope

ar.name: حصن كاشيلا.
description:
كانت قشتالة دراق المقر الإداري لإقليم زراعي تم ضمه إلى قرى أوسونوبا، وهو الأمر الذي تؤكده المصادر المكتوبة اعتباراً من القرن العاشر الميلادي. فالبكري والإدريسي في القرنين الحادي عشر والثاني عشر يتحدثان عن كاشيلا كمنطقة قروية من غرب الأندلس. وحسب الإدريسي، يتعلق الأمر بقلعة مبنية على ساحل البحر، ذات كثافة سكانية وفيها بساتين وحقول تين. كما كانت مسقط رأس ابن دراق القشتالي (958 – 1030 ميلادي)، شاعر بلاط المنصور.  
يقع الحصن المبني من الحجر الكلسي على جرف يشغل موقعاً استراتيجياً بالنسبة للحاجز القديم الذي يقع على مدخل القنوات الداخلية المحمية لنهر فروموزا. مخططه مربع الزوايا ويبلغ طول ضلعه 40 مترا، ويضم أبراجا مربعة ومدخلا مكوعا. هدم زلزال عام 1755 التحصينات، وبالتالي فإن مظهره الحالي هو نتيجة أعمال إعادة البناء التي تمت في عام 1794.  
يدل اكتشاف حي إسلامي في المحيط الخارجي لأسوار كاشيلا التي هُجرت في نهاية الفترة الموحدية البرتغالية على تزايد في عدد السكان خلال تلك المرحلة، وأغلب الظن أن ذلك يعود إلى هجرات السكان المسلمين القادمين من الشمال. وخلال النصف الثاني من القرن 12 الميلادي، كان حصن كاشيلا مقر عمليات حربية ترمي إلى فتح الموحدين لقرية تافيرا، وهو الأمر الذي تحقق في عام 1168 ميلادي. تمت المعركة في البر وفي البحر لأن لكاشيلا منفذاً إلى البحر عبر قناة تافيرا. وتعود أعمال إعادة البناء وتدعيم أسوار التحصينات إلى فترة استقرار السلطة الموحدية في الغرب.

كانت قشتالة داراق المركز الإداري لإقليم قرى أوسونوبا، كما تشير إلى ذلك مختلف المصادر منذ القرن 4 الهجري / القرن 10 الميلادي. يحتلُّ الحصنُ الذي بني فوق قمة رابية موضعاً استراتيجيا، بالقرب من المدخل القديم نحو المياه المحمية داخل "لا ريا فورمازا"؛ وينتظم في تصميم مربع الزوايا بجوانب تصل إلى 40 متر؛ ويحوي أبراجاً مربعة ذات مداخل مكوعة في كل زاوية. دَمَّرت الهزةُ الأرضية لعام 1755 القلعة، ومظهرها الحالي نتيجة لإعادة البناء التي أنجزت عام 1794.
place: فيلا ريال دي سانتو أنطونيو؛ فارو.
dynasty: الفترة المرابطية، النصف الثاني من القرن 5 الهجري / نهاية القرن 11 الميلادي- النصف الأول من القرن 12 الميلادي.
keywords: عمارة عسكرية؛ حصن؛ كاشيلا؛ مرابطون.

en.name: Castle of Cacela.
description:
Qastala Darrague was the administrative headquarters of *iqlim* or rural district that was part of the *cora* (province) of Ossónoba, mentioned in written sources from the AH 4th / AD 10th century onwards. Al-Bakri and Al-Idrisi in the AH 5th and 6th / AD 11th and 12th centuries refer to Cacela as a village in the Gharb al-Andalus. Al-Idrisi adds that Cacela is a fortress built on the seashore, well populated and with many vegetable plots and fields of fig trees. Cacela was the birthplace of Ibn Darraj al-Qastalli (AH 347–422 / AD 958–1030), a poet at the court of al-Mansur.  
The castle is a construction of limestone masonry built on a cliff, occupying a strategic position close to the old harbour entrance to the inner sheltered waters of the Formosa Estuary. It is square in plan, its sides measure nearly 40 metres and it has square towers at the corners and an entrance at an angle. The fortification was destroyed in the earthquake of 1755 and its present appearance is the result of reconstruction work carried out in 1794.  
The discovery of an Islamic district on the outer perimeter of the walls of Cacela, which was abandoned at the end of the Almohad period in Portugal, suggests an increase in the population during this period, probably corresponding to the migration of Islamic populations from the north. In the second half of the AH 6th / AD 12th century, the castle of Cacela was the centre of military operations for the Almohad conquest of the town of Tavira, which took place in AH 563 / AD 1168. The battle was waged on land and sea, as Cacela had navigable access via the Tavira canal. The work of rebuilding and reinforcing the walled structure may date from the period when Almohad authority was being established in the Gharb.

Qastala Darrague was the administrative centre of the *iqlim* or rural district in the *kura* of Ossonoba, as recorded in various sources since the AH 4th / AD 10th century. The castle, which sits on top of a cliff, occupies a strategic position beside the old entrance to the inner sheltered waters of the Formosa Estuary. It is quadrangular with sides measuring some 40 m, and has square towers with chicane entrances in each corner. The earthquake of 1755 destroyed the fortress and its current appearance is the result of reconstruction work carried out in 1794.
dates: Hegira second half of 5th–first half of 6th century / AD end of 11th–first half of 12th century.
keywords: castle; Cacela; Almoravids; military architecture
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

es.name: Castillo de Cacela.
description:
Qastala Darray fue sede administrativa de un *iqlim* o distrito rural integrado en la *kura* de Ossonoba, y se menciona en las fuentes desde el siglo IV / X. Al-Bakri y al-Idrisi, en los siglos V-VI / XI-XII, se refieren a Cacela como una población de Garb-al-Andalus. Al-Idrisi añade que era una fortaleza construida a orillas del mar, bien poblada y con muchas huertas y campos de higueras. Cacela fue patria de Ibn Darray al-Qaltalli (958-1030), poeta de la corte de al-Mansur. El castillo, construido en albañilería de piedra caliza, se alza sobre un acantilado, en una posición estratégica junto a la antigua barra de entrada a los canales interiores de la ría Formosa. Tenía planta cuadrangular, con cerca de 40 m de lado, torres cuadradas en las esquinas y entrada acodada. El terremoto de 1755 destruyó la fortaleza, su aspecto actual se debe a las obras de reconstrucción realizadas en 1794.  
El descubrimiento de un barrio islámico en el perímetro exterior de las murallas de Cacela, que fue abandonado después del periodo almohade en Portugal, indica un aumento de población en ese periodo, que posiblemente corresponde a la migración de poblaciones llegadas del norte. En la segunda mitad del siglo VI / XII, el castillo de Cacela fue el centro de operaciones militares para la conquista almohade del poblado de Tavira (1168). La batalla se libró por tierra y por mar, dado que Cacela tenía acceso navegable por el canal de Tavira. Las obras de reconstrucción y refuerzo de la estructura amurallada datan quizá del periodo de implantación del dominio almohade en al-Garb.

Qastala Darray fue sede administrativa de un *iqlim* o distrito rural integrado en la *kura* de Ossonoba, tal como mencionan las fuentes desde el siglo IV / X. El castillo, situado sobre un acantilado, ocupaba una posición estratégica junto a la antigua barra de entrada a los canales interiores y resguardados de la ría Formosa. La construcción tenía planta cuadrangular, de cerca de 40 m de lado, torres cuadradas en las esquinas y entrada acodada. El terremoto de 1755 destruyó la fortificación, y su aspecto actual se debe a las obras de reconstrucción realizadas en 1794.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo V–primera mitad del VI de la Hégira / XI– XII d. C.
keywords: Arquitectura militar
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Château de Cacela.
description:
*Qastala Darrague* a été le siège administratif d'un *iqlim* ou district rural, intégré à la *kura* d'Ossonoba, ce qui est attesté par des sources écrites depuis le Xe siècle J.-C. al-Bakri et al-Idrisi aux XIe et XIIe siècles J.-C. se réfèrent en effet à Cacela comme à une bourgade du Gharb al-Andalus. D'après al-Idrisi, il s'agissait d'une forteresse construite au bord de la mer, avec une population dense, possédant des vergers et des champs de figuiers. Elle a été le berceau d'Ibn Darrague Alcacetali (958-1030), poète de la cour d'al-Mansour.  
Le château, en maçonnerie de pierre calcaire, est situé sur une falaise, occupant une position stratégique par rapport à l'ancienne barre d'entrée des canaux intérieurs et protégés de la Ria (rivière) Formosa. Son plan, quadrangulaire, mesuraitenviron 40 mètres de côté, présentant des tours d'angles carrées et une entrée coudée. Le tremblement de terre de 1755 a détruit la fortification, son aspect actuel est donc le résultat des travaux de reconstruction réalisées en 1794.  
La découverte d'un quartier islamique dans le périmètre extérieur des murailles de Cacela, abandonnées à la fin de la période almohade portugaise, indique une augmentation de la population durant cette période, due probablement à la migration de populations islamiques provenant du nord. Durant la seconde moitié du XIIe siècle J.-C., le château de Cacela a été le siège d'opérations militaires en vue de la conquête almohade de l'*alcaria* de Tavira, qui s'est matérialisée en 1168. La bataille s'est effectuée par terre et par mer, Cacela ayant accès à la mer par le canal de Tavira. Les travaux de reconstruction et de renforcement de la muraille d'enceinte datent sans doute de la période d'implantation du pouvoir almohade dans le Gharb.

Qastala Darrague était le centre administratif de l'*iqlim* (district rural) dans le *kura* de Ossonoba, comme le mentionnent différentes sources depuis le IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.). Le château, érigé au sommet d'une colline, occupe une position stratégique à côté de la vieille entrée vers les eaux abritées de l'intérieur de la Ria Formosa. Il est quadrangulaire, avec des côtés de 40 m environ, et possède des tours carrées à entrées en chicane à chaque coin. Le tremblement de terre de 1755 a détruit la forteresse et son apparence actuelle est le résultat d'une reconstruction réalisée en 1794.
dates: Seconde moitié du Ve siècle de l’Hégire (fin du XIe siècle-première moitié du XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: château ; Cacela ; Almoravides ; architecture militaire
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Castelo de Cacela.
description:
*Qastala Darrague* foi sede administrativa de *iqlim* ou distrito rural integrado na *kura* de Ossónoba, referenciado pelas fontes desde o século X. Al-Bakri e Al-Idrisi nos séculos XI e XII referem Cacela como povoação do Gharb-al-Andalus. Al-Idrisi acrescenta que Cacela é uma fortaleza construída à beira-mar, bem povoada e com muitas hortas e campos de figueiras. Cacela foi berço de Ibn Darrague Alcacetali (958-1030), poeta da corte de Almançor.  
  
O castelo é uma construção de alvenaria de pedra calcária localizada sobre uma falésia, ocupando uma posição estratégica junto da antiga barra de entrada nos canais interiores e abrigados da Ria Formosa. Tinha planta quadrangular, medindo cerca de 40 metros de lado e tinha nos cantos torres quadradas e entrada em cotovelo. O terramoto de 1755 destruiu a fortificação e o seu aspecto actual deve-se às obras de reconstrução realizadas em 1794.  
  
A descoberta de um bairro islâmico no perímetro exterior das muralhas de Cacela, que foi abandonado no final do período almóada em Portugal, indicia um aumento populacional neste período, provavelmente correspondente à migração de populações islâmicas vindas do norte. Na segunda metade do séc. XII, o castelo de Cacela foi o centro de operações militares para a conquista almóada da alcaria de Tavira, que se concretizou em 1168. A batalha travou-se por terra e por mar, dado que Cacela tinha acesso navegável pelo canal de Tavira. As obras de reconstrução e reforço da estrutura amuralhada podem datar do período de implantação do poderio almóada no Gharb.

*Qastala Darrague* foi sede administrativa de *iqlim* ou distrito rural integrado na *kura* de Ossonoba, referenciado pelas fontes desde o século X. O castelo, localizada sobre uma falésia, ocupava uma posição estratégica junto da antiga barra de entrada nos canais interiores e abrigados da Ria Formosa. A construção apresentava uma planta quadrangular, media cerca de 40 metros de lado e tinha nos cantos torres quadradas e entrada em cotovelo. O terramoto de 1755 destruiu a fortificação e o seu aspecto actual deve-se às obras de reconstrução realizadas em 1794.
dates: Segunda metade do séc. V – primeira metade do séc. VI AH / final do séc. XI – primeira metade do séc. XII AD.

en.name: Seljuq Rug
description: A “Konya Group” rug found in the Konya Aladdin Mosque and acquired by the museum in 1911. The condition of this rug is poor, nevertheless it is possible to perceive the general decoration. The rug is in three pieces, the remaining parts of a large carpet. The main border is wide and light red in colour. Stylized *kufic*letters in dark red are contoured with brown and placed side by side. The main border is separated from the basic ground by a yellow band framed with a narrow brown line. The dark blue ground is a diamond pattern with hooked ends. There are small heart shapes in their middle of these diamond shapes. Seljuq rugs were commonly woven in large sizes. They were decorated in plain geometric patterns, generally with a small number of colours in various shades contrasted with a wide *kufic* border.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
keywords: Middle Anatolia; Konya; Seljuq Rug
materials: Natural wool coloured with natural dyes; Gördes knot; symmetrical knot
tags: Natural wool coloured with natural dyes
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

en.name: Ceiling, custom-made for Shangri La's living room
description: The living room ceiling at Shangri La was custom-made by Moroccan artisans working under the supervision of the Rabat-based firm S.A.L.A.M. René Martin. It is carved, painted, and gilded throughout. The central field features recessed octagrams in interlocking, knotted niches, predominantly orange and brown in tone. The bottommost border consists of a moulded plaster frieze of floral motifs in an arcade repeated throughout.

en.name: Mirror
description: This circular copper alloy disc or mirror was used as a beauty accessory. One side is smooth and plain, the other side decorated in relief with two sphinxes either side of a tree. Around the rim is a band of blessings in *kufic* script.

en.name: Goblet
description: Cut glass goblet engraved with crown and thistles. This goblet is thought to have been used at a banquet in honour of King George IV's visit to Edinburgh in August 1822. During the late-eighteenth and early-nineteenth centuries, both the Caledonian Glass Works (Holyrood) and the Edinburgh Glasshouse Company (Leith) were known for producing decorative cut glass tableware. The crown and thistle would have been appropriate designs to welcome the British king to the Scottish capital. During this visit, various pageants, balls and banquets were organised with Sir Walter Scott leading the planning. Scott wanted to present a distinctive, loyal, Scottish population to the king. He encouraged the use of materials and motifs associated with Scotland, such as the thistle and tartan.
place: Leith or Holyrood Glass Works, Edinburgh
keywords: glass; Scottish George IV

en.name: Alfândega Velha (Old Customs House)
description:
D. Manuel I ordered the construction of the Customs House, and Pêro Anes, who also worked on the cathedral, was responsible for erecting it in 1508. In this enterprise, he had the help of a certain Bartolomeu.  
A 17th-century drawing shows the twostorey Manueline structure made up of two parallel wings, as can be seen by the line of the roof. The doors and windows were surrounded by stonework and the main floor had a panel that divided the window openings. The northern doorway had a lowered arch and foliate capitals. The Casa do Despacho (Dispatch Office), on the ground floor, is divided by parallel arcades of three depressed arches on cylindrical pillars with naturalist capitals, with the same design as that of the corbels. The chamfered pillars and arches are solid and imposing, as is the *Mudejar* ceiling of the Casa dos Contos (Counting Office), in the style of those of the cathedral aisles and transept with tracery, roses and geometric designs. The main door and windows opened onto a terrace overlooking the sea. On the eastern side, the building was more compartmentalised, and there are still two small Manueline doors; on the upper floor the smaller rooms also has *Mudejar* ceilings.

ar.name: بلاطة جدارية.
description:
بلاطة جدارية متعددة الألوان ومزخرفة بنمط هندسي متداخل الخطوط، بطبقات رقيقة من الأبيض والبني- العسلي والبني الداكن والأخضر النحاسي الفاتح، تفصل بينها حدود غير مزججة، واضحة المعالم، تعرف بتقنية (cuerda seca)، أي الحبل الجاف بالأسبانية. ويقصد بالحبل تلك الحدود غير المزججة الفاصلة بين كتل الأشكال اللونية التي يتشكل منها النمط. إن تقنية الحبل الجاف تقتضي ضغط النمط المقولب برفق فوق سطح الصلصال، ثم تغطَّى حواف النمط وحدوده بمزيج من أكسيد المنغنيز والزيت لمنع الطبقات اللونية المختلفة من التداخل. وبعد الانتهاء من تطبيق المادة الزيتية والطبقات الملونة بالرصاص الأبيض، تُعرَّض البلاطة للنار. وبينما تنصهر الطبقات الملونة داخل قوام البلاطة وتتقسَّى، يتلاشى المزيج الزيتي مخلِّفاً وراءه خطاً 'حبلاً' غير مزجج، واضح المعالم، يحيط بكامل الأجزاء المكوِّنة للرسم المصمم.  
أعيد فتح طليطلة على أيدي المسيحيين في عام 477 / 1085، ولكن التصاميم الهندسية للمدجَّنين ظلت شائعة، واستمر استخدامها في الزخرفة ضمن مجالات عديدة في فن العمارة بطابعيه الديني والدنيوي وصولاً إلى بداية القرن العاشر / السادس عشر.

هذا البلاط الجداري المُلَّون، المجلوب من طليطلة، مُزيَّن عبر اعتماد تقنية تُعرف باسم "كويردا سيكا"، حيث يتمّ تغليف أطر القالب النافر بمادة دهنية، لمنع أصبغة الأشكال المختلفة من التناضح، أثناء عملية الشيّ، في أفران الخزّافين.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.

en.name: Wall tile.
description:
A colourful wall tile decorated with a geometric interlace pattern in white, honey-brown, dark-brown, and light copper-green glazes that are separated by unglazed well-defined borders, using a technique known as *cuerda seca*, meaning 'dry cord' in Spanish; the 'cord' referring to the unglazed borders separating the masses of coloured shapes making up the pattern. The *cuerda seca* technique involves pressing a patterned mould gently onto the surface of the clay; the outlines and boarders of the pattern are then coated with a mixture of manganese-oxide and grease to prevent the different coloured glazes from running into each other. After completing the application of the greasy substance and the coloured lead-based glazes, the tile is fired. While the coloured glazes fuse themselves to the body of the tile and harden, the greasy mixture burns away leaving a clearly defined unglazed outline, 'cord', round all the compartments that make up the design.  
  
Toledo was re-conquered by the Christians in AH 477 / AD 1085, but Mudéjar geometric designs remained popular, and continued to be made and used decoratively in a number of contexts in both secular and religious architecture right up to the beginning of the 10th century / 16th century.

This colourful wall tile from Toledo is decorated using a technique known as *cuerda seca*, where the outlines of the embossed pattern are coated in a greasy substance to stop the paints of the different shapes from flowing over each other while being fired in the potter’s kiln.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
keywords: Palatial architecture; Geometric decoration; cuerda seca
tags: Glazed fritware with cuerda seca decoration.

es.name: Azulejo.
description:
Colorido azulejo decorado con un diseño geométrico entrelazado y vidriado en blanco, marrón miel, marrón oscuro y un ligero verde cobre, colores separados por bordes no vidriados realizados con la técnica de la cuerda seca.  
Se llama “cuerda” al surco sin vidriar que separa las superficies coloreadas y delinea el dibujo. La técnica de la cuerda seca consiste en estampar suavemente un molde en relieve en la superficie de la arcilla. Los contornos del diseño se rellenan después con una mezcla de óxido de manganeso y grasa para evitar que los vidriados de colores se mezclen entre sí. La pieza se cuece después de aplicar esta sustancia grasa y los vidriados plumbíferos. Mientras que los vidriados se funden con el azulejo y se endurecen, la mezcla grasa se quema y deja un contorno no vidriado, la “cuerda”, alrededor de cada parte del diseño.  
Los cristianos reconquistaron Toledo en 477 / 1085, pero los diseños geométricos islámicos, realizados por los mudéjares, siguieron siendo populares y se utilizaron para decorar edificios tanto seculares como religiosas hasta principios del siglo X / XVI.

Azulejo de Toledo decorado con la técnica de la cuerda seca: antes de cocerlo en el horno, se aplica en los contornos del dibujo (estampado con un molde) una sustancia grasa que evita que los colores de las distintas partes se mezclen entre sí.

dates: Siglo IX de la Hégira / XV d. C.
keywords: arquitectura palatina; decoración geométrica; cuerda seca

fr.name: Carreau mural.
description:
Carreau mural très coloré décoré d'un entrelacs géométrique de glaçures blanche, brun-miel, brun foncé et vert cuivré, séparées avec précision par des bordures non vernies, au moyen de la technique de la *cuerda seca* (corde sèche, en espagnol). Cette “corde” se réfère aux parties non vernies séparant les formes colorées constituant le motif. Cette technique consiste à presser délicatement un moule (portant le motif) à la surface de l'argile. Les contours et bordures du motif sont ensuite enduits d'un mélange d'oxyde de manganèse et de graisse pour empêcher les différentes glaçures colorées de couler et de déborder les unes sur les autres. Le carreau est cuit une fois l'application de cette substance grasse et des glaçures de couleur à base de plomb achevée. Pendant que les glaçures s'intègrent au carreau en durcissant, le mélange gras se consume en laissant une zone bien délimitée et dégagée de toute glaçure – la “corde” – autour des compartiments qui constituent le décor.  
Tolède fut reconquise par les chrétiens en 477 H / 1085 J.-C., mais le style des motifs géométriques mudéjars conserva sa popularité et fut utilisé dans de multiples applications décoratives jusqu'au début du Xe/XVIe siècle.

Ce carreau mural coloré de Tolède est décoré selon la technique dite de la *cuerda* seca, où les contours des motifs en relief sont enduits d’une substance graisseuse pour empêcher les couleurs des différents motifs de déborder les unes sur les autres lors de la cuisson dans le four du potier.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: architecture palatiale ; décoration géométrique
materials: Céramique frittée vernie, décor à la “cuerda seca”.
tags: Céramique frittée vernie, décor à la “cuerda seca”.

ar.name: طبق.
description: طبق مسطح وملون تحت التزجيج ذو حافة عمودية، وهو مزين بباقة من الأزهار الملونة بالأزرق الفاتح والغامق والأخضر والبنفسجي الرمادي، وتشتمل الأزهار على الخزامى وزنبق الوادي والأزهار الياقوتية. تحمل الأزهار الثلاثة الأكبر حجماً أشرطة متموجة متعرجة ضمن مساحتها الداخلية، وتتكرر هذه الأشرطة بشكل أصغر حول قاعدة الباقة. وقد عمل الفنان على إضفاء الحياة على التركيب إذ مثل الأزهار في حالة التمايل وتجنب بذلك الشكل المتناظر القاسي، وهو من ميزات الخزف الإزنيقي الأفضل.

صحن صغير، ذو حافة منحنية إلى الخارج، مُزخرف بأزهار التوليب، والبنفسج، وتظهر أيضاً ثلاث زهرات، كبيرة الحجم، رُسم داخل كل منها شريط من الغيوم المتلاصقة. تقنية صنع هذه القطعة يجعلنا نجمع بينها وبين قطع أخرى، صُنعت بالعجل على يد فنان يسمى "موصلي".
keywords: زخرفة زهرية؛ خزام

en.name: Dish.
description: A shallow dish with an upturned edge, painted under the glaze. The dish is adorned with a spray of flowers, painted in light- and dark-blue, sage-green, and greyish purple; they include tulips, lilies-of-the-valley, and hyacinths. The three largest flowers bear sinuous cloud-bands in their blossoms, which are reflected in the smaller cloud-bands flanking the base of the bouquet. As with the best of Iznik wares the artist has enlivened the composition by depicting the flowers swaying gently, thus avoiding a rigid and deadening symmetry.

A shallow dish with an upturned edge, adorned with a spray of flowers including tulips and hyacinths. The distinctive cloud-band motif in each of the three largest flowers lets us relate this plate to several other wares made by the circle of an artist named Musli.
keywords: floral decoration; hyacinths

es.name: Plato
description:
Plato llano de borde recto. Está pintado bajo vidriado con un ramo de flores en azul claro y oscuro, verde salvia y morado grisáceo. Componen el ramo tulipanes, lirios de los valles y jacintos. Las tres flores mayores tienen estilizadas nubes en su centro, idénticas a los que se aprecian a ambos lados del arranque del ramo.  
Como en las mejores cerámicas de Iznik, el artesano ha animado la composición representando con esmero las ondulantes flores, evitando una simetría rígida y carente de vida.

Plato llano de borde recto y decorado con un ramillete de flores, entre las que destacan tulipanes y jacintos. El característico motivo de las nubes del centro de las flores mayores permite relacionar este plato con otras varias cerámicas salidas del círculo de un artesano llamado Musli.
keywords: decoración floral; jacintos

fr.name: Plat.
description: Plat creux à bord relevé, peint sous glaçure. Il est orné d'un bouquet de fleurs – tulipes, muguet, hyacinthes –, peintes en bleu clair et bleu foncé, vert sauge et gris-violet. Au centre de la corolle des trois grandes fleurs figurent des rubans de nuages sinueux, que l'on retrouve en réduction au pied du bouquet. Comme dans les meilleures productions d'Iznik, l'artiste a su animer la composition en faisant délicatement onduler les tiges des fleurs afin d'éviter une symétrie rigide et ennuyeuse.

Plat creux à bord retourné et décor de bouquet de fleurs, dont des tulipes et des yacinthes. Le motif caractéristique de ruban de nuages dans chacune des trois plus grandes fleurs associe ce plat à plusieurs autres pièces réalisées dans l'entourage d'un artiste du nom de Musli.
keywords: Décoration florale; jacinthes
